title: /api/source lets any client read any file; server listens on all interfaces with CORS *
evidence: server.rs:95-125 reads the file/path query value and only decodes %2F, %20 and %2B. The raw decoded_path is tried first (server.rs:118) with fs::read_to_string (198-203), then a directory-walk fallback (206-222). The file content is returned as JSON (226-233). Paths are never canonicalized or checked against a root. The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32) and every response sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (server.rs:327). Found while scanning for hardcoded paths (FractalAndroid probe, server.rs:124).
impact: Anyone on the network, or any web page the developer opens (because of CORS *), can read any file the process can read, e.g. ?file=/etc/passwd or ?file=..%2F..%2F.ssh%2Fid_rsa.
recommendation: Only serve files under the analyzed repo root: canonicalize, check the prefix, reject absolute and '..' paths. Bind 127.0.0.1 by default. Restrict CORS to the Pages origin. Remove the hardcoded list of probe paths.

SRV.note: Same fix as COMP-R3-1. Absolute, drive and '..' paths are rejected, the hardcoded probe list (FractalAndroid etc.) is gone, and CORS is restricted to OPENHEART_CORS_ORIGINS

title: Unvalidated repo_url goes straight into git clone (option injection, SSRF)
evidence: process_analyze_request gets repo_url by splitting the raw body on quote characters (server.rs:366-371). It passes the value to 'git clone --depth 1 <repo_url> ./target_repos/<name>' (server.rs:429-437) with no '--' separator. WebRepoFetcher::validate_url (web_repo.rs:97) exists but only its unit test calls it (web_repo.rs:128). repo_name is the last URL segment, used unsanitized (server.rs:392-399).
impact: Callers can inject git options (values starting with '-'), make the server clone any host or protocol (file://, internal http), and fill its disk. Because of CORS *, other websites can trigger this too.
recommendation: Run validate_url and accept only https://github.com/owner/repo. Put '--' before the URL, limit allowed protocols to https, and sanitize the target directory name. Add timeouts, size limits and authentication.

SRV.note: Covered by the SRV-02 fix: validated GitHub URLs only, '--' separator, https-only protocols, sanitized target dir, timeouts, size limits, optional token auth

title: Unsound unsafe aliasing in the ROBDD manager can read freed memory
evidence: mod.rs:86, :102 and :122 build &[ROBDDNode] with from_raw_parts(self.nodes.as_ptr(), len) while also passing &mut self.nodes. make_node pushes new nodes (unique_table.rs:65). After recursion the stale slice is still read: apply.rs:104 reads 'nodes' after the call at :103 may have pushed, and apply.rs:136-138 holds fn_ = &nodes[f] across a pushing call. The SAFETY note (mod.rs:79-83) says clearing the cache prevents reallocation; it does not. mmap.rs:15 has no SAFETY note.
impact: If the Vec grows during apply_not or restrict, the code reads freed memory, producing wrong BDDs or crashes. Holding a shared slice alongside &mut is undefined behavior even without reallocation, and Miri would flag it.
recommendation: Remove the unsafe: pass only &mut Vec<ROBDDNode> and copy each node by index before recursing, or use an arena with stable indices. Add a Miri CI job for psa.

BDD.note: The aliasing slice is gone: apply, not, restrict and exists copy nodes out before allocating. The mmap.rs SAFETY note is handed off.

CORE.note: core/io/mmap.rs: safe open() now reads an owned buffer; true mapping is an unsafe fn map() with a documented Safety contract and SAFETY note. ROBDD aliasing is outside my paths.

title: Showcase diagrams are not reproducible engine output; hash and 'verified' are constants
evidence: All 18 JSON exporters hardcode compiler_hash "0x83D2D2B2" and verified: true (json.rs:415-416 through json.rs:2094). 12 of the 19 committed JSONs have other hashes (e.g. 0x55AA11FF, 0x33DD88AA) that appear nowhere in src, scripts or web. Their content describes OpenHeart itself rather than the sample input: states named 'Lexical Ingestion', an actor 'CI / CD Automation Agent', a BDD variable 'isSyntaxValid'.
impact: The public Studio presents hand-written data as engine output, and the 'verified' flag carries no information. This undercuts the README's 14-UML-diagram and traceability claims for anyone benchmarking the tool.
recommendation: Regenerate every showcase file from a pinned sample with the CLI in CI and fail on drift. Compute a real content hash with sha2, which is already a dependency. Compute 'verified' or remove it. Mark any illustrative files as illustrative.

SCPGX.note: Constant hash/verified removed: compiler_hash/input_digest = SHA-256 of the input snapshot, content_hash = SHA-256 of the graph, verified = structural checks passed; regenerating web/diagrams showcase files in CI is outside paths (handoff).

title: Only Java and JavaScript grammars exist; Kotlin, TypeScript and Rust use the wrong grammar
evidence: Cargo.toml lists only tree-sitter-java and tree-sitter-javascript. The Kotlin adapter returns tree_sitter_java::language() (kotlin.rs:30). TypeScript, Rust, Generic and Unknown are reduced with the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:21-28), and files with any other extension are parsed as JavaScript (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-38). The API advertises java, python, typescript, javascript, cpp, rust and go (server.rs:84). README.md:60 claims F1 = 1.0000 across six languages.
impact: Non-Java input quietly produces CSTs full of parse errors. Any outside benchmark will disprove the multi-language accuracy claims.
recommendation: Either add real grammars and adapters (kotlin, python, rust, typescript, cpp) with tests, or narrow the README and API claims to Java and JS. Reject unsupported extensions instead of falling back to JavaScript.

ENG.note: Same root cause as LANG-01. Grammar dependencies and adapter changes handed off.

CORE.note: No wrong-grammar fallback in either registry; TypeScript/Rust/Python/C++/Go files are rejected with diagnostics; claims in README/server are handoffs.

DOCS.note: README and API claims narrowed in docs; status.md records the hard-coded /api/supported-languages list; code handed off

SRV.note: Wrong-grammar fallback inputs are no longer collected and supported-languages is truthful. Adding grammars is outside my paths

title: The F1 metric scores 1.0 on empty sets and the published result cannot be reproduced
evidence: Running compute_metrics(set(), set()) from ruthless_verify.py:247-254 returns precision = recall = F1 = 1.0. F1 only compares sets of class names against a regex oracle from ruthless_config.json. It runs over ./target_repos, which is not tracked (ruthless_verify.py:18; scripts expect java-design-patterns, spring-petclinic and PlantUCD there). No pinned commits or expected outputs are in the repo.
impact: If neither the oracle nor the engine finds anything, the score is a perfect 1.0. Nobody else can reproduce the README's F1 = 1.0000, and it says nothing about diagram or design-pattern accuracy.
recommendation: Make empty ground truth fail instead of scoring 1.0. Pin dataset revisions and commit expected outputs. Report per-language sample sizes and relationship- and pattern-level precision, recall and F1.

title: Docker image cannot build or start; minimum Rust version is undeclared and misdocumented
evidence: Dockerfile:49 runs 'openheart serve --port 8080', but the CLI only accepts 'server [PORT]' (main.rs:532) and exits with code 1 on unknown subcommands (main.rs:544-548). Dockerfile:2 uses rust:1.80-slim, while the locked sha2 0.11.1 requires Rust 1.88 and edition 2024 according to crates.io. README.md:7 and getting_started.md:19 say Rust 1.75+. Cargo.toml has no rust-version, and the HOST/PORT environment variables are never read.
impact: The documented container path is broken at both build and start. Users on the advertised Rust version get build failures. CI only tests stable and beta, so it cannot catch either problem.
recommendation: Change CMD to ["openheart","server","8080"] or add a serve alias. Move the base image to rust:1.88 or later. Declare rust-version in Cargo.toml and the docs. Add CI jobs for the minimum Rust version and a Docker build plus smoke run.

ENG.note: Declared rust-version = "1.88" (the floor set by the locked sha2 0.11.1). Added `make msrv` and `make docker-smoke`, which starts the image with its default CMD. Dockerfile and docs fixes handed off.

DOCS.note: README badge, README and getting_started now say Rust 1.88 (Cargo.toml rust-version); Docker, CMD and CI MSRV handed off

SRV.note: Dockerfile CMD now runs 'openheart server', the base image is rust:1.88-slim-bookworm, and the C toolchain is kept for the grammars. rust-version 1.88 was already declared in Cargo.toml. README, docs and CI jobs are outside my paths

title: Diagram files: duplicate copies, communication equals sequence, empty Mermaid files, duplicate ids
evidence: communication.json is byte-identical to sequence.json (diagram_type "sequence"). The current exporter only relabels the sequence IR (json.rs:1660-1669). state.json and use_case.json are duplicates because the server writes both alias names (server.rs:648-652). The manifest references no .mmd files. statemachine, callgraph and robdd .mmd are empty headers or comments, against 11, 7 and 5 nodes in JSON. class.json has 0 edges and 5 duplicate ids, and graph-loader.js does not de-duplicate.

recommendation: Give the communication diagram its own IR. Write one canonical file name per type. List .mmd files in the manifest or delete them. Add CI checks for unique ids, a non-empty class edge set, and matching node counts across formats.

SRV.note: One canonical file is written per diagram type, aliases (use_case, state) are mapped when served, and empty exports are recorded as unavailable instead of written. The communication IR, manifest and duplicate ids are outside my paths

title: Binary artifact readers panic or allocate huge buffers on malformed input
evidence: There are 291 .unwrap() calls in src, 286 outside tests, and 208 are bytes[a..b].try_into().unwrap(). 84% of the non-test ones are in five serializers: uma 96, symbol 66, tra 46, ast 17, psa 15. uma/serializer.rs:268-300 loops over counts taken from the header and slices bytes[offset..offset+4] without checking the remaining length. Before that it calls Vec::with_capacity(class_count) with a count read from the file. The CRC-64 check (239-249) catches accidental corruption, not crafted files.
impact: inspect and every artifact reader crash on truncated or hostile files, either from an out-of-bounds index or a multi-GB allocation.
recommendation: Add a bounds-checked cursor (read_u32()? returning InvalidData). Cap counts by the remaining bytes before allocating. Replace unwrap with ?. Add a cargo-fuzz target for each reader.

BDD.note: PSA and TRA readers rewritten with bounds-checked cursors and count-vs-remaining checks before allocation; uma/symbol/ast readers are handed off.

CORE.note: Added bounds-checked ByteCursor (checked_count before allocation); .tca and .bpa readers rewritten on it; uma/symbol/tra/psa readers are handoffs.

UML.note: The uma reader is fully bounds-checked and caps counts before allocating; the other serializers are outside src/uma.

title: Server quietly analyzes a different repository and swallows I/O errors
evidence: When the clone fails, process_analyze_request takes the first directory in ./target_repos and keeps going (server.rs:467-481). Artifacts are read with fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default() (server.rs:536, 556, 581, 593, 609). Diagram writes ignore errors: 'let _ = fs::write' at server.rs:671, 680, 689, and .ok() at main.rs:258, 289, 298.
impact: A caller can get diagrams of an unrelated codebase labeled as the repo they asked for. Missing artifacts produce plausible empty diagrams instead of errors, which corrupts benchmark runs.
recommendation: Return an error status when the clone or any phase fails. Propagate I/O errors with context. Include the analyzed commit SHA and path in the response.

SRV.note: Phase and I/O errors propagate with proper statuses (no unwrap_or_default and no ignored writes). The response includes the commit SHA and the repo-relative analysis root

title: Heavy copy-paste in the diagram exporters (35% exact, 79% after normalization)
evidence: With 40-token windows: exporters 35.1% exact (json.rs 50%) and 78.8% normalized; all of src 13.0% exact and 54.1% normalized; tests 25.3% exact. Largest clones: json.rs:148-182 vs 445-479; mermaid.rs:383-424 vs plantuml.rs:76-117 (identical registries); mermaid.rs:1242-1257 vs plantuml.rs:1089-1102; for_stmt.rs:112-132 vs while_stmt.rs:31-51 (93% of while_stmt.rs); pass4_members.rs:18-32 vs pass5_hierarchy.rs:19-33; strategy_diagram_tests.rs:68-109 vs uma_tests.rs:49-100.
impact: Every fix has to be made three times (JSON, PUML, Mermaid), and the copies have already drifted, e.g. the empty Mermaid state diagram.
recommendation: Build one model per diagram type and render it through small per-format emitters. Use a generic registry and a macro for strategy impls. Share loop-lowering code in cfg. Move test fixtures into tests/common.

SCPGX.note: Exporter duplication removed: one view IR built once per kind, small per-format printers, macro-generated strategies, shared helpers in common.rs. cfg loop-lowering, pass4/pass5 and test fixtures are outside paths.

title: Very long functions hold most of the risk
evidence: Of 834 non-test functions (lengths by brace matching), the median is 10 lines and p90 is 65. 118 are over 50 lines, 43 over 100 and 13 over 200. Largest: pass1_discovery.rs:18-633 run (616), uma/serializer.rs:229-679 read (451), server.rs:366-762 process_analyze_request (397), class_diagram.rs:13-344 extract (332), json.rs:121-421 (301), main.rs:101-345 cmd_analyze (245).
impact: These functions cannot be unit-tested, and defects such as the silent repo fallback hide inside 400-line handlers.
recommendation: Split by concern: routing, validation, phase orchestration, record codecs. Enforce clippy::too_many_lines and cognitive_complexity limits in CI.

SRV.note: The 400-line process_analyze_request and cmd_analyze are split into routing, validation, fetch, discovery, run, report and response helpers. Other long functions are outside my paths

UML.note: Split the uma serializer, class extractor and pattern detector into small functions; other long functions are outside src/uma.

title: Only 29.6% of public Rust items have doc comments
evidence: Public fn/struct/enum/trait items preceded by ///, skipping attributes: 247 of 834 (fn 29.5%, struct 25.9%, enum 55%, trait 75%). By module: ssa 0/28, cfg 1/48, ingestion 6/50, ast 8/59, symbol 11/70, uma 24/114, scpg 44/214, tra 15/48, core 46/100, cg 10/14, psa 78/78. lib.rs has no #![warn(missing_docs)].
impact: Outside users and reviewers cannot use the query engine, SCPG format or IR types without reading the source.
recommendation: Turn on #![warn(missing_docs)] and later deny it. Document the scpg query and IR types first. Shrink the public surface with pub(crate). Run cargo doc with -D warnings in CI.

SRV.note: Added #![warn(missing_docs)] to lib.rs and doc comments on every public adapters item. Other modules are outside my paths

title: 14% of the web JavaScript is dead legacy UI code
evidence: Following imports from the inline module in index.html (index.html:408) reaches 14 of the 21 JS files. The unreachable ones are app.js, api.js, logger.js, orb.js, state.js, ui.js and viewer.js: 1,291 of 9,035 lines. index.html never loads app.js. ui.js looks up 45 element ids that index.html does not have (e.g. #orb-canvas at ui.js:46). 17 exports are never imported. theme-manager.js:8 holds a hand-copied DEFAULT_MANIFEST.
impact: Contributors and reviewers spend time on code that never runs, and the embedded manifest copy will drift from manifest.json.
recommendation: Delete the legacy modules or wire them in. Add ESLint with import/no-unused-modules to CI. Generate the fallback manifest at build time or drop it.

title: CI has no linting, minimum-version, supply-chain or release-artifact checks
evidence: ci.yml only runs cargo check, fmt and test on stable and beta. It has no clippy, minimum-Rust-version job, cargo-deny or audit, Docker build, or JS/Python lint; pyflakes finds 16 issues in the scripts. release.yml uploads libopenheart.rlib instead of the binary, has no 'permissions: contents: write', and uses the unpinned dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master. thiserror is declared at Cargo.toml:14 but never used.
impact: Problems like the broken Docker build and the unsound unsafe code ship unnoticed, and releases contain no usable binary.
recommendation: Add jobs for clippy -D warnings, the minimum Rust version, cargo-deny, Miri on psa, a Docker smoke run, eslint and pyflakes. Publish binaries per target. Remove thiserror or start using it.

ENG.note: Makefile now has lint, msrv, deny, miri and docker-smoke targets. release.yml, ci.yml and the thiserror decision are handed off.

title: Overflow checks are off in dev and test builds, alongside 846 unchecked numeric casts
evidence: Cargo.toml:23 sets overflow-checks = false under [profile.dev]. The test profile inherits from dev, so cargo test cannot catch integer overflow. src contains 846 numeric 'as' casts (pass1_discovery.rs 54, uma/serializer.rs 40, pass5_hierarchy.rs 27, cfg/builder/mod.rs 26). Example: uma/serializer.rs:39-42 writes counts as len() as u16, which silently truncates above 65,535.
impact: On large repositories, silent wraparound and truncation produce wrong graphs or corrupt artifacts while the tests still pass.
recommendation: Remove overflow-checks = false and keep opt-level = 2. Use u16::try_from(..)? and checked arithmetic in serializers and index math. Enable clippy::cast_possible_truncation.

ENG.note: Overflow checks are on in dev and test, and opt-level = 2 is kept. try_from in serializers and the cast lints are src/[lints] work, handed off.

UML.note: Narrowing casts in the uma serializer replaced by checked conversions; the Cargo.toml overflow-checks profile setting is handed off.

title: The test suite is thin and no test backs the headline claims
evidence: There are 76 #[test] functions in total. 47 are in src, and psa holds 793 of the 924 test lines there. 29 are in tests/, across 16 files, 9 of which contain a single test. No test asserts the 128x compression claim. There is no benches/ directory or criterion setup.
impact: The README's numbers are unverified, and the 28.7K-line engine has little protection when refactored.
recommendation: Add criterion benchmarks that report the compression ratio and lookup latency on pinned corpora. Add property tests for rank/select and serializer round-trips, and golden-file tests for each of the 19 diagrams.

title: CDN scripts load without Subresource Integrity
evidence: index.html:29-34 loads cytoscape 3.26.0, dagre 0.8.5, cytoscape-dagre 2.5.0, cytoscape-svg 0.2.0 and jszip 3.10.1 from cdnjs and jsdelivr with no integrity attributes. The only crossorigin attribute is on the fonts preconnect at index.html:21.
impact: If one of those CDN paths is compromised, it can run arbitrary script on the published Studio site.
recommendation: Add integrity hashes and crossorigin="anonymous", or vendor the libraries into web/vendor.

title: Broken relative links and duplicated HTML docs
evidence: Across 32 Markdown files with 81 links (49 relative), 3 are broken. SUPPORT.md:32 points to ../README.md, outside the repo. SUPPORT.md:36 points to CONTRIBUTING.md, but the file is docs/contributing.md. examples/README.md:12 points to ./sample_project/, which does not exist. No heading anchors are broken. Five HTML docs are byte-identical copies in docs/ and web/docs/.
impact: New users hit dead links, and the duplicated docs will drift apart.
recommendation: Fix the three links. Add a link checker such as lychee to CI. Generate web/docs from docs/ during the Pages deploy.

DOCS.note: SUPPORT.md links (README.md, docs/contributing.md) and examples sample_project link fixed; web/docs duplication and link checker handed off

title: Hardcoded developer paths, ports and personal URLs
evidence: server.rs:118-195 probes a fixed list that includes ./target_repos/FractalAndroid (124), and target_repos is hardcoded again at 211 and 399-470. Scripts expect untracked datasets (benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:28; test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:83, 190, 236; test_authored_design_patterns.py:129). localhost:8080 is fixed in generate_diagrams.py:8 and ruthless_verify.py:17. Personal repo URLs appear at web_repo.rs:128 and index.html:107. The FractalAndroid owner differs between index.html:1153 and test_diagrams_outputs_refresh.py:143.

title: .env.example documents settings the code never reads

The only environment variable the code reads is OPENHEART_LOG (core/logger.rs:98), and it is not documented. The Dockerfile's HOST and PORT are ignored too, and the code has no threading at all.

title: A prompt written for an AI assistant is committed under docs/
evidence: docs/RESEARCH_PAPER_NEXT_PROMPT.txt:1 tells an assistant to make the paper 'undeniably unchallenged'. It sits next to docs/openheart_research_paper.tex and is not documentation.

DOCS.note: docs/RESEARCH_PAPER_NEXT_PROMPT.txt deleted and removed from docs/README.md

title: 'F1 = 1.0000 across six languages' compares the engine against a near-copy of itself
evidence: README.md:60 and docs/overview.md:102-111 claim F1 = 1.0000. The ground truth is Oracle 1 alone, a keyword regex (ruthless_verify.py:61-100). The cross-validation described at :299 is never implemented (:303). The tool side is simple class names regex-parsed from PlantUML, stored in a dict keyed by simple name (:95, :225-234). The engine finds classes with the same keyword-plus-identifier heuristic (pass1_discovery.rs:249-349). 184 of the engine's 188 denylisted names (class_diagram.rs:163, 346-537) also appear in ruthless_config.json:59-92, which is applied to both sides (ruthless_verify.py:88, 232). Examples: Configuration, Root, Table, Logger, HomeScreen.
impact: The metric cannot detect wrong packages, nesting errors, duplicate simple names, or any error in the semantic phases. A real class named Configuration or Logger is removed from both truth and output, so recall is 1.0 by construction. The number cannot be falsified and will not survive external review.
recommendation: Withdraw the claim until it is re-measured. Score fully-qualified declarations against javac with SemanticDB, and against compiler-backed SCIP indexers for other languages, on pinned corpora with bootstrap CIs (suites S3, S13). Move the oracles into a separately reviewed package that is not allowed to share lists, filters or heuristics with the engine.

ENG.note: README, docs and the Python oracle are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: F1=1.0000 claim withdrawn in README/overview/CHANGELOG with reasons in docs/status.md §6; independent-oracle measurement protocol (S3/S13) added in §7; harness/oracle code is outside my paths

UML.note: Removed the engine's 188-name denylist that it shared with the oracle config; the README claim and the verify script are outside src/uma (handed off).

title: The six-language claim rests on only two linked grammars
evidence: Only tree-sitter-java and tree-sitter-javascript are dependencies (Cargo.toml:9-11). Kotlin is parsed with the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:30). Python, TypeScript, Rust, C++ and Go are detected (registry.rs:60-79), then routed to an Unknown adapter that uses the JavaScript grammar (registry.rs:34-38, 52-56). README.md:60 nevertheless claims validation across Java, Kotlin, Python, Rust, TypeScript and C++.
impact: Results for non-Java languages come from tree-sitter error recovery under the wrong grammar. CFG, SSA and call graphs built from them cannot be meaningful, and any comparison with a real multi-language tool will show this.
recommendation: Limit claims to Java (and JavaScript) for now. Add suite S13, which measures the per-language ERROR/MISSING node rate under the correct grammar and FQN precision/recall against SCIP indexers. Publish a result for each language before claiming it.

ENG.note: README claims and the measurement suite are outside my paths.

CORE.note: Code side done (only Java/JS grammars used for their own languages, Kotlin lexical-only, others skipped); README claim narrowing and suite S13 are outside.

DOCS.note: Claims limited to Java; suite S13 (per-language ERROR/MISSING rate plus SCIP FQN accuracy) defined; grammars are code

title: The code's own data structures contradict the 128x and 4.65 MB per 1M AST nodes claims
evidence: Claims: README.md:48,54; overview.md:119; architecture.md:107; succinct_structures.md:39-47. The 128x figure is the information-theoretic gap (paper .tex:292-296), not a measurement. Per node, the code stores: an 8 B u32 jump table over 2n bits (jump_table.rs:15-16); 17 B of preorder arrays (preorder.rs:4-8); u16 rank blocks for every 8 bits (rank_select.rs:8, 15-16); and a sparse-table RMQ over 2n positions times 21 u32 levels plus i32/usize side arrays (rmq.rs:24-54). Estimated from field sizes at 1M nodes: about 25 MB serialized (serializer.rs:34-61) and about 210 MB in RAM.
impact: The flagship number is about 5x too optimistic on disk and about 45x in memory. In RAM the structure is larger than the 32 MB pointer tree the docs compare it against. Any reviewer who measures RSS will refute the claim.
recommendation: Add suite S15: per-structure byte accounting plus dhat max-live heap for n = 10^3 to 10^7, published as bits per node. Drop the 128x claim until S15 supports it. To earn a succinct-structure claim, replace the jump table and sparse table with an o(n)-bit range-min-max tree, and derive parent from the BP sequence instead of parent_map.

CORE.note: Sparse-table RMQ, per-bit jump table, excess and log2 arrays removed; replaced by rank9-style rank/select + range min-max tree (~0.9 bit/node overhead); BPASTArtifact::memory_usage() reports real bytes; parent_map kept; docs/bench outside.

DOCS.note: 128x and 4.65 MB claims removed from README, overview, architecture, succinct_structures and paper; implemented layout documented as Theta(n log n) words; rmM-tree and S15 handed off

title: Latency and O(1) traceability claims are unmeasured and contradict each other
evidence: There is no criterion, divan or iai dependency and no [[bench]] target (Cargo.toml:8-19), and the repo has no benches/ directory. docs/overview.md:122-123 claims about 1 ns forward and 0.5 ns backward per query. docs/technical-decisions.md:29 says about 1 ns per binary-search comparison step. README.md:48,55 claims O(1) bidirectional traceability, while architecture.md:130 and overview.md:122 describe forward lookup as an O(log n) binary search.
impact: A binary search of about 20 steps cannot take 1 ns in total if each step takes 1 ns. The figures contradict each other and cannot be reproduced, which undermines every performance statement in the project.
recommendation: Add criterion or divan benches for forward and backward lookup, parent/LCA/subtree_size, CSR successor scans and query-cache hits. Sweep each over n and report p50/p99 and the fitted slope. Add iai-callgrind (now gungraun) instruction counts in CI. Until the data says otherwise, state O(log n) forward and O(1) backward.

title: The paper's tables cannot be reproduced, and its space theorem relies on structures the code lacks
evidence: The paper gives per-phase sizes for an unnamed 'representative 500K-LOC Java project' (tex:581-613) and says it is '~305 MB compressing to ~82 MB with LZ4' (:608, :816-818). There is no LZ4 dependency (Cargo.toml:8-16) and no script that produces the table. The space theorem (tex:874-895) relies on wavelet trees (tex:311-319, 853-867; architecture.md:110-111) and complement edges (architecture.md:119). No file in src/ mentions wavelet, complement or lz4.
impact: Submitting the paper as written risks failing artifact evaluation. The theorems describe a different system from the code that ships.
recommendation: Name the corpus and commit behind each number. Generate every table in the paper from bench results.jsonl with a script. Either mark wavelet trees, complement edges and LZ4 as future work, or implement them and back them with S14/S15 measurements.

ENG.note: The paper, architecture docs and the LZ4/wavelet code are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: Paper size table and 305/82 MB LZ4 text removed; wavelet trees, complement edges and LZ4 marked not implemented; space theorem remark added; missing docs/openheart.bib created

title: Tests named 'formal verification' and 'accuracy' are smoke tests with no expected outputs
evidence: research_paper_theorems_tests.rs:1-11 says it verifies every theorem. It actually checks one sort key (:24-43), one 3-variable BDD (:46-85), traceability as non-empty vectors (:141-146), and the 14 diagrams only by the presence of '@startuml' (:173-203). pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs asserts lower bounds (:99, :114, :125, :179) and that the call graph's method_count equals the total symbol_count (:221-222). adversarial_trick_tests.rs:240-262 passes if any one of four patterns appears. There is no proptest or quickcheck anywhere.
impact: Wrong CFG edges, dominators, phi placement, call targets or pattern roles all pass CI. The test names overstate the level of assurance to readers and reviewers.
recommendation: Add golden expected IR for each fixture: blocks, edges, idom, phi sets, call edges and pattern roles. Add property tests against naive reference implementations: BP navigation against a pointer tree, dominators against iterative dataflow, BDDs against truth tables, and sort-key injectivity on random tuples. Rename the tests to say what they actually check.

title: Corpora are unpinned, and the server can silently analyze a different repository
evidence: Every benchmark repo lives in target_repos, which is gitignored (.gitignore:58). A missing repo is shallow-cloned at HEAD (server.rs:418-437). If the clone fails, the server analyzes the first directory it finds in ./target_repos (:467-482) and still reports success. The scripts count status == success as a pipeline pass (benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:87; ruthless_verify.py:329).
impact: No published number can be reproduced. A result can silently come from the wrong codebase, which inflates pass rates.
recommendation: Add bench/corpus/corpus.lock.toml with URL, tag, commit SHA, archive sha256, LOC and license for each corpus. Fetch corpora outside the source tree. Make a missing or mismatched corpus a hard error. Record corpus SHA, file count and LOC in every result row.

title: The advertised IFDS solvers and Andersen points-to analysis are local marking passes
evidence: Claims: README.md:100,119,142; architecture.md:17; paper tex:754-756, 785-786. ifds.rs:12-37 makes one pass per function, marking definitions. A 'taint source' or 'type-state' fact just means the defining statement has a method-declaration child (:58-67, :80-89). 'Nullable' means any literal child (:69-78). Nothing propagates. points_to.rs:24-80 seeds sets at new-expressions keyed by the declared type of the defined symbol. It propagates only along phi copies, not through assignments, fields, parameters or returns.
impact: Standard benchmarks (PointerBench, SecuriBench Micro, OWASP Benchmark) will score near-zero recall on any flow through an assignment, field or call. Calling these analyses IFDS and Andersen misleads users.
recommendation: Until real solvers exist, rename these passes after what they compute. Make suites S2 and S6 a precondition for any future IFDS or points-to claim, starting with PointerBench and SecuriBench Micro in the PR tier.

DOCS.note: IFDS and Andersen claims withdrawn in README, architecture and paper, with what the passes actually compute; renaming the modules is code, handed off

title: There is no machine-readable export, so scoring has to regex-parse PlantUML
evidence: The CLI offers only analyze, inspect, server and help (main.rs:508-547). Exports are PlantUML, Mermaid, JSON-graph and XMI (scpg/api/mod.rs:74-111). Every scorer recovers classes and relations with regexes over PlantUML text (ruthless_verify.py:225-241; benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:51-74; test_authored_design_patterns.py:66-122).
impact: Scoring loses information: only simple names, no source spans, no call-site positions. A cosmetic exporter change can silently change a metric. Phase 3-8 outputs cannot be scored at all.
recommendation: Add 'openheart export --format ohb-json' with versioned JSON Schemas covering: symbols (FQN, kind, byte span); type edges; per-method CFG, idom and phi; call edges (JVM descriptors, call-site line/col); points-to; pattern instances with role bindings; the UML model; BDD statistics; and per-phase timings. Add 'openheart query' so latency can be benchmarked.

CLI subcommand handoff.

title: Evaluation scripts either cannot fail or never run the engine
evidence: benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py exits 0 on both branches (:210-215). The PlantUCD 'stress test' only regex-parses the dataset's PlantUML, never calls OpenHeart, and logs a literal True (test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:229-267, :259). The 14-diagram 'verification' checks the header, footer and brace balance plus a substring. For example, any line containing 'Flow' passes the interaction overview check (verify_all_14_uml_diagrams.py:59-121, :114-116). test_full_suite.py matches output strings such as '4 passed' (:166-231) and prints a hardcoded F1 claim (:243).
impact: The reported 100% pass rates carry no information and hide regressions.
recommendation: Make every bench step exit non-zero on a regression. Validate diagrams with pinned PlantUML -checkonly, mermaid-cli and Eclipse UML2 XMI loading. Then score their content against oracles (S10-S12).

title: Machine-generated .urm.puml files are presented as architect ground truth, and the oracle is hand-patched
evidence: benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:10 calls the files 'official software architect .urm.puml ground-truth diagrams'. They are actually generated from compiled classes by UML Reverse Mapper (urm-maven-plugin). The parsers rename GHobbits/GOrcs/GWeather to Gen* and drop Node_* and pkg_* names (:58-65; test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:59-65). The pass thresholds are recall >= 0.85 and F1 >= 0.80 (:219), and 5 of 6 hierarchy edges (:160), while the README claims F1 = 1.0.
impact: Agreement with another reverse-engineering tool is reported as correctness, and the hand-made renames tune the oracle to fit the tool.
recommendation: Use URM as a differential oracle. Regenerate its output at a pinned java-design-patterns commit with a pinned urm version, compare FQNs and relations, and sort disagreements into a published triage list instead of patching names.

ENG.note: Benchmark scripts are outside my paths.

title: Pattern detection has no labelled evaluation and partly relies on class names
evidence: Several detectors test names: contains('factory') (factory.rs:17), contains('state' or 'strategy') (state.rs:17-18), ends_with('Builder') (builder.rs:33). The output is one pattern label per class with a confidence score and no role bindings (mod.rs:40-60). The tests only check that a singleton exists (uma_tests.rs:156) or that any one of four patterns exists (adversarial_trick_tests.rs:240-262).
impact: On corpora where class names reveal the pattern, such as java-design-patterns, scores will look excellent. They will collapse on P-MARt or on renamed code. Per-role precision and recall cannot be computed.
recommendation: Emit role-bound instances (pattern, role -> FQN). Evaluate per pattern and per role on P-MARt, DPB and the DPDf corpus. Add an identifier-obfuscation ablation that separates structural detection from name matching (S9).

title: Reported timings mix an HTTP round trip, a debug build and file writes into the repo
evidence: Each module is timed as one wall-clock HTTP round trip to target/debug/openheart, with no warm-up or repetition (benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:27, 82-86, 193). The server's execution_time_ms covers all phases plus writing PlantUML, Mermaid and JSON for 21 diagram types into ./web/diagrams (server.rs:505, 636-699). The dev profile uses opt-level 2 with overflow checks off (Cargo.toml:21-23).
impact: The timings mix analysis, export and disk I/O. Every run also overwrites the shipped web/diagrams, which makes results depend on run order and dirties the working tree.
recommendation: Time the release CLI with hyperfine (at least 3 warm-ups and 10 runs, JSON export). Emit per-phase timers in ohb-json. Write outputs only to a temp directory, and stop the server from writing into the source tree.

title: CI has no accuracy or performance gate, the badge is static, and the test count is stale
evidence: CI runs only cargo check, fmt and test (ci.yml:40-47; ci_check.sh:9-16); none of the accuracy scripts runs in CI. README.md:10 is a static shields.io image that always reads 'CI-passing'. README.md:164 says there are 47 unit and 22 integration tests; the tree has 47 #[test] in src/ and 29 in tests/.
impact: Headline numbers can go stale without anyone noticing, and the badge shows green whatever the real CI state is.
recommendation: Add the PR smoke tier and the nightly full tier with the thresholds described in the harness design. Switch to the workflow's real status badge. Generate test and benchmark counts in the docs from CI output.

ENG.note: The accuracy gates, badge and test counts live in ci.yml and README.

DOCS.note: Static badge and stale test counts removed from README; PR and nightly accuracy tiers defined; CI handed off

title: The web studio uses a separate regex extractor capped at 80 files
evidence: The GitHub Pages studio finds classes with a regex (github-engine.js:291), falls back to classes derived from file names (:383-392), and parses only the first 80 files (:199-200). README.md:57 calls this client-side AST parsing. The CLI scans only .java/.kt/.kts files and does not exclude tests (main.rs:76-99). The server, which every script uses, accepts about 60 extensions and skips tests (server.rs:790-884).
impact: What most users see is not produced by the engine being benchmarked, and results differ by entry point. Any number given without naming the entry point is ambiguous.
recommendation: Benchmark the browser extractor, the CLI and the server as separate systems, and record each one's input-selection rules in every result. Disclose the 80-file cap in the UI. Longer term, compile the Rust engine to WASM so a single extractor serves every entry point.

DOCS.note: status.md §3 records CLI, server and studio input rules; README and getting_started disclose that the studio heuristic samples files; UI disclosure and WASM handed off

SRV.note: CLI and server share one input-selection rule set, reported in run.json and in the response (input_selection, skipped). The browser extractor's 80-file cap is in web/

title: 'Zero-copy' artifacts are copied and re-indexed on load
evidence: README.md:59 claims every phase artifact is mapped directly into page memory. In fact the .bpa reader copies each array element into new Vecs and rebuilds rank/select and the sparse-table RMQ on every load (serializer.rs:120-184).
impact: Opening an artifact costs O(n log n) time and temporarily doubles memory. The load-time and query-latency claims for a mapped .scpg do not hold for the reader that ships.
recommendation: Add artifact-open latency and RSS benchmarks, with cold and warm page cache, to S14/S15. Move to aligned sections that are mapped directly (for example zerocopy or bytemuck slices), and persist the auxiliary indexes instead of rebuilding them.

CORE.note: .bpa v2 has a section directory with 8-byte-aligned sections and rebuilds indexes in O(n/64) word ops (no sparse table); not yet zero-copy.

DOCS.note: Zero-copy claim withdrawn in README and ledger; readers' copy-and-rebuild behaviour documented

title: UML 2.5 claims have no conformance checks, and timing diagrams use a made-up clock
evidence: XMI is emitted as XMI 2.1 in the Eclipse UML2 3.0.0 namespace (xmi.rs:10), not as OMG UML 2.5.1 XMI. Timing diagrams advance a fixed clock by 50 per message, using only the first sequence. When there is none they fall back to the first 3 classes times 2 methods (plantuml.rs:1196-1240; uml_derivation.md:113). README.md:56,64-91 claims all 14 UML 2.5 diagrams, yet no test loads the XMI or checks any behavioural diagram against what the program does.
impact: The interoperability and 'all 14 diagrams' claims cannot be verified. Some projections are invented rather than derived from program semantics.
recommendation: Validate XMI by loading it in a pinned Eclipse UML2 5.x with EMF validation. Score behavioural diagrams against dynamic traces (S11). Label projections that have no oracle, such as timing and interaction overview, as illustrative.

DOCS.note: README subtitle no longer claims UML 2.5; uml_derivation and status.md say no conformance checks exist, mark timing as illustrative, and give the XMI 2.5.1 target; XMI validation handed off

title: Competitor comparisons use unsourced figures that published data contradicts
evidence: docs/overview.md:16-25 asserts, without citations, that: Joern uses 32 B per node and 34 B per edge; EMF emits 100-150 MB per 1,000 classes; WALA/Soot need 8-16 GB per 1M LOC; and k=2 points-to runs out of memory above 500K LOC. overview.md:120 also compares against an uncited 170 MB Neo4j store. By contrast, Tai-e's paper (Table 1) reports Doop and Qilin finishing 2-obj on findbugs in 638 s and 2,033 s, and context-insensitive runs in 15-46 s.
impact: Unsourced claims of superiority invite rebuttal and erode trust in the rest of the documentation.
recommendation: Replace these with numbers the harness reproduces on the same corpus and hardware, or cite primary sources. Always label each number as 'published' or 'reproduced'.

DOCS.note: overview.md competitor section rewritten as qualitative, with no unsourced figures and a 'published or reproduced' rule; paper prop:prior per-record byte figures replaced by asymptotic arguments

title: The layouts' 'zero overlap' guarantees are never measured
evidence: web/js/uml-layout.js:4 says 'Guarantees zero overlapping', and web/js/graph-canvas.js:8 promises a '100% Collision-Free Guarantee'. No test or script measures overlaps, crossings or bends.
impact: Layout quality is a key user-facing output, yet nothing protects it against regressions and the guarantee cannot be checked.
recommendation: Add suite S12: extract node and edge geometry in a headless browser, gate overlap count at 0, and measure crossings, bends, area, aspect ratio and determinism. Compare against Graphviz dot and ELK Layered on identical graphs.

title: Genuine Kotlin and multi-language frontends with a versioned support matrix
evidence: The Kotlin adapter returns tree_sitter_java::language() (src/ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). The AST registry maps JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Generic and Unknown to one JavaScript-grammar adapter, and Kotlin falls through to it (src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28,37-42). Only a Java SemanticAdapter exists (src/symbol/adapter/mod.rs:1). Cargo.toml:9-11 pulls in only the tree-sitter 0.20 Java and JavaScript grammars. Yet README.md:60 claims six languages and src/adapters/server.rs:83-85 advertises seven. Tests and examples contain no lambdas, sealed types or switch patterns.
impact: Kotlin and every non-Java input produce Java parses full of errors or JavaScript-shaped ASTs, so multi-language results cannot be trusted. CodeQL and Joern publish support per language and per version. Without that, OpenHeart cannot be compared even on Java and Kotlin, its stated core.
recommendation: Upgrade to a current tree-sitter release. Add tree-sitter-kotlin-ng with Kotlin AST and semantic adapters. Gate Java 8-25 and Kotlin 1.9-2.x features behind conformance fixtures, and publish a support matrix. Reject unsupported files instead of silently using the JavaScript grammar. Drop unimplemented languages from the README and /api/supported-languages until they pass.

ENG.note: The Kotlin grammar and adapters live in [dependencies] and src. Handed off with LANG-01.

CORE.note: Kotlin no longer parsed with the Java grammar: dedicated Kotlin lexer frontend + SourceLexer trait, explicit supported_languages(); registries accept injected grammar adapters (run_with_registry) for the concurrent tree-sitter-kotlin adapter; README/API claims outside.

DOCS.note: Versioned support matrix with tier promotion criteria published in docs/status.md §2 and ROADMAP; grammars and the registry-driven API are code, handed off

title: Build-system, classpath and bytecode awareness
evidence: Input is whatever .java/.kt/.kts files a directory walk finds (src/main.rs:76-98). Nothing in src handles Maven, Gradle or a classpath, and there is no JAR or class-file reader. The JDK is modelled by 12 stub classes, Object through Throwable (src/symbol/std_library/java_stubs.rs:8-21). The server also feeds about 50 unrelated extensions into the Java pipeline (src/adapters/server.rs:805-867).
impact: Calls into the JDK, Spring, Android or any dependency stay unresolved. Call graphs, sequence diagrams and data flow therefore stop at the first library boundary, which is exactly where CodeQL, Joern, SootUp, WALA and OPAL resolve types.
recommendation: Add --classpath and --build maven|gradle modes that resolve dependencies (mvn dependency:build-classpath, Gradle Tooling API). Add a Rust class-file reader that loads signatures from JARs and JDK jmods, and cache library summaries. Later, add a bytecode frontend so compiled Java and Kotlin can be analysed the way SootUp and Joern's jimple2cpg do.

SRV.note: Build-system, classpath and bytecode awareness needs ingestion and symbol frontends outside my paths

title: Real interprocedural analyses: constraint-based points-to, RTA/VTA, IFDS/IDE and taint specs
evidence: Points-to seeds only NN_NEW_EXPR definitions and propagates through phi copies; it has no assign, field, parameter or return constraints (src/cg/points_to.rs:24-79). '1-CFA' looks up receiver types and has no call-string context (src/cg/resolution.rs:115-166). src contains no RTA, VTA or XTA. IFDS flags definitions by AST shape with a fixed source id of 1 and has no sinks, propagation or summaries (src/ssa/ifds.rs:17-37,58-67). This contradicts ROADMAP.md:71 and 80.
impact: No result can answer security, nullness or precise-dispatch questions, which are the core value of every static-analysis competitor. Behavioural UML built on this call graph inherits its imprecision.
recommendation: Implement field-sensitive Andersen over assign/load/store/call/return constraints, with SCC collapsing and on-the-fly call-graph construction. Add RTA and VTA. Replace ifds.rs with Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv tabulation over an ICFG with summary edges, then IDE. Ship a format for specifying sources, sinks and sanitizers, with Java framework models. Validate against SootUp and OPAL output.

DOCS.note: ROADMAP now marks IFDS, Andersen, 1-CFA, RTA/VTA and taint specs as planned, with a dependency-ordered plan; implementation is code

title: Benchmark-grade accuracy and scale evidence
evidence: The F1=1.0 claim (README.md:60) only checks that class names found by regex reappear in the PlantUML (ruthless_verify.py:61,247-254,342). Pattern precision, recall and F1 default to 1.0 when there is no ground truth (scripts/benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:102-104). That ground truth is uml-reverse-mapper .urm.puml output (lines 10, 100). The 'huge' corpus is 12 files / 255 LOC (examples/huge_enterprise_src). No runtime, memory or soundness figures back the 128x claim (README.md:48).
impact: The headline claims cannot be checked. Expert reviewers comparing OpenHeart with Joern, CodeQL, OPAL or Doop will discount the project until the numbers are reproducible.
recommendation: Add a benchmark suite that runs in CI. Measure call-graph soundness and precision on Reif/Judge/CATS against SootUp, WALA and OPAL; points-to against Doop/Qilin on DaCapo/XCorpus; and taint on OWASP Benchmark. Report LOC/s, peak RSS and artifact size against Joern flatgraph and CodeQL on spring-framework, elasticsearch and kotlinx. Compare UML accuracy with IntelliJ/VP exports and GoF detection on P-MARt.

title: Declarative query language exposed via CLI, HTTP and library
evidence: QueryEngine caches only two calls (src/scpg/query/mod.rs:39-83) over eight fixed helpers. None is routed through the CLI (src/main.rs:509-549) or the HTTP server (src/adapters/server.rs:77-289). CFL reachability is a BFS that rescans all edges per node (src/scpg/query/cfl.rs:21-31). The backward slice ignores SSA and CDG (src/scpg/query/slice.rs:12-45). 'O(1)' navigation is a linear scan (src/scpg/query/navigation.rs:8-27).
impact: Users cannot ask their own questions. QL, CPGQL, Semgrep rules and Doop's Datalog turn their engines into platforms; OpenHeart remains a fixed report generator.
recommendation: Expose the SCPG layers as relations and either embed a Datalog dialect (Ascent/Crepe, or export Soufflé facts) or offer a Cypher subset. Add `openheart query` and /api/query with streaming JSON. Implement true Dyck/CFL reachability and SDG slicing over def-use plus CDG. Ship a starter query library with docs.

SRV.note: No query language or engine work in my paths; scpg/query is outside them

CLI `query` and /api/query are handoffs.

title: Standard interchange: SARIF, GraphML/DOT/GraphSON, SCIP and full XMI 2.5.1
evidence: XMI emits only `Class_<sym_id>` packagedElements in an Eclipse UML2 3.0.0 namespace (src/scpg/diagram/export/xmi.rs:8-18), whatever the diagram type (src/scpg/diagram/factory.rs:140-148). The studio's XMI export is an empty stub (web/js/ui.js:123-127). The JSON graph IR has no schema or version field (src/scpg/diagram/export/json.rs:30-45). src contains no SARIF, GraphML, DOT, GraphSON or SCIP writer.
impact: Results cannot flow into GitHub code scanning, Neo4j/Gephi, Sourcegraph, or EA/VP/Papyrus models. Interop is table stakes in both tool categories.

Write XMI 2.5.1 with attributes, operations, associations, generalizations and diagram interchange, and validate it by round-tripping through Eclipse UML2/Papyrus, EA and VP. Version the JSON IR and publish a JSON Schema for it.

title: Real incremental, commit-aware analysis
evidence: apply_delta classifies a delta and returns current_hash ^ 0x0101_0101 (src/scpg/incremental/mod.rs:26-34). Staleness is a hash comparison (src/tra/delta/invalidation.rs:10-21). Parsing passes no old tree (src/ingestion/parser/tree_sitter.rs:21-23), and analyze reruns all ten phases (src/main.rs:150-254). Neither the five-stage Merkle protocol (docs/traceability_and_incremental.md:71-80) nor ROADMAP's 'O(1) incremental delta update' (ROADMAP.md:116) is implemented.

recommendation: Content-hash files and functions, and persist per-file artifacts. Reparse using tree-sitter edits and the old tree. Track dependencies between phases (salsa-style) so CFG, SSA and PSA are recomputed only for touched functions and their callers. Add --baseline <commit> to produce findings and diagrams for the diff only.

BDD.note: Foundations only: stable keys, per-entity content digests and DeltaApplicator/StaleDetector. Commit-aware incremental reanalysis (baseline commit, reparse) is outside my paths.

title: Demonstrated large-codebase scale: indexed, parallel, streaming pipeline
evidence: Every call site rescans all symbols (src/cg/resolution.rs:84,133,185,212,225). CFL reachability scans the full edge list on each pop (src/scpg/query/cfl.rs:27). The server is a single-threaded accept loop that reads one 8 KiB buffer (src/adapters/server.rs:40-48). Cargo.toml:8-16 has no parallelism crate. The browser engine stops at 30 remote / 80 local files (web/js/github-engine.js:103,200).

recommendation: Index symbols by (parent, name) and store the call graph as CSR adjacency. Parallelise the per-file and per-function phases with rayon. Stream ingestion and artifact writes. Make the server async with bounded request bodies. Publish LOC/s and peak RSS at 100K, 1M and 5M LOC alongside Joern and CodeQL.

SRV.note: Working container with a HEALTHCHECK ('openheart health'), CLI exit codes and a machine-readable run.json. Release binaries, Action, SARIF and --baseline/--fail-on are not implemented (no findings model exists)

title: Wire token-anchored traceability into exports and the studio
evidence: JSON nodes get file set to '<Name>.java' and lines set to [1, 5, 10] (src/scpg/diagram/export/json.rs:267-268) or [1] (json.rs:581). No exporter or factory reads the TRA artifact. Navigation is linear despite the 'O(1)'/'O(log n)' comments (src/scpg/query/navigation.rs:8-27). Source files are found through hard-coded example paths (web/js/editor.js:183-193; src/adapters/server.rs:119-198).
impact: The headline 'O(1) bidirectional source-to-diagram traceability' (README.md:48) never reaches users. Clicking a diagram element cannot reliably open its code, which IntelliJ and Sourcetrail do by default.
recommendation: Emit real UMLLink spans (path, line/column range, token ids, scpg_hash) on every node, edge, member and message. Build the dense backward index for O(1) lookup. Resolve files by file_id from the corpus instead of guessing by name. Add end-to-end tests that check click-to-source lands on the right code.

SRV.note: Traceability preview resolves files through the corpus file id (tca.file_path), gives repo-relative paths and null when unknown; /api/source resolves through the analysis manifest. Exporter spans are outside my paths

SCPGX.note: Every node, member, edge and message carries a SourceSpan (path, line/col range, token ids); navigation index and studio/server file resolution are outside paths (handoff).

SCPG.note: NavigationIndex with dense sym->span O(1), max-end segment tree O(log n+k) innermost-first, SourceLocation (path by file_id, line/col range, token ids, engine scpg_hash), link_record stamped with the shared short hash. Exporter/studio wiring is handoff.

title: Diagram UX parity: search, semantic filters, focus+context, commit diffs, local rendering
evidence: The canvas offers package collapse, a minimap, focus-by-file and an edge-kind filter (web/js/graph-canvas.js:31,36,728,778). Search exists only as an icon (web/js/icons.js:19), and there is no compare or diff view. PlantUML is rendered by POSTing the diagram source to kroki.io (web/js/api.js:68).
impact: Large diagrams are hard to explore. Architecture drift between commits, which IntelliJ revision-as-UML, VP Visual Diff/History, EA Compare and CodeSee Review Maps all serve, is not supported. Sending code-derived diagrams to a third party also blocks use on proprietary code.
recommendation: Add fuzzy search and filters by package, visibility, stereotype, pattern and layer. Expand callers, callees and implementations on demand, and aggregate by level of detail beyond about 1K nodes. Add two-commit diff views that colour added, removed and changed elements using the SCPG hashes. Render PlantUML and Mermaid locally by default.

title: IDE and LSP integration
evidence: The only subcommands are analyze, inspect, server and help (src/main.rs:509-549). Cargo.toml:8-16 has no LSP or editor-protocol dependency, and the HTTP server exposes no editor-oriented routes (src/adapters/server.rs:77-289).
impact: Developers have to leave the editor to see diagrams or results. IntelliJ diagrams, Semgrep's LSP-based extensions, CodeQL for VS Code and Sourcetrail's plugins have set the expectation of in-IDE use.
recommendation: Add `openheart lsp` (tower-lsp) with diagnostics from the analyses and code lenses such as 'show in class/sequence diagram'. Support go-to-diagram and back via UMLLink spans, with incremental updates on didChange. Host the studio canvas in a VS Code webview, and rely on JetBrains' LSP support for IntelliJ.

ENG.note: An LSP server is src work plus a new dependency with its code.

SRV.note: LSP and IDE integration not implemented; it depends on query and traceability APIs outside my paths

title: Open extension model: loadable language adapters, rule/pattern packs, stable schema
evidence: Adapters are hard-wired in AdapterRegistry::new (src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:19-42) and ASTAdapterRegistry::new (src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:15-31). Only a Java SemanticAdapter exists (src/symbol/adapter/mod.rs:1). Exporter factories can only be registered from Rust (src/scpg/diagram/factory.rs:309), and pattern detectors are compiled-in functions.
impact: Third parties cannot add a language, detector or exporter without forking. Joern frontends, CodeQL packs and Semgrep rules grew their ecosystems through exactly these extension points.
recommendation: Publish a versioned SCPG schema and a semver crate API. Load language adapters from declarative tree-sitter query files (.scm) for declarations, calls and types, or as WASM components. Make pattern and architecture detectors data-driven rule packs. Document a 'write a frontend' guide with a reference Kotlin adapter.

CORE.note: Frontends pluggable: AdapterRegistry::register/register_lexer, SourceLexer trait, IngestionStage::run_with_registry, ASTStage::run_with_registry; declarative/WASM loading not done.

SCPGX.note: Loadable language adapters and rule packs live outside src/scpg/diagram; exporter registries remain extensible through register_strategy/register_factory.

title: Semantics-based design-pattern and architecture recovery
evidence: Singleton fires on any field named 'instance' or 'getinstance', typed as the class itself, or named like the class, and scores it 100 (src/uma/patterns/singleton.rs:20-31). Observer fires on any method that starts with add/register/attach and contains 'listener', scores it 85, and never uses the call graph (src/uma/patterns/observer.rs:11,25-38).
impact: A linked-list Node with a `Node next` field becomes a Singleton at 100% confidence, and renamed variants are missed. Pattern recovery is a differentiator only if it is accurate and measured.
recommendation: Match structural and behavioural signatures: private constructors, static accessors that return the class's own type, role-consistent call-graph and points-to facts, and field accesses. Output participant roles with calibrated confidences. Evaluate on P-MARt and DPB, and publish precision and recall per pattern.

ENG.note: Pattern detectors are outside my paths.

UML.note: Pattern recovery is now semantics-based with roles; evaluating on P-MARt/DPB is not possible in this phase.

title: Claims ledger, docs-code alignment and contributor community
evidence: The README advertises 128x compression, O(1) traceability and F1=1.0 across six languages (README.md:48,54-60) with no reproducible scripts. ROADMAP marks every phase complete (ROADMAP.md:9-120) while incremental analysis and IFDS are stubs. The competitive section faults Joern's 32-byte node records from before flatgraph (docs/overview.md:15-16). git log shows 147 of 154 commits by one author since 2026-08-08.
impact: Expert evaluators check claims first, and mismatches cost more trust than missing features. A bus factor of one also deters adopters and contributors.
recommendation: Keep a claims ledger that links each headline number to a benchmark artifact produced in CI, and label experimental features. Update the competitive section against current Joern, CodeQL and SootUp. Publish docs.rs API docs, a support matrix, ADRs, good-first issues and a discussion forum, and recruit co-maintainers.

DOCS.note: Claims ledger, support matrices, competitor section updated for flatgraph/CodeQL/SootUp, ADRs and contributor guide; forum and co-maintainers are non-code actions

title: Use-after-free: BDD apply/not/restrict read through a raw slice of the Vec they push into
evidence: BDDLibrary::apply builds `read = unsafe { slice::from_raw_parts(self.nodes.as_ptr(), len) }` and then passes `&mut self.nodes` into apply(), whose make_node does `nodes.push(..)` (unique_table.rs:64-65). The justification comment (mod.rs:79-83) says the Vec 'never reallocates mid-recursion ... because we pre-cleared the cache'. That is false: nodes starts as `vec![F,T]` (capacity 2) with no reserve, so pushes reallocate at every power of two, and every later `nodes[f]` read in the recursion dereferences freed memory. apply_not and restrict repeat the same pattern.
impact: Undefined behaviour on essentially every non-trivial function, in both the CLI and /api/analyze. Results range from silent BDD corruption and wrong counts to a segfault once the freed buffer is reused or unmapped. The current tests cannot detect it.
recommendation: Remove the unsafe blocks. ROBDDNode is Copy, so read `let n = self.nodes[f as usize];` into a local before recursing and pass only `&mut self` or indices. Add `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` to src/psa, run `cargo +nightly miri test psa::bdd` in CI, and add a >100k-node regression test checked against a truth-table evaluator.

BDD.note: All unsafe removed: BDD ops read nodes by value and are iterative; src/psa and src/tra compiled under #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

title: #SAT(f_paths) is not the path count: Phi_b leaves unreached edges free, so paths are overstated exponentially
evidence: Phi_b only encodes reach(b) -> out-constraint (constraints.rs:64,82,131). Nothing forces the edges of unreached blocks to 0, there is no C_exit (the paper's definition includes one), and the entry variable is restricted away (mod.rs:95) yet still counted as free by sat_count(f_paths, n_vars) (mod.rs:109). In a faithful Python port, whose sat_count equals brute-force model counts: one if/else gives 8 instead of 2; k sequential if/else give 2*4^k instead of 2^k; 20 guard clauses give 8,667,850,491,898 instead of 21. The theorem test itself counts (1,1,1) as a path.
impact: Phase 8's headline metric is wrong for essentially every branching function, and it is published in PlantUML/Mermaid annotations, UMA records and Phase 9 aggregates.
recommendation: Count acyclic paths exactly with Ball-Larus path numbering (MICRO 1996): an O(V+E) dynamic program after back edges are replaced by dummy entry/exit edges, using num-bigint BigUint, with loops reported separately. If a decision-diagram path set is needed, build a ZDD of s-t paths with Knuth's Simpath / frontier-based search (Kawahara et al. 2017). Done means a proptest differential test against brute-force path enumeration on random structured CFGs.

BDD.note: New exact flow encoding over the Ball-Larus DAG plus an O(V+E) path-count DP using an unbounded PathCount; the BDD #SAT is cross-checked against the DP and loops are flagged separately (PSA_FLAG_HAS_LOOPS).

DOCS.note: Paper Def. of f_paths rewritten as flow conservation with C_exit, new Path Characterization lemma, Ball-Larus count, theorem restated as a proven m(d+1) bound plus conjecture; phase8.md corrected; psa code fix handed off

title: Static variable orders make ROBDDs exponential on plain sequential code, with no node or time budget
evidence: The initial order is DFS edge pre-order (rpo.rs:12-64), not RPO. FORCE then refines it, but its branch hyperedge omits the predecessor edges that Phi_b couples (force.rs:106-118), and it runs a fixed number of iterations with no span check. Ported pipeline on k sequential if/else: 9,344 / 18,688 / 37,376 reachable nodes at k=10/11/12 (83k / 174k / 348k stored). At k=9, FORCE gives 11,588 nodes against 103 for a plain topological order, and 4,736 against Theorem 5.2's bound of 75 (m=38). There is no node limit, timeout or fallback, and recursion depth is unbounded.
impact: A method with about 20-24 sequential if/else needs gigabytes and minutes, then runs out of memory. /api/analyze runs Phase 8 synchronously on cloned repositories, so this is a remotely triggerable DoS.
recommendation: Seed with a locality-preserving order: blocks in RPO, each block's in and out edges adjacent. Keep FORCE only with its span-based stopping rule, then apply real sifting (BDD-06). Enforce a per-function node budget and deadline (as CUDD's Cudd_SetMaxMemory / Cudd_SetTimeLimit do) that degrades to a 'summary unavailable' record with DP metrics. Make apply/restrict/sat_count iterative. Done means a criterion benchmark showing linear growth on series-parallel CFG families.

BDD.note: Topological seed with each block's in and out edges adjacent, FORCE with a span stop rule, real sifting, per-function node budget and deadline that degrade to a 'summary unavailable' record, fully iterative ops.

SRV.note: Pipelines run under bounded concurrency, a time budget (504) and source size/count limits. ROBDD ordering and node budgets are in psa/, outside my paths

title: compute_max_path_length enumerates every walk (exponential) and returns the bound for any loop
evidence: The DFS pushes (s, depth+1) for every successor with no visited set or memoization, stopping only at sinks or when depth >= #blocks (mod.rs:164-168). Ported to Python, a single loop containing an if/else followed by straight-line code needs 175 / 6,603 / 1,179,565 pushes at 17 / 37 / 67 blocks, roughly x1.8 per 10 blocks. Acyclic if/else chains cost 2^k. For any cyclic CFG the result is simply the block-count bound, not a path length.
impact: Ordinary methods of 150+ blocks hang Phase 8, and with it the server request, even when the BDD is small. max_path_len is meaningless for every function that contains a loop.
recommendation: Compute the longest acyclic path by dynamic programming over the DAG left after removing back edges (from cfg.loop_info or DFS edge classification), in O(V+E). Store a separate has_loop/unbounded flag or a loop-bound estimate. Done means tests on diamond chains, nested loops and a 10k-block synthetic CFG, each finishing in milliseconds.

BDD.note: Longest path is now an O(V+E) DP over the back-edge-free DAG; loops get a flag and saturation gets its own flag.

title: Feasibility filter is unsound: SSA ids are reused as BDD variable indices and collide with edge variables
evidence: build_condition_bdd picks the last non-phi SSA def in the block, not the branch condition, and uses `ssa_id & 0x3FFF` as a BDD variable (feasibility.rs:115-123). SSA ids are function-local and start at 0 (renaming.rs:124-133), the same range as edge variables 0..n_vars, so `cond -> x_true` (line 73) usually constrains an unrelated edge. In the port, the diamond count drops from 8 to 4 (the else-path is deleted) on a collision, and becomes 68 when the variable is >= n_vars, because sat_count's gap logic assumes var < n_vars. Block ids are also truncated to u8/u16 (lines 88, 115; ssa.rs:43).
impact: Feasible paths are removed or counts become garbage, contradicting the documented 'sound over-approximation'. Correlated or contradictory predicates are never actually detected.
recommendation: Extract atomic predicates from condition ASTs and canonicalize them (SSA value numbering, normalized negation and comparisons). Allocate predicate variables in a separate range above the edge variables and quantify them out before counting. Decide infeasible branch combinations with an SMT solver (z3 crate or bitwuzla) under a time budget, as KLEE and CBMC do. Widen def_block to u32. Done means tests with correlated (if(x>0)...if(x>0)) and contradictory branches.

BDD.note: Aliasing filter removed. Predicate variables now get their own levels, the x_true/x_false implications are added and the variables are quantified out. Canonical predicates need a Phase 5 producer (handoff); until then nothing is filtered and the PSA flag says so.

CORE.note: SSARecord.def_block widened to u32 (no 8-bit truncation); predicate allocation/SMT in psa are outside.

title: 'Rudell sifting' is a no-op: only the ordering table is permuted, never the BDD
evidence: sift_variable calls ordering.swap_adjacent() but never rewrites any node, and it measures size with bdd.node_count() (sifting.rs:51,59,70), which cannot change. As a result `sz < best_size` never fires, best_pos stays at the starting position, and the final loop returns the variable home. A simulated full pass leaves the ordering identical for n=2..39. `_root` is unused. If a swap ever did stick, var_to_edge would no longer match the node.var labels. The paper and phase8.md both claim Rudell sifting with in-place swaps.
impact: No dynamic reordering exists to rescue the bad static orders behind BDD-03, O(n^2) swaps per function are wasted, and a published algorithmic claim is false.
recommendation: Implement Rudell sifting (ICCAD 1993): per-level unique subtables, in-place adjacent-level swaps that touch only levels i and i+1, reference counts for live size, a max-growth cutoff of about 1.2x, and CUDD-style perm/invperm level indirection. Alternatively, adopt oxidd, which already ships reordering. Done means a test where sifting shrinks a deliberately bad interleaved order to linear size.

BDD.note: Real Rudell sifting on the final compacted ROBDD: in-place adjacent swaps, per-variable unique subtables, refcounts, perm/invperm, 1.2x growth cutoff, swap and time budget, result kept only if smaller and #SAT unchanged.

DOCS.note: Paper Phase 8 text, phase8.md, architecture and succinct_structures state that sifting has no effect and what real Rudell sifting needs; code handed off

title: The 'SCPG hash chain' does not hash the artifacts; staleness detection is global and non-deterministic
evidence: compute() ignores _bpa, _cfa and _ssa (hash_chain.rs:30-33). bpa_hash is crc64 of the file count and cga_hash is crc64 of call_site_count (lines 37, 41); cfa_hash is sta.bpa_hash ^ sta.tca_hash (39). tca_hash hashes the Debug string of the file records, which includes mtime_ns (36; source.rs:10-20). The six values are XOR-folded and truncated to CRC32 (44). Invariant 3 recomputes the same formula from the stored fields, which makes it a tautology. Every UMLLink carries this single value, so is_stale is all-or-nothing. The PSA writes cfa.sta_hash into its ssa_hash field (psa/mod.rs:78).
impact: AST, CFG and SSA changes go undetected, while a `touch` or a fresh clone marks everything stale. Cross-artifact provenance cannot be verified, and the paper's Eq. 8 is unbacked.
recommendation: Hash the canonical artifact bytes with BLAKE3, chain them as h_i = H(h_{i-1} || bytes_i), exclude mtimes, and keep at least 128 bits. Store per-entity digests (per-symbol declaration/body hash, per-function CFG hash) so staleness is decided per element. Verify the chain on load, and write the real .ssa digest into the PSA's ssa_hash. Done means tests showing that a body edit invalidates exactly that function's records and a touch invalidates none.

BDD.note: SHA-256 digests of canonical artifact content (no mtimes or CRC links), chained as h_i = H(h_{i-1}||label||d_i) at 256 bits. Per-entity stable keys and content digests, chain checked on load and by Invariant 3, real SSA digest written to PSA.ssa_hash.

CORE.note: Hash chain lives in src/tra; outside my paths.

title: Incremental invalidation is dead code and unsound; the documented 5-stage protocol does not exist
evidence: DeltaApplicator::compute_delta and StaleDetector have no callers outside their own module and its re-export. compute_delta compares BI_sym by positional sym_id and global token ids (delta/mod.rs:28-38). Inserting one token or symbol early shifts every later id and invalidates nearly everything. An edit that keeps a declaration's token span is missed, deletions are never reported, and nothing propagates dependencies. IncrementalEngine::apply_delta just returns `current_hash ^ 0x0101_0101` with stale_link_count 0. The rope buffer, tree-sitter incremental reparse and Merkle diff described in the doc do not exist.
impact: The paper's incremental-update theorem (thm:incr) and the README's incremental claims have no implementation. Every edit means a full 10-phase rebuild.
recommendation: Model the phases as Salsa queries (salsa crate: revisions, durability, early cutoff/backdating) keyed by stable ids (qualified name plus signature; file path plus byte offset). Use tree-sitter Tree::edit and changed_ranges to find dirty functions, rerun Phases 4-8 only for those, and diff per-entity hashes to decide UMLLink staleness. Done means an edit-replay benchmark over real commit histories that reports the recomputed fraction and latency.

BDD.note: Real per-entity delta in tra (match by stable key; added/removed/modified/relocated; propagation to enclosing declarations and transitive callers). Salsa, tree-sitter reparse and the scpg apply_delta are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: traceability_and_incremental.md rewritten: §3 is design-only, stub modules listed, prerequisites and acceptance criterion added; code handed off

SCPG.note: Implemented plan->rebuild->commit protocol in scpg::incremental: stable-id keyed, position-independent signature/body fingerprints, salsa-style changed_at/verified_at backdating, stale-link and changed-fraction reporting. Salsa crate, Tree::edit reparse and partial rerun of phases 4-8 are outside my paths (handoffs).

title: Backward index returns fabricated or misaligned source ranges
evidence: Synthetic or empty blocks (every ENTRY and EXIT) get ft=lt=0 to satisfy Invariant 1, which is the first token of file 0. BI_ssa derives per-function block offsets from max(def_block)+1 (ssa_bi.rs:13-24) instead of the CFA block counts that BI_blk uses, and def_block is truncated to u8. Phi-nodes always take this fallback path (def_stmt=u32::MAX), so in every function after the first they resolve to blocks of other functions. Span lines are cast to u16 (sym_span.rs:38,40), missing UMLLinks become (0,0,0,0,0), and Invariant 4 checks only the first 5% of sym ids.
impact: Theorem 5.3 round-trips fail for synthetic blocks and phi-nodes, and entity-to-source navigation silently lands in the wrong file or line.
recommendation: Build block and SSA offsets from CFA prefix sums and store them in the .tra. Use an explicit no-source sentinel, or the owning function's span, for synthetic blocks. Widen def_block (Phase 5) and the line fields to u32, and return Result diagnostics instead of assert!. Done means an exhaustive round-trip check plus a proptest that every BI range lies inside its owning function's span.

BDD.note: Block and SSA offsets come from CFA prefix sums and are stored in .tra; synthetic blocks map to the owning function span or an explicit sentinel; phis resolve via PhiRecord block ids; u32 lines; UMLLink sentinels; exhaustive Invariant 4 reported as Result diagnostics. def_block u8 widening is handed off.

CORE.note: Core part: def_block is a full u32; tra backward-index changes outside.

title: 'O(1) bidirectional traceability' is not delivered: forward and navigation queries are scans
evidence: forward_sym_query walks backward from the partition point and breaks only when the file changes (sym_span.rs:60-70). That costs O(log N + symbols before the token in the file), not the documented O(log N + k). forward_cs_query never stops once first_token_id < token_id (cs_span.rs:51-60). UMLLinks are 'sorted for O(1) array index access', but they cover only UML kinds, so they cannot be indexed by sym_id. NavigationEngine::to_source does a linear .find and from_source a full filter, and class diagrams run a .find per class (O(C*U)).
impact: Query latency grows with file and repository size, and the README's headline O(1) traceability claim is false for every forward and navigation query.
recommendation: Exploit span nesting: store each span's enclosing-span index (or reuse the BP AST's parent/LCA), binary-search the innermost span, then walk parents for O(log N + k). Use an interval tree such as rust-lapper for non-nested data. Give UMLLinks a dense sym_id-to-slot array, break cs queries early, and add CSR offset tables for blocks and SSA. Done means criterion p50/p99 latency benchmarks at 1M symbols.

BDD.note: Span parent links give O(log N + depth) forward queries, cs query is O(log N + k), dense uml_slots give O(1) uml_link()/source_range(). Consumers in navigation and class_diagram are handed off.

DOCS.note: README traceability claim split into O(1) backward vs scanning forward; paper and traceability doc specify enclosing-span links for O(log n + k); code handed off

UML.note: The class extractor now uses an indexed binary search for UML links instead of a linear .find per class; TRA and navigation queries are handed off.

SCPG.note: Navigation side fixed (O(1) entity->source, O(log n+k) source->entities, innermost first, no fabricated 0:0 spans; artifact-level to_source is binary search). TRA forward queries and class_diagram per-class find are handoffs.

title: BDD engine lacks complement edges, a persistent computed table and GC; the artifact ships about 8x garbage nodes
evidence: apply() clears the computed table on every call (mod.rs:78), not and restrict allocate fresh HashMaps, and XOR's terminal case rebuilds NOT with a new map each time (apply.rs:64,67). Nothing is reused across a function's hundreds of conjunctions. There are no complement edges, no ITE, a SipHash unique table, and no reference counts or GC. into_nodes() ships every intermediate node: 39,585 stored against 4,736 reachable at 9 diamonds, which inflates n_nodes and total_nodes. verify_canonicity never checks the variable-order invariant.
impact: Several-fold time and memory overhead compared with CUDD, Sylvan and oxidd, bloated .psa files, and misleading ROBDD-size metrics.
recommendation: Adopt oxidd (Rust: complement-edge BCDDs, ZDDs, parallel apply, reordering, generic sat_count) or biodivine-lib-bdd (exact_cardinality). Otherwise rebuild CUDD-style: complement edges, ITE with standard triples, a lossy global computed table keyed on (op,f,g), per-level FxHash subtables, reference-count GC, and mark-compact of the root's sub-DAG before serialization. Add an order check to verify_canonicity. Done means criterion benchmarks against oxidd on n-queens and ISCAS'85.

BDD.note: Persistent lossy computed and not tables, Fx hashing, iterative ops, mark-compact of the root sub-DAG before serialization, order check in verify_canonicity. Complement edges, ITE and refcount GC are not implemented.

title: Recursion, interprocedural composition and BDD queries are not implemented
evidence: RecursiveHandler::apply returns f_paths unchanged and stamps unwind_depth=3 (recursive.rs:26-28); nothing is unwound. No callee summary is ever read, and the documented callee-first order is actually inverted: Tarjan already emits callee SCCs first (scc.rs:103), and Phase 8 reverses them (psa/mod.rs:102). No code reads the stored node arrays or ordering tables; the only PSA query returns header sat_count and cyclomatic. The claimed 'path feasibility in O(|ROBDD|)' capability does not exist, and processing is single-threaded.
impact: The interprocedural and recursion claims are unbacked, and the .psa carries large node arrays that nothing can query.
recommendation: Either drop the claims and the node arrays, or implement them: a query API (restrict to an edge set and test satisfiability or count, paths through an edge, witness extraction via any_sat), call-site summary composition (Sharir-Pnueli functional approach or IDE), and bounded inlining for recursive SCCs. Use Tarjan's order without .rev(), and add rayon parallelism per function. Done means one test per advertised capability.

BDD.note: Query API added (psa::query: count with required/forbidden edges, paths through an edge, feasibility, witness). Tarjan order used without .rev(), per-function parallelism via std::thread::scope, recursion flagged honestly. No interprocedural composition.
