SCPG.note: PathSummaryIndex stores the ROBDD node arrays and ordering and answers count_paths under edge restrictions, is_feasible, witness (any_sat), paths_through_edge with ordering/bounds validation; ROBDDQueryEngine returns Option. Recursion unwinding, summary composition and Tarjan order fix are in psa (handoff).

title: edge_index_of linear scans make Phase 8 O(E^2) and map parallel edges to one variable
evidence: edge_index_of is `cfg.edges.iter().position(|(f,t,_)| f==from && t==to)` (rpo.rs:106-107). It is called for every predecessor and successor of every block during Phi_b construction, hyperedge building, DFS ordering and feasibility filtering, so each pass is O(E^2). Matching on the (from,to) pair also merges parallel edges, which Phase 4's add_edge never dedupes, into one variable. For a binary branch, XOR(x,x)=FALSE would then make the block unreachable.
impact: Large generated methods (switch tables and parsers with around 10^4 edges) cost about 10^8 comparisons per pass, and multi-edges would silently zero out paths.
recommendation: Have Phase 4 emit edge ids in the CSR (a succ_edge_id[] parallel to succ_adj, plus pred_edge_id[]) and index BDD variables by edge id, giving O(1) lookups. Keep parallel edges as distinct variables, or merge them explicitly with multiplicity weights for counting. Done means an O(E) construction pass and a test with a duplicated edge.

BDD.note: PathGraph builds edge-id CSR in O(V+E); variables are indexed by edge id so parallel edges stay distinct; all edge_index_of scans removed.

title: No reference/occurrence index and no stable symbol identity (gap against Kythe/SCIP)
evidence: The .tra holds only declaration spans (BI_sym, sym_span, UMLLinks), and neither the STA nor the TRA records use-site occurrences. Find-references, go-to-definition from a use, and role-tagged occurrences are therefore impossible. All keys are positional: sym_id is the STA vector index, token ids are corpus-global, and file_id is the manifest position cast `as u16` (ingestion/mod.rs:70), which wraps beyond 65,535 files.
impact: Below the Kythe/SCIP/LSIF baseline: no cross-reference navigation, no cross-repo linking, no IDE or Sourcegraph interoperability, and links that do not survive a rebuild.
recommendation: Add an occurrence table (file, byte range, symbol, roles: definition/reference/read/write/import) populated during Phase 3 name resolution, with SCIP-style stable symbol strings (scheme, package, descriptor#method(sig).). Emit a SCIP index via the scip crate, report LSP positions (UTF-16 columns), and use u32 file ids. Done means `scip lint` passes and precision/recall is measured on a labelled Java corpus.

BDD.note: Stable symbol identity added: 128-bit stable_key from kind, name path, parameter-type signature and ordinal. An occurrence table needs Phase 3 use-site data (handoff).

CORE.note: Occurrence index/SCIP is Phase 3/7 work outside my paths.

title: Phase 7/8 tests and the 'theorem' tests are tautological; no ground truth, Miri, fuzzing or benchmarks
evidence: The 'Theorem 5.2' test hand-builds (x1|x2)&x3 rather than deriving it from a CFG, and asserts sat_count = 3, treating the both-branches assignment as a path. 'Traceability Totality' asserts only len() > 0, and the 'hash chain' test only checks scpg_hash != 0. psa_tests checks sat_count >= 1, which over-counting always satisfies, and tra_tests looks up the first span's own token. CI runs only check, fmt and test, and the dev profile sets overflow-checks=false.
impact: The 'formal verification' framing is unsupported, and regressions like BDD-01 through BDD-08 are invisible to CI.
recommendation: Add proptest differential suites: path counts against brute-force enumeration on random structured CFGs, and BDD operations against truth tables for n <= 12. Add Miri on psa::bdd, cargo-fuzz targets for the PSA and TRA readers, and criterion benchmarks (BDD ops against oxidd, traceability latency) tracked in CI. Check Theorem 5.2 empirically on generated series-parallel CFGs, and turn overflow checks on for tests.

title: sat_count silently saturates at u64::MAX, and consumers then wrap
evidence: Counts above 2^64 return u64::MAX through saturating operations (sat_count.rs:60,79,90,92), with no flag marking the result as inexact. Phase 9 sums them with a plain `+=` (uma/visitor.rs:214), which wraps because overflow-checks=false. PathMetrics serializes `mean = sat_count as f32`, which is not a mean, and from_bytes drops unwind_depth.
impact: Functions with 64 or more independent decisions, common in generated code, get clamped counts, and the aggregate totals wrap to small nonsense values.
recommendation: Count with num-bigint BigUint, as biodivine-lib-bdd's exact_cardinality and CUDD's Cudd_ApaCountMinterm do, and store a log2 f64 plus an exactness bit in the 16-byte record. Use checked adds in consumers. Done means a test with 80 sequential branches reporting exactly 2^80.

ENG.note: With overflow checks on, the wrapping `+=` in uma/visitor.rs now panics in dev and test instead of wrapping silently. The exact-count fix is handed off.

BDD.note: Counting is exact (PathCount). Headers carry a clamped u64 plus PSA_FLAG_COUNT_SATURATED; metrics store log2 f64, flags and unwind_depth, and the fake 'mean' is removed. The uma consumer's += is handed off.

UML.note: The visitor sums saturate, flag saturation and count only known metrics; an exact BigUint sat_count in PSA is handed off.

title: PSA/TRA readers trust header counts; the PSA uses a different and slow CRC-64 variant
evidence: Both readers slice `bytes[pos..pos+N]` and call `Vec::with_capacity(n)` using untrusted u32 counts, without validating them against the remaining length. A crafted file with a recomputed CRC therefore panics, or attempts a multi-GB allocation through the CLI inspect path. The PSA's bit-serial CRC-64 (init/xorout all-ones, augmented form) differs from ingestion's CRC-64/ECMA-182, despite the comment saying it 'matches all other serializers' (serializer.rs:262).
impact: Local DoS on malformed artifacts, inconsistent integrity checks across formats, and bit-at-a-time hashing of large files.
recommendation: Parse through a bounds-checked cursor (binrw, zerocopy, or get() with checked_mul), and validate each count against the remaining bytes before allocating. Use one standard checksum everywhere (the crc crate's CRC_64_ECMA_182 with table/SIMD) or BLAKE3. Add cargo-fuzz targets for both readers. Done means an hour of clean fuzzing.

BDD.note: PSA uses the shared ingestion CRC-64/ECMA-182. The reader validates every count, offset, ordering table, node array and root, and rejects trailing bytes. The TRA reader does the same.

SRV.note: The inspect path through the PSA and TRA readers is panic-contained. Count validation and CRC unification are outside my paths

title: Only Java has a real grammar: Kotlin is parsed as Java then JavaScript; Python/Rust/TS/C++ as JavaScript
evidence: KotlinLanguageAdapter::ts_language() returns tree_sitter_java::language(), and Cargo.toml has only the java and javascript grammars. AdapterRegistry::get falls back to a LangId::Unknown adapter built on tree_sitter_javascript, so .py/.rs/.ts/.cpp/.go files, all of which the server collects, are lexed as JavaScript. Phase 2 registers no Kotlin adapter, so Kotlin is reduced by the generic JS reducer. The generic Phase-1 adapter keeps include_anonymous()=false, so it emits no keywords, operators or punctuation, and it types any alphabetic named leaf as Keyword. No test ingests a .kt file.
impact: Every non-Java file produces error-ridden CSTs and meaningless ASTs, so later phases fall back to token heuristics. The README's 'F1 = 1.0000 across Java, Kotlin, Python, Rust, TypeScript, C++' is not supported by Phases 1 and 2.
recommendation: Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25 and add real grammars (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng, -python, -typescript, -rust, -cpp, -go). For each language, write Phase 1/2 adapters whose classification tables are generated from or tested against the grammar's node-types.json, with a test that fails on any unclassified kind. Skip unsupported extensions with a diagnostic instead of re-parsing them with another grammar. Done = per-language golden AST snapshot tests and published per-language accuracy on a public corpus.

ENG.note: The grammar upgrade and per-language adapters live in [dependencies] and src. Handed off.

CORE.note: Registries no longer fall back to the JS grammar: unsupported languages are skipped with SkipReason::UnsupportedLanguage diagnostics, Kotlin gets a real spec-based lexer (lexical-only, flagged), JS gets a proper Phase 1 adapter; grammar upgrade and new grammars not added (Cargo/lib.rs outside paths).

DOCS.note: README scoped to Java; per-language support matrix in docs/status.md §2; grammar and adapter work handed off

SRV.note: CLI and server now feed only .java/.kt/.kts; every other file is skipped and counted. Phase 1 skip and syntax-error diagnostics are surfaced. /api/supported-languages reports java as supported and kotlin as experimental. Real grammars belong in ingestion/ast (handoff)

title: Java reducer's default Drop silently discards constructor bodies, switch bodies, try-with-resources and generic types
evidence: classify() ends in `_ => Drop`, which discards the whole subtree. No arm names constructor_body, switch_block, try_with_resources_statement, explicit_constructor_invocation, enum_constant, generic_type, array_type, scoped_type_identifier, catch_formal_parameter, inferred_parameters or ERROR, all of which tree-sitter-java emits, and none of these strings appear anywhere in the repo. Switches parse as switch_expression, so the switch_statement arm is likely dead, and the CFG dispatches only NN_SWITCH_STMT. With the catch parameter gone, try_stmt.rs:62-66 takes the catch body as the 'param' and never dispatches its statements.
impact: For ordinary Java, statements and calls inside constructors, switches and try-with-resources vanish from AST, CFG, SSA and call graph. Generic, array and qualified types (`List<Foo>`, `new HashMap<>()`, `Foo[]`) also disappear, which degrades type resolution and UML associations.
recommendation: Make Eliminate the default and keep Drop for an explicit allowlist of trivia. Classify every named kind in tree-sitter-java's node-types.json, enforced by a unit test that fails on unclassified kinds. Add insta snapshot tests for constructors, switch rules and groups, try-with-resources, enums, lambdas, generics, records and patterns, and record a per-file count of nodes lost to ERROR.

CORE.note: Java reducer now defaults to Eliminate, Drop only for explicit trivia; constructor_body, switch groups/rules/labels, try-with-resources, explicit ctor invocation, enum constants, generic/array/scoped types, catch params, inferred params, ERROR all classified (node-types test skipped per phase rules).

title: Java NodeAttr encoding matches modifier substrings (annotations included), maps 9 operators, and its decoder is a stub
evidence: encode_attrs runs `text.contains("public")`, `contains("final")` and so on over the whole modifiers node, annotations included: `@Column(name = "is_public") private boolean isPublic;` becomes PUBLIC, and `@Column(name = "final_price")` sets MOD_FINAL. Only static/final/abstract are detected. VISIBILITY_PACKAGE_PRIVATE is never emitted, so members without modifiers fall back to default_visibility() = Public. Operators cover only = + - * / == != && ||, and unpack_operator_id returns Assign for any nonzero value. The lookup uses child_by_field_name("modifiers"), but tree-sitter-java's modifiers is an unnamed child, so this likely always returns None.
impact: UML visibility (+/-/#) and {static}/{final} are wrong for common JPA- or Jackson-annotated members, and possibly for every member. Phase 3 reads these bits directly. The relational operators that path conditions need are never recorded.
recommendation: Find the modifiers node by kind, iterate its children and match exact keyword kinds (`child.kind() == "private"`), skipping annotation children. Emit package-private explicitly. Encode all Java modifiers, and all binary, unary and assignment operators from the operator token's kind. Implement unpack_operator_id as an exhaustive TryFrom<u8>. Add unit tests per modifier and per operator, including annotation strings that contain keywords.

CORE.note: Modifiers read from the modifiers child by token kind (annotations never text-matched), all Java modifiers + JLS implicit modifiers/visibility, explicit VISIBILITY_PACKAGE_PRIVATE, all binary/unary/assignment/update operators from operator token kind, exhaustive TryFrom<u8> for OperatorId.

title: The 'succinct' AST costs ~209 B/node in memory and ~25 B/node on disk, against the documented 4.65-9.65 MB per 1M nodes and the 128x claim
evidence: Per BP bit the code keeps a u32 match_pos, an i32 excess, a usize log2 entry and a Vec<Vec<u32>> sparse table of about log2(2N) levels. The rank directory stores a u16 per 8 bits, which is 200% overhead, not o(n). From the code, N=1M nodes needs BP 0.25 MB, sparse table 160 MB, match_pos 8 MB, log2 16 MB, excess 8 MB and preorder arrays 17 MB: about 209 MB in total. The docs claim 4.65-9.65 MB, and the 32 MB pointer tree they claim to beat is smaller. The .tca also stores two byte-identical 16-byte-per-token arrays.
impact: Memory grows as n log n (about 2.4 GB for 10M nodes), so large codebases run out of RAM in Phase 2. The headline compression and O(1)-navigation claims are false.
recommendation: Replace match_pos, SparseTableRMQ and the hand-rolled rank with a range min-max tree (Navarro & Sadakane, ACM TALG 2014; Arroyuelo et al., ALENEX 2010): for example vers-vecs RsVec with its BP tree, or a port of sdsl-lite bp_support_sada with rank_support_v5/select_support_mcl. Use rank9 or poppy for rank. Keep a single token array. Done = a measured topology overhead of at most 3 bits/node in a criterion+RSS benchmark, with the docs regenerated from measurements.

CORE.note: Topology now BP + rank9 + rmM-tree (o(n) bits), single token array on disk when identical, aligned .bpa v2; parent_map retained and docs regeneration outside.

DOCS.note: All 4.65-9.65 MB and 128x memory claims corrected; succinct_structures §1.3 explains the topology-only ratio and the implemented layout

title: Silent narrowing casts cap the system at 65,535 files, 65,535 columns, 64 KB tokens, 256 blocks/method and 65,535-member SCCs
evidence: Narrowing casts: `file_id as u16`, header file_count `len() as u16`, `col: start.column as u16` (wraps), token len `.min(u16::MAX)` (truncates the text), `def_block: (def_block & 0xFF) as u8`, `raw_members.len() as u16`. The 24-bit line limit is only a debug_assert, and overflow-checks are off. In a minified .js (the server collects .js) wider than 65,535 columns, tokens at col c and c+65,536 share a sort_key, and finalize aborts the run with 'Invariant 2 Violation'. Consumers index the sorted token_records by token_id, so any reordering silently corrupts lookups.
impact: Repositories the size of the JDK, or containing a single minified bundle, fail Phase 1. Methods with more than 256 blocks map SSA definitions and traceability to the wrong block; feasibility.rs even documents the truncation.
recommendation: Key tokens by (file_id: u32, byte_offset: u32) and keep a per-file line-start table for line/column, as rustc's SourceMap or the line-index crate do. Widen def_block, member_count and the file counts to u32. Replace `as` casts with `try_from(...)?` and typed errors, and enable overflow-checks in CI builds. Add tests with 70K synthetic files, a 200K-column line and a 300-block method.

ENG.note: Overflow checks are back on in dev and pinned on in [profile.test], so CI builds trap on overflow. Widening the IDs and replacing `as` with try_from is src work, handed off.

BDD.note: In my paths: the u8/u16 truncations in feasibility are removed, TRA span lines widened to u32, ssa_bi no longer aliases def_block for functions over 256 blocks. Ingestion, ssa and cg casts are handed off.

CORE.note: Unrepresentable lines/columns skip the file with an explicit diagnostic (try_build_sort_key), >65535 files is a hard error, long tokens keep full text (u32 string lengths, LEN_SATURATED flag), def_block and SCC member_count widened to u32; byte-offset keying not done.

UML.note: UMA uses try_from or saturating conversions and u32 counts throughout; the u16 file and column ids in TCA are upstream (handed off).

title: lca() is wrong for most queries; select1 returns 0 (root) for absent ranks and for the last node in ~1% of corpora
evidence: lca maps the min-excess position m to rank1(m)-1-1 (the previous preorder node) instead of the parent of m+1, so for R(A(C),B), lca(C,B) returns A. A faithful Python port of rmq.rs and rank_select.rs gave 2758/4000 wrong LCAs on random trees. On an exact hit, select1 steps back one superblock. When the trailing superblock holds no 1-bits, std's binary_search lands on the sentinel, select1(node_count) returns 0, and first_child(last leaf) = Some(1). The port hit this in 29/3000 AST-like trees. Tests cover only a 6-bit tree.
impact: first_child, next_sibling, depth and subtree_size all go through select1. The phantom child sends walkers such as associations.rs:95-110 into file 0's tree, producing wrong compositions and possibly never terminating on single-file input. Each select is also an O(log n + 512) bit scan.
recommendation: Implement lca per Sadakane & Navarro (SODA 2010): return x if y <= findclose(x), else enclose(rmq(x, y) + 1). In select1, use `superblocks.partition_point(|&c| c < t) - 1` and return Option<usize>. Replace the get_bit scan with sampled select plus broadword in-word select. Add proptest differential tests against a naive pointer tree for random trees up to 10^5 nodes, including BP lengths that straddle 512-bit boundaries.

CORE.note: lca per Sadakane-Navarro (ancestor check via find_close, else parent of node after rmq minimum); select1 uses partition_point with sampled select, select1_checked returns Option and select1 returns a one-past-end sentinel instead of 0.

title: Artifact readers trust file-supplied lengths; Phase 2 never checks the .tca's magic, version or CRC; `inspect` claims 'VERIFIED VALID' without checking
evidence: ASTStage::run parses the mmapped .tca at fixed offsets without checking TCA_MAGIC, the version or the stored CRC. BPASTSerializer::read slices buf[offset..offset+8] using lengths taken from the file, so a CRC-valid file with inconsistent lengths panics. It also ignores _format_ver, never checks bit_count against words.len() (get_bit then panics), and passes file-controlled u32 counts to with_capacity, which can abort on a multi-GB allocation. CRC-64 is not a MAC. path_str_offset holds a text_id in memory but a byte offset on disk, and read() discards the paths. cmd_inspect prints 'VERIFIED VALID' after matching only the magic.
impact: Corrupt, stale or crafted artifacts are either consumed silently or crash the process. The README's 'zero-copy, CRC-64 verified' format is neither: sections are unaligned and get copied (the BP words start at offset 68).
recommendation: Define one versioned container with magic, version, a section table (offset, length, alignment) and 8- or 64-byte-aligned sections, all validated before use. Read it through zerocopy/bytemuck try_from_bytes for real mmap views, or adopt rkyv with validation, FlatBuffers or Arrow IPC. Use checked arithmetic, cap allocations by the bytes remaining, and give each field one meaning. Make inspect actually verify, and add cargo-fuzz targets for every reader.

CORE.note: Phase 2 validates the full .tca (CRC, magic, version, every count/offset) or takes it in memory; .bpa reader validates lengths, alignment, bit_count, balance and parents; path_str_offset is a text_id everywhere; inspect fix is a main.rs handoff.

DOCS.note: README CRC/zero-copy claims corrected; security §3.2 lists the unchecked .tca, trusted lengths and inspect behaviour with a hardening target; code handed off

SRV.note: inspect validates with each format's reader, reports per format whether a CRC-64 was verified, and contains panics. Reader bounds checks are outside my paths

title: Safe wrapper over unsafe mmap combined with in-place truncating writes to fixed, predictable paths
evidence: MemoryMappedFile::open is a safe fn wrapping `unsafe { Mmap::map(&file)? }` and exposes &[u8] with no stated invariant. Artifacts are written with File::create (truncating) straight to fixed names (corpus.tca, ast.bpa), either in ./openheart_output or, for SCPGPipelineBuilder::new(), in std::env::temp_dir(). Two concurrent runs sharing a directory truncate a file the other run has mapped: SIGBUS on Unix, an error on Windows. On a shared /tmp, a planted symlink at /tmp/corpus.tca is followed and its target overwritten (CWE-377/CWE-59). Writes are not atomic.
impact: Concurrent runs crash or corrupt artifacts. Library users of the default builder face a local file-clobber hazard.
recommendation: Hand the in-memory Phase 1 artifact to Phase 2 instead of mmapping it. If mmap stays, make the constructor an `unsafe fn` with a documented contract and take an advisory lock (fd-lock). Write each artifact to a tempfile::NamedTempFile in the target directory and persist() it (atomic rename). Default to a fresh tempfile::TempDir rather than fixed names in temp_dir().

CORE.note: Safe open + unsafe map, atomic temp+rename writes for .tca/.bpa/.sta/diagrams, create_new temp files, builder defaults to a unique fresh temp dir, Phase 2 fed in memory by the builder; main/server wiring is a handoff.

SRV.note: Each run writes into a fresh create_dir'd work directory; the CLI publishes with per-file atomic renames and the server keeps a per-session dir. MemoryMappedFile::open now copies (another engineer's change)

title: No syntax-error model, no parse timeout, recursive CST walks on the caller's stack, and a 2023-era grammar
evidence: Neither walker checks is_error/is_missing/has_error. Zero-width MISSING leaves such as ';' become empty-text Punctuation tokens, while the Java reducer's `_ => Drop` discards ERROR subtrees, which tree-sitter's recovery can make large. SourceFileRecord.flags is always 0, although the spec reserves bits for has_bom and crlf. parse() sets no timeout or cancellation flag. walk_recursive and reduce_and_encode recurse once per CST level and allocate a TreeCursor per internal node, so input nested thousands of levels deep can overflow the stack (Windows' main thread has 1 MB). The grammars are tree-sitter 0.20.10 and tree-sitter-java 0.20.2.
impact: Files that contain errors or newer Java syntax silently lose code, and adversarial or generated input can hang or abort the CLI and the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Traverse iteratively with a single TreeCursor (goto_first_child, goto_next_sibling, goto_parent). Treat ERROR as Eliminate, skip MISSING leaves, and record per-file diagnostics in the .tca: error and missing counts, byte ranges, BOM, CRLF. Use Parser::set_timeout_micros plus a cancellation flag. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25 and tree-sitter-java 0.23.x. Fuzz ingestion with cargo-fuzz, seeded from tree-sitter corpus tests.

ENG.note: Syntax-error model, timeouts and iterative walks are src work. The grammar upgrade is handed off with LANG-01.

CORE.note: Iterative single-cursor walker and reducer, ERROR eliminated, MISSING skipped, per-file diagnostics (counts, byte ranges, BOM/CRLF flags, DIAG section in .tca), parse timeout; grammar upgrade and cancellation flag not done.

DOCS.note: phase1 spec flags note, status ledger and security stack-depth note added; ingestion code handed off

title: Each file is read three times and parsed twice, single-threaded, with no content check between phases
evidence: Phase 1 reads each file once to hash it (mod.rs:53) and again to parse it (mod.rs:111). Phase 2 reads it a third time from the stored path and re-parses it (ast/mod.rs:142-143), never comparing against content_sha256, and silently skips any file whose read or parse fails (`if let Ok`). There is no rayon: the Mutex<StringInterner> and the AtomicU32 allocator guard single-threaded loops. close_node walks every open ancestor for each node (O(N*depth)), although the reducer already propagates token ranges. A bit-at-a-time CRC-64 runs at least three times over the .tca.
impact: Throughput is a fraction of what one core could deliver, and the other cores sit idle. A file edited mid-run yields an AST that silently disagrees with the token corpus, and unreadable files simply disappear.
recommendation: Parse each file once and emit tokens plus the reduced AST in one pass, either by keeping the Tree or by building a rowan-style green tree. Use rayon par_iter over files with per-file buffers merged in file order, plus a concurrent interner (lasso ThreadedRodeo). Verify SHA-256 before reuse and fail loudly on unreadable files. Swap the CRC for crc64fast-nvme or xxh3/BLAKE3, delete the ancestor loop, and use tree-sitter incremental parsing (Tree::edit) in the server. Done = criterion LOC/s that scales with cores.

CORE.note: Phase 1 reads each file once; Phases 1 and 2 parse in parallel (scoped threads, deterministic merge); Phase 2 verifies SHA-256 and fails loudly; table-driven CRC-64; ancestor loop removed; still parses twice.

title: Artifacts are not reproducible: wall-clock time and mtimes feed every downstream hash link
evidence: The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() in nanoseconds, and every file record embeds mtime_ns. Phase 2 sets tca_hash to the crc64 of the entire .tca and writes it into the .bpa header. Phase 3 hashes tca_bytes again, and the .scpg integrity hash XORs these links together. As a result, every hash link changes on every run, even for identical sources. Paths are stored exactly as passed in, so the same sources reached through another path or checkout location also produce different bytes.
impact: Golden-file regression tests, content-addressed caching and incremental re-analysis are impossible, and benchmark outputs cannot be checked bit for bit.
recommendation: Remove build timestamps from hashed content, or honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH as reproducible-builds.org recommends. Keep mtime out of artifacts, or put it in a metadata section that is not hashed. Store normalized repo-relative paths. Derive hash links from content: BLAKE3 over source hashes, configuration and tool version. Add a CI test that runs the pipeline twice and asserts byte-identical artifacts.

title: The token corpus is lossy and partly mis-typed, so it cannot serve as a faithful lexical layer
evidence: The Java adapter drops anonymous tokens that map_node_type does not list: `?` and `:` (ternary, labels, enhanced-for, case), `@interface`, `sealed`, `permits`, `non-sealed` and the module keywords. `octal_integer_literal` becomes Unknown. Javadoc is never classified CommentDoc, so the default include_doc_comments=true has no effect. The generic adapter keeps no anonymous tokens at all. When a node's first token is missing, reducer.rs:95-116 borrows a neighbouring token on the same line, which can lie outside the node. The builder's 'Invariant 1: Monotonicity' is a comment with no check behind it.
impact: Phase 3's token-level heuristics (its fallback for Kotlin and the other languages), clone detection, source reconstruction and doc-based traceability all run on an incomplete stream, and node-to-token ranges are imprecise.
recommendation: Make the lexical layer lossless, in the style of rust-analyzer's rowan green tree or Roslyn's full-fidelity trees: emit every leaf, with trivia as flagged ranges. Classify tokens from tables derived from node-types.json, and detect `/**` as CommentDoc. Add a round-trip property test: concatenated token and trivia text equals the original file bytes.

CORE.note: Complete Java token table (?, :, @interface, sealed/non-sealed/permits, module keywords, octal), CommentDoc detection, JS adapter, generic adapter keeps anonymous tokens, exact node token spans (no neighbour borrowing), Invariant 1 enforced; trivia round-trip not done.

title: Logger writes every message at every level to two files under a global mutex; phase timers never fire
evidence: log_event applies the level only to console output. Its file branch formats each line and write_all()s it to both files for Trace and Debug too, under LOGGER_STATE's Mutex. Callers build messages eagerly with format!: there are 15 log_trace and 12 log_debug call sites, including one per call site in cg/call_sites.rs:57. The persistent log appends forever, with no rotation. PhaseTimer has no Drop and finish() is never called in Phases 1-2, so no stage timings are logged. The generic reducer prints `[TS-KIND]` to stdout for every 'class' or 'export' kind.
impact: Logging spends I/O and lock time in proportion to trace volume even when tracing is off. Logs grow without bound, and there is no timing telemetry to benchmark against.
recommendation: Adopt tracing, with tracing-subscriber's EnvFilter for per-sink levels and tracing-appender's non-blocking rolling writer. Use the macros so that disabled levels cost nothing. Model each phase as a span so timings come for free. Remove the debug println.

CORE.note: Level gating before lock/IO with separate file level, oh_trace!/oh_debug! macros skip formatting, persistent log size rotation, PhaseTimer logs on Drop, debug println removed; call-site conversion is a handoff.

title: Pipeline abstraction is decorative: the stage template has no implementors and orchestration is copy-pasted three times
evidence: PipelineStageTemplate, with its verify_invariants and timing hooks, has zero implementors. SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute, cmd_analyze and the server each wire all 10 phases by hand, with different error handling. The server uses fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default() and passes empty bytes onward. diagram_formats is stored but never used. Every phase writes its artifact and the caller reads it back with fs::read. Phases 7-10 return plain values and cannot report errors. Errors are Strings or io::Error; thiserror is a dependency but is never used.
impact: The CLI, server and library behave differently. There is no caching, cancellation, per-stage metrics or partial re-run, and errors lose their structure.
recommendation: Define one Stage trait with typed inputs and outputs and a thiserror error enum, driven by a single Pipeline that the CLI, server and library all use. Hand artifacts over in memory and persist them optionally. Key each stage's output by a hash of its inputs and config so unchanged stages are skipped, salsa or Bazel style. Add cancellation tokens and per-stage timing and RSS metrics, and either wire up or remove diagram_formats.

ENG.note: The Stage trait and pipeline unification are src work.

CORE.note: SCPGPipelineBuilder uses a thiserror PipelineError, PipelineStageTemplate implemented for Phases 1-2, timed phases 3-10, in-memory Phase 1->2, diagram_formats wired to export; CLI/server unification is a handoff.

SRV.note: Single runner for CLI and server: thiserror PipelineError, per-stage timing, panic containment, diagram formats wired, Phase 1 bytes taken in memory from run_with_report. core::pipeline::SCPGPipelineBuilder is still a separate copy (handoff)

title: Phase 1/2 tests only cover toy inputs: no BP over 512 bits, no property, fuzz, golden or performance tests
evidence: The succinct-structure tests use 4-6-bit sequences plus one ~40-bit HelloWorld, so superblock boundaries, select over duplicate counts, LCA on non-trivial trees and absent ranks are never exercised. No test ingests Kotlin, switch, try-with-resources, constructor bodies, enums, syntax errors, CRLF/BOM/non-UTF-8 input, long lines or many files. There is no proptest or quickcheck, no cargo-fuzz target, no criterion bench (there is no benches/ directory) and no determinism test. Nothing in the repo produces the performance table in docs/overview.md.
impact: The defects in CORE-01 through CORE-06 ship undetected, and none of the published performance or accuracy numbers can be reproduced.
recommendation: Add proptest differential tests of every BP operation against a naive tree, and insta snapshot tests of reduced ASTs per construct per language (tree-sitter corpus style). Add cargo-fuzz targets for TokenCorpusSerializer::read, BPASTSerializer::read and ingestion. Add criterion benches on pinned corpora (Defects4J projects, Apache Commons, the JDK) that report LOC/s, bytes per node and peak RSS, gated in CI by regression thresholds.

title: Source discovery follows symlinks, aborts on the first I/O error, ignores .gitignore and generated code, and neither dedups nor caps file size
evidence: collect_source_files recurses via Path::is_dir(), which follows symlinks, so a symlink cycle recurses until the OS returns an error. Any read_dir or entry error propagates through `?` and aborts the whole analysis. The server's copy also follows symlinks. There is no .gitignore, hidden-directory or build-output filtering (target/, build/generated/), and extension matching is case-sensitive. IngestionStage::run sorts paths but never dedups them, so one file reached by two paths gets two file_ids, and fs::read loads files of any size, twice.
impact: Real repositories with symlinks, unreadable directories or generated sources either fail or produce duplicate symbols, and one huge generated file can exhaust memory.
recommendation: Use the ignore crate's WalkBuilder (gitignore and hidden-file handling, follow_links(false) or loop detection, max_filesize, parallel walk) with globset include/exclude configuration. Canonicalize and dedup paths. Log and skip unreadable entries. Tag generated files (@Generated, build directories) so they can be excluded or analysed separately.

CORE.note: Phase 1 canonicalizes and dedups paths, caps file size (skipped with diagnostic), case-insensitive extensions; directory walking lives in main/server (handoff).

SRV.note: Discovery uses the ignore crate: symlinks not followed, hidden, build, dependency and test dirs skipped, .gitignore honored, unreadable entries logged and skipped, canonical dedup, case-insensitive extensions, per-file, total and count limits

title: Unseeded FNV-1a with linear probing leaves the interner open to hash flooding
evidence: intern() places each string at `fnv1a_64(text) & table_mask` and resolves collisions by linear probing. FNV-1a is unkeyed and resize() rehashes with the same function, so identifiers crafted to share low hash bits stay in one cluster across resizes. Collisions are resolved correctly, because bytes are compared (interner.rs:67), but each insert probes the whole cluster.
impact: A malicious repository fed to the single-threaded server can make Phase 1 interning quadratic and stall the server.
recommendation: Keep insertion-ordered IDs, which preserves determinism, but hash with a seeded fast hasher (foldhash or ahash with a per-process random seed) through hashbrown::HashTable, or adopt lasso or string-interner. Keep the byte comparison.

CORE.note: Interner table hashes with per-process randomly keyed RandomState (SipHash); ids stay insertion-ordered, byte comparison kept, FNV kept only for the persisted header index.

title: Kotlin and 'six-language' support is illusory: Kotlin goes through the Java and JavaScript grammars, everything else through JavaScript
evidence: KotlinLanguageAdapter::ts_language() returns tree_sitter_java::language() (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2's registry has no Kotlin entry, so .kt falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Kotlin is therefore tokenized as Java and reduced as JavaScript. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ have no adapters and also fall back to JavaScript (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39). The only grammar dependencies are java and javascript (Cargo.toml:9-11). The CLI ingests only .java/.kt/.kts (main.rs:76-99). Tests and examples contain zero non-Java fixtures, and ROADMAP.md:127 still lists C++/Rust/Go adapters as future work.
impact: Every Kotlin file yields wrong tokens and an AST that disagrees with Phase 1. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ input silently produces garbage. The README's F1 = 1.0000 claim is false for five of the six languages it names.
recommendation: Scope the README to Java now and label every other language experimental. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25+/0.26 with a current tree-sitter-java and a real Kotlin grammar (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng). Register one adapter per language for both Phase 1 and Phase 2 from a single table, and return an error instead of falling back to JavaScript for unknown extensions. Add per-language fixture suites in tree-sitter corpus style, and have CI track the rate of ERROR/MISSING nodes per file.

ENG.note: The crate description no longer claims six languages: it now names only Java. README scoping and the grammar upgrade are handed off.

DOCS.note: Six-language claim removed from README, overview and CHANGELOG (corrected 1.1.0 entry); ROADMAP lists frontends as planned; code handed off

title: The 'F1 = 1.0000' validation is methodologically invalid and cannot be reproduced
evidence: Ground truth is a regex scan. A 'keywords' blacklist is stripped from both the ground truth (ruthless_verify.py:88) and the tool's output (:232). It lists tool placeholders ('SystemNode', 'Node_0', 'Unknown') and real class names from the target repos ('HomeScreen', 'INVESTOR'), so phantom and missing classes are erased by construction. The '3-Oracle' system uses only Oracle 1 (:299-300). Sets hold simple names, so same-named classes in different packages collapse, and only class names are scored. The benchmark script renames classes by hand (GHobbits to GenHobbits, benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:61-63) and exits 0 even on failure (:212-215). The evaluated repos are unpublished and unpinned, and the server hardcodes ./target_repos/FractalAndroid (server.rs:124).
impact: The published accuracy figures can be neither reproduced nor trusted. The harness also cannot catch regressions in relations, diagrams, call graphs or pattern detection, which are the outputs users actually consume.
recommendation: Create a bench/ harness with corpora pinned by commit SHA (spring-petclinic, iluwatar/java-design-patterns with its .urm.puml files, Apache Commons, Guava; for Kotlin, ktor and kotlinx.coroutines) and annotated golden expectations. Score fully qualified classes plus extends/implements/association edges against javac/JavaParser-derived truth, and package dependencies against jdeps. Score call graphs on Judge/CATS (Reif et al., ISSTA'19) against Soot/OPAL, and GoF detection per pattern on P-MARt/DPB. Delete the blacklists and renames, emit JSON, and fail CI on regressions with ruff-ecosystem-style diffs.

title: Use-after-free from unsafe aliasing in BDDLibrary on the production Phase 8 path; no Miri, and the docs claim forbid(unsafe_code)
evidence: apply, apply_not and restrict each build `read = from_raw_parts(self.nodes.as_ptr(), len)` and also pass `&mut self.nodes` (psa/bdd/mod.rs:86,102,122). The recursion pushes new nodes (unique_table.rs:65), and the second recursive call reads through the stale slice (apply.rs:103-104). The SAFETY comment says the Vec 'never reallocates', but it starts at capacity 2 and doubles as it grows, so any growth frees the buffer that `read` points into. Phase 8 uses BDDLibrary for every function (construction/mod.rs:53). No #![forbid(unsafe_code)] appears anywhere in src, contrary to security-architecture.md:11.
impact: This is undefined behaviour: depending on allocator state, path summaries and #SAT counts can be silently wrong or the process can crash. The tests pass by luck, because freed memory usually still holds the old nodes.
recommendation: Remove the unsafe code: after each recursive call, read nodes by index through `all_nodes`, or use an append-only arena (elsa::FrozenVec, or index-based storage plus a read-only snapshot). Add a nightly `cargo miri test` job over psa and an AddressSanitizer job. Deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn and clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks, and put #![forbid(unsafe_code)] on every module that needs no unsafe. Correct security-architecture.md.

DOCS.note: security-architecture rewritten with the unsafe inventory, the BDD history, Miri/ASan checks and no false forbid(unsafe_code) claim; the current tree has no unsafe under src/psa; CI Miri job handed off

title: Integration tests mostly check that the pipeline didn't panic: tautologies, non-emptiness, prefixes and round-trips
evidence: scpg_tests.rs:120 and :128 assert `is_reach || !is_reach` and `is_some() || is_none()`. Line :165 asserts a constant string from a format literal (scpg/diagram/mod.rs:28). The recursion fixture checks only `!sccs.is_empty()` (cg_tests.rs:81). The SSA test checks `total_ssa_vars >= 1` and never checks phi placement (ssa_tests.rs:86). GoF detection passes if any one of four patterns is found (adversarial_trick_tests.rs:259-262). The 'formal verification' of the paper's theorems is one 3-variable BDD plus `len() > 0` checks (research_paper_theorems_tests.rs:46-85,142-146). By a rough heuristic, about 60% of 284 assertions check only existence, round-trips or substrings. 40 of the 47 unit tests are in psa, and the ~5.8K LOC of exporters have none.
impact: Wrong call edges, phi nodes, patterns or diagram content still pass CI, so regressions in user-visible output go unnoticed. The test table in codebase-guide.md misleads contributors about what is covered.
recommendation: Assert exact expectations on small fixtures: call edges, SCC membership, phi nodes at join blocks, pattern roles. Share one fixture helper across tests. Measure suite strength with cargo-mutants and set a budget for surviving mutants, and add cargo-llvm-cov with per-module floors. Run under cargo-nextest with slow-timeout so hangs fail instead of being #[ignore]d. Root-cause the ignored test at scpg_tests.rs:169: it calls the same Phase3Stage::run as the CLI. Rewrite the codebase-guide test table from what the tests actually assert.

title: No property-based, differential, fuzz or snapshot tests; binary loaders panic or over-allocate on crafted artifacts
evidence: The only dev-dependency is tempfile (Cargo.toml:19-20); there is no benches/ or fuzz/ directory, no proptest and no insta. The loaders trust header counts. The TRA loader calls `Vec::with_capacity(n_ast)` and then slices `buf[offset..offset+4]` without bounds checks (tra/serializer.rs:174-176). CRC is not a MAC, so a crafted file passes the check and then panics or allocates gigabytes. MemoryMappedSCPG checks the size for 11 sections but then iterates over the file's own section_count (scpg/mmap/mod.rs:35-58). The two 'CRC-64/ECMA' functions disagree on '123456789': 6C40DF5F0B497347 (ingestion/serializer.rs:16) vs D428DA62D41203D6 (psa/serializer.rs:263), even though the psa doc comment says they match (:262).
impact: Crafted or truncated artifacts crash the CLI and server or exhaust their memory. Core invariants (BP navigation, rank/select, dominators, SCCs, #SAT) are checked on only a handful of examples, so edge-case bugs ship.
recommendation: Add proptest suites with reference oracles: BP and rank/select against a pointer tree and naive popcount, dominators against petgraph::algo::dominators::simple_fast, SCCs against petgraph's tarjan_scc, BDD sat_count against truth-table enumeration up to 16 variables, and sort_key round-trips over full ranges. Add cargo-fuzz targets for every deserializer and for the whole pipeline on arbitrary source text, aiming for OSS-Fuzz. Snapshot all 19x3 exporter outputs with insta, validated by plantuml -checkonly and mermaid-cli. Replace both CRCs with the crc crate's CRC_64_ECMA_182 plus known-answer tests.

title: Artifacts are non-deterministic (wall-clock time, file mtimes, raw paths), so the hash chain changes on every run
evidence: The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() (ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84), each file's mtime_ns (ingestion/mod.rs:62-67, written at serializer.rs:115) and paths exactly as passed in. Phase 2 hashes the whole .tca (ast/mod.rs:48) and each later phase chains on upstream bytes. As a result, identical source yields different hashes in all ten artifacts on every run, and so does a git checkout that only touches mtimes. The .scpg header adds now_ns and writes source_hash as zeros (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136-146). The published demo diagrams are whatever the last local server run wrote into web/diagrams (server.rs:637).
impact: Staleness and incremental detection (the paper's Eq. 8, 'O(1) invalidation') can never report 'unchanged'. Byte-level golden tests, build caching and cross-machine reproduction of benchmark artifacts are all impossible.
recommendation: Make serialization a pure function of content. Drop wall-clock time and mtimes from hashed bytes; if needed, keep them in an unhashed sidecar that honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Store project-relative paths normalized to '/', and chain on content digests (BLAKE3 or SHA-256 over canonical sections) rather than whole-file CRCs. Generate demo diagrams in CI from a pinned input. Add a CI job that runs the pipeline twice, on two OSes, and byte-compares every artifact, as reproducible-builds.org recommends.

title: No error model: String errors, an unused thiserror, panics in Phases 7-9, silently dropped files and integer truncation
evidence: thiserror is declared (Cargo.toml:13) but never used, and src has no error enum. 27 signatures return Result<_, String>, and callers re-stringify errors with {:?}. Phases 7-9 return bare artifacts and panic! when a write fails (tra/mod.rs:43, psa/mod.rs:154, uma/mod.rs:98). Phase 2 silently skips any file it cannot read or parse (nested `if let Ok`, ast/mod.rs:140-152). The server hashes `fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default()` (server.rs:536-609). `file_id as u16` (ingestion/mod.rs:70) wraps past 65,536 files and `column as u16` (walker.rs:59) past column 65,535, although security-architecture.md:26 claims these values saturate. 291 unwraps remain.
impact: A full disk or a permission error aborts the server. Unreadable files vanish from the results with no warning. Large monorepos and minified files get colliding sort keys and wrong traceability, all silently.
recommendation: Define typed errors per layer with thiserror, for example ArtifactError {Truncated, BadMagic, CrcMismatch{expected, found}, Version} and IngestError {Io{path}, Parse{path}}, and use anyhow or miette only in the CLI. Make every stage return Result, and record per-file diagnostics instead of skipping files. Replace `as` casts with u16::try_from plus explicit errors, or widen the IDs. Deny clippy::unwrap_used, expect_used, panic and indexing_slicing in library code, following the Rust API Guidelines (C-GOOD-ERR).

ENG.note: Typed errors are src work. thiserror is kept in Cargo.toml for that adoption. Handed off.

DOCS.note: ADR-008 (typed errors per layer) added; the saturation claim is replaced by the try_build_sort_key rejection behaviour; code handed off

title: Headline performance claims (128x, O(1), zero-copy) are unmeasured or contradicted, and no benchmark infrastructure exists
evidence: '128x compression' is the paper's theoretical gap between 32-byte pointer nodes and a 2n-bit encoding (tex:292-296), not a measurement; docs/overview.md:119 itself claims 6.9x. For 'O(1) traceability', NavigationEngine::to_source is a linear find, and from_source, documented as O(log n), is a linear filter (navigation.rs:9-27). For 'zero-copy mmap', MemoryMappedSCPG::open calls fs::read (mmap/mod.rs:18). The paper defers empirical evaluation to future work (tex:217-220) yet tabulates sizes for a '500K-LOC' project (tex:582). The repo has no benchmarks, its 'enterprise-scale benchmark' is 255 LOC (examples/README.md:14), and the web studio displays hardcoded execution_time_ms values (github-engine.js:164,256).
impact: No performance statement can be verified. Regressions and quadratic cliffs, such as the linear external-symbol scan per type reference, stay hidden until users hit them on real repositories.
recommendation: Add criterion or divan micro-benchmarks for rank/select, BP navigation, CRC, the interner, BDD apply and traceability queries. Add macro-benchmarks on pinned corpora measuring LOC/s, peak RSS (dhat-rs or /usr/bin/time), artifact bytes per LOC and query-latency percentiles. Track them on every PR with CodSpeed or Bencher, as ruff and Biome do. Generate BENCHMARKS.md from the harness, recording hardware and commit, and remove or footnote every README number the harness does not produce.

DOCS.note: 128x, O(1) and zero-copy claims removed or qualified; examples are no longer called benchmarks; measurement protocol added; benches and the hard-coded studio timings handed off

title: 'All 10 phases COMPLETED' and the Phase 10 readiness checklist mark stubs and missing features as done
evidence: IncrementalEngine::apply_delta only XORs the hash with 0x01010101 and returns stale_link_count 0 (incremental/mod.rs:27-33), so two edits restore the old hash. The ROADMAP's 'Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv IFDS' (ROADMAP.md:71) is per-statement pattern marking with no propagation (ifds.rs:12-37). 'CFL-reachability' is a plain BFS that rescans every call edge (cfl.rs:21-31). The XMI exporter emits only 'Class_{id}' names (xmi.rs:13). The checklist ticks mmap, LZ4, per-section CRC verification, SHA-256 staleness detection, an LSP bridge and a FileWatcher (phase10.md:532-566); none exist in code. source_hash is written as zeros (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:146), and docs/plans/phase4.md is empty.
impact: Status markers cannot be trusted. Integrators who rely on incremental updates, IFDS taint, CFL queries or XMI interchange get stubs that return plausible-looking wrong answers.
recommendation: Adopt a status rule: each roadmap or spec item links to the module and the test that prove it, and anything lacking either is marked 'planned'. Mark incremental, IFDS, CFL, XMI and LSP experimental now. Then implement them against reference designs: Salsa for incremental recomputation (as in rust-analyzer), a real IFDS/IDE tabulation solver modelled on Heros or PhASAR, Reps-style CFL-reachability with call/return matching, and XMI 2.5.1 validated by loading it into Eclipse UML2 or Papyrus.

DOCS.note: Status rule adopted in ROADMAP, status.md and contributing; 'All 10 phases COMPLETED' removed; phase10 readiness checklist replaced by an evidence-based status table

title: CI runs only check/fmt/test on Linux: no lint, MSRV, coverage, Miri, audit or docs gates, and the CI badge is static
evidence: ci.yml runs cargo check, fmt and `test --all-targets` (which skips doctests), on ubuntu-latest only. There is no clippy or RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings, though contributing.md:17 demands zero warnings. There is no MSRV job: README.md:7 claims Rust 1.75+, but lockfile v4 needs Cargo 1.78 and sha2 0.11 needs Rust 1.85 ([manifest](https://docs.rs/crate/sha2/0.11.0/source/Cargo.toml)). There is no rust-toolchain.toml. CI also lacks llvm-cov, Miri, cargo-deny/audit/machete, nextest timeouts, rustdoc, Docker, Python and JS checks, and never runs on Windows. The cache key uses only Cargo.lock, with no restore-keys. README.md:10-11 shows hardcoded 'passing' and 'enforced' badges.
impact: Real defects merge unnoticed: an MSRV break, undefined behaviour, an unused dependency, warnings. Neither the badge nor the documented toolchain can be trusted, which blocks benchmark-grade status.
recommendation: Add these jobs: clippy --all-targets -D warnings; RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc; an MSRV check via `rust-version` with cargo +1.85 check (or cargo-hack); cargo-nextest with slow-timeout and JUnit output; cargo-llvm-cov to Codecov with coverage floors; nightly Miri on psa; cargo-deny for advisories, licenses, bans and sources; and cargo-machete. Extend the matrix to Windows and macOS, use Swatinem/rust-cache, build the Docker image, run ruff on scripts and Biome on web/, and replace the static badge with the real workflow badge.

ENG.note: Makefile gates added: lint (clippy -D warnings), doc (-D warnings), msrv, nextest, coverage, miri, asan, deny, machete, docker-smoke, plus ci and ci-full. `make test` now also runs doctests. ci.yml and the static badge are handed off.

DOCS.note: Static CI and 'security enforced' badges replaced by the workflow badge; README and contributing document make ci/ci-full; ci.yml jobs handed off

title: Ten-phase orchestration is hand-wired at 18 call sites through positional raw-hash parameters, and has already broken the hash chain
evidence: The ten-phase wiring is hand-copied at 18 IngestionStage::run call sites: main.rs:150-255, core/pipeline.rs:170-225, adapters/server.rs:527-615 and 13 test files. PipelineStageTemplate (pipeline.rs:34-78) has no implementors. SCPGPipelineBuilder never reads its diagram_formats field and defaults to the shared temp directory with fixed file names (pipeline.rs:113,159-168). Stages take long positional argument lists with adjacent raw `&[u8]` hash inputs (cg/mod.rs:37-38; Phase 9 takes 10 arguments). That plumbing has already broken the chain: psa/mod.rs:78 stores `cfa.sta_hash` in the PSA's 'CRC-64 of the SSA artifact' field (psa/serializer.rs:37).
impact: Every fix must be repeated at 18 sites, and the copies drift: the server ignores errors the CLI reports. Swapped hashes compile without complaint, and concurrent runs with default settings overwrite each other's artifacts.
recommendation: Make one orchestrator the only entry point for the CLI, the server and tests: a typed stage DAG in which each artifact is a newtype carrying its own content digest (for example Artifact<Tca> with .digest()), so hashes cannot be swapped. Default to a per-run tempfile::TempDir. For incremental runs, use Salsa queries (as rust-analyzer and Astral's ty do) instead of re-running every phase. Provide a test helper such as analyze_fixture(src) returning PipelineArtifacts.

title: The single-threaded pipeline reads every file three times, parses each twice, and logs through a logger that formats and flushes on every event
evidence: There is no rayon or threading anywhere, though .env.example:14 advertises OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS, which the code never reads. Each file is read three times (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; ast/mod.rs:142) and parsed twice (ingestion/mod.rs:117; ast/mod.rs:143). The SHA-256 recorded on the first read is never checked against the later reads. Log call sites run format! before the level check. Every event, whatever its level, is written to two files and flushed under a global Mutex (logger.rs:124-159). Phase 8 logs one INFO line per function (psa/mod.rs:132), and a debug println! remains in library code (generic.rs:27). The external-type lookup scans every symbol for each reference (pass3_types.rs:108-116).
impact: Throughput is single-core and I/O-bound, and the symbol fallback costs O(types x symbols), so large repositories will be slow or appear to hang. A file edited during a run gets tokens that no longer match its recorded SHA.
recommendation: Read each file once into an Arc<[u8]>, parse it once, and hand the tree or reduced CST to Phase 2. Parallelize per file in Phases 1-2 and per function in Phases 4, 5 and 8 with rayon, merging results deterministically. Replace the logger with tracing and tracing-subscriber: EnvFilter on RUST_LOG, per-phase spans, and a buffered non-blocking file writer from tracing-appender. Index external symbols in a HashMap, and confirm the gains with the ENG-08 harness.

title: Distribution is broken: the release workflow has never run and ships an .rlib; the Docker image can neither build nor start
evidence: `git tag -l` is empty, so the tag-triggered release.yml has never run. It sets no `permissions: contents: write` and would likely get a 403 under the read-only default token. It uploads target/release/libopenheart.rlib (release.yml:26), which only the exact rustc version that built it can use. Dockerfile:2 builds with rust:1.80, but the locked sha2 0.11 needs Rust 1.85 ([manifest](https://docs.rs/crate/sha2/0.11.0/source/Cargo.toml)). Dockerfile:49 runs `openheart serve --port 8080`, but the CLI only knows `server [PORT]` (main.rs:532). Versions disagree: 0.1.0 in Cargo.toml and the CLI banner (main.rs:32), 2.0.0 in CHANGELOG.md:10, and SECURITY.md:9-13 lists 1.1.x, 1.0.x and 0.1.x as supported.
impact: Users and anyone reproducing benchmarks have no usable binaries or containers. Version numbers cannot be mapped to code, so bug reports and published results have no anchor.
recommendation: Use cargo-dist (or taiki-e/upload-rust-binary-action) to build Linux, macOS and Windows binaries with SHA-256 checksums, attest them with actions/attest-build-provenance, and attach a CycloneDX SBOM; publish the crate to crates.io. Drive versions and the CHANGELOG with release-plz from conventional commits so tags, Cargo.toml and the CHANGELOG agree. Fix the Dockerfile: rust:1.85+, an exec-form CMD running `openheart server 8080`, a non-root USER and a healthcheck. Build the image in CI.

ENG.note: Declared rust-version. `make dist` produces archives with SHA-256 files, and `make docker-smoke` probes /api/health. release.yml, Dockerfile, CHANGELOG and SECURITY.md are handed off.

DOCS.note: CHANGELOG milestones re-headed as untagged with a versioning note; SECURITY.md lists only main/0.1.x; release.yml and Dockerfile handed off

title: Cargo.toml has a wrong description, missing metadata, overflow checks off under test, tree-sitter six minor versions behind, and an unused dependency
evidence: The description reads '...token corpus pipeline for cardiac/code processing' (Cargo.toml:6) and covers only Phase 1. There is no license, repository, readme, rust-version, keywords, categories or include/exclude field. [profile.dev] sets overflow-checks = false (:21-23), which also applies to `cargo test`, so arithmetic overflow in bit-packing and rank/select code wraps silently under test. There is no tuned release profile and no profiling profile. tree-sitter is locked at 0.20.10 with 0.20.x grammars while 0.26.x is available ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/tree-sitter/0.26.9/source/Cargo.toml)). thiserror is declared but has zero references in src.
impact: Tests cannot catch overflow bugs, release builds leave performance unclaimed, and the crate cannot be published as-is. Current grammar crates, including Kotlin's, target the newer tree-sitter Language API and cannot be added without upgrading.
recommendation: Fix the description and add license (MIT), repository, readme, rust-version (1.85), keywords, categories and include/exclude. Remove overflow-checks = false, or confine it to a custom fast-dev profile that tests do not use. Add a [profile.release] with lto = thin and codegen-units = 1, plus a [profile.profiling] with debug info. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25+/0.26 and current grammars. Drop thiserror or adopt it (ENG-07). Consider moving to edition 2024, since the MSRV is already 1.85.

ENG.note: Package metadata done: new description, license, repository, homepage, readme, rust-version, keywords, categories, include. Overflow checks on in dev/test; release has lto=thin and codegen-units=1; new profiling profile. Edition stays 2021 because migrating needs a validated build. tree-sitter upgrade and thiserror handed off.

title: Supply-chain posture fails key OpenSSF Scorecard checks (pinning, token permissions, SRI, SAST)
evidence: Every action uses a mutable ref (checkout@v4, cache@v4, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master, softprops/action-gh-release@v1) rather than a commit SHA, failing Pinned-Dependencies. ci.yml and release.yml declare no `permissions:` block, failing Token-Permissions. deploy_pages.yml publishes web/ on every push to main regardless of CI results. web/index.html:29-34 loads five CDN scripts with no integrity= attribute. There is no CodeQL or other SAST, no dependency review, no fuzzing and no signed releases. Dependabot does not track the CDN libraries and has no grouping configured.
impact: A compromised action tag or CDN file can run in CI with repository tokens, or in every Studio visitor's browser. Failing Scorecard checks also signal immaturity to adopters.
recommendation: Pin actions by full commit SHA with version comments; Dependabot will keep them updated. Set a top-level `permissions: contents: read` and grant more per job. Gate the Pages deploy on CI with needs or workflow_run. Vendor the web libraries through package.json plus a lockfile, or add SRI hashes. Enable CodeQL and actions/dependency-review-action, run the OpenSSF Scorecard action and publish its badge, and add cargo-deny source policies.

ENG.note: `make deny` checks advisories, bans and sources, and licenses too once deny.toml exists. Action pinning, permissions and SRI are in workflows and web, handed off.

title: Everything is public, mostly undocumented, stringly typed and in one crate; the CLI and JSON handling are hand-rolled
evidence: lib.rs makes all 12 modules public, including the HTTP server and a module named `core` that shadows Rust's core crate. There are about 970 pub items and 593 pub fields against 3 pub(crate) uses; roughly 27% of pub items have rustdoc, and there are no crate docs and no #![warn(missing_docs)]. Diagram kinds are strings such as 'statemachine', returning Option (factory.rs:314). The CLI strips flags after its length check, so `openheart --debug` indexes args[1] out of bounds and panics (main.rs:491-508), and an invalid port silently becomes 8080 (:534). The server parses JSON with split('"') (server.rs:367-371) and builds responses with unescaped format! strings, even though serde_json is a dependency.
impact: Every internal refactor is a breaking change and semver cannot be checked. The library cannot target wasm32 (a ROADMAP goal) or be embedded without the server, and CLI and JSON edge cases crash or produce invalid output.
recommendation: Split into a workspace: openheart-core (pure, no I/O), openheart-lang-* crates behind features, openheart-cli (clap derive) and openheart-server (serde for all JSON). Expose a small facade, such as Analysis::from_paths(..).run() returning Result<Scpg>, and make internals pub(crate). Model diagram kinds and formats as enums marked #[non_exhaustive]. Follow the Rust API Guidelines, enable #![warn(missing_docs)], and run cargo-semver-checks in CI once the API settles.

title: Docs and repo hygiene: a committed LLM prompt, an empty Phase 4 spec, stale paths, and false security and config statements
evidence: docs/RESEARCH_PAPER_NEXT_PROMPT.txt is an LLM instruction ('MAKE SURE THE PAPER IS UNDENIABLY UNCHALLENGED AND CAN'T BE PROVEN FALSE'), yet docs/README.md:29 lists it as 'Prompt specification'. docs/plans/phase4.md is 0 bytes. contributing.md:18 and security-architecture.md:12 cite src/phase1/, which does not exist. security-architecture.md claims #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (:11), value saturation (:26) and configuration via environment variables (:34). .env.example lists five variables, but the code reads only OPENHEART_LOG. examples/README.md:12,34 point to examples/sample_project, which does not exist and is gitignored. web/docs/ duplicates the HTML in docs/, and one copy has already diverged.
impact: Newcomers follow broken instructions, and security reviewers are misled about unsafe code and input handling. The committed prompt invites the reading that the paper was written to be unchallengeable rather than measured.
recommendation: Delete the prompt file, and fill in or remove phase4.md. Build the docs from one source (mdBook or Docusaurus deployed through Pages) and link-check them in CI with lychee. Tie every security and configuration statement to code, or delete it. Make .env.example list only variables the code reads, ideally via clap's env feature. Pull the README into rustdoc with #![doc = include_str!("../README.md")]. Record the major decisions (custom server, custom logger, file hand-off between phases, String errors) as MADR ADRs.

DOCS.note: Prompt file and empty phase4.md deleted; index, paths, security and config statements fixed; LLM preamble removed from phase2 spec; ADRs added; .env.example, web/docs, lychee and include_str handed off

title: CFG never wires edges into or out of try and do-while; their bodies and all later code are pruned
evidence: Both builders rely on flush_pending, but add_pending_exit (state.rs:76) has no caller, so pending_exits is always empty. try: no edge from the current block to try_entry (try_stmt.rs:50-52), and none from the try-body, catch or finally ends (57, 69, 78). do-while: no edge into body_entry (do_while.rs:24-25) and none from body end to cond (36). The sink patch (builder/mod.rs:70-77) links every dangling block to EXIT, then RPO compaction (92) drops the rest: `a=1; try{f();}catch(E e){g();} h();` becomes ENTRY→[a=1]→EXIT.
impact: Every method with a try or do-while loses that statement and everything after it from the CFG, SSA, PSA, activity diagrams and block traceability, while all invariants still pass.
recommendation: Wire explicit edges (current→entry; try/catch/finally/body exits→join), or make every builder register its fall-through via add_pending_exit. Replace the silent sink→EXIT patch with an assertion that only return/throw blocks may lack successors. Add golden tests for try/catch/finally, do-while and nested combinations, diffed against the CFG of the same source compiled by javac and read through SootUp, WALA or ASM.

title: Java AST reduction (Phase 2 root cause) discards switch bodies, constructor bodies and try-with-resources before Phases 4-6
evidence: Unlisted tree-sitter kinds hit `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129), which discards the whole subtree (adapter/mod.rs:19-20). Unlisted: switch_block/switch_rule/switch_label, try_with_resources_statement, constructor_body, explicit_constructor_invocation, yield_statement, enum_constant. NN_SWITCH_CASE is never produced, so build_switch is dead code; as far as I know, tree-sitter-java ≥0.19 also emits statement switches as switch_expression, which dispatch_stmt does not handle. Constructors have no NN_BLOCK child, so cfg/mod.rs:60-75 skips them; the accuracy test asserts function_count == 2 for a file with three bodies.
impact: Statements and call sites inside switches, constructors (including super()/this() chains), try-with-resources and enum-constant bodies vanish from the CFG, SSA and call graph: silent data loss on idiomatic Java.
recommendation: Map these kinds (Keep/Eliminate) and add a coverage test generated from tree-sitter-java's node-types.json that fails if any statement or expression kind is dropped. In Phase 4, handle NN_SWITCH_EXPR, arrow rules, patterns and yield; desugar try-with-resources per JLS 14.20.3 (close() and suppressed exceptions); model constructor prologues (super/this call, field initializers) as an <init> body, as Soot and WALA do.

CORE.note: Phase 2 now preserves switch bodies (cases + AUX_CASE_ARROW/DEFAULT flags, statement-position switches as NN_SWITCH_STMT), constructor bodies as NN_BLOCK, explicit this()/super() calls, yield, try-with-resources (resources precede body), instance initializers wrapped; CFG semantics outside.

title: Loop builders choose children by position, dropping enhanced-for bodies and mis-wiring for-loops
evidence: Reduction discards tree-sitter field names, so build_for guesses roles from the child count (for_stmt.rs:14-36). In `for(;i<n;i++)` the condition becomes the init and `i++` the condition. `for(int i=0,j=n;i<j;i++,j--)` has five children, so `j--` (children[3]) becomes the body and the real block is never dispatched. build_enhanced_for takes the first three children (88-101), but `for (String s : xs) {...}` reduces to [TYPE_REF, s, xs, BLOCK], so `xs` is treated as the body and the block is skipped. `while (x);` returns early (while_stmt.rs:19-22).
impact: The bodies of the most common enhanced-for form (simple element types such as String, int or Order) and of multi-update for-loops are missing from the CFG, SSA and PSA.
recommendation: Preserve tree-sitter field roles in the BPA (a per-node role byte, or synthetic NN_FOR_INIT/COND/UPDATE/BODY wrappers) and select children by role, never by count. Add a golden test for each loop shape: empty parts, multiple init/update expressions, modifiers or annotations on the loop variable, and generic and array element types.

title: SSA keys variables by AST-node occurrence, so no φ-function or def-use edge is ever produced
evidence: extract_stmt_vars uses the declaration node (`let sym_id = node`, liveness.rs:134) or an assignment's LHS node as the def key, and each identifier or RHS-expression node as a use key; the symbol table is ignored (`_sta`, ssa/mod.rs:34). Def and use keys are disjoint, so vstack.top(u) (renaming.rs:150) never hits and is_live_in(y, var_sym) (placement.rs:45) is never true. The result is zero φ and an empty def-use CSR on every input, including the if/else example in tests/ssa_tests.rs. Parameters are never defined; initializer uses, `x++` defs and compound-assignment uses are lost.
impact: SSA, def-use chains, the DFG, slicing and the points-to analysis built on them are empty or meaningless. Liveness keys are never killed, so live sets grow to O(blocks × identifier occurrences).
recommendation: Have Phase 3 emit an occurrence→SymbolId table for locals, parameters and fields. Build SSA on symbols: Braun et al. 2013 during CFG construction (as Cranelift's SSABuilder and libFirm do), or Cytron with pruned liveness on bitsets. Define parameters and this at ENTRY; handle fields and arrays via heap or memory SSA, φ at handler entries, and captured lambda variables. Add an SSA verifier: every use dominated by its def, φ arity equal to the predecessor count.

title: Call-target resolution returns the enclosing method, so the call graph is mostly self-loops
evidence: resolve_method_target never compares names. It (1) matches symbols whose decl_node is the call node (lambdas only); (2) takes the first identifier child, which is the receiver in `obj.m()`; (3) compares that with methods' first_token_id, the declaration's first token (pass1_discovery.rs:139,178), which never equals a call-site token; (4) returns the first METHOD/CONSTRUCTOR whose token range encloses the call, i.e. the caller. So `t.helper()` in main gives main→main, `new T()` in a method gives caller→caller, and lambda sites give lambda→lambda.
impact: Sequence diagrams, impact analysis, slicing, CFL queries and Phase 8 recursion flags (nearly every calling method is classed self-recursive) are wrong. The accuracy test asserts that no multi-method SCC exists (:222).
recommendation: Implement JLS 15.12 method selection. Infer the receiver's static type from Phase 3, which needs generic, qualified and array types kept in the AST. Select by name, arity, applicability and most-specific rule, then dispatch (FLOW-12). Index methods by (class, name, arity). Validate edges against the invokevirtual/invokeinterface/invokestatic targets in the javac-compiled bytecode and against the CATS suite.

title: User-facing CFG, DFG, CDG and call-graph diagrams are hard-coded templates, not analysis output
evidence: Every exporter for diagrams 15-19 takes only (uma, sta, tca) and never reads .cfa/.ssa/.cga. The PlantUML/Mermaid CFG is a fixed Entry→Gate→Then/Else→Exit template. The DFG prints `var_name: retries` v0/v1/φ for the first three classes. The CDG always shows `(amount > 0)` → `repository.saveOrder()`. The call graph chains methods in HashSet order, labelled `CHA/1-CFA dispatch`, plus a fake `Tarjan SCC cycle` self-edge. The JSON CFG and CG describe OpenHeart's own pipeline (`v0 = load manifest`, `cooper_dominators()`). The code is in src/scpg (Phase 10).
impact: Users see fabricated flow diagrams for every input, contradicting README lines 88-90, and the fabrication hid the Phase 4-6 defects in this report.
recommendation: Render these diagrams from the artifacts (blocks, edges and idom; φ and def-use; the CDG CSR; CG edges and SCCs) with deterministic ordering and per-function selection. Add snapshot tests that check every rendered node and edge against an artifact entity. Show 'not available' instead of a placeholder when an analysis did not run.

DOCS.note: README/uml_derivation list CFG/DFG/CDG/CG/ROBDD views as templates and say exporters must report 'unavailable'; exporter code handed off

SCPGX.note: Same as SCPG-01: flow diagrams rendered from blocks/edges/idom, phi/def-use, CDG CSR, CG edges+SCCs with deterministic ordering, per-function budgets and focus; real output needs callers to pass the artifacts (handoff).

title: Exceptional control flow and finally semantics are not modeled
evidence: Only an explicit `throw` creates Except edges; calls, `new`, array access, casts and division never do. throw jumps to handlers.first() of the innermost try regardless of exception type, and skips finally when a catch exists (throw_stmt.rs:20-37). return, break and continue go straight to EXIT or loop targets, bypassing finally. finally always falls through to post_try, even when entered exceptionally. catch_formal_parameter is unmapped, so the catch body is added as one opaque statement and never dispatched (try_stmt.rs:63-67). resolve_catch_type returns AST node ids as type ids (84-97).
impact: Even after FLOW-01, handler reachability, finally coverage and exception paths are wrong, which rules out sound taint, resource-leak and null analyses.
recommendation: Model potentially-excepting instructions (JLS 11.2) with edges to the innermost catch clauses whose type may match (a subtype test on the class hierarchy), then to finally, outer frames and an exceptional EXIT, as Soot's ExceptionalUnitGraph and WALA do. Duplicate finally on every abrupt exit (javac style) or route through a dispatch block. Keep separate normal and exceptional EXIT nodes.

title: Labeled break/continue, synchronized, switch expressions and short-circuit operators are unsupported
evidence: Loops push frames with label None (while_stmt.rs:33-34) and the labeled-statement arm (stmts/mod.rs:47-53) never records the label, while break/continue compare AST node ids of different label occurrences (break_stmt.rs:24). So `break outer;` gets no edge, and the sink patch sends it to EXIT. NN_JAVA_SYNCHRONIZED, NN_SWITCH_EXPR, NN_YIELD_STMT and asserts fall to the default arm as one opaque statement, so a return inside synchronized never reaches EXIT. &&, || and ?: stay single nodes. `while(true)` always gets a False exit edge (while_stmt.rs:49).
impact: Paths are wrong for idiomatic concurrent and nested-loop code, which distorts path counts, the CDG and slicing.
recommendation: Keep a label stack keyed by interned label text. Add dispatch arms for synchronized (monitor enter/exit plus an exceptional exit), switch expressions, arrow rules (no fall-through), patterns and yield, and assert. Lower &&, || and ?: into branch blocks as javac and Jimple do. Give constant-true loop conditions no exit edge. In build_switch, stop treating non-literal labels (Color.RED, patterns) as default. Add a golden test per construct.

title: CDG equals the CFG edge set because the post-dominator DFS walks the wrong adjacency
evidence: The reverse-graph DFS from EXIT iterates rev_preds, i.e. forward successors (cdg.rs:37-51), so it visits only EXIT. The fallback loop (53-57) then runs a forward DFS from ENTRY, making rev_rpo[0] = ENTRY. compute_idom_cooper roots at rpo[0] (dominators.rs:21), and ENTRY is nobody's successor, so every other ipdom stays UNDEFINED; the FOW walk (65-86) then marks each edge target as dependent on its source. A faithful Python port gives ipdom=[0,U,U,U,U,U] on an if/else diamond, with the join dependent on both arms. All non-False labels become TRUE.
impact: Every function's control dependence is wrong, so PDG slicing and the advertised CDG cannot be trusted. A correct compute_post_idom exists in postdom.rs but is never called.
recommendation: Reuse compute_post_idom. Add a virtual EXIT fed by all exits and by one node per reverse-unreachable region (as LLVM's PostDominatorTree chooses roots), plus the ENTRY→EXIT augmentation edge (Ferrante-Ottenstein-Warren 1987). Keep branch labels (true/false/case value/exception type). Property-test post-dominators and the CDG against a naive fixpoint on random CFGs, as the forward dominators already pass.

title: The advertised IFDS solver is a three-predicate syntactic stub
evidence: IFDSAnalyzer::analyze visits each SSA record once. A 'taint source' is a defining statement with a direct NN_METHOD_DECL child (ifds.rs:58-67). 'Nullable' means any direct NN_LITERAL child, so a for-init `i = 0` counts as nullable while `String s = null;` does not. Type-state reuses the method-declaration test (80-89). There is no supergraph, flow function, path edge, summary edge or worklist, so it is not even intraprocedural dataflow. README.md:100 advertises an 'IFDS Solver', and phase5.md describes RHS tabulation in supergraph.rs/tabulation.rs files that do not exist.
impact: Taint, nullness and type-state facts are noise; any security or null-safety use of them is unsupported.
recommendation: Implement Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv 1995 tabulation over an ICFG, which needs call nodes in the CFG and a correct call graph. Add the Naeem-Lhoták-Rodriguez 2010 extensions, and IDE (Sagiv-Reps-Horwitz 1996) for typestate and constant propagation, using Heros, PhASAR and FlowDroid as references. Make sources, sinks and sanitizers configurable, and benchmark on SecuriBench Micro and the OWASP Benchmark. Until then, drop the claim.

DOCS.note: README IFDS claim removed; phase5.md §5.2.6 marked not implemented, with what ifds.rs really does; code handed off

title: 'Andersen' points-to has no real constraints and merges SSA ids across methods
evidence: Seeds fire only when an SSA def_stmt is itself an NN_NEW_EXPR (points_to.rs:28-30), but def_stmt is the enclosing declaration or expression statement, so allocations are virtually never seen. The only constraints are copy edges from φ arguments (46-53), and no φ is ever placed (FLOW-04). There are no assign, load, store, call or return constraints, no fields and no cycle detection. The allocation 'type' looks up sta.symbol() with an AST node index (31). pts is keyed by ssa_id, which restarts at 0 in every function (renaming.rs:124,159), so facts from different methods merge.
impact: Points-to sets are empty or wrong, so no precision reaches dispatch or alias queries. The spec's BDD-based Andersen with O(n^1.5) empirical cost (phase6.md:549) is not implemented.
recommendation: Number variables globally (a per-function base offset) and model allocation sites as abstract objects, with field-sensitive address/copy/load/store/call/return constraints and an on-the-fly call graph. Use a worklist with difference propagation (Pearce et al. 2004), lazy and hybrid cycle detection (Hardekopf & Lin, PLDI 2007) and sparse bitsets (roaring), or write it in Datalog (Doop's rules on Soufflé, or Rust ascent). Benchmark against Doop and SootUp/Spark on DaCapo.

DOCS.note: phase6.md 1-CFA and Andersen sections annotated as not implemented; paper and README corrected; code handed off

title: Dispatch model is weaker than CHA: name-only, downward-only, no RTA, initializers, lambdas or libraries
evidence: resolve_cha gathers same-name, non-abstract METHOD and CONSTRUCTOR symbols in subtypes (resolution.rs:84-93). Overloads are conflated, and there is no upward lookup for inherited implementations or default methods (JVMS 5.4.6). CG_EDGE_INTERFACE is unreachable because it tests a method symbol for SK_INTERFACE (call_sites.rs:113).
