'resolve_1cfa' is not call-string 1-CFA, and it is dead because receiver_ssa is effectively never found (129-140). There is no RTA, entry-point model, lambda→SAM linking, super/this()/<clinit> edge or reflection (CG_EDGE_REFLECTION is unused). Calls in field and instance initializers are dropped (32-35).
impact: Even after FLOW-05, soundness and precision would sit far below CHA as implemented by Soot, WALA or OPAL.
recommendation: Build per-class method tables with JVMS-correct virtual, interface and default-method resolution. Layer CHA, then RTA (Bacon & Sweeney 1996), then VTA or on-the-fly points-to. Add entry points (main, tests, frameworks), LambdaMetafactory-style lambda and method-reference modeling, <init>/<clinit> semantics, JDK models from jmods or class files, and reflection handling via string analysis or TamiFlex logs. Measure with CATS and Judge (Reif et al., ISSTA 2019) and dynamic call-graph recall on DaCapo/XCorpus.

CORE.note: Phase 2 preserves inputs CHA/RTA need (explicit ctor invocations with SUPER/QUALIFIED flags, instance/static initializers, anon bodies, ctor method refs); call-graph algorithms outside.

title: Linear scans over symbols and SSA records make Phases 4-6 quadratic
evidence: find_enclosing_method scans all symbols at every AST ancestor of every call node (call_sites.rs:70-91). resolve_method_target does up to three full symbol scans and runs twice per site. extract_receiver_ssa scans every SSA record of every function per site. resolve_cha rescans all symbols and TH edges per hierarchy type, and resolve_catch_type scans all symbols per catch. CSR building is blocks × edges. Liveness clones HashSets per block per pass (capped at 100 passes), and renaming snapshots the full version-stack map per block. I estimate 10^11-10^12 comparisons at 500K LOC, against a claimed 'under 3 seconds' (phase6.md:553).
impact: Large repositories take hours, and the single-threaded server is blocked meanwhile, so submitting one big repo to /api/analyze is a denial of service.
recommendation: Build indexes once: a preorder-interval node→function map, a decl_node→symbol HashMap, (class, name, arity)→methods, def_stmt→SSA id, and a subtype CSR. Use counting-sort CSR construction, bitset worklist liveness (fixedbitset or roaring) and version stacks that pop per block. Add criterion benchmarks on Guava- and Elasticsearch-scale corpora, with time and memory budgets enforced in CI.

title: Unbounded recursion on CFG size can abort the analysis server
evidence: The RPO, loop and CDG DFS, the dominator-tree renaming (12 arguments plus a HashMap per frame) and Tarjan's strongconnect all recurse. Depth tracks block count, not AST depth: K sequential ifs give a DFS path of about 2K blocks and a dominator tree about K deep. The server binds 0.0.0.0, clones any GitHub repo posted to /api/analyze (server.rs:429), and runs every phase on the main thread, whose stack is 1 MiB on Windows. A Rust stack overflow aborts the process; it is not a catchable panic.
impact: One generated or crafted method with a few thousand sequential ifs can crash the server. Tarjan will face the same risk once the call graph is real.
recommendation: Rewrite the DFS walks, renaming and Tarjan with explicit stacks (as in LLVM's po_iterator, petgraph's iterative tarjan_scc, or Pearce 2016). Run per-function work on worker threads with an explicit std::thread::Builder::stack_size and catch_unwind isolation. Add stress tests with generated 10^5-block methods and very deep call chains.

SRV.note: Every CLI and server pipeline runs on a dedicated thread with an explicit stack (OPENHEART_STACK_MB, default 256 MiB) and per-phase catch_unwind. Iterative DFS rewrites are outside my paths

title: Phase 4-6 tests are smoke tests that pass on these defects, and some encode them
evidence: pipeline_accuracy_tests expects function_count == 2 for three method bodies (:142) and asserts sccs.len() == symbol_count, which forbids any multi-method SCC (:222). Its per-function CFA checks iterate deserialize()'s always-empty functions vector (:144-160). ssa_tests checks only total_ssa_vars >= 1 on the canonical φ example (:86); cg_tests checks a non-empty SCC list and a round trip. The only analysis unit test is one 4-node diamond. No test covers try, switch, do-while, labels, enhanced-for, φ, def-use, CDG or call targets, and there is no proptest or criterion dependency.
impact: The defects above are invisible to CI, so 'CI passing' and the F1 figures say nothing about flow-analysis correctness.
recommendation: Write golden tests per Java construct (expected blocks, edges, idom, φ, def-use, control dependence and call edges), diffed against javac bytecode CFGs via SootUp, WALA or ASM. Add proptest checks of dominators, post-dominators, DF and SCC against naive references, and run an SSA verifier on every test. Use CATS for call-graph soundness, measure precision and recall against Soot/WALA/OPAL on DaCapo/XCorpus, and add criterion benchmarks.

title: No intermediate representation: statement-level AST blocks block precise SSA, ICFG and IFDS
evidence: Basic blocks hold whole AST statements (BasicBlock.stmts; add_stmt_to_current). Calls, allocations, short-circuit operands and implicit operations (unboxing, iterator()/next(), close(), string concatenation) are not CFG nodes. Evaluation order and temporaries are implicit, and no excepting instruction is explicit. Every consumer (SSA, points-to, call graph, IFDS) re-walks AST subtrees with ad-hoc logic such as extract_stmt_vars, and call sites cannot be mapped to CFG nodes (call_block falls back to 0).
impact: Benchmark-grade interprocedural analyses (IFDS/IDE, Andersen, context-sensitive call graphs) cannot be built on this representation.
recommendation: Lower to a typed three-address IR with explicit temporaries, call/return nodes and excepting instructions (Jimple/Shimple, WALA's SSA IR, OPAL's TAC), or to Joern-style expression-level CFG nodes, and build SSA during lowering (Braun et al. 2013). Consider a bytecode front end for javac/kotlinc class files, as Soot, WALA, OPAL and Doop use, to get exact lambda, switch, finally and Kotlin semantics.

CORE.note: IR lowering is in cfg/ssa; outside my paths.

title: Loop nesting and cyclomatic complexity are miscomputed
evidence: Back edges are DFS retreating edges with no dominance check (loops.rs:39), and depth is incremented once per back edge (62-85), not once per loop header. Each continue adds a LoopBack edge to a while or enhanced-for header (continue_stmt.rs:30-31), so `while(x){ if(a) continue; if(b) continue; work(); }` reports max_loop_depth 3 instead of 1. Irreducible regions are not detected: a non-dominated tail floods the natural-loop walk to ENTRY. V(G) = E−N+2 (builder/mod.rs:183-185) counts synthetic sink→EXIT edges and pruned bodies, and is truncated to u16.
impact: The loop depth and V(G) passed to Phase 8 and to diagram labels are inflated or deflated.
recommendation: Build a loop-nesting forest: treat an edge as a back edge only if the header dominates the tail, merge natural loops per header (as LLVM LoopInfo does), and flag irreducible SCCs (Havlak 1997, Ramalingam 2002). Compute V(G) as decision points + 1, or on a deduplicated CFG without synthetic edges, and unit-test both.

title: .cfa/.ssa/.cga encodings are lossy, partly write-only and mis-indexed
evidence: .cfa stores exit = blocks.len()-1, but RPO numbering places EXIT before loop-body blocks, so in any function with a loop it names a body block; block statements and token ranges are not stored. CFGArtifact::deserialize and SSASerializer::read return empty function lists. .ssa directory offsets omit seven u32 length prefixes per function, drifting by 28 bytes each. SSARecord.def_block is a u8, which Phase 8 (feasibility.rs:114-119) and Phase 7 then alias. φ orig_sym_id is written as u16, and SCCRecord.member_count is a u16.
impact: External readers of .cfa/.ssa get wrong data or none. Functions with more than 256 blocks get mis-attributed SSA defs downstream, and an SCC with more than 65,535 members trips Invariant 3 and aborts Phase 6.
recommendation: Use u32 for ids and counts, derive directory offsets from the bytes actually written, store the EXIT id explicitly, implement full readers, and add round-trip property tests. Consider a versioned zero-copy schema (rkyv, FlatBuffers or Cap'n Proto).

BDD.note: Phase 8 no longer reads the aliased u8 def_block; ssa_bi uses it only where exact (256 blocks or fewer). cfa/ssa encodings are outside my paths.

CORE.note: Core types widened (def_block u32, SCCRecord.member_count u32); .cga/.ssa/digest serializers are handoffs.

title: Call-site records carry the wrong token, arity and block, and the CG spans every symbol
evidence: call_token is the first identifier child, i.e. the receiver in `obj.m()` (call_sites.rs:153-170). arg_count = children−1 (172-180) is off by one when a receiver exists, and counts anonymous-class members. call_block is found only when the call node is itself a block statement; otherwise it is 0, the ENTRY block (142-151). flags are always 0 (43). method_count = sta.symbol_count (cg/mod.rs:110) puts classes, fields and locals into the CG and SCC table, contrary to phase6.md:23. Tarjan emits SCCs callee-first, but psa/mod.rs:98-102 reverses them believing the opposite.
impact: Traceability highlights the wrong token, there is no call-site→CFG link to build an ICFG on, and the SCC order contract is misread downstream.
recommendation: Record the name token and argument list explicitly, map each call to its CFG node (see FLOW-16), and restrict CG nodes to callables through a dense method index. Document and test the SCC order (Tarjan's output is reverse topological, i.e. callee-first). Replace Vec::contains deduplication with sort+dedup.

BDD.note: psa/mod.rs now follows Tarjan's callee-first order without .rev() and also schedules CFG functions the call graph does not cover. Call-site record fixes are outside my paths.

title: Kotlin (and the other advertised languages) get no CFG, SSA or call graph
evidence: Only Java has an AST adapter. Kotlin falls back to the generic adapter bound to tree_sitter_javascript (registry.rs:19-41), so .kt files are parsed as JavaScript. Kotlin `fun` symbols come from a token sweep that leaves decl_node = u32::MAX (SymbolRecord::UNINIT, pass1_discovery.rs:439-447), and Phase 4 skips such symbols (cfg/mod.rs:55-58); their call sites have no enclosing method and are dropped. Cargo.toml has no Kotlin, Python or C++ grammar.
impact: The Java/Kotlin flow-analysis claim, and the multi-language F1 claim as applied to Phases 4-6, hold for nothing except Java.
recommendation: Add tree-sitter-kotlin (or analyze kotlinc bytecode) with a dedicated reduction adapter and a Kotlin lowering for when, expression-bodied functions, ?., !!, inline lambdas and suspend state machines. Scope README claims per phase and language until golden tests cover them.

ENG.note: Kotlin lowering is src work.

CORE.note: Kotlin is now explicitly lexical-only (flagged, reported in Phase 2) instead of JS-parsed; real Kotlin AST requires the grammar adapter wiring handoff.

DOCS.note: README and support matrix scope phases 4-6 to Java and say Kotlin gets no CFG/SSA/CG; code handed off

title: Per-function phases are sequential and never incremental
evidence: Phases 4 and 5 loop over functions sequentially, although each function is independent, and no parallelism crate is a dependency. There is no per-function fingerprint or cache: SSA ids are per-run positions and the call graph is rebuilt from scratch, while the incremental-sync doc promises to 'Recompute CFG, SSA, and ROBDD summaries only for affected functions'.
impact: Wall-clock time grows linearly with codebase size even for one-line edits, and extra cores sit idle.
recommendation: Use rayon par_iter over functions in Phases 4-5 with a deterministic merge order. Cache CFG and SSA per function, keyed by an AST-subtree hash. Update the call graph incrementally (re-resolve sites in changed methods plus a CHA delta), and use incremental dominator updates (Georgiadis et al.) for small edits.

DOCS.note: Traceability doc marks per-function incremental recomputation as planned; rayon/caching handed off

title: Compiler-IR diagrams (CFG/DFG/CDG/call graph/ROBDD) and several views are hard-coded templates, not analysis output
evidence: The JSON CFG, DFG, CDG, call-graph, ROBDD, timing, interaction and profile builders take `_uma,_sta,_tca` and emit constants that describe OpenHeart itself ("v0 = load manifest", "v3 = compute_idom(v2)", "x2: ASTAcyclic", "@60ms: 8 Threads"). The PlantUML and Mermaid CDGs ignore their inputs and print "(amount > 0)" and "repository.saveOrder()". Every function gets the same fixed 4-block CFG diamond. The DFG is a φ template with "var_name: retries". The call graph chains methods in HashSet order with invented "CHA/1-CFA dispatch" edges and a fake SCC self-loop. Exporters never receive .cfa/.ssa/.cga/.psa.
impact: Every analyzed program gets identical or invented control-flow, data-flow, dependence, call and BDD graphs. The README claim of "19 projections derived from binary graph layers" is false, and users can be misled about their own code.
recommendation: Pass exporters a DiagramContext: CFA CSR with idom, SSA DefUseCSR/CDGCSR/phis, CGA callee_csr with SCCs, PSA ROBDD node tables and TRA spans. Use it to render the real graphs (CFG with back-edges and dominator tree, def-use with φ, CDG, SCC-clustered call graph, actual BDD nodes). Until then, drop these types from the registry and the README. Done means golden tests on fixture methods whose expected CFG and CDG were checked by hand.

DOCS.note: README/architecture/uml_derivation/status.md now label diagrams 04,05,07,09,12-19 as template or not derived; the '19 projections derived' claim is withdrawn; exporter code handed off

SCPGX.note: CFG(+back edges, idom tree), SSA def-use with phi, CDG, SCC-clustered call graph and real ROBDD nodes now render from CFA/SSA/CGA/PSA via DiagramContext; without those artifacts they are explicit 'not available' views. CLI/server must pass the context (handoff); README claim and golden tests outside paths.

title: The unified .scpg stores only element counts; the 'memory-mapped' open is a full copy, and no query uses it
evidence: Ten of the eleven sections hold a single LE count (`tca.token_records.len() as u32`, `sta.symbol_count`, `cga.call_site_count`, `psa.total_nodes`). Only StringTable carries real bytes, and no section deserializer exists. `MemoryMappedSCPG::open` calls `fs::read` into a Vec, although a memmap2 wrapper exists in core/io/mmap.rs. `OpenHeartEngine.mmap` is never read, and every query takes in-memory artifacts as arguments. Sections are unaligned (4-byte payloads, directory u64 fields at offsets ≡4 mod 8), so zero-copy views are impossible.
impact: Phase 10's main output carries no analysis data, and a .scpg cannot be reopened to answer a query. The claims of "<1 ms mmap open", an "82 MB LZ4" file and hot/cold paging are not backed by code.
recommendation: Make each section hold the full canonical artifact (or columnar CSR arrays, as in Joern flatgraph), aligned to 64 B or 4 KiB, with a per-section zstd/LZ4 codec and checksum. Map it with memmap2 from an immutable, atomically renamed file, expose typed views through zerocopy or bytemuck (or rkyv with bytecheck), and run QueryEngine over that view. Done means opening and querying a 500 KLOC .scpg without re-running phases 1-9, with latency measured by criterion.

CORE.note: Only the core/io/mmap.rs part: a sound unsafe map() exists for zero-copy views; .scpg sections and queries are outside.

DOCS.note: README/phase10/status say sections hold counts and open() reads the whole file; zero-copy claim withdrawn; code handed off

SCPG.note: All 11 sections now hold full columnar indexes (tokens, files, AST ranges, symbols+stable ids, hierarchy, call graph+SCC+reach index, SDG, spans, UML, ROBDD nodes, canonical .cfa), 64B/4KiB aligned with CRC-64; real memmap2 mapping; OpenHeartEngine::open serves queries without phases 1-9. Sections are decoded into owned Vecs (no zero-copy views), no compression codec.

title: State, object, component, deployment, composite, use-case and activity views ignore UMA data and invent content
evidence: State machines always show "Uninitialized" and "Active" states with "entry / onInit()", "do / executeWork()" and "exit / cleanup()", and never read `sm.states`. Object diagrams draw one object per class with "references" edges between consecutive classes, while `uma.objects` (allocation sites) goes unused. Components get an invented `I{name}` interface, deployments get "art_X.jar" nodes, and composites get `port in_port/out_port`. Use-case actors are classes whose names end in "Service" or "App". JSON activities chain nodes in a line and ignore `act.edges`. Every Mermaid gantt task is `0, 1s`.
impact: Most behavioral and deployment views look plausible but contain no program facts. They mislead reviewers and make the "14 UML 2.5 diagrams" claim impossible to verify.
recommendation: Render only modeled facts: states and transitions with guards from StateRecord/TransitionRecord, objects from ObjectRecord plus points-to links, component interfaces from provided/required sets, activity flow from ActivityEdge, and sequence fragments from CombinedFragment. When a diagram has no evidence, emit an explicit "no data" note instead of a placeholder. Note that UMA's own state model is a 2-state placeholder, which is another auditor's area. Done means golden fixtures whose every element traces back to a source span.

SCPGX.note: States/transitions/guards/actions from StateMachineRecord, objects from ObjectRecord plus ObjectLinkRecord, component provided/required interfaces, activity flow from ActivityEdge with guards, sequence fragments from CombinedFragment; empty inputs yield explicit 'not available' notes; no invented ports, interfaces, artifacts or actors.

UML.note: UMA now produces real states and transitions with guards, objects and links, component interface lists, activity guards and fragments; the exporters still have to render them (handed off).

title: Exporters key classes by sanitized simple name, merging same-named types and misattaching edges
evidence: PlantUML maps names to symbols in `class_by_name: BTreeMap<String,u32>` and keys edges by `(src_name,dst_name)`. JSON uses `id: name.clone()`, and Mermaid keys `class_package_map` by name. As a result, many nested `Builder`s or `a.Config`/`b.Config` collapse into one node. The shipped class.json has 5 duplicate node ids (CurrentState, IDAssigner, Module…). `sanitize` maps `Foo$Bar` and `Foo_Bar` to the same id. Mermaid's fix for duplicate packages appends the root's initial, so `com.a.util` and `com.b.util` both become `util_C`. Since PlantUML 1.2023.2, packages are namespaces, so edges keyed by bare names are also fragile across versions.
impact: Common Java codebases, such as those using nested Builders or per-module Config/Utils classes, get merged boxes and edges between the wrong classes. JSON consumers receive ids that are not unique.
recommendation: Derive stable unique ids from sym_id or the fully qualified name (SCIP or Kythe-style symbol strings) and print display names separately: PlantUML `class "Builder" as C_1234`, Mermaid `class C_1234["Builder"]`, JSON id = FQN, xmi:id = hash(FQN). Resolve edges by symbol, never by name. Done means a test with two inner Builders and two Config packages yields distinct nodes in every format.

SCPGX.note: Element keys are FQN (FQN#sym on collision), aliases unique per view via AliasTable, display names quoted (PlantUML class "X" as alias, Mermaid class alias["X"]), relations resolved by symbol/key, Mermaid namespaces flat per unique package alias, JSON ids unique.

title: JSON Graph IR fabricates source provenance and 'verified' metadata
evidence: Class nodes get `file: Some(format!("{}.java", name))` and `lines: vec![1, 5, 10]`. Sequence, state and object nodes get `"{name}.java"` with line 1. The composite root is "OpenHeartEngine.java" for every input. Each GraphIR carries the constants `compiler_hash: "0x83D2D2B2"` and `verified: true`. Meanwhile every ClassRecord has `uml_link` holding the real file, line and column, and the web editor navigates by `nodeData?.file`. The shipped class.json assigns TypeScript interfaces and Python classes to `.java` files.
impact: Click-to-source opens files that do not exist or the wrong lines, which contradicts the 'O(1) bidirectional traceability' headline. The 'verified' flag is meaningless.
recommendation: Fill file and range from `class_rec.uml_link` or TRA sym_span, taking the path from tca.file_records, and emit null when unknown. Set compiler_hash to the real snapshot digest. Either drop `verified` or compute it from real checks (unique ids, all edge endpoints resolve). Add a JSON Schema for GraphIR and validate against it in CI. Done means every node with a span maps back to its declaring token range.

SCPGX.note: file/lines/span come from UMLLink or the symbol's declaring token range (null when unknown); real input digest; verified computed from unique-id/endpoint/parent/cycle checks; versioned Graph IR with JSONExporter::json_schema().

UML.note: Class uml_link comes from TRA, else from the declaring tokens, else an explicit unknown marker, and uml_link_is_known() is provided; the JSON exporter must emit null for unknown and fix compiler_hash/verified (handed off).

title: Generated PlantUML and Mermaid is invalid for common inputs, and nothing validates it
evidence: The Mermaid DFG emits `v2_0["...join: Block 2"]"]` with a stray `"]`, and the shipped dfg.mmd contains it. PlantUML activity prints `if (eval_branch) then (yes)` for each decision node but never `endif`, then closes the partition `}` while the if is still open. Mermaid places relations inside `namespace {}` blocks (at the package LCA) and nests namespaces, but namespace bodies accept only class statements and nesting needs Mermaid 11.15 or later. The PlantUML sequence declares `act_ExternalActor` but sends messages from an undeclared `part_Actor`; the shipped sample shows both lifelines. Mermaid flowchart ids are raw lifeline names, so a name like `end` breaks parsing.
impact: Typical code triggers render errors: any method with an if, and any relation between classes in the same package. The Mermaid DFG never renders at all.
recommendation: Print from a typed IR with per-format printers that emit structured blocks (if/else/endif from region analysis), keep relations outside namespaces, and alias every id (`P1`, `C_1234`) with quoted labels. In CI, parse every fixture output with `plantuml -checkonly` and `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (mmdc) or mermaid.parse, and fail on any error. Done means zero parse errors across the fixtures and examples/.

SCPGX.note: Stray quote gone; activity/CFG printed as state-notation graphs (no unterminated if); Mermaid relations outside namespaces, no nested namespaces; actor declared and used under one alias; all ids prefixed aliases (never 'end'); labels escaped per format. CI parse checks are test work (skipped).

title: .scpg loader never verifies CRC or version and panics or aborts on corrupt or hostile files
evidence: The writer uses a bitwise CRC-32/IEEE (0xEDB88320), not the CRC-64 the README claims. `open` reads the CRC and `format_version` but checks neither. `section_count` comes straight from the file into `Vec::with_capacity`: 0xFFFFFFFF asks for about 103 GB and aborts, and count 12 on a 392-byte file panics on an out-of-range slice. `get_section` computes `start + byte_length` unchecked, so it can wrap and then panic on slicing. There is no header checksum, duplicate sections are accepted, and `fs::write` is not atomic. `inspect` prints "SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY" without verifying anything.
impact: Truncated, corrupted or version-skewed files are silently accepted or crash the process. A 392-byte crafted file kills the CLI.
recommendation: Validate before allocating: magic, a known major version, section_count up to a fixed maximum, checked_add offsets that stay inside the file, and unique, non-overlapping sections. Verify a header CRC and a per-section CRC-64/NVME or xxh3 checksum (crc64fast or xxhash-rust) lazily, and return Err on mismatch. Write via temp file, fsync and rename. Add a cargo-fuzz target for open. Done means a clean fuzz run of 24 hours and corruption tests that return Err.

DOCS.note: phase10 checklist no longer ticks CRC verification; security doc lists the unverified loader behaviour; loader hardening handed off

SRV.note: inspect contains loader panics and reports the .scpg checksum as NOT VERIFIED instead of 'PRODUCTION READY'. Loader validation is in scpg/, outside my paths

SCPG.note: Loader validates magic/major version/section_count<=64/header+directory CRC-64/NVME/file length/codec/alignment/checked bounds/uniqueness/overlap before allocating; lazy cached per-section CRC; verify_all checks SHA-256 digest; writes go through core::io::fs::write_atomic. Fuzz target skipped (tests); inspect wording handed off.

title: 'Backward/forward slice' is a caller and parent-symbol closure that ignores SSA/CDG and drops nodes under the depth limit
evidence: The doc says the slice works "via CDG + def-use CSR", but `_ssa` is unused. The walk adds callers from `site_to_edge_map` plus `parent_sym` (class, then package), so it returns symbols, not statements. Each FunctionSSAData already holds `def_use: DefUseCSR` and `cdg: CDGCSR`. The depth-limited DFS marks a node visited the first time it is reached, even via a deep path. A Python port with edges X→R, Y→R, X→Y, Z→X and depth 2 returns {R,X,Y} and misses Z, which is 2 hops away. Each expansion also scans every edge, giving O(V·E).
impact: Because data and control dependences are ignored, the results are not slices. Users doing impact analysis or debugging get wrong sets that also vary with the depth limit.
recommendation: Build an SDG: a PDG per method from DefUseCSR and CDGCSR, call and parameter-in/out edges, and heap edges from points-to. Implement Horwitz-Reps-Binkley two-phase slicing with summary edges (Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv-Rosay 1994), and offer thin slicing (Sridharan-Fink-Bodík, PLDI'07). Enforce the depth limit with a BFS that keeps each node's best depth. Done means statement-level slices that match WALA or Joern on Defects4J fixtures.

SCPG.note: New statement-level SDG (def-use with phi resolution, CDG control deps, call/param-out edges, actual-in nodes) and Horwitz-Reps-Binkley two-phase slicing, thin mode, best-depth BFS+Dijkstra. Heap edges not modelled (documented); backward_slice signature now takes &CFGArtifact (test handoff).

title: 'CFL-reachability' is plain call-graph reachability with an O(V·E) inner loop
evidence: The "cubic worklist tabulation" stores pairs `(source,u)` with a fixed source, which is just a BFS visited set. There are no call/return labels, summary edges or ICFG, so it cannot express realizable (matched-parenthesis) paths. For every dequeued node it scans the whole `site_to_edge_map`. A port on a 2,000-node chain made 3,998,000 edge visits, even though `callee_csr`, `caller_csr` and `edges_of()` already exist.
impact: The query is mislabeled, and its run time collapses on large codebases: about 1e9 edge scans at 15K methods and 60K edges. That contradicts the claim "sub-second for 15K methods".
recommendation: For method reachability, use CSR adjacency plus SCC condensation (the .cga already has Tarjan SCCs) and a reachability index: bitset closure for small graphs, GRAIL or pruned landmark labeling for large ones. For true CFL reachability, implement IFDS tabulation (Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv) or Dyck reachability (Reps 1998) over the ICFG with summary edges. Done means criterion benchmarks on 100K-edge graphs, cross-checked against a Soufflé reference.

CORE.note: src/scpg/query; outside my paths.

DOCS.note: phase10.md and uml_derivation state cfl.rs is BFS with an O(V*E) loop and how real CFL reachability would be built; code handed off

SCPG.note: CallGraphIndex: CSR adjacency, iterative Tarjan condensation, bitset closure (<=4096 SCCs) or 3-label GRAIL + pruned DFS; is_reachable/call_path/transitive BFS. True CFL (Dyck) dependence reachability via CFLReachability::flows_to over the SDG.

title: Incremental engine is a stub, and its hash update undoes itself, so cached results can go stale
evidence: `SourceDelta` holds only a file_id and three booleans the caller asserts; there is no byte range or text. `classify` tests comment-only first, so a delta flagged both body-only and type-changed is classified as Behavioral. `apply_delta` rebuilds nothing, always returns `stale_link_count: 0`, and sets `new_scpg_hash = current_hash ^ 0x0101_0101`. Two deltas restore the original hash (port: 83D2D2B2 → 82D3D3B3 → 83D2D2B2), and that hash is the key the cache uses to decide validity. Nothing calls this code.
impact: The documented 'O(|delta|), 80-200 ms' updates do not exist. If this code were wired in as is, alternating edits would serve stale reachability and slice results.
recommendation: Derive deltas from tree-sitter incremental parsing (Tree::edit plus changed_ranges) and an AST diff (GumTree). Track per-file content hashes and phase dependencies in a demand-driven engine (salsa-style red/green as in rust-analyzer; compare Glean stacked DBs and CodeQL overlay databases). Version snapshots with strong digests. Done means an edit-replay benchmark proving incremental results equal a clean rebuild.

DOCS.note: phase10 §10.6.2 documents the XOR stub and the hash self-cancellation; checklist marks incremental not implemented; code handed off

SCPG.note: SourceDelta derived from real old/new text (TextEdit -> tree_sitter::InputEdit); ordered RebuildScope fixes the classify bug; token/comment-aware classifier; commit diffs stable-id fingerprints and the new hash is the content digest (no XOR). Actual partial phase re-execution lives in pipeline/ingestion (handoff).

title: XMI export is a placeholder: class shells with numbered names and obsolete namespaces, unreachable from CLI and server
evidence: The output is `<uml:Model xmi:version="2.1" xmlns:xmi="http://schema.omg.org/spec/XMI/2.1" xmlns:uml="http://www.eclipse.org/uml2/3.0.0/UML">` with one `<packagedElement xmi:type="uml:Class" xmi:id="sym_N" name="Class_N"/>` per class. It has no real names, packages, attributes, operations, generalizations, realizations or associations, and the Model itself has no xmi:id. `XMIFactory` ignores the diagram type. The CLI and server write only .puml, .mmd and .json files.

Include nested packages, ownedAttribute with type refs, multiplicity and aggregation, ownedOperation/ownedParameter, generalization, interfaceRealization and Association memberEnds, with stable FQN-hash ids. CLI/server/api wiring is outside (handoff).

title: Phase 10 tests are tautological, and the published diagram gallery is hand-edited rather than generated
evidence: The tests assert `is_reach || !is_reach` and `to_src.is_some() || to_src.is_none()`, and the slice assertion is always true. The only nested-package test is `#[ignore]` and expects output the code cannot emit. Other tests only check prefixes or the absence of "SystemNode". Commit c27884d ("100% diagram suite perfection") changed 26 web/diagrams files and no src files. The exporters cannot produce statemachine.puml (Idle→LexicalIngestion) or cfg.json (hash 0x6FE2910B). /api/analyze also overwrites web/diagrams in place.
impact: Regressions and fabricated output go undetected, and the public gallery misrepresents what the tool actually produces.
recommendation: Add insta snapshot tests for each diagram type and format, CI syntax checks (PlantUML -checkonly, mmdc, XMI import), proptest round-trips for .scpg, and cargo-fuzz targets for the loaders. Add query oracles that compare against Soufflé or WALA, plus criterion benchmarks on a fixed corpus. Regenerate the gallery in CI from a pinned sample repository. Done means the gallery is byte-identical to CI output.

title: Diagram and .scpg output differ from run to run
evidence: The JSON class and package diagrams iterate a HashMap or HashSet with RandomState when emitting nodes, edges and sequential `edge_{n}` ids, so ids and order change per process. Mermaid inserts nested packages from a HashSet and sorts only the root's children; `sort_children_and_edges` is never called. Call-graph views chain nodes in `HashSet::into_iter` order. The .scpg header embeds `creation_ts_ns`.
impact: Diffs are noisy, web layouts shift, and golden tests and content-addressed caching are impossible. This contradicts the README's 'deterministically derives' claim.
recommendation: Use BTreeMap or IndexMap, or sort by stable keys (FQN, sym_id) before emitting. Derive edge ids by hashing (src, kind, dst). Call the recursive sort. Keep timestamps out of hashed bytes and honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Done means a test that runs each exporter in two separate processes and asserts byte-equal output.

DOCS.note: Determinism claims withdrawn; phase10 notes creation_ts_ns and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; code handed off

SCPGX.note: Exporter output is deterministic: BTreeMap registries, sorted nodes/edges, edge ids = hash(source, kind, target, discriminator), no HashSet-order emission, timestamp-free digests. The .scpg header timestamp lives in src/scpg/serializer (outside).

SCPG.note: The .scpg content digest excludes the timestamp, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is honored, and all section encodings are sorted and deterministic. HashMap-order fixes in the diagram exporters are outside my paths (handoff).

title: Query cache flushes everything when full, uses a weak 32-bit XOR key, and sits behind one global Mutex
evidence: The 'LRU' cache clears every entry when full. Its scpg_hash key XORs nine values. One of them is a token count, and `ssa.cfa_hash` and `psa.cfa_hash` are both `crc64_ecma(cfa_bytes)`, so they cancel out; the result is folded to 32 bits. TRA stamps links with a different scpg_hash formula. Results are cached by the engine's hash, but artifacts arrive with each call. All queries are serialized by `Arc<Mutex>`, and a poisoned lock silently returns false. EngineBuilder's options are never used and it has no build().
impact: Stale or colliding cache hits are possible, links cannot be checked against the engine's hash, and server queries cannot run concurrently.
recommendation: Key snapshots with a SHA-256 or BLAKE3 digest of the canonical section bytes (sha2 is already a dependency), store it in the header's empty source_hash, and share one hash definition with TRA. Use moka or lru over immutable Arc snapshots so reads need no Mutex. Return Result on a poisoned lock and implement build(). Done means a concurrency benchmark and a collision property test.

BDD.note: One shared SHA-256 hash definition (tra::uml_link::digest) and a 256-bit chain_digest for cache keys; the scpg cache, Mutex and EngineBuilder are outside my paths.

SCPG.note: QueryKey carries kind + exact params + 32-byte SHA-256 digest; 16-shard true LRU (O(1), evicts one entry); queries run on the immutable Arc snapshot without a global Mutex; a poisoned shard is cleared and reused; EngineBuilder options now take effect and it has open() and build(). TRA's separate hash is a handoff.

title: Impact, navigation and ROBDD queries miss their stated semantics and complexity
evidence: `impact_set` promises "callers, overrides, and dependents" but ignores `_sta` and follows only reverse call edges, scanning every edge per node. `to_source` is documented as O(1) but is `uml_links.iter().find`. `from_source` is documented as O(log n) but is a linear filter that returns every overlapping link instead of the innermost one. TRA's dense `bi_sym` and `sym_span` arrays go unused. `path_count` and `cyclomatic` return 1 for unknown symbols. No CLI command or HTTP route exposes any of these queries.
impact: Change impact is under-reported when virtual dispatch is involved, every navigation lookup is O(n), and unknown symbols report fake metrics.
recommendation: Compute impact as reverse reachability over call, override (CHA/RTA), field read/write and type-reference edges, or use Chianti-style atomic changes. Navigate with `bi_sym[sym_id]` plus an interval tree or binary search over sorted spans that returns the innermost entity. Return Option for unknown ids, and expose the queries through the CLI and an HTTP or LSP API. Done means tests for override-aware impact and benchmarks that confirm the stated complexity.

BDD.note: TRA accessors added: uml_link, source_range, innermost_symbol_at, symbols_at, function_blocks, function_ssa. Impact and navigation rewrites in scpg are handed off.

SRV.note: Query semantics and their exposure through the CLI or HTTP depend on scpg/query, outside my paths

SCPG.note: Impact covers callers, overridden/overriding methods, subtypes, type references and declaring-type members, with reasons and depth; navigation O(1)/O(log n) innermost-first; path_count/cyclomatic return Option. CLI/HTTP exposure is a handoff.

title: No large-graph strategy: arbitrary first-N truncation and single giant diagrams that exceed renderer limits
evidence: Views silently keep the first N UMA records: `take(6)` classes × `take(3)` methods for use cases, `take(6)` activities, `take(2)` for ROBDD, `take(12)` objects. The shipped robdd.mmd and callgraph.mmd are empty because the first classes are enums. The sequence exporter puts every scenario in one diagram. The shipped sequence.puml is 110 KB with 699 calls and 699 returns, well beyond PlantUML's default 4096 px limit. Mermaid's maxTextSize (50,000) and maxEdges (500) defaults are ignored.
impact: On real repositories, diagrams come out arbitrarily partial, empty or cropped, or the renderer refuses them.
recommendation: Add view scoping (focus symbol, package or entry method plus a depth), deterministic size budgets with degree or PageRank ranking, package collapsing or Louvain clustering, one diagram per scenario with `newpage`, renderer-limit checks, and the ELK layout. Done means the examples/ projects produce bounded, renderable diagrams along with a list of omitted elements.

SCPGX.note: Added ViewOptions focus scoping, node/edge budgets with degree ranking, whole-function budgets, omitted-element lists in legends/metadata, per-scenario pages with message budget, Mermaid maxTextSize/maxEdges handling and package collapsing via the optimizer; Louvain clustering and ELK layout not implemented.

title: The three exporters are divergent re-implementations; shared helpers and the edge optimizer are dead or buggy
evidence: There are four copies of sanitize, resolve_name and is_primitive, each with different rules. Mermaid drops any user class named `Entity` or `args`, PlantUML drops one named `Class`, and DiagramUtils is never called. PlantUML builds edges from fields and keeps one edge per class pair, so a realization overwrites a decorator's has-a link. Mermaid uses `association_syms` and draws nesting as `*--`. PlantUMLOptimizer is never called, ignores its thresholds, and drops an inheritance edge whenever the same pair also has a cross-package association (confirmed with a port). JSON silently falls back to a class diagram for unknown types.
impact: The same model renders differently in each format, every fix has to be made three or four times, and the dead code advertises behavior that would be wrong if it were enabled.
recommendation: Build one typed IR per view (stable ids, typed members, edge kinds, spans) and implement PlantUML, Mermaid, XMI and JSON as printers that visit it. Keep one set of filter rules keyed by resolved type rather than by name. Fix the optimizer so it honors thresholds and never suppresses generalization, or delete it. Return None for unknown diagram types. Done means a cross-format test that asserts identical node and edge sets.

SCPGX.note: One typed IR per view with stable ids, typed members, edge kinds, spans; PlantUML/Mermaid/JSON/XMI/DOT/GraphML are printers over it; single filter rule (declared-symbol membership); optimizer now honors thresholds, never suppresses generalization and is wired for large class diagrams; unknown JSON types return None.

title: Class-diagram detail falls far short of UML reverse-engineering tools
evidence: Methods print as `name() : Ret` with no parameters (UMA stores only param_count), so overloads show up as identical lines. Each type is reduced to a single symbol name, so generics, arrays and nullability disappear. Static and abstract markers, multiplicities and role names are missing. Composition is inferred from the `final` modifier. JSON marks a field as aggregation whenever its type name contains "List", "Set" or "Array", which catches names like `Settings` and `Listener`. Mermaid prints fields as `+name Type`.
impact: The diagrams lack the detail users expect from IntelliJ UML or Papyrus reverse engineering, and some relationship kinds are wrong.
recommendation: Extend the UMA model and the IR with full signatures (parameter names and types, type arguments, array and nullable flags, modifiers). Render them with PlantUML `{static}`/`{abstract}` and quoted generic labels, and with Mermaid `~T~` generics. Derive aggregation and multiplicity from resolved Collection subtypes, and use composition only for owned lifecycles. Done means fixture parity with a reference generator such as the PlantUML Maven or Gradle plugins.

SCPGX.note: Members now show parameter names/types, return types, {static}/{abstract} (PlantUML) and $/* (Mermaid), multiplicities, role names and collection element types (Mermaid ~T~); aggregation/composition only from UMA assoc kinds. Full generic type arguments need a Phase 3 TypeRef (handoff).

UML.note: UMA now carries parameter syms and types, u16 modifiers, multiplicities, element types and association kinds; exporter rendering is handed off.

title: No standard interop or query surface (SCIP/LSIF, a query language, LSP) and no stable symbol ids
evidence: QueryEngine offers just two hard-coded Rust calls, reachability and backward slice, and the u8 `query_type` field is not extensible. The CLI has only analyze, inspect, server and help. The LSPBridge, FileWatcher and didChange-to-SourceDelta pieces described in the docs do not exist. Entities are positional u32 sym_ids that change between builds, so cross-build diffs and external links are impossible.
impact: OpenHeart cannot plug into Sourcegraph, IDEs or CI, and users cannot write their own analyses. Joern (CPGQL), CodeQL (QL), Glean (Angle) and Kythe/SCIP all support this.
recommendation: Assign stable SCIP-style symbol strings or Kythe VNames, and export SCIP using the scip crate. Add a query layer, for example Datalog via ascent or crepe, a Trustfall adapter, or a Gremlin-like DSL. Add a tower-lsp server for definition, references and hover backed by TRA. Done means `scip lint` passes and an LSP smoke test works in VS Code.

DOCS.note: ROADMAP interop item (SCIP ids, query language, LSP) added; phase10 checklist marks LSP and FileWatcher absent; code handed off

SRV.note: SCIP, query layer, LSP and stable ids belong to scpg and tra, outside my paths

SCPG.note: Every symbol has a SCIP-syntax stable id (scheme, escaped descriptors, arity/ordinal disambiguators) with lookups by stable id/FQN/name, plus the Datalog query layer. SCIP protobuf export and an LSP server are not implemented.

title: /api/source reads arbitrary files; basename walkdir fallback + CORS * enables cross-origin exfiltration
evidence: `decoded_path` is built from three `.replace` calls (%2F,%20,%2B) then used verbatim as the first read candidate: `direct_candidates = [decoded_path.as_str(), ...]` and `fs::read_to_string(candidate)` (server.rs:119-205). So `GET /api/source?file=/etc/passwd` or `?file=../../../../etc/passwd` returns file contents. If that misses, `walkdir_find` returns the first file matching the basename anywhere under examples/target_repos/web (:207-224). Responses carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (:327), so any website's JS can read a developer's local files cross-origin.
impact: Full unauthenticated read of any file the server user can access (SSH keys, .env, source), locally and cross-origin from any browser tab, on the default 0.0.0.0 bind.
recommendation: Treat file params as untrusted: reject absolute paths and `..`, then `fs::canonicalize` and verify `starts_with` an allowed root, exactly as the static route at server.rs:254-286 already does. Remove the basename `walkdir_find` fallback (it defeats confinement). Replace ad-hoc `.replace` decoding with real percent-decoding (percent-encoding crate) and reject non-UTF8. Drop CORS `*` for an explicit localhost allowlist. Serve this through axum + tower-http ServeDir.

SRV.note: Real percent-decoding (invalid escapes, NUL and control characters rejected), canonicalize plus starts_with checks, no disk walk by basename, no ACAO *

title: /api/analyze clones an unvalidated URL: SSRF, git argument injection, arbitrary transports, path traversal; validate_url is dead code
evidence: `repo_url` is parsed from the body and passed straight to `Command::new("git").args(["clone","--depth","1",repo_url, &format!("./target_repos/{}",repo_name)])` (server.rs:429-437) with no scheme/host check. `repo_name` is the last `/`-segment (:393-398), so `..`/`.git` games escape target_repos. The URL may be `file:///…`, `ssh://`, `ext::sh -c …`, or start with `-` (git option injection, e.g. `--upload-pack`). `WebRepoFetcher::validate_url` (web_repo.rs:97) exists but is never called from the server. Clones are never cleaned up (no cleanup of ./target_repos on failure) and have no size/time bound.
impact: Unauthenticated SSRF to internal hosts, local-file and arbitrary-transport cloning, potential command execution via git `ext::`/option injection, disk exhaustion, and directory traversal — from any origin on the default bind.
recommendation: Do not clone attacker URLs server-side by default; make it opt-in and sandboxed. Enforce an allowlist (https host == github.com), reject URLs beginning with `-` and any non-https scheme, and pass `--` before the URL. Run git with `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https`, `-c protocol.ext.allow=never`, a timeout, a disk quota (temp dir on a size-limited mount), and guaranteed cleanup. Wire the (fixed) validate_url in before any clone. Consider gitoxide (gix) to avoid shelling out entirely.

SRV.note: parse_repo_url is wired in (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>[/tree/<ref>/<path>] only). git runs with '--' before the URL, protocol.allow=never plus https only, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https, no prompts or credential helpers, core.symlinks=false, a timeout and a size cap. Clones go to a scratch dir that is renamed into place. Cache keys are sanitized owner/repo/ref, and a cached checkout's origin is verified before reuse

title: Docker default command invokes a 'serve' subcommand the CLI does not implement; container exits immediately
evidence: Dockerfile ends with `CMD ["openheart", "serve", "--port", "8080"]`. main.rs only matches `analyze|inspect|server|help`; any other first arg hits the `unknown =>` arm which prints usage and `std::process::exit(1)` (main.rs:544-548). So the documented container fails on startup. Even with `server`, the port is positional (`args[2].parse::<u16>()`, main.rs:533-536), so `--port 8080` would parse-fail and silently fall back to 8080, and a real `--port 9000` would be ignored.
impact: The primary advertised deployment (Docker) never starts the server at all; anyone running the image gets an immediate exit(1). The Dockerfile/CLI contract is inconsistent.
recommendation: Align the CLI and container: add a real `serve`/`server` subcommand parsed by clap with a `--port`/`-p` option and env fallback, then set `CMD ["openheart","server","8080"]` (or the clap form). Add a CI smoke test that builds the image and curls `/api/health` so this cannot regress.

SRV.note: Docker CMD is 'openheart server'. A 'serve' alias and '--port/-p' were added; a bad port is now a usage error (exit 2) instead of a silent fallback to 8080

title: Single-threaded serial accept loop runs the full 10-phase pipeline (and a network clone) per request with no limits
evidence: `for mut stream in listener.incoming().flatten() { Self::handle_connection(&mut stream); }` (server.rs:40-42) handles connections serially on one thread. A POST /api/analyze synchronously runs ingestion→…→UML export (server.rs:505-699) plus a `git clone` over the network. There is no thread pool, no request queue bound, no per-request CPU/time budget, and no body-size cap.
impact: A single in-flight analyze request blocks every other client for the full pipeline duration; one unauthenticated request against a large repo is a trivial denial of service for the whole server.
recommendation: Move to an async runtime (tokio) with axum/hyper; offload the CPU-heavy pipeline to a bounded `spawn_blocking`/rayon pool, cap concurrent analyses (tower `ConcurrencyLimit`/semaphore), and add tower-http `TimeoutLayer` and `RequestBodyLimitLayer`. Return 429/503 when saturated rather than head-of-line blocking.

SRV.note: Bounded worker pool with 503 when the queue is full, an analysis semaphore with 503 and Retry-After, a per-request read deadline, a body cap, a 504 analysis budget and async jobs. Std-only (no tokio)

title: Binds 0.0.0.0 with CORS * and no authentication or CSRF protection
evidence: `let addr = format!("0.0.0.0:{}", self.port)` (server.rs:32) exposes the server on all interfaces. OPTIONS replies `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with methods GET/POST (server.rs:72) and every JSON response sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *` (:327). There is no auth token, no Origin check, and no CSRF defense on the state-changing POST /api/analyze.
impact: Any web page a developer visits can script the local server: trigger clones, run analysis, and read local files via /api/source, with responses readable cross-origin. On a shared network the whole API is exposed to the LAN.
recommendation: Default-bind 127.0.0.1 (make the interface an explicit, documented flag). Replace CORS `*` with an allowlist of expected origins and drop wildcard allow-headers. Require a local auth token (printed at startup) for mutating/file-reading endpoints, following tower-http CorsLayer and OWASP ASVS V13 API guidance.

SRV.note: Loopback by default. Host validation blocks DNS rebinding, Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks reject cross-site requests (CSRF), and CORS is allowlist-only. Optional bearer/cookie token, mandatory on non-loopback binds. Analyze requires a JSON content type

title: Non-compliant HTTP parsing: Content-Length ignored, body is one 8 KiB read gated on a substring, 500 ms timeout truncates, HEAD returns a body
evidence: Request reading is a single `[0u8;8192]` read with a 500 ms timeout (server.rs:47-52); larger or slower requests are truncated or dropped. The body is parsed by splitting on the first blank line and taking the remainder (extract_body, :292-300), Content-Length is never consulted, and only one extra 4 KiB read happens, conditioned on the raw request not already containing the substring `"repo_url"` (:242-250). HEAD is treated as GET (`is_get_or_head`, :69) and `serve_file` writes the file body for HEAD (:302-312), violating RFC 9110. Keep-alive/chunked are unsupported.
impact: Legitimate requests with headers pushing the body past 8 KiB, bodies split across TCP segments, or a field ordering where `repo_url` appears late are silently mis-parsed, producing wrong or failed analyses; HEAD responses are malformed.
recommendation: Stop hand-rolling HTTP. Use hyper/axum, which parse Content-Length/transfer-encoding, framing, and HEAD correctly. If a minimal server must remain, read until Content-Length bytes are consumed with a configurable total timeout and a max-body guard, and send HEAD responses with headers only.

SRV.note: New http.rs: Content-Length framing with a body cap and a deadline across all reads, 100-continue, 501 for Transfer-Encoding, conflicting lengths rejected, HEAD sends headers only, no Content-Length on 204/304, a Date header

title: Silent fallback analyzes the first directory in ./target_repos, returning a different repo's results as success
evidence: On clone failure the code only logs (server.rs:446-459) and continues. If the derived `repo_dir` still does not exist, it iterates `./target_repos` and picks the first directory: `target_dir = entry.path(); logs.push("Using fallback local repository path…")` (:467-482), then analyzes that tree and returns `status":"success"`. The substituted repository is reported only as a log line the UI treats as progress text.
impact: When a clone fails (network, bad URL, auth), the server silently analyzes an unrelated cached repository and labels it success, so users receive diagrams/metrics for a codebase they never requested — silently wrong results.
recommendation: Remove the first-directory fallback. On clone failure or missing target, return a structured error (`status":"error"`) with the git stderr and an HTTP 4xx/5xx; never substitute a different repository. Key cached clones by a sanitized owner/repo and verify the resolved path matches the requested URL before analysis.

SRV.note: First-directory fallback removed. Clone or lookup failures return structured errors with 4xx/5xx statuses, and the cache is keyed by owner/repo/ref with origin verification

title: validate_url panics on index [1] for URLs without a repo segment, and is never called on the clone path
evidence: After stripping the host prefix, `let parts: Vec<&str> = …split('/').collect();` then `let repo = parts[1]…` (web_repo.rs:111-112) indexes position 1 unconditionally. Input `https://github.com/owner` (no trailing repo) yields a one-element vector, so `parts[1]` panics with index-out-of-bounds. The only tests cover well-formed URLs (:126-139). This function is also dead code relative to the actual clone in server.rs, which does its own unchecked parsing.
impact: If this validator is ever wired into the request path (its stated purpose) it panics the thread on a common malformed URL; today it gives a false sense of input validation while the clone path has none.
recommendation: Use `parts.get(0)`/`parts.get(1)` with explicit `Err` on missing segments, reject empty/`..`/control characters, and return the normalized owner/repo. Add tests for host-only, trailing-slash, `-`-prefixed, and non-github URLs. Then actually call it before every clone (ties to SRV-02).

SRV.note: Panic removed, validator is called before every clone, and malformed URLs get explicit errors

title: Artifact deserializers slice fixed header offsets after only a minimal length check, panicking on truncated-but-magic-valid files
evidence: `inspect` dispatches on magic then calls sub-deserializers. Readers validate only a coarse minimum length (e.g. `bytes.len() < UMA_HEADER_SIZE + 8`, uma/serializer.rs:230) or `buf.len() < 96` (tra:114) and then index many fixed ranges via `try_into().unwrap()` and derive counts used to slice payloads. A file with a valid magic/CRC-consistent prefix but a truncated or oversized declared count can panic on slice-out-of-range during body parsing. No `catch_unwind` guards these.
impact: `openheart inspect` on a crafted or corrupted artifact can panic instead of returning the intended 'corrupted artifact' error; the same parsers are reachable from the engine open path.
recommendation: Bounds-check every read against remaining length and return `io::Error` on shortfall (consider a small cursor helper or the `zerocopy`/`bytes` crates). Validate declared element counts against remaining bytes before allocating/slicing. Add fuzz targets (cargo-fuzz) for each `.tca/.bpa/.sta/.cfa/.ssa/.cga/.tra/.psa/.uma/.scpg` reader.

BDD.note: TRA (and PSA) deserializers are bounds-checked, verify the CRC before trusting counts, and return InvalidData instead of panicking; main.rs and uma are handed off.

SRV.note: inspect contains reader panics and returns a corrupted-artifact error. Hardening the readers is outside my paths

UML.note: The uma reader validates all lengths and counts and returns InvalidData; the tra/other readers are outside src/uma.

title: Hand-rolled CLI: silent flag dropping, positional-only port, no --version, subcommand name drift
evidence: Argument handling is manual `Vec<String>` matching (main.rs:490-549). Verbosity flags are `retain`-filtered anywhere in argv but any other `--flag` is ignored or misread as a positional. `server` takes a positional port (`args[2].parse::<u16>().unwrap_or(8080)`, :533-536), so `--port` is unsupported (conflicting with the Dockerfile) and a bad port silently becomes 8080. There is no `--version`, no `--help` for subcommands, and exit codes are inconsistent (help prints usage/ok; missing args print usage then exit 1).
impact: Confusing, error-prone CLI that silently ignores or misinterprets options; mismatched with the container command and with Rust CLI norms, undermining benchmark-grade polish.
recommendation: Adopt clap (derive API) with real subcommands (`analyze`, `inspect`, `server`), typed `--port`/`-p` with env fallback, `--verbose`/`--trace` as global flags, auto `--help`/`--version` (from CARGO_PKG_VERSION), and documented exit codes. Follows the Rust CLI Book / clap conventions.

SRV.note: Strict CLI parser: --port/-p, --host, env fallback, --version/version, 'serve' alias, per-subcommand options, unknown options rejected, exit codes 0/1/2. clap was not added because the one-dependency budget went to 'ignore'

title: Docker image is unhardened: root user, no healthcheck, build errors swallowed, no .dockerignore, base-image/version drift
evidence: Runtime stage `FROM debian:bookworm-slim` runs with no `USER` (root) and no `HEALTHCHECK`. The dependency-cache layer uses `cargo build --release || true` (Dockerfile:16), hiding real build failures. There is no .dockerignore (confirmed absent), so `COPY src`/`COPY tests` pull in whatever is present and the build context is unbounded. Builder is `rust:1.80-slim` while README/getting_started claim support for Rust 1.75+. `git` is installed in the runtime image to enable the SSRF-prone clone (SRV-02).
impact: Larger attack surface and image size, no container liveness signal, masked build breakage, and an unverified MSRV claim — below distroless/non-root container-hardening norms.
recommendation: Add a non-root `USER`, a `HEALTHCHECK` curling `/api/health`, and a read-only root FS with a writable tmpfs for clones. Remove `|| true` (use proper dependency caching via cargo-chef). Add a .dockerignore (target/, .git/, web/diagrams outputs). Move to a distroless or `gcr.io/distroless/cc` runtime; drop `git` unless server-side cloning is retained and sandboxed. Reconcile the base image with the documented MSRV (CI job pinned to 1.75).

SRV.note: Non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, no '|| true', crate roots touched so the placeholder build is never shipped, toolchain on bookworm to match the runtime, state under /var/lib/openheart (works with --read-only). No .dockerignore (outside my paths). Not distroless, because git is needed for cloning

title: No security headers on server responses; Pages app loads CDN scripts without SRI or CSP
evidence: `serve_file`/`respond_json` emit only Content-Type, Content-Length and CORS headers (server.rs:305-333) — no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, or `Referrer-Policy`. index.html pulls five third-party scripts (cytoscape, dagre, cytoscape-dagre, cytoscape-svg, jszip) from cdnjs/jsdelivr with no `integrity`/`crossorigin` attributes (index.html:29-34) and the page defines no CSP meta (confirmed none).
impact: MIME-sniffing and clickjacking exposure on the local server; on the public GitHub Pages studio, a compromised or MITM'd CDN can execute arbitrary JS in users' browsers with no subresource-integrity backstop.
recommendation: Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive CSP to all server responses (tower-http `SetResponseHeaderLayer`). On the web app, pin each CDN `<script>` with an `integrity="sha384-…"` SRI hash and `crossorigin="anonymous"`, or vendor the libraries locally, and add a `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` restricting script/connect sources (allowing api.github.com and kroki.io).

SRV.note: Every server response carries nosniff, a CSP (strict for data, scoped for studio HTML), X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and CORP. SRI and a CSP meta tag in web/index.html are a handoff

title: Duplicated pipeline orchestration; server omits Phase 10 yet reports 'All 10 phases verified' and writes into the live served web/diagrams
evidence: `process_analyze_request` re-implements the pipeline that `cmd_analyze` already contains (main.rs:101-345), but runs only Phases 1–9 (no Phase10Stage call anywhere in server.rs) while logging `"Pipeline complete… All 10 phases verified."` (server.rs:696-699). It also writes every diagram into `web/diagrams` (`Path::new("web").join("diagrams")`, :636-691) — the directory the server serves to all clients — with no per-request isolation, then deletes only its temp dir (:693).
impact: Two divergent orchestrations drift out of sync; the server's own success message is false (Phase 10 never runs); concurrent or sequential requests overwrite shared web/diagrams, so one user's analysis is served to another and results race.
recommendation: Extract a single `run_pipeline(files, out_dir) -> Artifacts` used by both CLI and server, returning in-memory results. Write per-request outputs to a unique temp/session directory and stream them in the response instead of mutating the shared web/diagrams tree. Make the server's phase log reflect what actually executed.

SRV.note: One shared runner (adapters/runner.rs) serves the CLI and the server and runs all 10 phases. Server output goes to per-session dirs served through a session cookie, and web/diagrams is never written. Logs report the phases that actually ran

title: Security/config docs describe controls the code does not implement (env knobs, forbid(unsafe_code), module paths, supported versions)
evidence: security-architecture.md states env vars `OPENHEART_MAX_MEMORY_MB`, `OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENHEART_ARTIFACT_DIR` are 'managed via .env with safe fallback defaults' and that ingestion modules carry `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. grep finds no code reading those vars (logger reads only `OPENHEART_LOG`, logger.rs:98; .env.example advertises `RUST_LOG`, which is unused), `forbid(unsafe_code)` appears in no source file, and the cited `src/phase1/parser/tree_sitter.rs` path does not exist (it is src/ingestion/parser/…). SECURITY.md lists supported versions 1.0.x/1.1.x though the crate is 0.1.0.
impact: The advertised memory cap (a DoS mitigation) and unsafe-code guarantee are fictional, and the version-support table is false — misleading for a project positioned as benchmark-grade and auditable.
recommendation: Either implement the knobs (read and enforce OPENHEART_MAX_MEMORY_MB as a real cap, honor OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS/ARTIFACT_DIR, support RUST_LOG) or delete them from docs and .env.example. Add `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` to the modules that truly contain none, fix the module paths, and correct SECURITY.md to the versions that exist. Add a doc-lint/test asserting every documented env var is referenced in code.

CORE.note: Logger honors RUST_LOG fallback, OPENHEART_FILE_LOG, OPENHEART_LOG_MAX_BYTES; ingestion/AST honor OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS; builder honors OPENHEART_ARTIFACT_DIR; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] on ingestion and ast; docs outside.

DOCS.note: security-architecture rewritten with config tied to code, correct module paths and no forbid claim; SECURITY.md versions fixed; status.md §8 lists the variables read; .env.example handed off

SRV.note: .env.example lists only variables the code reads, now including the logger's, OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Added forbid(unsafe_code) to main.rs and the adapter modules. SECURITY.md and security-architecture.md are a handoff

title: No automated tests or lint/audit gates for the server, CLI, or clone adapter; release ships a .rlib, not the binary
evidence: CI runs only `cargo check`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo test` (ci.yml:40-47) — no clippy, no cargo-audit/deny, and no MSRV (1.75) job despite the claim. The server/CLI behavioral tests live in Python scripts (scripts/test_*.py) that are not invoked by CI. The release workflow uploads `target/release/libopenheart.rlib` (release.yml:26), a library artifact users cannot run, instead of the `openheart` binary, and builds no cross-platform artifacts.
impact: The security- and robustness-critical surface (HTTP parsing, path handling, clone adapter, CLI dispatch) has no regression safety net, and published releases are not usable binaries — both block benchmark-grade status.
recommendation: Add Rust integration tests driving the server over a socket (spawn on :0, assert health, 404s, traversal rejection, malformed-body handling) and CLI tests via `assert_cmd`. Gate CI on `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo audit`/`cargo deny`, and a pinned-1.75 MSRV job, and run the Python suite. Fix release.yml to build and upload the `openheart` binary per-OS (and the Docker image), not the .rlib.

title: Server leaks internal filesystem paths and raw git stderr to clients and stdout
evidence: `serve_file` prints `"[SERVER ERROR] Failed to read file '{}': {}"` with the path to stdout (server.rs:313-314). Analyze logs — returned to the client in the JSON `logs` array — include raw `git clone` stderr (:446-451), the server-side absolute/relative target path via `target_dir.display()` (:474-502), and the requested `repo_url`. `[SERVER] Backend analyzing repository: {url}` is printed to stdout (:384).
impact: Internal directory layout, cached repository names belonging to other analyses, and git error detail are disclosed to unauthenticated callers, aiding reconnaissance for the traversal/SSRF issues above.
recommendation: Return generic client-facing errors and move diagnostic detail to server-side logs only. Strip filesystem paths and raw subprocess stderr from the `logs`/`errors` fields. Adopt a structured logger (tracing) with levels so verbose diagnostics are opt-in and never serialized into API responses.

SRV.note: Clients get generic messages: no server paths, no git stderr, no raw phase errors. Details stay in server logs. Responses use repo-relative paths, and the generated token prints to stdout only

title: Cross-file type resolution does not work: import declarations never reach Pass 2 and same-package lookup is missing
evidence: The Java adapter has no arm for import_declaration, so `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129) discards it, and Drop returns None without visiting children (reducer.rs:17). Pass 2 therefore never fires. If imports did arrive, Pass 2 joins tokens with spaces (pass2:63), so `.*` never matches and simple names become ' List'. It also files every import under the module's declared-in scope, which is the global root (15-18). Pass 3 maps imported FQNs to new SK_EXTERNALs, never to project symbols (pass3:71-78). Same-package lookup, promised in phase3.md:429, does not exist, and wildcard_imports is never called.
impact: Every reference to a type declared in another file becomes an SK_EXTERNAL keyed by simple name. Exporters then re-match by simple name (plantuml.rs:443-477), which is wrong whenever simple names collide across packages.
recommendation: Emit package and import nodes from Phase 2. In Pass 1, build a global FQN→SymId index and one package scope shared by all compilation units of a package. Resolve per JLS 6.4.1 and 7.5: local and member types, then single-type imports, then same package, then on-demand imports, then java.lang; static imports for members. Encode this as scope-graph import edges with path ordering (Neron et al. 2015; Statix). Done when a 3-file, 2-package fixture with clashing simple names matches javac's bindings.

CORE.note: Phase 2 emits NN_PACKAGE_DECL / NN_IMPORT_DECL (AUX_IMPORT_STATIC / AUX_IMPORT_ON_DEMAND) with one qualified NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR child; Pass 2/3 resolution is a handoff.

DOCS.note: phase3.md annotated (imports dropped, no same-package lookup, JLS 6.4.1/7.5 order); status ledger row added; symbol code handed off

title: Declaration names come from token-window heuristics and are wrong for annotated members, every parameter and long class headers
evidence: Methods take the last identifier before the first '(' (pass1:696-745), and fields the last before the first '=' (748-791). Parameters fall through to the first identifier (793-889). The class keyword must appear within 15 tokens (645). The Annotation skip (703) never fires, because annotations are never leaf tokens (ingestion java.rs:69-70). A re-implementation (scratchpad sim_pass1.py) gives `@GetMapping("/x") ... getUser(` → GetMapping; `@GeneratedValue(strategy=..) Long id` → strategy; parameter `String name` → String; `final Long id` → final; `@Entity @Table(..) class User` → Entity; `@Import({A.class,B.class}) class Cfg` → B. A Spring/Lombok blocklist is hardcoded at 865-883.
impact: In Spring, JPA and JUnit 5 code, members and classes are named after annotations, and every parameter takes its first token's text as its name. Call graph, UML, traceability and resolution inherit these names, and the downstream 'Entity' blocklist hides real classes.
recommendation: Extract names structurally. In Phase 2, record in a side array the token of each declaration's tree-sitter `name` field (type declarations, methods, constructors), plus each variable_declarator and formal_parameter name; Pass 1 reads it. Emit one SK_FIELD or SK_LOCAL_VAR per declarator: java.rs:42 currently emits the declaration and its declarators, and `int a, b;` yields one field named b. Delete the hardcoded name lists. Done when golden name tests pass on Spring PetClinic and a JPA entity fixture.

CORE.note: New name-token side array (PreorderArrays.name_tokens, BPASTArtifact::name_token, persisted in .bpa v2) for every declaration, declarator, parameter, call; annotation-name identifiers typed Annotation in Phase 1; Pass 1 consumption is a handoff.

UML.note: The class_diagram name blacklist is deleted; naming declarations structurally has to happen in pass1/Phase 2 (handed off).

title: Scope lookup ignores symbol kind and Java scope rules: self references bind to constructors, parameter types bind to the parameter
evidence: resolve_lexical returns the first declaration of any kind whose name matches (resolver.rs:20-23; predicate at pass3:51-62). Constructors sit in the class scope, which is searched before the file scope holding the class. So with an explicit constructor, `static Singleton instance;` and `Node next;` bind to the SK_CONSTRUCTOR. Parameters carry their type's name (SYM-02) and live in the method scope, so in `f(Order order)` the parameter's type ref resolves to the parameter itself, and `Order` locals bind to it. Scopes open per declaration (pass1:185-189), never per block, for or catch (contrary to phase3.md:54-61).
impact: type_id is wrong for self-typed fields and returns (Singleton, Builder, Composite, linked nodes), for most reference-typed parameters, and for many locals. Pass 4/5 and the pattern heuristics read these wrong bindings.
recommendation: Make lookup kind-directed per JLS 6.5, as javac's Resolve does with KindSelector. Give each scope separate type, variable, method and package namespaces, and let type contexts see only type declarations and type parameters. Open scopes per JLS 6.3 (block, for, catch, lambda, switch rule), respect local declaration order, and index scopes as HashMap<(ns, name_id), SmallVec<SymId>>. Add tests for Singleton, a linked-list Node and `void f(Order o){Order p=o;}`.

DOCS.note: phase3.md scope section annotated with kind-agnostic lookup and missing block scopes, and the JLS 6.5 design; code handed off

title: Secondary token sweep fabricates classes and fields in pure Java and misplaces Kotlin members
evidence: The sweep runs for every language. Java `var` locals and identifiers named `val` create public SK_FIELDs on current_class_sym (414-453), which is never reset at class end or file change (257). Class literals, or variables named record or object, followed by a capitalized identifier create phantom SK_CLASS/SK_RECORD symbols in the root scope (396-407). On one Java test, sim_pass1.py produced TestConfig, ErrorCode and Mode plus fields order, result and compute. Only the first (file, name) pair gets a symbol (433). Kotlin depends entirely on this sweep: its AST falls back to the JS grammar (registry.rs:19-28), and ingestion uses the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:29-30).
impact: Java output gains fake classes and fields, and because they sit in the global root scope, any file's lookups can capture them. Kotlin members attach to the wrong class and never get types. Downstream ALL_CAPS filters only mask the problem.
recommendation: Disable the sweep for languages that have an AST adapter. Give Kotlin a real front end: the tree-sitter-kotlin grammar (fwcd) plus a KotlinSemanticAdapter covering primary-constructor properties, companion objects, extension receivers, top-level file facades, nullable types and typealiases. Alternatively ingest semanticdb-kotlinc output. Add a regression test asserting that Java fixtures produce no symbols without a decl_node other than externals and packages.

CORE.note: Kotlin now gets an accurate token stream from a real lexer instead of Java-grammar recovery; disabling the sweep for AST languages is a Pass 1 handoff.

UML.note: UMA excludes Java types that have no declaration node (sweep-fabricated); disabling the sweep in pass1 is handed off.

title: Containment tree corrupted: append_child re-links already-chained symbols and orphans are parented to the first file's module
evidence: append_child never unlinks a child from its previous sibling chain (builder.rs:83-96). Pass 1 re-appends top-level classes to their package while they stay in the module's chain (579-620). The safety sweep then parents every orphan, including the modules of files 2..N and the root packages, under symbol 0, the first file's module, to satisfy Invariant 2 (623-628). sim_chain.py on package com.a with File1 {A, B} and File2 {C} yields children(com.a) = [A, B, Module(File2), com]: C is lost, its own parent package appears as a child, and com's parent is Module(File1).
impact: Package class and subpackage counts, component interface counts and the pattern detectors' member lists are wrong even for a two-file project. The package tree is rooted under an arbitrary file's module.
recommendation: Treat parent_sym as the only source of truth. Finish all reparenting, then derive children once as CSR sorted by (parent, declaration order), and rebuild or drop first_child/next_sibling. Add a synthetic project root and real package roots instead of symbol 0. Turn Invariant 2 into a check that chains are acyclic and agree with parent_sym. Add multi-file, multi-package fixtures that assert exact child lists.

UML.note: All of UMA treats parent_sym as the only source of truth for containment; fixing the builder chains is handed off.

title: Type hierarchy comes from token scans: type arguments, bounds and Kotlin property types become supertypes
evidence: Phase 2 drops generic_type, so the AST path (40-74) misses `extends Base<T>`. The token path (76-157) treats every identifier after extends, implements or ':' up to '{' or ';' as a supertype. sim_pass5.py: `class OrderService extends BaseService<Order,OrderRepository> implements Auditable<User>` gives EXTENDS BaseService, Order and User, and class_diagram.rs:283-288 then reports User as the superclass. `class Repo<T extends BaseEntity>` gives EXTENDS BaseEntity. Kotlin `data class Invoice(val customer: Customer..)` gives EXTENDS Customer and scans on into the next declaration. Cross-file interfaces get TH_EXTENDS edges to SK_EXTERNALs (60-68), and interface-to-interface becomes TH_IMPLEMENTS (141-146).
impact: Generalization is wrong for generic base classes (Spring Data, generic services and DAOs) and for most Kotlin data classes. CHA dispatch follows the spurious edges, and sanitize_th_graph may delete correct edges to break the resulting cycles.
recommendation: Read supertypes only from tree-sitter fields: superclass, interfaces, extends_interfaces, permits, and Kotlin delegation_specifiers. Resolve the head of each generic_type and keep type arguments separately. Allow at most one superclass per class, and choose the relation from both declaration kinds (JLS 8.1.4, 8.1.5, 9.1.3). Store the superclass explicitly, delete the token path, and report cycles as diagnostics instead of deleting edges.

UML.note: UMA checks TH edges against the declaration header at bracket depth 0, drops type-argument and bound edges, recovers missing supertypes, and picks a unique superclass; fixing Phase 2/5 is handed off.

title: Type references are bare identifiers: generic, array, qualified and wildcard types are dropped, and type parameters are unnamed
evidence: generic_type, array_type, scoped_type_identifier, type_parameter and wildcard have no adapter arm, so they are dropped with their subtrees. As a result `List<Order> xs`, `Order[] xs`, `Map.Entry e`, `java.util.Date d` and `Optional<User> find()` have no NN_TYPE_REF, and type_id stays u32::MAX (pass4:46-57). type_parameters survives as one NN_TYPE_PARAM whose range is just '<', so it is unnamed, and every `T` becomes one global SK_EXTERNAL 'T' (pass3:86-89). Pass 3 reads only the first token (26-36). type_param_count and the array flag are never set. phase3.md:453 claims type arguments are resolved.
impact: Collection, array and Optional fields and generic return types, the main source of 0..* associations, carry no type at all. Generics are invisible to UML and signatures, and no erasure exists for overloads.
recommendation: Add a TypeRef table {head SymId, args[TypeRefId], array_dims, wildcard kind and bound, annotations}. Create one SK_TYPE_PARAM per type_parameter, with bounds, scoped to its class or method. Implement erasure (JLS 4.6) and basic subtyping. For `var` (JLS 14.4.1), infer from `new T(..)` or a typed call, otherwise mark UNKNOWN. Persist TypeRefs in .sta. Done when field and return-type tests over generic, array, nested and qualified types pass.

CORE.note: Phase 2 keeps generic_type/array_type/scoped_type_identifier/wildcard as NN_TYPE_REF with AUX flags and one NN_TYPE_PARAM per type_parameter (named via name token); TypeRef table in Pass 3 is a handoff.

DOCS.note: phase3.md line about resolved generics annotated with the dropped type forms; code handed off

title: UML association inference is constant-folded and unused: every resolvable field is aggregation 0..*, and composition is unreachable
evidence: `is_collection = builder.std_lib.stubs.contains_key("List") || ..` (associations.rs:40) is always true, because List is a stub (java_stubs.rs:57-62). So every non-external field type, java.lang.String included, becomes an Aggregation with 0..* (pass5:203-207). is_array tests flag 0x08, which is never set. Composition is unreachable and would accept any `new` in any constructor (95-111), although Phase 2 drops constructor bodies anyway. Primitive pseudo-ids default to SK_EXTERNAL (pass5:171-174), producing Dependency records and TH_USES edges to nonexistent ids. mult_min is always 0, there is no bidirectional pairing, and nothing reads sta.associations.
