impact: Phase 3's association output is wrong for essentially every field and is ignored. Phase 10 re-derives associations by simple name and marks every final field as composition (plantuml.rs:482-488), so the plan in phase3.md:155-171 is never realized.
recommendation: Implement the phase3.md decision table over TypeRef. Value types (primitives, boxed types, String, java.time) are attributes. Collection, Iterable, Map value and array types give 0..* to the element type; Optional gives 0..1; a primitive or @NonNull gives 1. Pair opposite ends into bidirectional associations (JPA mappedBy). Composition needs lifecycle evidence (an owned, non-escaping `new`, via Phase 5/6) per Guéhéneuc & Albin-Amiot 2004. Phase 9 must consume these records.

SCPGX.note: Exporters stopped inferring composition from 'final' and render UMA assoc kinds/multiplicities only; the Phase 3 association decision table is in src/symbol (handoff).

title: Quadratic loops (O(R·S), O(E²), O(C·S)) contradict the O(n_a) claim and expose the serial server to CPU exhaustion
evidence: get_or_create_external scans every symbol for each unresolved type ref (pass3:113-117), which is O(R·S). add_th_edge scans every edge on each insert (builder.rs:117-123), and there is one TH_USES per field, so O(E²). The sweep calls position() over all symbols per class keyword (pass1:373-382). resolve_lexical UTF-8-decodes each candidate (pass3:56-58) and reaches a root scope holding every file's module. There are three interner lookups per token (274-276), and each declaration allocates a scope plus three HashMap entries. The paper claims O(n_a) (tex:599). The server runs the pipeline inside a serial accept loop bound to 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:31-41).
impact: Phase 3 is super-linear: roughly 10^11 record visits for a ~1M-LOC repository, an estimated tens of minutes. A crafted repository with many distinct field types can stall the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Key externals by FQN in a HashMap. Deduplicate TH edges with a HashSet<(from,to,rel)>, then build CSR. Give each scope a name_id→decls index and compare interned ids only. Use dense Vecs for node_to_symbol and type_ref_resolutions, open scopes only for scope-forming constructs, and parallelize per-file passes with rayon. Add criterion benchmarks at 10K, 100K and 1M LOC with a log-log slope gate of 1.1, and give the server a per-request time and size budget.

DOCS.note: Paper pipeline table now gives model cost plus implementation status, and sec:impl notes the quadratic passes; code handed off

SRV.note: Server applies per-request file, size and time budgets and an analysis concurrency cap. The quadratic loops are in symbol/, outside my paths

title: No reference resolution beyond type identifiers: no expression names, calls, field accesses, inherited members or overload resolution
evidence: Pass 3 visits only NN_TYPE_REF (pass3:21-24). Nothing binds NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR, NN_CALL_EXPR, NN_FIELD_ACCESS or NN_METHOD_REF. Methods carry only param_count (pass1:945-955): no parameter types, descriptor or erasure. There is no member lookup through supertypes (JLS 8.4.8, 15.12.1) and no applicability or most-specific selection (JLS 15.12.2). Phase 6 therefore resolves callees by token position, falling back to the enclosing method's range (cg/resolution.rs:179-238), and CHA matches by name only (84-92).
impact: No phase has ground-truth bindings. Overloads collide, inherited and static-imported members are invisible, and call-graph, def-use and traceability precision are capped far below javac, Eclipse JDT or JavaParser SymbolSolver.
recommendation: Add an attribution pass analogous to javac's Attr/Resolve. Compute static types for literals, locals, fields, `new`, casts and call results. Resolve invocations per JLS 15.12.2 (strict, loose, varargs, most specific) over inherited and static-imported members. Emit an occurrence table {node → SymId | Unresolved(reason) | Ambiguous(cands)} in .sta, exportable as SCIP. Validate against semanticdb-javac/scip-java ground truth.

title: JDK model is 12 hand-written stubs without members; no classpath, and java.util is treated as implicitly imported
evidence: get_java_stubs lists 12 types: Object, String, Integer, Boolean, List, Map, Set, Collection, Iterable, Exception, RuntimeException and Throwable. They have no members or supertypes, and name_id is u32::MAX (122-143). java.util types resolve with no import (pass3:80-84). Long, Double, Number, Optional, Stream, Comparable, Runnable, CharSequence, StringBuilder, Enum and Class, plus every Spring, JPA or Jackson type, become SK_EXTERNALs qualified only by simple name (pass3:86-89). Same-named externals from different packages merge into one (113-117).
impact: Type hierarchies stop at the project boundary, so there are no Object, Comparable or Iterable members for dispatch. Library calls cannot resolve, and unrelated same-named library types are conflated.
recommendation: Load real signatures from ct.sym (release-specific, javac --release N) or from jmods/jimage, parsed with a Rust classfile crate such as cafebabe or ristretto_classfile. Index the build classpath lazily by package, using Maven dependency:build-classpath, a Gradle init script or scip-java's build integration, and cache by JDK or jar hash. Represent unknowns as SK_UNRESOLVED with their syntactic FQN and a reason. Done when the resolution rate is at least 99% on Spring PetClinic with its Maven classpath.

title: Declaration coverage gaps: enum constants, anonymous classes, records, interface constants, and catch/resource/for-each/pattern variables
evidence: The Java adapter has no arm for enum_constant, constant_declaration, annotation_type_body, catch_formal_parameter, resource_specification, inferred_parameters, compact_constructor_declaration or constructor_body, so all of them hit Drop with their subtrees. SK_ENUM_CONSTANT and SK_ANON_CLASS are never constructed, yet class_diagram.rs:209 and tra/builder.rs:84 consume them. Anonymous-class methods become children of the enclosing local-variable or method symbol. Record components become SK_PARAMs with no implicit fields or accessors (JLS 8.10.3), and for-each and pattern variables get no symbol at all.
impact: Enums render without literals, and anonymous listeners and strategies are invisible to CHA and pattern detection. Records have no attributes. Constructor bodies, which carry dependency-injection wiring, never reach Phase 4 to 6 or the composition check.
recommendation: Write a JLS declaration-kind coverage test with one fixture per kind, then add adapter arms and symbols for each. Create SK_ANON_CLASS with a TH edge to the instantiated type. Synthesize implicit members: record fields, accessors and canonical constructor (JLS 8.10.3), and enum values/valueOf (8.9.3). Scope catch, resource, for-each and pattern variables to their construct.

BDD.note: Java adapter declaration coverage lives entirely in src/ast and src/symbol, outside my paths.

CORE.note: Phase 2 now emits enum constants, anonymous class bodies, interface constants, record components (flagged), compact ctors, catch/resource/for-each/lambda params; symbol synthesis is a handoff.

UML.note: UMA reports SK_ENUM_CONSTANT as enumeration literals and scans constructor bodies from tokens; the missing AST adapter arms are handed off.

title: No resolution-level tests or oracle; the only accuracy metric compares class-name sets
evidence: tests/symbol_tests.rs has three tests: one checks that kinds are present and that counts survive a round trip, one runs Pass 1 against an empty TCA, and one checks a manual cycle. Its sample avoids generics, annotations and imported project types (19-42). src/symbol has no #[test], and pipeline_accuracy_tests asserts only symbol_count >= 15 (124-126). ruthless_verify.py, the source of README's 'F1 = 1.0000', compares class-name sets against a regex oracle (61-105, 247-268).
impact: Every defect in this report passes CI, and the F1 claim says nothing about names, bindings, types or hierarchy. A resolver rewrite would have no regression net.
recommendation: Build a ground-truth harness. Run scip-java (semanticdb-javac), or a javac TaskListener that dumps Tree→Symbol bindings, over fixtures and real repositories (PetClinic, commons-lang, Guava, JUnit 5, Kafka). Diff declaration names, reference bindings, supertypes, field and return types, and associations, and gate CI on per-category precision and recall. Add insta snapshot tests per JLS feature and a cargo-fuzz no-panic target.

title: .sta drops resolution results, is byte-nondeterministic, and uses positional symbol ids
evidence: type_ref_resolutions (builder.rs:30) and the import edges and mappings (scope_graph/mod.rs:15-16) are never serialized, and import_table_off is always 0. Project symbols never get a qual_name_id. Package maps are written in HashMap order (serializer.rs:165-185), so the bytes and CRC vary between runs, and that CRC is embedded in .cfa and .cga (cfg/mod.rs:30, cg/mod.rs:46). Symbol ids are pre-order positions (builder.rs:68), so adding one local renumbers every later file, contradicting the paper's incremental theorem (tex:1126-1127). TH edges are written as a flat list despite the 'CSR' doc (serializer.rs:2).
impact: Downstream phases must re-resolve by name, artifacts are not reproducible, and incremental or cross-build diffing is impossible.
recommendation: Persist an occurrence section and per-file import tables, writing every map sorted (BTreeMap). Give each symbol a stable SemanticDB/SCIP descriptor (e.g. com/acme/User#find(+1).) and keep the dense id only as an index; consider stack-graphs-style per-file partial results for incrementality. Store TH edges as CSR and check format_version on read. Add tests that two runs are byte-identical and that a body edit keeps other files' symbol keys unchanged.

DOCS.note: Paper incremental theorem now requires stable file-local ids and says positional ids break it; ADR-002 and ADR-007 record the consequence; code handed off

title: Visibility and modifiers are probably never extracted for Java, and the defaults make package-private members public
evidence: encode_attrs calls node.child_by_field_name("modifiers") (ast java.rs:139). In tree-sitter-java, modifiers appears to be an unnamed child: corpus trees show (class_declaration (modifiers) name: ..) [https://hackage-origin.haskell.org/package/tree-sitter-java-0.7.0.2/candidate/src/vendor/tree-sitter-java/corpus/declarations.txt]. If so, the call always returns None, and Pass 1 uses default_visibility: Package for types, Public for all members (java.rs:125-133), contrary to JLS 6.6.1. When modifiers are found, contains("public") also matches annotation text. Only static, final and abstract are mapped, so pass1:927-941 is dead code.
impact: UML visibility markers, abstract and static stereotypes, CHA's abstract filter (cg/resolution.rs:89) and any singleton or composition heuristic would see empty or wrong modifiers.
recommendation: Walk the modifiers child's children by node kind (keyword tokens, marker_annotation, annotation) and never substring-match. Apply the JLS implicit modifiers: interface members public, interface fields public static final, enum constructors private, record fields private final. Set DEFAULT, VARARGS, SEALED and NON_SEALED. Add a test that `public static final` yields non-zero attrs, plus a fixture covering every modifier.

CORE.note: Modifiers found by kind, JLS implicit modifiers/default access applied in Phase 2, DEFAULT/VARARGS/NON_SEALED/STRICTFP/DEPRECATED encoded in lang flags; Pass 1 reading the new lang bits is a handoff.

title: Phase 3 invariants are tautological: the data is repaired before it is verified
evidence: Invariant 2 holds by construction: the safety sweep reparents every orphan to symbol 0 before verification runs (pass1:623-628). Acyclicity holds because sanitize_th_graph deletes edges first (builder.rs:161-234, called at pass5:218). It removes the first edge whose two endpoints are both unvisited, which can be a legitimate edge downstream of a cycle rather than on it. 'Invariant 4: BPA/TCA hash verification' exists only as comments (builder.rs:259, 292), and the cycle error is mislabelled Invariant 4 (352).
impact: The invariants can never catch a resolution bug, and cycles caused by spurious edges silently delete edges that may be correct.
recommendation: Make verify_invariants pure, with no mutation. Report cycles as diagnostics listing the SCC (Tarjan) and keep the edges, flagged. Implement the hash check. Add invariants that matter: every NN_TYPE_REF is resolved or explicitly Unresolved, every non-external symbol has a decl_node, and child chains are acyclic and consistent with parent_sym. Fail CI on any violation over the fixture corpus.

title: Dead and misleading code in the symbol module
evidence: symbol::uml_meta::PatternDetector is unused; the live detector is uma::patterns. Its is_observer passes a TCA name_id to qual_names.lookup_by_id (patterns.rs:118-121), and get_name treats ids below 0x80000000 as raw indexes (qual_name_table.rs:40-47), so it compares arbitrary strings. wildcard_imports, is_th_reachable (O(V·E)) and is_collection_type are never called. ScopeGraph::new creates root scope 0, Pass 1 creates a second root, scope 1 (pass1:29-31), and the ROOT_SCOPE fallback (pass3:103) points at the disconnected scope 0. Every class is logged at INFO (pass1:151-157).
impact: Plausible-looking but broken APIs invite reuse, and the two roots make scope semantics ambiguous.
recommendation: Delete the unused detector and helpers, or wire them up behind tests. Use a single root scope. Make QualifiedNameTable reject ids that are not offsets. Move per-symbol diagnostics to trace level.

title: Seven of 14 UML diagrams are templated or hard-coded, yet labeled '100% Symbol-Grounded' and verified:true
evidence: JSON timing ignores its inputs (`_uma, _sta, _tca`) and always emits tracks CompilerCore, MemoryPool ('@60ms: 512MB') and ParallelWorkers. State machines are Uninitialized→Active per class with invented actions (`entry / onInit()`, `do / executeWork()`, `exit / cleanup()`). Use cases are `classes.take(6)` × `methods.take(3)`; deployment nodes are packages with 'artifact: X.module'; the JSON composite root is a hard-coded 'OpenHeartEngine.java'; the communication fallback invents calls between the first four classes (`invoke_{dst}`). Every JSON diagram sets `compiler_hash: 0x83D2D2B2, verified: true` and `file: {Name}.java, lines: [1]`. renderers.rs reports class counts as the composite, profile and use-case counts.
impact: Users receive invented timings, states, use cases and deployment topology that look like analysis results. Reviews or tool comparisons built on these diagrams are wrong, and the verified flag gives false assurance.
recommendation: Tag every diagram and element with a provenance tier (derived / heuristic / unavailable) in GraphIR and the rendered output. Return an explicit 'not statically derivable' result instead of placeholders for timing, deployment, use case and state machine until real extractors exist (see UML-03, UML-14). Delete hard-coded names, `.java` guesses and the constant verified/compiler_hash; take file and line from UMLLinkRecord/TRA. Add a CI metamorphic test that fails when a diagram's output does not change with its input.

SCPGX.note: All templates deleted; every view/node/edge carries a provenance tier; timing, deployment, use case are explicit 'not statically derivable'; state machines only from UMA records; file/lines from uml_link/token spans or null; compiler_hash is the SHA-256 input digest and verified is computed; renderers.rs reports None for non-derivable types.

title: Field-type TH_USES edges are treated as supertypes, so nearly every class with a field is reported as Decorator and Composite
evidence: Pass 5 adds a TH_USES edge from each class to every field type, primitives included (`builder.symbol(0xB000_0005)` is None, so `.unwrap_or(SK_EXTERNAL)`). decorator.rs and composite.rs take all `th_edges` with `from_sym == sym_id`, with no relation filter, then test `parent_types.contains(&f.type_id)`, which holds for any typed field: Decorator 85, Composite 75. facade.rs counts fields with `type_id != u32::MAX`; primitive ids qualify, so three ints earn Facade 70. A Python re-implementation over examples/test_patterns_codebase gives 37 reports on 13 of 35 classes, and only 9 name a real participant (precision ≈0.24). The Facade and Adapter samples display <<Decorator>>, which is checked first.
impact: Pattern stereotypes drawn on class diagrams are wrong for most classes of a real codebase, and pattern counts and the visitor's pattern_frequency metric are dominated by noise.
recommendation: Build a supertype index restricted to TH_EXTENDS/TH_IMPLEMENTS once and use it in every rule; exclude primitives, stubs and external types from structural predicates. Require call-graph evidence for Decorator/Composite/Adapter: an overriding method that forwards to the wrapped field, and for Composite a loop over a collection of the component type. Add negative fixtures (POJO, DTO with three ints, linked-list Node) asserting no pattern, and gate per-pattern precision in CI.

SCPGX.note: Exporters show every pattern recorded for a class with its uncalibrated evidence score (no first-checked-wins); detector precision fixes are in src/uma/patterns (handoff).

UML.note: Supertypes now come only from validated TH_EXTENDS/TH_IMPLEMENTS edges, and primitives, stubs and externals are excluded; Decorator, Composite, Adapter and Proxy now need a forwarding or loop call, not just a typed field.

title: Phase 9 has no working extractor for six diagram types: the state machine is a fixed template, four extractors are empty, and the object extractor misreads AST ids
evidence: StateMachineExtractor ignores `_ssa` and emits, for every class, states {0 initial, 1 final} plus one 0→1 transition per method. The composite, communication, interaction-overview and timing extractors have empty bodies and return (); behavioral/mod.rs:48-50 calls them for no output. ObjectDiagramExtractor calls `sta.symbol(ssa_rec.orig_sym_id)`, but SSA's orig_sym_id is an AST node index (`let sym_id = node;`), so objects are arbitrary symbol hits, and it stores ssa_id as label_text_id. No exporter reads `uma.objects`; objects and label_texts are never serialized. The paper and ROADMAP claim IFDS type-state state machines and thread-analysis timing.
impact: Object, composite-structure, state-machine, communication, interaction-overview and timing diagrams have no analysis behind them (deployment, use case and profile have no extractor at all), so the paper's tab:uml and the 14-diagram claim are not backed by code.
recommendation: Implement real extractors or drop the types. Object diagrams: Andersen allocation sites plus field points-to links (Tonella and Potrich, Reverse Engineering of Object Oriented Code, 2005). State machines: enum- or int-typed state fields with guarded assignments via SSA, CDG and ROBDD guards (Sen and Mall, SoSyM 2016), emitting nothing when no state variable exists. Communication diagrams: sequence records plus object naming (Rountev and Connell, ICSE 2005). Persist ObjectRecords and labels in .uma, and correct the paper and ROADMAP.

DOCS.note: Paper UML section and sec:impl, ROADMAP Phase 9 and uml_derivation mark the state machine as a template and the empty extractors as not derived; code handed off

UML.note: Real extractors for state machines (enum field assignments with guards), objects and links from allocations, composite structure, communication and interaction overview; timing dropped; objects and labels persisted.

title: Pattern rules are name and keyword heuristics that miss canonical GoF instances and flag unrelated classes
evidence: Singleton scores 100 for any field named 'instance' or typed as its own class, so `class Node { Node next; }` is a Singleton. It has no static or constructor checks and rejects enums. Factory means the name contains 'factory'. State means it contains 'state' or 'strategy' (IfStatement, RealEstate, every *Strategy). Observer needs add/register/attach plus 'listener', so the repo's own NewsAgency.attach(Observer) is missed. Template Method needs a protected method, so DataMiner is missed, and Logistics (Factory Method) is missed too: recall 6/9 on the repo's corpus. `has_private_constructor` scans SK_METHOD only, while constructors are SK_CONSTRUCTOR. The structural Singleton in src/symbol/uml_meta/patterns.rs is never called.
impact: Detection follows identifier spelling rather than design: renaming a class flips the result, textbook Observer/Factory Method/Template Method and enum, holder or Kotlin-object Singletons go undetected, and recursive data types become Singletons.
recommendation: Re-specify each pattern as structural plus behavioral constraints in the style of PINOT (Shi and Olsson, ASE 2006). Singleton: private constructors, a static self-typed field and a static accessor that assigns it (CFG/SSA), plus enum, holder and Kotlin `object` variants. Observer: a collection of an interface type and a loop invoking its method. Factory Method: an overridden method returning an abstract type that allocates a concrete subtype. Template Method: a concrete method calling abstract hooks (CGA). Use names only as a weak prior; revive or delete the dead detector.

UML.note: Rules are now structural plus behavioral: private constructors, static self field and accessor, enum and Kotlin object singletons, Observer via loop dispatch, Factory Method via an overridden allocating method, Template Method via calls to abstract hooks; no name tests.

title: Class extractor silently drops legitimate user types through a 188-name blacklist and lexical filters
evidence: `is_reserved_keyword` rejects user classes named Context, Singleton, Logger, Root, Entity, Configuration, Table, Value, Error, Update, List or Thread, plus project-specific names (HomeScreen, INVESTOR, OpenHeart). Context and Singleton are canonical GoF participant names, and src/uma/mod.rs:70 runs detection only over extracted classes, so the textbook Singleton is never examined. The repo's own examples/huge_enterprise_src/.../core/Entity.java interface is dropped. Names with `$` or non-ASCII letters, *Binding names and lowercase names are rejected. Test exclusion matches only '/src/test/', while ingestion stores raw OS paths, so on Windows test classes are kept.
impact: Class diagrams, pattern detection and every derived diagram omit real types without warning, and output differs between Linux and Windows.
recommendation: Delete the blacklist and fix the misclassifications it hides at their source in Phases 1-3 (annotations, constants or framework names emitted as SK_CLASS). Filter only on symbol kind and origin (synthetic, external, generated), accept full JLS and Kotlin identifiers, normalize paths before test detection, and make test inclusion a CLI flag. Add regression fixtures declaring Context, Singleton, Entity, Root and a Unicode-named class.

CORE.note: class_diagram blacklist is outside; path-normalization handoff recorded.

SCPGX.note: Exporters no longer drop classes by name (Entity/args/Class filters removed); relation targets filtered by symbol membership only. Extractor blacklist and path normalization are in src/uma (handoff).

UML.note: Blacklist and lexical filters removed; filtering is by kind and origin only; full Unicode identifiers accepted; paths normalized for test detection; include_tests option added (CLI wiring handed off).

title: The 'F1 = 1.0000' validation is circular and measures class names only; tests assert no ground truth for patterns or behavior
evidence: ruthless_verify.py removes every config 'keywords' name from the ground truth (lines 88/172/216/232). That list repeats 184 of the extractor's 188 blacklisted names (Entity, Configuration, Root, Singleton, HomeScreen, INVESTOR) plus engine placeholders (SystemNode, Node_0-2, MB), so dropped classes cannot lower the score, and only class-name sets are compared. design_pattern_architecture_tests.rs only prints pattern counts. The adversarial test passes if any of four kinds appears (`has_decorator || has_strategy || ...`), and its diagram checks require only @startuml/@enduml and no 'SystemNode'. uma_tests asserts non-emptiness. examples/ carries no role labels.
impact: The published F1 says nothing about members, relationships, behavioral diagrams or patterns, regressions in all of them pass CI, and docs/codebase-guide.md:263 overstates what the tests cover.
recommendation: Use an independent oracle (JavaParser, Spoon or javac -Xprint) with no shared exclusions, and score members, relationship kinds and multiplicities, not just names. Add a harness over P-MARt (Guéhéneuc 2007) and DPB (Arcelli Fontana et al., CSMR 2012) that reports per-pattern, role-level precision/recall/F1 with CI thresholds. Add golden-file tests per diagram, negative fixtures, and metamorphic tests (consistent renaming must not change detection).

ENG.note: Oracle and tests are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: F1 withdrawn; codebase-guide test table no longer claims ground-truth verification; examples README says fixtures carry no labels; tests are out of scope

title: Sequence diagrams list messages in the wrong order with no nesting, returns or fragments, and all scenarios merge into one diagram
evidence: Callers are expanded from a LIFO stack after all of a method's calls are emitted, so for A→B, A→C the sub-calls of C print before those of B, and each method is expanded once, wherever it is popped. `combined_fragments` is always empty, although `_cfa` is passed and docs/uml_derivation.md:89 promises ROBDD-derived alt/loop/opt. There is no depth bound or library filter. PlantUML emits activate/return/deactivate right after each call, so activations never nest. The actor is declared `act_Actor` but its messages come from `part_Actor`, creating a phantom participant. Every entry-point scenario is concatenated into one diagram.
impact: Sequence diagrams misstate call order and nesting, the core semantics of the notation, and become unreadable walls of messages on any non-trivial project.
recommendation: Emit one diagram per scenario by ordered, depth-bounded inlining of call sites in CFG order (Rountev, Volgin and Reddoch, PASTE 2005). Map branch and loop regions to alt/opt/loop/break fragments with guards, emit replies and nested activations, and mark async calls (Thread.start, Executor.submit, CompletableFuture). Name lifelines by receiver object via points-to (Rountev and Connell, ICSE 2005), and choose entry points from framework semantics (main, @RequestMapping, JUnit, Android lifecycle).

DOCS.note: uml_derivation §3.1 rewritten with the design (CFG-ordered inlining, fragments, per-scenario) and baseline defects; code handed off

SCPGX.note: Sequence printer renders UMA messages in ordinal order with replies, balanced nested activations, async/create kinds, fragments, hierarchical numbers, one page per scenario (PlantUML newpage, Mermaid export_sequence_scenarios) and message budget; phantom participant fixed. Ordering/receiver lifelines/entry points are extractor work (src/uma).

UML.note: Per-scenario ordered, depth-bounded inlining with nesting, replies, loop/alt/opt fragments, async/create messages, framework entry points, bounds and determinism; naming lifelines by receiver via points-to is blocked because SSA ids are AST nodes.

title: Class diagrams lose multiplicity, collection element types, relationship kinds and member signatures, and collide on simple names
evidence: `is_collection: 0` is hard-coded. Type refs resolve from their first token, so `List<Observer>` becomes List and the one-to-many link to Observer vanishes. Phase 3's `sta.associations` (AssocKind, multiplicity, role names) is never read. Return types are recorded as associations (they are dependencies), while parameters, locals and `new` yield nothing. With multiple interface extends only the last survives. Member modifiers are cast `as u8`, losing default/sealed/varargs bits. Exporters treat composition as 'final field', draw nesting as `*--` (Mermaid), omit parameters and key classes by simple name, so nested Builders merge. PlantUML keeps one edge per pair; XMI emits only `Class_{id}`.
impact: Diagrams omit the relationships reviewers need most (one-to-many, ownership, usage), misrender overloads, generics and same-named types, and cannot round-trip to UML tools.
recommendation: Model type arguments in Phase 3 (a TypeRef tree), consume sta.associations, and classify relationships per Guéhéneuc and Albin-Amiot (OOPSLA 2004): association, aggregation or composition by exclusivity and lifetime, with multiplicity from collection or array types. Add «use»/«create» dependencies. Key elements by qualified name, and emit operation signatures, UML templates, {static}/{abstract} and enumeration literals. Export OMG XMI 2.5.1, validated against UML 2.5.1 and import-tested in Papyrus, Enterprise Architect and Visual Paradigm, to reach IntelliJ/ObjectAid-level fidelity.

CORE.note: Foundation only: Phase 2 now emits generic (head + args), array (dims), qualified and wildcard NN_TYPE_REF nodes and per-parameter type params; UML consumption outside.

SCPGX.note: Exporters consume FieldRecord assoc kind, multiplicity, element type and role; no composition-from-final; nesting is its own relation; parameters and return types printed; static/abstract markers; one edge per field (no per-pair overwrite); XMI full. Phase 3 type-argument modelling is outside (handoff).

UML.note: Multiplicity, collection element types, composition/aggregation, dependencies, all generalizations, u16 modifiers, parameter types and qualified-name labels added; the Phase 3 TypeRef tree and exporter/XMI fidelity are outside src/uma (handed off).

title: Quadratic and cubic scans in sequence, class, component and pattern extraction create performance cliffs on large codebases
evidence: For each entry point the extractor rebuilds a HashMap of all `site_to_edge_map` entries, and for each visited method it scans every `cga.call_sites` entry: O(entries × reachable × sites) time, with unbounded memory and no depth limit. Each class scans all `sta.th_edges` and runs `tra.uml_links.iter().find`, giving O(C·E + C·L). Four pattern rules repeat the full th_edges scan per class. Component extraction re-runs package extraction and scans all th_edges per package. One info-level log line is written per class candidate.
impact: At 1M LOC (about 50K classes, 500K TH edges, thousands of entry points) these loops reach roughly 10^10 or more iterations, so Phase 9 runs for hours or exhausts memory instead of scaling.
recommendation: Build CSR indexes once (supertypes by from_sym, call sites by caller, uml_links by sym_id). Bound the sequence builder by depth and size, memoize per-method message summaries, and parallelize per class and per entry point (rayon). Add criterion benchmarks on Spring Framework, Apache Commons and JHotDraw with time and peak-RSS budgets enforced in CI.

UML.note: Indexes built once (children, supertypes, call sites by caller, UML links by binary search); sequence building bounded and memoized; per-class info logging removed; no rayon added.

title: The .uma reader misparses the design-pattern table and desynchronizes on large records; objects and labels are never persisted
evidence: The writer emits each pattern as class_sym u32, `pattern_kind as u32`, `confidence as u32` and reserved u32 (16 bytes). The reader consumes u32+u16+u16+u32 (12 bytes): confidence always reads 0, every later record is misaligned, and there is no end-offset check. Counts are written `as u16` while all records follow, so above 65,535 messages or blocks the reader desynchronizes, unchecked `bytes[offset..]` slicing panics, and `with_capacity` trusts header counts. Objects and label_texts are never written. Artifact inspection prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID'; the round-trip test compares only version and hash.
impact: Every consumer of a persisted .uma reads corrupted pattern data, and large projects can crash the reader, so the artifact is not a faithful interchange format.
recommendation: Define the layout once with derive-based codecs (binrw or zerocopy) or a schema (FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto), and use u32 counts. Make reads bounds-checked and error-returning, assert the payload ends exactly at the CRC, add sections for objects and labels, and add a proptest asserting read(write(x)) == x for every record type.

ENG.note: src/uma/serializer.rs is outside my paths.

SRV.note: inspect contains reader panics and states checksum status truthfully. The .uma codec fixes are in uma/serializer.rs, outside my paths

UML.note: Format v2: section-framed, u32 counts, every read bounds-checked and returning an error, exact end-of-payload check, 16-byte pattern table, sections for objects, labels and the new records.

title: Pattern output has no roles, participants, calibrated confidence or conflict resolution, and covers 11 of 23 GoF patterns
evidence: DesignPatternRecord holds only {class_sym, pattern_kind, confidence}: no instance id and no role→class map (Context, Strategy, ConcreteStrategy). ClassRecord.design_pattern is one u8 set by the first match, so rule order picks the stereotype. Confidences are uncalibrated constants (100/95/90/85/80/75/70). Mutually exclusive kinds both fire: PaymentStrategy gets State 85 and Strategy 95, and State is displayed. Visitor, Command, Proxy, Iterator, Mediator, Chain of Responsibility, Abstract Factory, Bridge, Flyweight, Memento, Prototype and Interpreter are absent. chain.rs re-implements detect_all as a second pipeline.
impact: Output cannot be scored against role-level benchmarks (P-MARt, DPB), cannot explain a match, and cannot tell Strategy from State or Decorator from Proxy.
recommendation: Introduce PatternInstance {pattern, roles: Map<Role, Vec<SymId>>, evidence: Vec<Fact>, score} and serialize it. Match with similarity scoring over relation matrices (Tsantalis et al., TSE 2006) or explanation-based constraint solving (DeMIMA, Guéhéneuc and Antoniol, TSE 2008). Calibrate scores (isotonic or Platt) on labeled data, and disambiguate (State if the context reassigns its delegate internally, otherwise Strategy). Cover all 23 GoF patterns and keep a single pipeline; consider DPDf-style learned features as a ranking layer.

UML.note: Added PatternInstanceRecord (roles, evidence mask, score), conflict resolution, a single pipeline and rules for all 23 GoF patterns; scores are explicitly uncalibrated because no labeled data is available.

title: Activity diagrams discard CFG guards, exception edges, loops and labels; the label extractor reads the wrong token
evidence: Every edge becomes EDGE_KIND_CONTROL with guard_text_id 0, although the CFG labels edges True/False/Except/Switch/LoopBack. loop_depth is always 0 despite `cfg.loop_info`; swimlane_count and end_node_count are hard-coded to 1; switch blocks with more than two successors become ACTION; FORK/JOIN/EXCEPTION nodes are never produced. The label is computed then discarded (`_label_text`; label_text_id = block_id). LabelExtractor treats `bpa.node_attr` (packed visibility/modifier/operator bits) as a token index, so plain statements read token #0. Its byte slice at max_chars-3 can panic mid-character on long non-ASCII tokens (latent). Exporters show only the first 6-8 functions, as 'Block_N' rectangles.
impact: Activity diagrams are unlabeled block graphs without decision guards or exception paths, short of the decision/merge semantics the paper claims.
recommendation: Map edge types to guards ([cond]/[else], case labels) using the branch condition's TRA token span, and render exception edges as UML exception handlers or interruptible regions. Emit explicit decision/merge nodes, fork/join for thread and async starts, and partitions for inlined callees. Build labels from statement token spans, truncate on char boundaries (`char_indices`), store them in label_texts, and render each node kind with its UML shape.

CORE.note: LabelExtractor/activity diagrams are outside; NodeAttr layout now documented, handoff recorded.

DOCS.note: uml_derivation §3.3, phase9 §9.2.2 and paper sec:impl document the discarded guards and labels; code handed off

SCPGX.note: Activity printer uses UMA guard labels, falling back to CFG edge types and branch-condition token text ([cond]/[else]/[exception]/[case]), exception flows, loop back edges, decision/merge/fork/join shapes and statement-span labels truncated on char boundaries; extractor-side fixes are in src/uma.

UML.note: Guards for true/false/switch/exception edges, loop depth, handler and decision nodes, end_node_count, labels from statement token spans with char-safe truncation, and labels interned into label_texts.

title: Phase 9 output is nondeterministic across runs because HashSet/HashMap iteration order leaks into records
evidence: `implements_syms` and `association_syms` come from `HashSet::into_iter()`, and sequence lifelines from `HashMap::into_values()`. Both use std's randomly seeded RandomState, so element order varies per process. That order is serialized into .uma (changing its CRC) and drives exporter edge and participant order, despite CHANGELOG 'Deterministic generation for all 14'.
impact: Identical inputs yield different .uma bytes and diagram layouts, defeating reproducible builds, hash-chain caching, golden-file tests and diagram diffs.
recommendation: Use BTreeSet/BTreeMap or sort before emission (by symbol id or qualified name). Add a test that runs Phase 9 twice on the same input and compares bytes, and audit the exporters for the same HashMap ordering.

DOCS.note: CHANGELOG 'Deterministic generation' entry corrected and ledger row added; code handed off

UML.note: Sorted sets and maps everywhere and first-appearance order for lifelines, so output no longer depends on HashMap iteration order.

title: Package, component and deployment views are containment counts with no dependency or build-metadata grounding
evidence: PackageRecord holds only class and subpackage counts, with no inter-package dependencies, although docs/uml_derivation.md:60 promises them. Components are exactly packages and `_cga` is unused. 'Provided' counts interfaces declared in the package, 'required' counts TH edges (duplicates included) to outside interfaces, and exporters render neither (bare boxes). Deployment reuses packages. No build or deployment metadata is read: pom.xml, build.gradle, module-info.java, DI annotations, Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests.
impact: Architecture views carry no information beyond the directory tree, whereas Structure101, jQAssistant/ArchUnit-based views or Enterprise Architect show dependency structure, cycles and layering.
recommendation: Compute package dependency edges from type references and call edges, with cycle detection (Tarjan SCC) and Martin's metrics (Ca, Ce, I, A, D). Derive components from Maven/Gradle modules, JPMS modules and Spring @Component/@Service beans, with implemented interfaces as provided and injected interface-typed fields as required. Derive deployment from Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes or Helm manifests, and mark it unavailable when they are absent.

DOCS.note: uml_derivation §2.2/2.3/2.6 specify dependency edges, Martin metrics and build/deployment-metadata sources, with baseline status; code handed off

SCPGX.note: Package view renders UMA package dependencies with reference counts, cycle stereotypes and Martin metrics (Ca, Ce, I, A, D); components show provided/required interfaces and bean/package kind; deployment is explicit 'not available'. Reading build/deployment descriptors is ingestion work (handoff).

UML.note: Package dependency edges, Tarjan cycles, Martin Ca/Ce/I/A/D, components from DI beans and packages with interface lists; no build or deployment metadata exists in the corpus, so that stays explicitly unavailable.

title: DOM XSS: repo file names, ZIP entries and shared .openheart.json reach innerHTML
evidence: github-engine.js:123 and :218 emit `Parsing AST (...): ${file.path.split('/').pop()}`, and index.html:915 and :971 write that string into `hudText.innerHTML`. Git allows any byte except '/' and NUL in a path, so a repo file named `.java` passes the extension filter. Running the real engine with a mocked fetch produced exactly that markup. Shared state files reach :1388 (diagram_type; it is uppercased, but numeric character-reference payloads survive), :682 (node textLabel, on hover) and :735 (edge uml_kind). ZIP and folder names reach :1066 and persist into the history dropdown at :1200. There is no CSP. A harmless symptom of the same sink: hovering shows 'Path Illuminated: <>', because `<>` (graph-loader.js:212) is parsed as a tag.
impact: Analysing a hostile public repo, ZIP or shared state file runs script on the github.io origin, which all the owner's Pages sites share. That script can read sessionStorage openheart_custom_files, which holds the full source of privately imported folders (index.html:984).
recommendation: Ban HTML-string sinks. Build status and HUD text with textContent or DOM nodes (or lit-html, which auto-escapes). Add eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized to CI. Externalise the inline module, then add a strict CSP meta tag plus Trusted Types (require-trusted-types-for 'script'). Use DOMPurify only where markup is genuinely needed. Add regression tests that use payload file names, ZIP entry names and crafted state files.

title: Studio fabricates diagrams, source code, traceability and 'Verified' metrics
evidence: For imported code, projectCustomDiagram returns fixed templates: a state machine Initializing->Ready->ProcessingRequest (graph-canvas.js:366-384), CFG blocks containing `let ctx = InitializeContext();` (:489-504), and DFG/CDG/ROBDD/timing views plus deployment artifacts named `${c.name}.dll` (:276-300, :476-578). editor.js:211-214 and :370-375 invent Java bodies labelled 'Grounded from Deep Program Graph Analysis'. Every class gets `lines: [1, 5, 10]` (github-engine.js:526). The engine also hardcodes `execution_time_ms: 280` and emits a random `compiler_hash` with `verified: true` (:164, :576-577). The progress text '[3/5] Compiling SCPG ... ROBDD' is driven by a timer (index.html:825-853). 'Invariant Verified (ROBDD Sat)' is shown as a default when no data exists (:658-672). files_processed counts all files although at most 30 are parsed (:103, :161).
impact: On GitHub Pages, 13 of the 19 projections, every traceability highlight and every 'Verified' badge shown for user code are invented. This contradicts the README and makes any demo or benchmark misleading.
recommendation: Delete the synthetic generators. When data is missing, show an explicit empty state, for example 'CFG requires the Rust engine'. Label in-browser results as approximate, for example 'regex, 30/1,234 files'. Show only metrics the engine provides, with provenance: engine version, phase, and a real content hash of the IR (crypto.subtle.digest). Traceability must come from token spans in the IR, not constants. Add a test that fails if the UI claims verification without a corresponding engine field.

title: Real Rust engine is effectively unreachable; backend results are discarded
evidence: index.html:861-862 aborts the /api/analyze request after 2,500 ms. The server, however, runs a synchronous `git clone --depth 1` plus all ten phases before it replies (src/adapters/server.rs:424-441), so real repos fall back to the regex engine. When the backend does answer in time, the UI ignores its payload (index.html:888-907). It re-fetches `diagrams/<type>.json` (graph-canvas.js:625), which the server has overwritten in the shared web/diagrams folder (server.rs:636-660), and any active customGraphIr takes precedence (graph-canvas.js:604-606). Engine `errors` are swallowed silently (index.html:877-884).
impact: Users rarely see the engine the README benchmarks. Concurrent users overwrite each other's results, committed demo assets get overwritten, and a previous local codebase can be shown under a new repo's name.
recommendation: Turn analysis into an async job API: POST returns a job id, progress arrives via SSE or WebSocket, and the job can be cancelled. Render the returned IR directly from session-scoped artifact URLs, and never write into web/. Show engine errors to the user. Longer term, compile phases 1-9 to WebAssembly (wasm-bindgen plus web-tree-sitter grammars) and run them in a Web Worker, so GitHub Pages runs the same analyzer and the regex engine can be retired.

title: In-browser analyzer builds wrong class models (member leakage, calls as methods, ID collisions)
evidence: Members are scanned from `code.slice(match.index + match[0].length)`, which is the rest of the file rather than the class body (github-engine.js:337-339). Running the real code in Node on a 3-class file, C0 got fields f0,f1,f2 and methods m0,helper,m1,helper,m2,helper. methodRegex accepts `name(...);`, so call statements become methods (:434), and fieldRegex captures local variables (:404). Node ids are bare simple names (:342) and edges are resolved by name (:554-556): two `App` classes in different packages produced ids 'App App'. Only the first 30 files in tree order are parsed (:103). Declarations must contain `{`, so Python classes are never found (:291).
impact: Class models, relations and LLM exports are wrong for real repos; the default preset, java-design-patterns, has an App.java in every module. Meanwhile the README advertises F1 = 1.0000 and in-browser 'AST parsing'.
recommendation: Replace the regexes with web-tree-sitter (tree-sitter-java, -kotlin and -python WASM grammars) and tree-sitter queries. Use fully qualified names, including nesting, as ids, and resolve relations through imports and package scope. Choose files by relevance (src/main, excluding tests and vendor code) instead of an alphabetical prefix. Add golden tests that compare JS output with Rust engine output on shared fixtures and report precision/recall for each relation kind.

title: Cubic regex backtracking in extractMethods freezes the tab on realistic files
evidence: methodRegex `([A-Za-z0-9_<>[\]]+)?\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*\(` (github-engine.js:434) can split a run of identifier characters in many ways. Timing the real function in Node: a 1 KB run took 0.39 s, 2 KB took 3.6 s and 4 KB took 29 s, roughly O(L^3). It runs on the main thread, once for each preceding class, over the rest of the file (:337-339). On the GitHub path it is applied to .js/.ts blobs with no vendor, minified-file or size filter (:89-94, :109-125), and there is no Worker or timeout. Long hex or identifier constants, such as crypto test vectors or embedded blobs, trigger it.
impact: A single file with a few KB of unbroken alphanumeric text hangs the UI for seconds to minutes. The browser may offer to kill the page, and the analysis cannot be cancelled.
recommendation: Move ingestion and parsing into a Web Worker with a per-file time budget and an AbortController. Skip blobs over about 512 KB (using the tree `size` field) and minified files (a max-line-length heuristic), and honour linguist-vendored/generated attributes. Replace the regexes with tree-sitter, which parses in linear time. Any regex that remains must be made unambiguous and checked in CI with a ReDoS checker such as recheck or safe-regex2.

title: Layout is grid packing, not graph layout; sequence diagrams and large exports break
evidence: The class/package layout packs at most 2 columns per package and ignores edges (uml-layout.js:105-123). Measured on the deployed class.json, 115 cards form a 1,942x16,000 px column, so the fit zoom is about 0.05. The sequence layout puts every lifeline on one row (:463-479): 20,900x60 px, with 699 messages drawn as taxi edges that collapse onto 71 source-target pairs. The hierarchical layout uses BFS ranks wrapped at 3 nodes per row, with no crossing minimisation and an O(n^2) queue.shift (:381-426). Edges use cytoscape's 'taxi' style (theme-manager.js:499), which does not route around nodes. dagre is loaded but never used (index.html:30-31). A 2x PNG of the sequence view (41,800 px wide) exceeds browser canvas limits (graph-canvas.js:1417-1421).
impact: The landing view and the bundled views are unreadable at fit zoom. UML sequence semantics (time order, activations, fragments) are missing, and exports of large views come out blank.
recommendation: Adopt elkjs, run in a Web Worker, for example through cytoscape-elk. ELK Layered provides network-simplex layering, layer-sweep crossing minimisation, Brandes-Koepf placement, orthogonal routing and compound nodes. Write a dedicated sequence renderer (lifelines, time-ordered messages, activation bars, alt/loop/par fragments), as PlantUML and Mermaid do. Pass maxWidth/maxHeight to cy.png and tile large exports. Remove dagre. Benchmark crossings and area against Graphviz dot.

title: Theme toggle and overlapping async renders discard user edits and race
evidence: setTheme restyles the graph and then re-runs renderGraph from scratch (graph-canvas.js:721-726). That recomputes the layout, clears undo history (:698-703) and replaces a loaded .openheart.json with the bundled `diagrams/<type>.json` (:623-646). renderGraph destroys cy and then awaits fetches with no generation token (:593-646). Every page load starts two overlapping renders: one from canvas.init (index.html:638, graph-canvas.js:51) and one from initTheme (index.html:778) via setTheme. Sidebar clicks also start renders without awaiting them (index.html:452), so a slower earlier response can replace a later selection.
impact: One theme click silently discards manual layout, deletions, collapses and loaded state. Every page load does the work twice. The visible diagram can differ from currentGraphType, so saved states and exports get the wrong label.
recommendation: Separate the document model from the view. On a theme change, update the stylesheet and regenerate card images in place inside one cy.batch, keeping positions. Give renderGraph a monotonically increasing render id (or an AbortController) and commit only the latest render. Initialise the theme before the first render. Persist edited layouts in the model rather than in the cytoscape instance.

title: No tests, lint, types, build or CI gate for roughly 10K lines of frontend
evidence: CI runs only cargo check, fmt and test (ci.yml:41-47). deploy_pages.yml publishes web/ on every push to main with no build, no tests and no `needs:` gate. The repo has no package.json, ESLint config, type checking or JS tests. About 1,100 lines of app logic sit inline in index.html (408-1502). The app.js chain (ui, viewer, orb, api, state, logger; about 1.3K lines) is never loaded, yet it still contains `viewport.innerHTML = svgText` (viewer.js:151) and code that posts source structure to kroki.io (api.js:65-82). Duplicate class methods silently override earlier ones (graph-canvas.js:75/764, 81/754). Four parsers that disagree with each other coexist: the Rust engine, github-engine, puml-parser and api.js.
impact: Most defects in this audit (highlighter corruption, ReDoS, duplicate methods, render races) would have been caught mechanically. Instead, every merge ships untested to the public site, and cached unversioned modules can mix versions after a deploy.
recommendation: Add a package.json with Vite and TypeScript (or JSDoc plus `tsc --checkJs`). Add ESLint with no-dupe-class-members and no-unsanitized, Vitest unit tests for the parsers, loader and layout, Playwright end-to-end tests with axe-core and screenshot diffs, and Lighthouse CI budgets. Make the Pages deploy depend on a web-ci job, build content-hashed assets, and pin actions by commit SHA. Delete the dead modules and the fallback parsers.

title: Render-blocking CDN scripts without SRI or CSP; unused libraries shipped
evidence: Five synchronous third-party scripts in <head> have no integrity or crossorigin attributes (index.html:29-34): cytoscape 3.26.0 from cdnjs; dagre 0.8.5, cytoscape-dagre 2.5.0 and cytoscape-svg 0.2.0 from jsDelivr; and jszip 3.10.1 from cdnjs. dagre and cytoscape-dagre are never used, because only the 'preset' layout is called. There is no Content-Security-Policy, and the roughly 1,100-line inline module (index.html:408) rules out a strict script-src. Google Fonts adds another third party (:20-22). The http-equiv Cache-Control and Pragma tags (:6-8) are ignored by browsers.
impact: A compromised CDN runs arbitrary code on the origin. A blocked CDN leaves 'cytoscape is not defined' and a dead app with no offline mode. Nothing mitigates the XSS in WEB-01.
recommendation: Bundle with Vite or esbuild: content-hashed, self-hosted vendor code, with fonts via @fontsource. Failing that, at least add SRI hashes and crossorigin. Remove dagre and cytoscape-dagre. Externalise the inline module and add a CSP meta tag: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com https://raw.githubusercontent.com; img-src 'self' data: blob:. Upgrade cytoscape to the current 3.3x release.

title: No Graph-IR validation; the bundled landing IR is internally inconsistent
evidence: loadDiagramState passes `savedState.elements` straight to cytoscape (graph-canvas.js:1383-1393). loadGraphIrToCytoscape trusts ids and parents (graph-loader.js:26-37). The version and $schema fields are written but never checked (graph-canvas.js:1367-1371). The deployed landing web/diagrams/class.json has 120 nodes with 5 duplicate ids (ScreenType, RawRequirementFeatures, CurrentState, IDAssigner, Module; ScreenType appears at lines 194 and 1874) and zero edges, yet its metadata says `verified: true`. communication.json is byte-identical to sequence.json, and state.json to statemachine.json.
impact: cytoscape rejects or drops duplicate ids, and edges attach to the wrong node. Users see a class diagram with no relationships badged as verified, and a 'communication' view that is just the sequence data.
recommendation: Define a JSON Schema for the Graph IR and for state files. Validate every load with Ajv (or Zod), checking for unique ids, dangling edges and parents, and parent cycles, and show diagnostics instead of rendering bad data. Check the version field and migrate old files. Add a CI step that validates web/diagrams/* and fails on duplicate ids or identical projections.

title: Undo/redo, edge filters and selection state are inconsistent
evidence: When a selected package is deleted, cytoscape's remove() also removes its descendants, but undo only replays `validTargets.union(validTargets.connectedEdges()).jsons()` (graph-canvas.js:2363-2380), so the children never come back. Loading a state file renders with preservePositions, which skips clearing history (:698-703), so old actions replay against the new diagram. hiddenEdgeKinds is never re-applied after a render or load (:1406-1411), and the `edge.layer-hidden` style is never used, so unchecked edge kinds stay visible. Selectors are built by string interpolation (:787, :2146), so a quote in an id throws. selectedNode is never cleared, so Backspace on a focused button deletes a node and arrow-key panning stops (:1205, :1248). The inspector headline shows the stereotype instead of the name (index.html:649).
impact: Undo can permanently lose diagram content, and the filter checkboxes and selection misreport what the canvas shows.
recommendation: Implement commands over a document model (immer patches or the Yjs UndoManager) that capture descendants() and every connected edge. Clear history on every load. Re-apply filters with class toggles after each render. Replace string-built selectors with `cy.edges().filter(e => e.data('uml_kind') === k)`. Clear the selection on background taps, bind Delete only while the canvas has focus, and take the headline from data.name.

title: Code viewer corrupts its own highlighting and fires request storms for missing sources
evidence: highlightSyntax first inserts ``, then its keyword pass matches the word `class` inside that inserted markup (editor.js:575-582). Running the real method, `@Override` becomes `class="syn-annotation">`, so every line containing a string or annotation shows the literal text `="syn-string">`. render() rebuilds the whole file as DOM on every gutter click and theme change, with one listener per line (:523-558). For an uncached file, loadFile tries raw_url, then /api/source, then up to 21 sequential `examples/...` guesses (:174-207), none of which exist on Pages. Nothing stops a stale response from overwriting a newer one (:139-225).
impact: Nearly every real Java or Kotlin file displays junk text, large files stall the panel, and each click on an uncached node costs about 22 round trips and can show the wrong file.
recommendation: Use a read-only CodeMirror 6 view (virtualized viewport, Lezer Java/Kotlin grammars, search, folding), or a single-pass tokenizer that escapes each token, as Shiki and Prism do. Resolve sources only from the IR's raw_url and file maps. Cancel superseded loads with an AbortController plus a request id. Add snapshot tests for highlighting.

title: GitHub ingestion ignores rate limits, truncation, slashed branches and sub-paths
evidence: Every call is unauthenticated, so the 60 requests/hour per-IP limit applies, and one attempt can spend up to 7 API calls trying six branch guesses (github-engine.js:54-80). A 403 rate-limit response is reported as 'Check if the repository is public' (:82-84). The `truncated` flag is never read: a mocked tree with truncated:true was parsed without complaint. A URL ending in tree/feature/login/src is parsed as branch 'feature' with subPath 'login/src' (:28-33), and subPath is never used (:48). Paths go into raw URLs unencoded, so '#', '?' and '%' break them, for example a `C#/` directory (:111). Files are fetched one at a time (:109-125). ZIP and folder imports have no size caps, so a zip bomb inflates entirely in memory (index.html:1069-1078).
impact: Users behind shared IPs hit the limit quickly and get a misleading error. Monorepos, slashed branch names and subfolder URLs analyse the wrong files, and a hostile archive can crash the tab.
recommendation: Accept an optional fine-grained PAT kept in memory or sessionStorage, never localStorage. Read X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset and show the reset time. Resolve refs through git/matching-refs. When the tree is truncated, walk subtrees non-recursively. Honour subPath. Encode each path segment with encodeURIComponent. Fetch through a 6-wide pool with an AbortController. Enforce size limits using the tree `size` field and JSZip's uncompressed sizes.

title: State is scattered across globals, storage keys and a DOM text sentinel
evidence: StudioState (state.js) is never loaded. Live state is split across canvas fields, sessionStorage keys (index.html:611-636, 980-988), seven localStorage keys, and the input text ' (Active Codebase)', which doubles as a mode flag (index.html:800, 999, 1006). Local imports are persisted but GitHub imports are not (index.html:935). A reload therefore restores the previous local codebase, and exports and state files keep the old openheart_custom_name (graph-canvas.js:1356). Only the preset chips clear that state (index.html:1137-1145). localStorage is read at startup without try/catch (index.html:425, graph-canvas.js:28, editor.js:17). When site data is blocked those reads throw and the app never initialises.
impact: Reloads and exports can show or name the wrong codebase, and users with site storage blocked get a blank studio.
recommendation: Introduce one typed store (a vanilla store or Zustand) with an explicit session model {source, ir, files, layout}. Persist it through a single guarded adapter, for example IndexedDB via idb-keyval with try/catch and an in-memory fallback. Drive the UI from store events, delete the text sentinel, and clear derived state atomically on every import.

title: Fails core WCAG 2.2 AA criteria: keyboard, focus, status messages, reflow, shortcuts
evidence: index.html has 2 aria-labels and no roles or aria-live regions, while progress and errors are innerHTML updates (fails 4.1.3). Graph nodes can be reached only with a mouse, and file-tree rows are click-handled divs with no tabindex or role (file-tree.js:207-277), failing 2.1.1. Focus outlines are removed (style.css:191, 939) and no :focus-visible rule exists (2.4.7). The global single-key shortcuts M, L, Space and Delete cannot be turned off (minimap-navigator.js:272-287), failing 2.1.4, and Alt is suppressed globally (graph-canvas.js:894-912). The fixed 280px/1fr/380px grid uses overflow:hidden and has no breakpoint below 1024 px (style.css:565-567, 1882-1897), failing 1.4.10. There is no prefers-reduced-motion support, and the wheel handler stops the layers list from scrolling (graph-canvas.js:921-923).
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot operate the studio. It is unusable on phones and tablets or at 200-400% zoom, which also blocks institutional adoption.
recommendation: Follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: a tree view with roving tabindex for files, tabs with role=tab and aria-selected, and menu buttons with aria-expanded and Escape handling. Provide an accessible outline of nodes kept in sync with the canvas (Tab and arrow keys to move, Enter to inspect). Add a polite aria-live status region, :focus-visible styles, a shortcut toggle or canvas-focus-only shortcuts, collapsible side panels for narrow screens and a reduced-motion query. Gate with axe-core in Playwright CI.

title: Rendering has no level-of-detail, spatial index or cache invalidation
evidence: Every node is a unique SVG data-URI background, regenerated on each render (graph-loader.js:196-221, uml-card-renderer.js:150-153). cytoscape runs with textureOnViewport and hideEdgesOnViewport both false (graph-canvas.js:682-684), while the custom rAF zoom loop calls cy.zoom() every frame (:857-889). With pan lock on, a tap scans every node calling style() and boundingBox() (:1335-1352), and every grab snapshots every node's position (:2076-2081). The loupe caches cytoscape's canvases once and never invalidates them (minimap-navigator.js:617-619), so after a re-render it samples detached canvases. The minimap thumbnail is redrawn only on render, not after moves, deletes or collapses (:357-411).
impact: Frame time and texture memory grow with node count, so pan and zoom will likely stutter beyond a few thousand cards (not profiled). The loupe and minimap go stale after routine actions.
recommendation: Add level-of-detail rendering: plain rectangles and labels below about 0.35 zoom, full cards above. Turn on textureOnViewport and hideEdgesOnViewport above about 1k elements. For 10k+ nodes, evaluate cytoscape's WebGL renderer (3.31 or later) or sigma.js. Use rbush or flatbush for hit tests, and invalidate the loupe and minimap caches on render and position events. Add a Playwright performance suite at 1k, 10k and 50k nodes that tracks frame times.

title: Entry constraint via restrict doubles every function's sat_count
evidence: Step 5 replaces f_paths with f|entry=1, which no longer mentions entry_var, but Step 8 still counts over ordering.n_vars(), so the dropped variable counts as free (x2). In a brute-force model of the exact encoding, straight-line ENTRY->B->EXIT gives 2 (true value 1). The entry edge is reached, so this survives a fix for BDD-02. restrict.rs and phase8.md even claim the step 'halves the search space'.
impact: Every function reports at least twice its real path count, so the sat_count==0 diagnostic is meaningless.
recommendation: Conjoin f_paths AND x_entry instead of restricting, or count over n_vars-1 with the restricted variable removed. Correct the 'halves' comments. Unit test: a straight-line method must give sat_count == 1.

title: Exit constraint is missing; loops are encoded as self-consistent cycles
evidence: phase8.md:135 requires 'at least one edge into EXIT is taken'. The code sets Phi_EXIT=TRUE and adds no exit clause. In a model of simpleLoop (7 edges), the assignment (1,1,1,1,1,0,0) enters the loop forever and never reaches EXIT, yet satisfies f_paths. Loop iteration counts cannot be represented. Unlike BDD-02, every block in that assignment is entered and constrained.
impact: Every function with a loop counts non-terminating pseudo-paths, so sat_count has no defined meaning there.
recommendation: Add the exit constraint and define loop semantics explicitly: for example, count acyclic paths with LoopBack edges cut (Ball-Larus), or use an acyclic ordering encoding. Test: a for-loop method yields 2 acyclic paths.

title: Feasibility filter cannot prune any path; its condition variables only inflate #SAT
evidence: Only cond -> x_true is conjoined, never NOT cond -> x_false. Condition variables are never existentially quantified before counting, and the library has no exists operation. Since EXISTS c.(f AND (c -> x)) = f, no edge assignment is ever removed; c is just counted as another variable. Unlike BDD-05, using fresh non-colliding variables would still filter nothing.
impact: Step 6 can only distort counts; the documented 'sound' filtering does nothing useful.
recommendation: Allocate condition variables after the edge variables, encode reached(b) -> (x_true <-> c), share c across branches that test the same SSA value, then quantify the conditions out before #SAT. Test: two `if (flag)` on the same flag give 2 paths, not 4.

title: Recursive BDD operations can overflow the stack on large functions
evidence: apply, apply_not, restrict and sat_count recurse once per BDD level, so recursion depth reaches the variable count (the number of CFG edges, up to 65535). The CLI and the server run Phase 8 on the main thread, whose default stack is 1 MB on Windows, and no large-stack worker thread is used. Other walks (count_var_nodes, RPO) already use explicit stacks. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite makes apply and not iterative.]
impact: A method with thousands of CFG edges can abort the whole process with an uncatchable stack overflow.
recommendation: Make all four routines iterative with explicit work stacks, or run Phase 8 on a thread with a large configured stack. Test with a 20k-edge straight-line CFG.

title: Switch exactly-one constraint is built with O(k^2) pairwise applies
evidence: For k successors, build_switch_constraint runs k(k-1)/2 iterations. Each does apply(And), apply_not (new nodes, fresh cache) and another apply(And) on the growing at_most_one BDD, and every apply clears the computed table. The cost is roughly cubic in k, and O(k^2) garbage nodes end up in the shipped node array.
impact: Large generated switches make Phase 8 very slow on a single function.
recommendation: Build exactly-one directly in variable order with O(k) nodes, using a two-state 'none seen / one seen' construction. Test: a 1000-case switch builds in milliseconds with about 2k nodes.

title: Phase 7/8 panic instead of returning errors, which kills the HTTP server
evidence: Both stages panic! on write errors. Phase 7 checks its invariants with assert!/assert_eq!, which stay on in release builds, and debug builds panic on canonicity failures. Phase7Stage::run and Phase8Stage::run return plain artifacts, while Phases 3-6 return a Result that the server turns into JSON errors. The server handles requests inline on the main thread with no catch_unwind.
impact: One failing request (full disk, unwritable path, invariant violation) shuts down the server for every user.
recommendation: Return Result from both run() functions, turn the invariant asserts into diagnostics or errors, and wrap request handling in catch_unwind.

title: Call-site TRA indexes are keyed by array position, not call_site_id
evidence: Phase 6 assigns call_site_id in AST preorder and then calls sort_unstable_by_key(caller_sym), so cga.call_sites[i].call_site_id != i. The unstable sort can also reorder sites that share a caller. BI_cs is documented as 'indexed by call_site_id' but is filled in sorted order, and CallSiteSpanRecord.call_site_id is set to the enumerate index cs_idx.
impact: BI_cs[call_site_id] lookups and forward_cs_query results point at the wrong call sites when joined with CGA edges.
recommendation: Index BI_cs by cs.call_site_id and store cs.call_site_id in the span records. Test with calls in methods whose symbol order differs from source order.

title: BI_ssa and BI_blk cannot be addressed: ids are function-local and there is no per-function directory
evidence: SSA ids restart at 0 in every function (rename_function allocates a new ssa_records), and block ids are also local to each function. Both indexes are flat concatenations in function order, yet they are documented as 'indexed by ssa_id' and 'global_block_id'. The TRA stores no sym_id -> (base, count) table, so a (function, ssa_id) or (function, block) pair cannot be resolved. Unlike BDD-09, this is about addressing entries, not their values.
impact: The SSA and block layers of tau cannot be queried from the artifact.
recommendation: Add per-function directories (sym_id, base, count) for blocks and SSA variables, or key the entries by (function, local id).

title: Most TRA content is write-only: no tau/tau^-1 API and no per-layer forward indexes
evidence: Nothing outside src/tra reads bi_ast, bi_blk, bi_ssa, bi_cs or cs_span (main.rs only prints their lengths). LayerKind and EntityRef are never used. Only symbol and call-site spans exist, although §7.2.2 specifies one span index per layer. Queries need a token_id plus a redundant file_id (a mismatch silently returns nothing), and there is no (file, line, col) entry point. The SCPG Traceability section stores only a count.
impact: The six-layer bidirectional traceability cannot be queried; the .tra file mostly costs build time and disk space.
recommendation: Add a TraceabilityIndex API with to_source(EntityRef) and from_source(file, line, col) -> Vec<EntityRef>, backed by per-layer interval indexes. Embed it in the SCPG, or drop the unused sections.

title: BDD library lacks exists, ITE, eval, any_sat and dag_size primitives
evidence: Only var, apply(And/Or/Xor), apply_not, implies, restrict and sat_count exist. Checking path feasibility needs eval or a witness path. A sound feasibility filter (BDD2-03) needs existential quantification. Without ITE or an Imp operation, implies builds a full negated copy. Sifting needs the reachable BDD size, but only the arena-wide node_count exists. Unlike BDD-12 (missing query layer), these core primitives are themselves absent.
impact: Blocks the fixes for feasibility, sifting and path queries.
recommendation: Add ite(f,g,h), exists(f, vars), eval(f, assignment), any_sat(f) and dag_size(root), each with truth-table tests.

title: SipHash maps and per-call allocations on every BDD hot path
evidence: make_node, apply, restrict and sat_count all hash with std's DoS-resistant SipHash. The restrict, sat_count and apply_not memos are keyed by dense node ids, yet each call allocates a fresh HashMap. Calling clear() on a grown apply cache costs O(capacity) on every call; this complements BDD-11. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite adds an Fx hasher.]
impact: Several-fold constant-factor slowdown in Phase 8.
recommendation: Use a fast non-cryptographic hasher or a custom open-addressing unique table, Vec-indexed memos with generation stamps, and a fixed-size lossy computed table.

title: PSA construction, ordering and builder code have no unit tests
evidence: constraints.rs, feasibility.rs, construction/mod.rs, recursive.rs, rpo.rs, sifting.rs, builder.rs and psa/mod.rs contain no #[cfg(test)] module. force.rs only checks that its output is a permutation, and ordering/mod.rs only tests swap_adjacent. A small unit test would catch each of BDD2-01, -02, -05, -22, -24 and -26.
impact: Core Phase 8 semantics are not verified at the unit level.
recommendation: Add straight_line_one_path, if_else_two_paths, two_ifs_four_paths, for_loop_acyclic_paths, phi_b_branch_exactly_one, switch_exactly_one_truth_table, same_condition_correlates, rpo_order_diamond, hyperedge_shapes, sifting_fixes_interleaved_order, finalize_sorts_by_sym_id, scc_order_callee_first.

title: XOR terminal shortcut rebuilds NOT with a fresh cache on every hit
evidence: In apply(Xor), the (TRUE, g) and (f, TRUE) cases call apply_not(..., &mut HashMap::new()) before the memo lookup. The same negation is therefore rebuilt for every parent pair that reaches it, which breaks the documented O(|f| x |g|) bound. Today XOR is only applied to two single-variable BDDs. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite may address this.]
impact: Latent super-quadratic cost if XOR is ever used on larger BDDs.
recommendation: Check the memo first and share one NOT cache per top-level call, or adopt complement edges (BDD-11).

title: apply and apply_not silently return FALSE for out-of-range node ids
evidence: The code comments 'Defensive: node IDs out of range — return FALSE as safe fallback'. An invalid id therefore yields the constant FALSE (zero paths) with no signal, while restrict and sat_count index nodes[] directly and panic on the same input. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite adds id assertions.]
impact: Internal id bugs show up as plausible wrong results (0 paths) instead of failures, and behavior differs between operations.
recommendation: Replace the fallback with an assertion or a Result, consistently in every operation; never fabricate FALSE.

title: sat_count gap factor clamps to 2^63 instead of saturating
evidence: (1u64 << lo_gap.min(63)) gives 2^63 for any gap of 64 or more, so with a child count of 1 the result is 2^63, not u64::MAX. Example: x0 with hi=TRUE over 71 variables returns 2^63 (true value 2^70). Unlike BDD-16, the output is a plausible unsaturated number, so even the saturation sentinel is lost. [HEAD; the uncommitted PathCount work may address this.]
impact: Functions with 64 or more free variables below a node report wrong but believable counts.
recommendation: Return u64::MAX when the gap is at least 64 and the child count is nonzero, or count with arbitrary precision. Add a test with gap 70.

title: sat_count's documented depth contract contradicts how it is called, and invalid variables pass silently
evidence: The doc says depth = n_vars - current_level, but BDDLibrary passes depth = n_vars for any root. Leading free variables are counted only through an implicit excess carried down to the TRUE terminal, so a caller who follows the doc undercounts by 2^root.var. For nodes with var >= n_vars (feasibility variables go up to 16383), saturating_sub produces a gap of 0 and silently corrupts the count.
impact: The public function is easy to misuse, and inconsistent BDDs produce garbage counts without any signal.
recommendation: Expose only sat_count(root, n_vars), multiply by 2^root.var explicitly, and assert var < n_vars. Tests: a root variable above 0, and an out-of-range variable.

title: Canonicity check omits ordering and child validity, and runs only in debug builds as a panic
evidence: verify_canonicity only checks lo != hi and that each (var, lo, hi) is unique. It does not check that var(child) > var(node), that lo/hi < len, or that ids 0 and 1 are the terminals. It runs only under cfg(debug_assertions) and uses panic!, so release builds never check. The BDDLibrary::finalize() named in the spec does not exist, and psa_tests repeats the same partial check.
impact: Ordering violations (from a future sifting fix or a crafted .psa) pass the check; debug builds abort the pipeline.
recommendation: Add ordering and child-range checks, return a Result or diagnostic instead of panicking, and also run the check on deserialized PSA files.

title: Three inconsistent definitions of 'terminal', and node arrays are publicly mutable
evidence: apply, restrict and sat_count treat ids 0 and 1 as terminals; is_terminal() tests var == 0xFFFF; is_true/is_false test flags and are used only in tests. var(0xFFFF) is accepted and creates an internal node that sifting and verify_canonicity treat as a terminal. The pub nodes field and the pub low-level modules contradict the module's rule to use BDDLibrary exclusively.
impact: Different routines classify malformed or deserialized nodes differently, and callers can break invariants.
recommendation: Use id < 2 as the only definition, reject TERMINAL_VAR in var() and make_node, and make nodes private behind read accessors.

title: Wrong or misleading doc comments in the BDD primitives
evidence: unique_table.rs links to a nonexistent UniqueTable::get_or_insert (a broken intra-doc link). It says terminals are 'pre-inserted by BDDLibrary::new', which they are not, and that len() counts 'live' nodes, although nothing is ever freed. sat_count claims about 500 SipHash lookups take under a microsecond. node.rs calls the 12-byte nodes 'cache-line efficient, 5.3 per line', but they straddle cache lines.
impact: Misleads maintainers, and rustdoc emits warnings.
recommendation: Correct the comments and deny rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links in CI.

title: Public apply() memo key ignores the operation
evidence: The public free function apply(op, ..., cache) memoizes on (min(f,g), max(f,g)) only. It is correct only because BDDLibrary::apply clears the cache on every call. A caller that shares one cache between AND and OR, which is the obvious optimization, gets wrong results. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite adds an op code to the key.]
impact: An API hazard that blocks a persistent computed table.
recommendation: Key the cache by (op, f, g), or make the low-level function private.

title: Dead or test-only PSA APIs
evidence: UniqueTable::insert_terminal, len and is_empty, VariableOrdering::from_edge_sequence and as_u32_edge_slice, PathSummaryArtifact::path_metrics, and ROBDDNode::is_true/is_false have no production callers. insert_terminal entries are unreachable because make_node returns before the lookup when lo == hi. from_edge_sequence truncates n_vars to u16 and ignores duplicates.
impact: Unmaintained code with latent bugs misleads readers about what is actually used.
recommendation: Remove these APIs, or wire them up and test them (for example, use from_edge_sequence when decoding PSA orderings).

title: No-op sifting still costs about 2n^2 swaps per function, and its driver is wrong
evidence: Each variable is swapped to the top, then to the bottom, then back: 2(n-1) swaps, about 2n^2 per function (8e8 for n = 20k). The priority list holds variable indices computed once, but they are used as positions after earlier sifts have moved variables. Size is measured with node_count(), the arena size, which never decreases. Unlike BDD-06, these defects would survive a fix that actually permutes the BDD.
impact: Wastes CPU on large functions; real sifting built on this driver would move the wrong variables and never see a gain.
recommendation: Skip the pass until real level swaps exist. Then track var<->level maps, measure live nodes per level, and sift toward the nearer end first with a growth bound.

title: FORCE runs a fixed number of iterations and returns the last ordering, not the best
evidence: n_iters is always min(10n, 200). There is no total-span metric and no convergence test, and the final order is the last iterate even if an earlier one had a smaller span; Aloul et al. stop at convergence and keep the best. Each iteration allocates and re-sorts in O(n log n). Unlike BDD-03, this is about the iteration policy.
impact: Wastes time on large functions and can return a worse order than one already found.
