recommendation: Compute the total hyperedge span each iteration, keep the best order, and stop when the span stops improving or after c*log n iterations. Test with a chain whose span must not increase.

title: rpo_edge_ordering is DFS edge-discovery order, not reverse postorder
evidence: Edges are appended when DFS first traverses them, which is preorder. For a diamond A->B, A->C, B->D, C->D it yields [A->B, B->D, ..., A->C, C->D], separating A's two branch edges that share an XOR constraint. Ordering by source RPO would give [A->B, A->C, B->D, C->D]. Phase 4 already numbers blocks in RPO.
impact: The name and docs are misleading, and the initial FORCE positions separate tightly coupled variables.
recommendation: Sort edges by (source block id, target), which is RPO by source, or rename the function and fix its docs. Add a diamond test.

title: VariableOrdering silently clamps and aliases edges beyond the u16 range
evidence: from_order caps n_vars at 65535, clamps out-of-range edge indexes to the last edge, and leaves unmapped edges at edge_to_var = 0. var_for_edge_idx and edge_for_var return 0 for unknown inputs, and var_to_edge stores edge indexes as u16. Functions with more than 65535 edges therefore map the extra edges onto variable 0, breaking the bijection promised at lines 6-9.
impact: Very large generated methods get silently wrong constraints and path counts.
recommendation: Return Option or Result, use u32 indices or emit an explicit 'too large' PSA record, and assert the bijection in debug builds.

title: Phase 8 processes SCCs caller-first, the opposite of its comments and §8.5.1
evidence: TarjanSCC pushes an SCC when its root finishes, so cga.sccs is already in callee-first order. Phase8Stage iterates it with .rev(), which gives caller-first order. The comment calls the last SCC 'a source node ... = a leaf callee with no outgoing call edges', which contradicts itself. Unlike BDD-12 (composition is missing), here the order itself is inverted.
impact: Harmless today, but interprocedural composition added later would find callee summaries missing.
recommendation: Iterate cga.sccs in its stored order, fix the comments, and add a test with a three-level call chain that checks processing order.

title: Cyclomatic Invariant 2 is never verified; the V(G) doc and unit test are wrong
evidence: finalize says Invariant 2 is 'verified during construction', but construction just copies cfg.cyclomatic (which Phase 4 clamps with max(1)), and psa_tests compares that copy with its own source. metrics.rs says V(G) equals the number of decision nodes, but it is decisions + 1. The cyclomatic_formula test invents a sixth edge to assert V(G)=3 for if/else (actually 5-5+2 = 2), and it never calls production code.
impact: The documented invariant is never checked, and the only V(G) unit test encodes a wrong value.
recommendation: Recompute E-B+2 from the CFG in finalize and report mismatches. Fix the doc. Replace the test with an if/else CFG that expects 2.

title: PSA metrics record drops unwind_depth and stores sat_count as a 'mean'
evidence: to_bytes never writes unwind_depth and from_bytes sets it to 0, so loaded metrics always look non-recursive. Bytes 12..16 hold sat_count as an f32 but are labelled 'mean'. cyclomatic, max_path_len and sat_count are already stored in the 32-byte directory entry. path_metrics(dir_idx) has no callers, and there is no accessor from sym_id to directory index.
impact: Data is lost on round trip, and the section is redundant and misleadingly named.
recommendation: Replace 'mean' with unwind_depth (with a format version bump) or drop the table. Add function_index(sym_id), and a round-trip test asserting unwind_depth.

title: 'Lazy-loaded' node arrays and 'always mmap'd' metrics are not implemented
evidence: read() loads the whole file with fs::read and eagerly decodes every ordering table and node array into Vecs. FunctionPSAHeader has no byte offsets for its ordering table or node array, so reaching function i means summing n_vars and n_nodes over all earlier functions. The PSA reader does not use the crate's mmap wrapper.
impact: Consumers pay the full load and decode cost just to read one header.
recommendation: Add per-function ordering and node offsets (format v2), memory-map the file, and decode node arrays on demand. Until then, fix the comments.

title: PSA and TRA readers skip version, reserved-field, sortedness and reference checks
evidence: Both readers read format_version but never check it. The PSA reader ignores dir_offset ('always HEADER_SIZE in v1') and drops _reserved. Nothing verifies that the directory is sorted (binary_search depends on it), that sym_span is sorted (forward queries depend on it), or that node lo/hi/var are in range. The TRA reader accepts a 96-byte file and takes its CRC from header bytes 88..96; the minimum should be 104. Unlike BDD-17, this is not about header counts.
impact: Future formats or CRC-valid malformed files are silently misread, and later traversals can panic or miss lookups.
recommendation: Reject unknown versions and nonzero reserved fields, verify sort order and reference ranges, and require at least 104 bytes for TRA files.

title: Artifact writers are non-atomic, fully buffered and unvalidated
evidence: Both writers build the whole file in a Vec, then write it straight to the final path with fs::write or File::create + write_all. A crash or full disk therefore leaves a truncated artifact in place. The PSA writer never checks that its four parallel Vecs have equal lengths or match the header's n_vars/n_nodes, so it can emit a file with a valid CRC that cannot be parsed.
impact: Failures or misuse leave partial or inconsistent artifacts, and peak memory doubles for large outputs.
recommendation: Write to a temp file and rename it, stream through a BufWriter with an incremental CRC, and validate section lengths (or store one Vec of per-function records).

title: UMLLink col_end overflows on long lines and is wrong for multi-line tokens
evidence: col_end = ce + end_tok.len adds two u16 values, for example column 65000 plus length 1000. It wraps silently in release builds (and in dev builds at HEAD, where overflow-checks = false), and panics when overflow checks are on. For a multi-line last token (text block, block comment) it adds the token's whole length to its start column. decl_last_tok is clamped to the corpus's last token without checking that it is in the same file.
impact: Wrong end positions in generated or minified code and in multi-line constructs.
recommendation: Compute the end line and column from the token's end position (store it in the TCA) using u32 checked arithmetic, and validate that last >= first and both are in the same file.

title: CallSiteSpanRecord truncates lines to u16; TRA line widths are inconsistent
evidence: cs_span stores line_start as u16, which wraps silently above line 65535 (BDD-09 cites only the sym_span instance of this). Line fields are u16 in SymbolSpanRecord and CallSiteSpanRecord, u32 in UMLLinkRecord and SourceRange, and u24 on disk for UML links.
impact: Wrong call-site line numbers in very large files, and confusing, lossy API types.
recommendation: Use u32 lines in every record (u24 on disk if needed), or recover the full values from tokens at query time.

title: UML kind list is duplicated, and Invariant 2 is a count tautology that can panic
evidence: The same nine-kind array is defined in both builder.rs and uml_link/mod.rs. Invariant 2 compares two counts produced by the same filter, so it can only fail when the copies diverge, and then assert_eq! aborts. The spec lists seven kinds. The success log says 'Invariants 1-4 asserted', but Invariant 1 is vacuous and Invariant 4 checks only the first 5% of symbols.
impact: Adding a kind in only one place crashes Phase 7, while the invariant verifies nothing.
recommendation: Define a single UML_KINDS constant, check for each symbol that a link with a valid range exists, report diagnostics, and make the log accurate.

title: Composite SCPG hash XOR-combines its components and truncates to 32 bits
evidence: combined = tca ^ bpa ^ sta ^ cfa ^ ssa ^ cga ignores component order, and changes cancel out when two components change by the same XOR delta. The result is then reduced to a CRC-32, so collisions are expected after about 2^16 builds. BDD-07 says the inputs are not real artifact hashes; this combiner stays weak even with correct inputs.
impact: Stale artifacts can go undetected once BDD-07 is fixed.
recommendation: Hash the ordered concatenation of the component hashes (sha2 is already a dependency) and store at least 64 bits.

title: Misleading TRA names: filter_stale keeps the stale ids, and the TRA_MAGIC comment has the wrong byte order
evidence: filter_stale is documented as 'Filters all stale records out', but it returns the sym_ids of the stale records. TRA_MAGIC = 0x5452413100010000 is written little-endian as bytes 00 00 01 00 31 41 52 54 ('....1ART'), not the 'TRA1' followed by 00 01 00 00 that the comment claims; PSA_MAGIC, by contrast, is built with from_le_bytes on the literal string. The TRA reader is named deserialize, while the PSA reader is named read.
impact: Callers can invert the staleness logic, hex dumps do not show the documented magic, and the two APIs are inconsistent.
recommendation: Rename filter_stale to stale_ids(), define the magic with u64::from_le_bytes on a byte string (with a format version bump), and align the reader names.

title: Phase 7/8 run independent per-function work sequentially
evidence: Each FunctionROBDDBuilder::build uses its own BDDLibrary and reads only that function's CFG and SSA; no callee summaries are consumed. Even so, all functions are built in one sequential loop. The eight Phase 7 index builds are also independent but run one after another.
impact: Phase 8 wall-clock time grows with total work, all on one core.
recommendation: Build functions in parallel (std::thread::scope or a thread pool) and sort the results by sym_id to keep the output deterministic.

title: BDD primitive and PSA serializer tests cover only trivial cases
evidence: apply tests use only TRUE/FALSE operands: no x0 AND x1, no x0 XOR x1, no NOT of a variable. restrict is never applied to a node above the restricted variable. sat_count is tested on one variable only, and the memo test repeats identical arguments. crc64_deterministic compares the function with itself. The round trip checks lengths, not node contents, metrics or unwind_depth. There are no bad-CRC, truncated-file or bad-magic tests.
impact: Regressions in the BDD algebra or the file format would go unnoticed.
recommendation: Add a random-formula truth-table property test (up to 8 variables) for apply, not, restrict and sat_count, a CRC known-answer test, a field-by-field round trip, and tests that reject corrupted files.

title: src/tra has no unit tests at all
evidence: No file under src/tra contains a #[cfg(test)] module. The only coverage is one integration test that checks counts, scpg_hash equality after a round trip, and a single forward query on the first span.
impact: Index addressing, source ranges and serializer fields are not verified.
recommendation: Add forward_sym_query_nested_and_adjacent, forward_sym_query_file_boundary, forward_cs_query_exact, cs_index_uses_call_site_id, sym_span_skips_invalid_tokens, uml_link_range_matches_tokens, scpg_hash_changes_per_component, tra_round_trip_all_fields, tra_rejects_short_and_bad_crc, compute_delta_detects_moved_symbol.

title: Sort-key 'Lemma 5.1' test checks two neighbours and no boundaries
evidence: Injectivity is asserted with two hand-picked tuples. build_sort_key masks the line with & 0x00FF_FFFF and only a debug_assert guards it, so line 2^24 aliases line 0. The test never tries line 0xFFFFFF or 0x1000000, column 0xFFFF, or the low-byte duplicate counter that ingestion ORs into the key.
impact: The claimed lemma is never tested at its limits.
recommendation: Add a property test over random tuples plus explicit boundary cases, and make out-of-range lines an explicit error instead of a masked alias.

title: Empty-function early return hard-codes metrics and ignores recursion
evidence: When rpo_order is empty, the builder returns cyclomatic 1, max_path_len 1 and unwind_depth 0, regardless of cfg.cyclomatic, the block count or is_recursive. The normal path uses cfg.cyclomatic and RecursiveHandler instead. Phase 4 always adds an ENTRY->first_real edge, so this branch is effectively unreachable today.
impact: Metadata becomes inconsistent if the CFG contract ever changes; until then the branch is dead code.
recommendation: Use cfg.cyclomatic, compute_max_path_length and the recursion flag here as well, or assert n_edges > 0.

title: compute_max_path_length depth counter overflows u16
evidence: depth is a u16 and is pushed as depth + 1. Past 65535 blocks it either wraps (in release, and in dev at HEAD where overflow-checks = false) or panics (when checks are on). For n > 65535 the depth >= bound cutoff can never trigger. Unlike BDD-04's exponential enumeration, this happens even on a linear CFG.
impact: Huge straight-line functions get a wrong max_path_len or a panic.
recommendation: Track depth as usize and saturate when storing it into the u16 field, or widen the field.

title: Phase 8 ignores CFG edge types
evidence: No PSA code reads cfg.edges[].2 or edge_types. Feasibility assumes succs[0] is the True edge (its doc names CFGEdgeType::CondTrue/CondFalse, which do not exist). That holds only because of insertion order; do-while, for example, emits LoopBack rather than True. Any block with two successors (an Except edge plus a normal edge, or a one-case switch plus default) is treated as a boolean condition. Except edges are counted as ordinary path alternatives.
impact: A condition can be tied to the wrong edge, and exceptional control flow silently inflates path counts.
recommendation: Select the True/False edges by CFGEdgeType, skip non-conditional blocks, and offer a mode that excludes Except edges or counts them separately. Add tests for do-while and try/catch.

title: Feasibility scans the whole taint and SSA lists for every branch block
evidence: For each block with two successors, is_complex_condition iterates all of ifds.taint_sparse and build_condition_bdd runs rfind over all ssa_records, so the filter costs O(blocks x records) per function. Unlike BDD-05 (soundness), this is a cost problem.
impact: Quadratic time on large functions.
recommendation: Bucket the taint facts and the last non-phi definition by block once, before the loop.

title: FeasibilityFilter docs describe behavior the code does not have
evidence: The module doc says heap access, virtual dispatch and non-linear arithmetic are classified as complex, and that nullable facts are used. The code only checks whether the block has any taint fact and never reads nullable data. apply() says the result is 'never smaller than before filtering', but a conjunction can only shrink the set of satisfying assignments.
impact: Reviewers overestimate how precise and sound the filter is.
recommendation: Rewrite the docs to match the implementation, or implement the classifier as described.

title: TRA duplicates BPA token ranges and has no section directory
evidence: BI_ast copies bpa.token_range for every AST node (8 bytes per node), although the BPA already stores token_ranges. The TRA header lists section counts but no section offsets, so reaching the UML link table means parsing every section before it.
impact: Artifacts are larger than needed, and sections cannot be accessed randomly or lazily.
recommendation: Drop BI_ast in favour of the BPA (or reference it), and add a section table with offsets for memory-mapped access.

title: f_paths conjunction schedule is a left fold in block-id order
evidence: f_paths is built with one apply(And) per block, in block-id order. There is no clustering by variable position, no balanced pairwise conjunction and no early simplification, so intermediate BDDs can be much larger than the final one. Unlike BDD-03, this concerns the conjunction schedule, not the variable order.
impact: Avoidable peak node counts and running time on branchy functions.
recommendation: Conjoin the Phi_b constraints sorted by top-variable position, or with a balanced tree reduction, and measure peak node counts in a benchmark.

title: Java reducer emits every variable_declarator as a second NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL, duplicating declarations
evidence: java.rs:42 maps both local_variable_declaration and variable_declarator to Keep(NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL). Declarators are children of field and local declarations, so `private int x = 1;` becomes FIELD_DECL[TYPE_REF, LOCAL_VAR_DECL[x, 1]] and `int a = 1;` nests two LOCAL_VAR_DECLs. Pass 1 creates a symbol for each such node, and create_symbol does no dedup.
impact: Every field gains a phantom SK_LOCAL_VAR child and every local is declared twice. Symbol counts, scopes and def/use attribution are skewed.
recommendation: Add a distinct NN_VAR_DECLARATOR kind, or Eliminate declarators and emit one decl node per declared name with the shared type. Make discovery create exactly one symbol per name, and add a golden test asserting one symbol for `int a = 1;`.

title: Enum constants are dropped from the AST, so SK_ENUM_CONSTANT is never produced
evidence: enum_body and enum_body_declarations are Eliminate, but enum_constant has no arm and falls to `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129), discarding the constant, its arguments and any constant body. ASTNodeType has no enum-constant kind. grep finds nothing that creates SK_ENUM_CONSTANT, although class_diagram.rs:209 and tra/builder.rs:84 consume it.
impact: Enums appear in UML and traceability with no literals. Constant arguments and constant-specific bodies are missing from the CFG, SSA and call graph.
recommendation: Add NN_ENUM_CONSTANT to ASTNodeType. Keep enum_constant with its name, argument_list and class_body, map it to SK_ENUM_CONSTANT in the semantic adapter, and add an enum golden test.

title: The BP AST stores no child roles, so consumers decode children by position and misread for and enhanced-for loops
evidence: PreorderArrays hold only type, attr, range and parent. Tree-sitter field names are discarded and NN_ELSE_CLAUSE is never emitted. `for (String s : list) {...}` yields [TYPE_REF, s, list, BLOCK], yet for_stmt.rs:88-101 takes the third child (`list`) as the body. In for_stmt.rs:26-35, `for (; i<n; i++)` and two-variable inits shift the init/cond/update/body positions.
impact: CFGs for common loops lose the real loop body or treat updates as conditions. A dropped then-branch moves the else branch into the then position.
recommendation: Persist a per-node role byte (the tree-sitter field id) in PreorderArrays and in the .bpa. Emit NN_ELSE_CLAUSE or placeholder nodes for omitted parts, and expose child_by_role accessors for the CFG builders.

title: Java reducer silently drops many constructs beyond those in CORE-02
evidence: Through `_ => Drop`, these tree-sitter-java 0.20 kinds vanish: package, import and module declarations, constant_declaration (interface fields), annotation_type_body, catch_formal_parameter, inferred_parameters, explicit_constructor_invocation, yield_statement, scoped_type_identifier, array_type, class_literal, dimensions_expr, throws, permits, annotation_argument_list, octal_integer_literal and hex_floating_point_literal. CORE-02 covers only constructor bodies, switch bodies, try-with-resources and generic types.
impact: Qualified supertypes, array parameter types, catch types, interface constants, lambda parameters and some operands disappear, so symbols, types and data flow are wrong.
recommendation: Make the default arm Eliminate, or at least log unmapped kinds. Add node types for imports, packages, catch parameters, class literals and qualified or array types. Add a test that walks node-types.json and fails on any unclassified named kind.

title: Anonymous class bodies and instance initializers get no declaration node
evidence: object_creation_expression is Keep(NN_NEW_EXPR) but its class_body is Eliminate (java.rs:110), so anonymous-class methods become direct children of NN_NEW_EXPR. An instance initializer (a bare block in class_body) is emitted as a plain NN_BLOCK, and NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT is never produced. grep shows SK_ANON_CLASS and SK_INSTANCE_INIT are never created.
impact: Anonymous-class methods are parented to the enclosing method, which breaks dispatch and UML. Initializer code is not analyzed as a body.
recommendation: Emit an NN_CLASS_DECL with an anonymous flag in NodeAttr for a class_body under object_creation_expression or enum_constant, and map bare class-body blocks to NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT.

title: A reloaded .tca cannot name its files: read() discards the paths and path_str_offset is reinterpreted
evidence: TokenCorpusArtifact has no path field. read() skips the path section (247-251) and returns the on-disk byte offset in path_str_offset. server.rs:714 and class_diagram.rs:132 resolve that field with interner.lookup_text as a text_id, its in-memory meaning (mod.rs:138), so after read() only file 0 resolves correctly. This differs from CORE-07: it is consumer-side data loss.
impact: Any tool built on TokenCorpusSerializer::read reports wrong file names in traces and in test-file detection.
recommendation: Add a file_paths field filled by both run() and read(), and give path_str_offset one documented meaning. Have write() take paths from the artifact; today a longer file_paths slice panics at serializer.rs:97. Add a round-trip test on resolved paths.

title: The tca_hash link and Phase 2 invariants 2-5 are documented as enforced but never checked
evidence: The spec says finalize() enforces Invariants 1-5 and that Phase 3 rejects a mismatched (TCA, BPA) pair. finalize() asserts only Invariant 1. No code compares bpa.tca_hash with the CRC of the .tca: symbol/serializer.rs:42-43 recomputes the CRCs but only stores them. The 'hash' is also a CRC-64, which is not collision-resistant.
impact: A stale or foreign .bpa paired with a different .tca is accepted silently, giving misattributed tokens and symbols.
recommendation: Verify bpa.tca_hash in Phase 3 and in the server, and fail with a clear error. Check Invariants 2-4 in debug builds or tests, consider SHA-256 for provenance links, and correct the spec.

title: Phase 2 silently skips files it cannot open or parse, and reopens paths relative to the working directory
evidence: Phase 2 rebuilds paths from the .tca, where they were stored with to_string_lossy exactly as given (often relative), and calls fs::read from the current directory. A non-UTF-8 path, a moved file, a different CWD or a parse failure each falls through nested `if let` with no else branch and no warning (mod.rs:141-154). This differs from CORE-10, which covers repeated reads.
impact: A file can have tokens but no AST and no error. Downstream phases quietly miss its classes and methods.
recommendation: Store canonical absolute paths, or a source root plus relative paths. Carry the bytes or a content hash over from Phase 1. Return an error, or at least log_warn with counts, for every skipped file.

title: SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute returns Result, but phases 7 to 10 panic on I/O errors
evidence: Phase7Stage::run through Phase10Stage::run return their artifacts directly and call panic! or expect when writing .tra, .psa, .uma or .scpg fails. execute() calls them without catch_unwind, so a full disk or a read-only output directory aborts the caller instead of yielding Err.
impact: Library and server callers crash on ordinary write failures. The builder's error contract is false.
recommendation: Change the four run() signatures to return Result, propagate with `?` in execute(), main.rs and server.rs, and add a test that uses a read-only output directory.

title: CGCSR::edges_of panics on the caller CSR because its edge_types array is always empty
evidence: edges_of checks `end <= self.adj.len()` and then slices `&self.edge_types[start..end]`. The caller CSR is built with `edge_types: Vec::new()` both in cg/mod.rs:175 and in the deserializer (serializer.rs:213). For any method with a caller, the slice range exceeds length 0 and panics. Nothing calls it yet, so the bug is latent.
impact: The first code that queries callers through this public API will crash on any non-leaf method.
recommendation: Bound the slice by edge_types.len() or fill the caller edge types. Better, give CGCSR a constructor that enforces equal adj and edge_types lengths. Add a unit test that calls caller_csr.edges_of.

title: The generic reducer erases identifiers and mis-types nodes by substring matching, even for JavaScript
evidence: identifier, property_identifier and JS formal_parameters fall to `_ => Eliminate`, so names and parameters produce no nodes. Kinds containing 'expression' become NN_EXPR_STMT (e.g. augmented_assignment_expression), and kinds containing 'declaration' become NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL (e.g. generator_function_declaration). function and arrow_function map to NN_METHOD_DECL, super maps to NN_THIS_EXPR, and encode_attrs always returns 0. This differs from CORE-01, which is about wrong grammars.
impact: JS ASTs carry no names, parameters or operators. Closures become methods and compound assignments are not treated as definitions.
recommendation: Replace the substring heuristics with explicit per-grammar tables. Keep identifiers as NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR, map function expressions to NN_LAMBDA_EXPR and augmented assignments to NN_ASSIGN_EXPR, and encode operators.

title: type_parameters becomes one NN_TYPE_PARAM node and each type_parameter is dropped
evidence: java.rs:83 keeps 'type_parameters', the whole `<K, V extends X>` list, as NN_TYPE_PARAM, while 'type_parameter' has no arm and is dropped. Because every child vanishes, the node's token range is just the `<` token. The semantic adapter turns that node into a single SK_TYPE_PARAM.
impact: Generic classes and methods get one nameless type-parameter symbol instead of one per parameter, and their bounds are lost.
recommendation: Eliminate type_parameters and Keep each type_parameter as NN_TYPE_PARAM, with its type_identifier and type_bound children.

title: select1 scans bit by bit and is O(n) for absent ranks; every navigation call pays this despite the O(1) claims
evidence: select1 binary-searches the superblocks, then loops over positions to bit_count calling bounds-checked get_bit for each bit (512 or more iterations), and scans to the end when the rank is missing. rank1 also builds its partial byte one bit at a time. first_child, next_sibling, subtree_size, is_leaf, depth and lca all start with a select1 call. This differs from CORE-06, which covers correctness.
impact: CFG and symbol traversals do hundreds of bit probes per step, far from the documented O(1) navigation.
recommendation: Store an open_pos[preorder] array or a sampled select index, use word popcount and broadword select, and correct the complexity claims in the docs.

title: Console logging uses println!/eprintln!, which panic on a closed pipe, and it mixes logs into stdout
evidence: log_event writes Info, Warn, Debug and Trace with println! and only Error with eprintln!. Both macros panic when the write fails, for example `openheart analyze src | head` (broken pipe) or a server whose console has closed. Warnings land on stdout alongside any program output. This differs from CORE-13, which covers the file sinks and the mutex.
impact: The CLI, or a server thread, can panic mid-run because a terminal or pipe closed.
recommendation: Write with writeln! to a locked stderr and ignore write errors, send all diagnostics to stderr, and keep stdout for command output.

title: Phases 1 and 2 have no incremental path, although hashes are recorded and the docs promise one
evidence: Per-file SHA-256 hashes and mtimes are stored but never compared. parse(source, None) never reuses an old tree or applies an InputEdit. Token ids and preorder indices form one global space with no per-file segments, so any edit renumbers everything. The docs describe incremental CST parsing and BP excision and insertion.
impact: Every change re-ingests and re-encodes the whole project, so IDE-style synchronization is impossible.
recommendation: Segment the corpus and the BP per file (file-local ids plus offset tables), skip files whose SHA-256 is unchanged, and keep per-file trees so tree-sitter can reparse incrementally.

title: NodeAttr has room for only 8 modifiers, so default, strictfp, non-sealed, varargs and Kotlin modifiers never reach symbols
evidence: NodeAttr packs modifiers into 8 bits (static through sealed). extract_modifiers builds SymbolModifiers from those bits alone, so STRICTFP, DEFAULT, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, DEPRECATED and RECORD_COMPONENT are unreachable. VISIBILITY_NONE and VISIBILITY_PACKAGE_PRIVATE both mean package access, and there is no Kotlin internal, open or override. This differs from CORE-03, which covers substring matching and the stub decoder.
impact: Interface default methods, varargs and Kotlin modifiers cannot be told apart in UML or symbol output.
recommendation: Widen the attribute word (u64, or a separate u16 modifier array), add the missing Java and Kotlin modifiers, and use a single package-private encoding.

title: close_node updates every open ancestor's token range, and that result is always overwritten
evidence: close_node walks the whole open_stack to merge the child's range (min/max) into every ancestor. The reducer already merges each child's returned (ft, lt) into its own range, and every ancestor's own close_node then overwrites its entry (line 164). The propagation is redundant O(depth) work per node.
impact: Deeply nested expressions make Phase 2 quadratic in nesting depth for no effect.
recommendation: Remove the ancestor loop, or propagate only to the parent, and assert in close_node that preorder_idx is the top of open_stack.

title: Phase 1 wraps columns above 65,535 while Phase 2 saturates them, so their sort keys disagree
evidence: walker.rs:59 uses `start.column as u16`, which wraps modulo 65,536. reducer.rs:56 uses `start.column.min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16`, which saturates at 65,535. On a minified line past column 65,535, Phase 2 builds keys that never match Phase 1's and falls back to an arbitrary token on the same line. This differs from CORE-05, which covers the cap itself.
impact: Nodes on very long lines are bound to the wrong tokens, corrupting ranges, names and traceability spans.
recommendation: Use one shared column-packing helper in both phases, ideally with a wider column field, and reject or flag files that exceed the limit.

title: Columns are tree-sitter byte offsets with mixed bases, which is undocumented
evidence: The walker stores `line: row + 1` (1-based) and `col: start.column` (a 0-based byte offset). With tabs or non-ASCII UTF-8 text, the byte column differs from the character or UTF-16 column that editors and LSP use. Neither token.rs nor the spec states the unit.
impact: L:C spans in traces and the web studio point to the wrong column on lines containing non-ASCII text.
recommendation: Document the unit. Either store character or UTF-16 columns, or convert in the traceability layer, and use consistent bases for line and column.

title: Phase 2 uses positions in the sorted forward index as token ids
evidence: Phase 2 reads Section 4, the forward table ordered by sort_key, and tok_table_lookup returns the binary-search index as the token id. Phase 1 token ids follow allocation order (SourceFileRecord.first_token_id and Section 5). The two coincide only while push order is already sorted, a dependency the spec itself admits.
impact: Any change to Phase 1 ordering, such as parallel ingestion or column wrap, silently desynchronizes AST token ranges from file token ranges.
recommendation: Resolve through the backward index and return the entry's token_id, or assert in finalize() that forward and backward order match, then drop the duplicate array.

title: Zero-width MISSING nodes become phantom tokens with empty text
evidence: walk_recursive emits every leaf without checking node.is_missing(). Tree-sitter error recovery inserts zero-width MISSING leaves (for example a missing `;` or identifier). These pass include_anonymous and map_node_type, are pushed with len 0 and are interned as an empty string. This differs from CORE-09: it is a concrete corruption of the corpus, not the general lack of an error model.
impact: Incomplete code produces fake punctuation and identifier tokens that downstream heuristics treat as real.
recommendation: Skip is_missing() leaves, or mark them in the sort-key flags byte, and count them as diagnostics.

title: Language detection ignores the adapter registry: ext_map is never read and detect() is a hardcoded static
evidence: register() fills ext_map, including a '*' key, but nothing reads it. detect() is an associated function with its own extension match, so a newly registered adapter's extensions are never detected. Overrides are looked up by the raw OsStr: case-sensitive, and a key with a leading dot never matches. IngestionStage builds its own registry, so callers cannot inject adapters.
impact: Adding a language means editing three places, and overrides silently fail for upper-case or dotted extensions.
recommendation: Make detect a method that uses ext_map, normalize override keys (lowercase, strip a leading dot), and let the manifest or the stage accept an AdapterRegistry.

title: The .tca string-header section is written but never used
evidence: write() emits a hash-sorted (fnv1a, offset) table at 12 B per string. read() parses it into str_headers and drops it, then rebuilds the interner by re-hashing and re-interning every stored string. String ids come back only because re-interning in storage order happens to reproduce them.
impact: The section wastes space and load time, and a duplicate string in storage would shift every later text_id.
recommendation: Either use the headers for zero-copy lookup (mmap plus binary search) or remove the section, and rebuild ids by position rather than by dedup.

title: TCA read() discards the filter flags, source-tree hash and timestamp; the tree hash ignores paths
evidence: read() binds _flags, _hash and _mtime (which is really the creation timestamp) and drops them, and the artifact has no fields to hold them. source_tree_hash hashes the per-file digests in path order without the paths themselves, so a rename that keeps the order goes unnoticed. The spec says SHA-256(sorted(...)) and promises LZ4 compression; neither is implemented.
impact: A reloaded corpus cannot be checked against its sources or its token filter, which blocks staleness checks.
recommendation: Store the filter, tree hash and timestamp in the artifact, include normalized paths in the tree hash, and align the spec with the code.

title: The TCA magic is written as a little-endian u64, so the file starts with reversed bytes
evidence: TCA_MAGIC = 0x544F4B434F525001 is documented as 'TOKCORP\x01', but write_u64 emits the bytes 01 50 52 4F 43 4B 4F 54, which read '\x01PROCKOT' (verified with Python struct). The .bpa writes its magic as a byte string, so the two formats use opposite conventions.
impact: File-type sniffing, hex inspection and external tools see a reversed signature.
recommendation: Write magics as byte strings everywhere (b'TOKCORP\x01'), and keep a compatibility reader for existing v1 files.

title: The .bpa header has a hardcoded file_count, an ignored version and no per-file root table
evidence: write() always stores file_count = 1 and format_version = 1, and read() discards both. node_types is written without a length prefix, unlike the other arrays. Nothing records which NN_MODULE root belongs to which file; consumers infer it from token ranges, which fails for nodes that have no tokens.
impact: Future format changes cannot be detected, the header is wrong, and mapping nodes to files is fragile.
recommendation: Write the real file count plus a per-file (file_id, root_preorder) table, validate the version on read, and length-prefix every array.

title: Phase 2 hand-parses .tca bytes with hardcoded offsets and cannot take the in-memory corpus
evidence: ASTStage::run accepts only a MemoryMappedFile. It re-implements the TCA layout (header offsets 12..16 and 16..18, record offset 36, alignment math) instead of calling TokenCorpusSerializer or using the TokenCorpusArtifact that Phase 1 just returned. It also builds an unused Phase1Registry. This differs from CORE-07, which covers missing validation.
impact: Two independent TCA parsers must change in lockstep, and every run forces a disk round-trip.
recommendation: Have ASTStage take a &TokenCorpusArtifact, or a zero-copy TCA view shared with the serializer, and delete the unused registry.

title: Phase 2 reserves memory for 2x token_count nodes, taken from the unvalidated header
evidence: tok_table reserves 16 B per header token, then BPASTBuilder::new(token_count * 2) reserves four preorder arrays (17 B per node) plus BP words, about 34 B per token, although kept nodes are usually fewer than tokens. token_count comes straight from the header with no check, so 0xFFFFFFFF requests over 140 GB and aborts. This differs from CORE-07 because it over-allocates even on valid input.
impact: Large corpora commit far more memory than needed, and a corrupt header aborts the process instead of returning Err.
recommendation: Estimate capacity from file sizes or grow dynamically, cap the reservation, and validate counts against the mapped length before reserving.

title: The interner hashes the full text but stores a truncated copy, and its u32 counters can wrap
evidence: intern() hashes all of the text, but store_string keeps only 65,535 bytes. For longer input `lookup_text(id) == text` never matches, so every call appends another copy. Storage offsets are `storage.len() as u32` and count is a u32, so both wrap past 4 GiB or 4 billion strings. Phase 1 truncates tokens before interning, but paths and other API callers are exposed.
impact: Repeated long strings grow memory without bound, and very large pools return wrong strings.
recommendation: Truncate or reject before hashing, use u64 offsets or checked arithmetic, and return an error when a limit is exceeded.

title: Interner and string-pool layouts waste memory
evidence: Each probe slot is (u64, u32), padded to 16 B, so the initial 65,536-slot table takes 1 MiB before any string is added. Storage keeps a u16 length prefix per string and also a separate u32 offsets array, so each length is effectively stored twice. The .tca then adds a 12 B header per string.
impact: Phase 1 holds about twice the necessary index memory for string-heavy corpora.
recommendation: Use (u32 hash fragment, u32 id) slots, derive lengths from consecutive offsets, and size the table from the expected number of unique strings.

title: The sort key's 'reserved' flags byte silently carries a duplicate counter that wraps at 256
evidence: The doc says bits 7..0 are reserved and zero, but Phase 1 ORs a dup_count into them when consecutive tokens share (file, line, col), for example zero-width tokens. dup_count is a u8 incremented with wrapping_add, so the 256th duplicate collides with the first. unpack_sort_key drops the byte. This differs from CORE-05.
impact: A collision aborts Phase 1 through Invariant 2, and readers cannot tell duplicate tokens apart.
recommendation: Document the byte as a discriminator, error out on overflow instead of wrapping, return it from unpack_sort_key, and remove the cause (no zero-width or wrapped tokens).

title: Log files grow without bound, session IDs collide within a second, and setup errors are swallowed
evidence: The persistent log is opened in append mode and never rotated or size-capped. The session ID has one-second resolution, so concurrent runs share an ID while both truncate the same session file. create_dir_all and open failures are discarded through `let _` and `.ok()`, and an unknown OPENHEART_LOG value is ignored without notice. This differs from CORE-13.
impact: Long-lived deployments fill disks, concurrent runs interleave their logs, and misconfiguration goes unnoticed.
recommendation: Add size-based rotation, build session IDs from the PID plus a nanosecond timestamp (or randomness), and warn on stderr when a log file cannot be opened or OPENHEART_LOG is invalid.

title: Infallible From<u8> conversions turn corrupt bytes into plausible values
evidence: Unknown bytes map to defaults: THRelation to TH_EXTENDS, SymbolKind to SK_EXTERNAL, CFGEdgeType to Uncond, ScopeKind to File, SymbolVisibility to Package, AssocKind to None, ASTNodeType to NN_UNKNOWN, and LangId and TokenType to Unknown. TokenType also uses from_u8/as_u8 while the other enums implement From.
impact: A corrupt or newer-version artifact yields fake inheritance edges and wrong kinds instead of an error.
recommendation: Implement TryFrom<u8> returning an error for unknown values, use it in every deserializer, and keep the lossy conversion only where it is explicitly wanted.

title: Record layout comments are wrong, and three repr(C) records have no size test
evidence: UMLAssociationRecord is documented as '28-byte fixed', but its repr(C) layout is 32 B, with padding after assoc_kind and is_navigable plus tail padding (checked with Python ctypes). SymbolRecord claims to be cache-aligned but has alignment 4. SSARecord claims '16-Byte Cache-Aligned' without repr(C) or align. Only SourceFileRecord, TokenRecord and TokenEntry have size_of tests.
impact: Anyone mapping these records zero-copy from disk will misread fields, and the comments mislead layout work.
recommendation: Reorder the fields (or pack carefully), fix the comments, and add size_of and align_of tests for SymbolRecord, ScopeRecord and UMLAssociationRecord.

title: Several TokenType and ASTNodeType variants are never produced
evidence: grep finds no producer for TokenType::TypeParameter, LabeledStmt, JavaGenericDiamond or JavaSealedKeyword; LabeledStmt and TypeParameter are syntactic categories, not lexical ones. NN_PATTERN_MATCH and NN_SYNTHETIC are never emitted. NN_ELSE_CLAUSE, NN_YIELD_STMT and NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT are covered by CORE2-03, CORE2-04 and CORE2-05.
impact: Consumers may write handling for kinds that never occur, and the alphabet misstates what Phases 1 and 2 emit.
recommendation: Remove or implement each variant, keep syntactic kinds out of the lexical alphabet, and document which adapter produces each value.

title: Flag constants in core types are never set, so is_polymorphic() always returns false
evidence: CALL_SITE_FLAG_IS_POLYMORPHIC, HAS_NULL_RECEIVER and IS_TAIL_CALL are never set (call_sites.rs:43 has `let flags = 0u8;`), so CallSite::is_polymorphic() is always false. SSA_FLAG_IS_PARAM_DEF, FIELD_DEF, RETURN_VAL and CONST, and CG_EDGE_REFLECTION, have no users outside core/types.
impact: The API advertises polymorphism, parameter and constant facts that are never computed.
recommendation: Set the flags where the information exists (virtual sites with several targets, parameter definitions), or delete the constants and the predicate.

title: The Artifact trait is implemented only by the token corpus and fixes the file count at u16
evidence: The doc says the trait is implemented by pipeline stage output artifacts, but only TokenCorpusArtifact implements it. token_count() and file_count() -> u16 are TCA concepts that do not fit the other artifacts, and the u16 writes the CORE-05 cap into the API.
impact: The trait adds no generic capability such as version checks, hashing or I/O, and it misleads readers.
recommendation: Redefine the trait around shared needs (magic, format_version, content_hash, write/read) and implement it for every artifact, or remove it.

title: The core module depends on every phase, inverting the layering
evidence: core::pipeline imports ast, cfg, cg, ingestion, psa, scpg, ssa, symbol, tra and uma, while all of those import core::types, core::io and core::logger. So 'core' is not a foundation layer, and a change to any phase touches the core API.
impact: Phases cannot be split into crates or tested in isolation, and dependency cycles stay hidden.
recommendation: Move SCPGPipelineBuilder and PipelineArtifacts to a top-level pipeline or driver module, and limit core to types, io and logging.

title: Error messages Debug-format strings and paths, which double-escapes them
evidence: execute() wraps String errors with `{:?}` (for example 'Phase 1 Ingestion Error: {:?}') and formats io::Error the same way; ingestion formats paths with `{:?}`. A Windows path therefore surfaces in quotes with backslashes doubled and then doubled again, and io errors appear as `Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, ... }`.
impact: Users see escaped, hard-to-read messages, unlike the CLI path, which uses `{}`.
recommendation: Format with `{}` and path.display(), or adopt a typed error enum with Display messages (thiserror is already a dependency).

title: The library pipeline writes graph.scpg where the CLI writes unified.scpg, and exposes no filter or override settings
evidence: SCPGPipelineBuilder names its Phase 10 output graph.scpg, while cmd_analyze and the usage text use unified.scpg. execute() always calls SourceManifest::new, so TokenFilter and language_overrides cannot be set through the builder. This is a concrete divergence on top of CORE-14's copy-paste finding.
impact: Tools that look for unified.scpg miss library output, and comment or doc-comment policy cannot be configured.
recommendation: Define the artifact file names once as shared constants, and add with_filter and with_language_override to the builder (or let it accept a SourceManifest).

title: BinaryReader allocates before reading, and the alignment helpers divide by zero
evidence: read_exact_bytes allocates `vec![0u8; len]` before read_exact, so a corrupt length allocates first and fails afterwards, and there is no remaining() to validate counts. align_to(0) and skip_alignment(0) compute `% 0` and panic. The .bpa serializer and Phase 2 bypass these helpers with hand-rolled try_into().unwrap() slicing. This differs from CORE-07: it is about hardening the helpers.
impact: Every reader built on these helpers inherits allocate-then-fail behavior, and the formats use inconsistent parsing code.
recommendation: Add remaining() and ensure(len) checks, read through take(len) into a growing Vec, reject an alignment of 0, and port the .bpa code to BinaryReader and BinaryWriter.

title: Loading a .bpa rebuilds rank/select and the sparse table, and both writers buffer the whole artifact
evidence: read() loads the persisted jump table, which could be rebuilt in one O(n) pass, yet rebuilds RankSelectIndex and the O(n log n) SparseTableRMQ on every load. Both writers assemble the entire file in a Vec, compute the CRC over it and only then write, holding a full second copy in memory. This differs from CORE-04 (resident size) and CORE-10 (source reads).
impact: Every load of a large AST costs O(n log n) time, and serialization roughly doubles peak memory.
recommendation: Persist the expensive indexes or build them lazily, and stream writes through a writer that updates the CRC as it goes.

title: BPASTArtifact::depth is 1-based while the builder's depth is 0-based, and four accessors are unused
evidence: depth() computes 2*rank1(open)-open-1, which gives 1 for a root, while BPASTBuilder::current_depth(), which is passed to classify, gives 0 for a root. Neither documents its base. grep finds no callers and no tests for depth, subtree_size, is_leaf or BPASTArtifact::lca.
impact: Off-by-one errors are likely once these APIs are used, and their correctness is unverified.
recommendation: Document a single depth base (0 for roots) and use it in both places, and add unit tests for each accessor against a naive pointer tree.

title: BPASTBuilder exposes mutable internals and panics instead of returning errors
evidence: All builder fields (bp, preorder, open_stack, node_count) are pub. close_node pops whatever is on top of the stack without checking that it matches preorder_idx. finalize() and JumpTableBuilder::build use assert! and expect on unbalanced input, so a buggy adapter crashes the process.
impact: Adapter bugs produce panics or silently malformed BP sequences rather than errors that can be diagnosed.
recommendation: Make the fields private, verify last-in-first-out closing in close_node, and return Result from finalize and from the jump-table builder.

title: Token classification runs the same string match twice per leaf
evidence: For anonymous leaves, include_anonymous calls map_node_type and the walker then calls it again, so two long match chains run per token. rustc lowers such matches to length and memcmp comparisons, not the 'perfect hash' the spec claims. walk_cst sizes its Vec from the root's child count, and its _source parameter is unused.
impact: Adds measurable per-token CPU in the hottest Phase 1 loop.
recommendation: Precompute a TokenType table indexed by node.kind_id() once per language, look it up once per leaf, and size the Vec from the source length.

title: tok_table_lookup binary-searches the whole corpus for every kept node
evidence: Every Keep node does a binary search over the tokens of all files, although nodes arrive in source order within a single file whose token range is known from first_token_id and file_token_count. This differs from CORE-12, which covers the lossy fallback.
impact: Phase 2 costs O(nodes x log tokens) instead of near-linear time.
recommendation: Restrict the search to the file's slice, and keep a forward-moving cursor with galloping search as the DFS advances.

title: Sources are assumed to be UTF-8, with no BOM or encoding handling
evidence: Files are read as raw bytes and passed to tree-sitter, and token text is interned as raw bytes. No code strips a UTF-8 BOM or decodes UTF-16 or Latin-1/Windows-1252 (grep finds none), and there is no javac-style encoding option. Downstream from_utf8 checks silently skip tokens that are not valid UTF-8.
impact: Legacy Windows-encoded Java files can yield ERROR nodes, shifted first-line columns and silently dropped identifiers.
recommendation: Detect and strip BOMs, support UTF-16 via its BOM, add a manifest encoding option that transcodes to UTF-8 before parsing, and record the encoding per file.

title: Phase 1 records file size from metadata read before the content, and some errors omit the file path
evidence: file_size_bytes comes from fs::metadata, taken before fs::read, so it can differ from the content that was hashed. The second read fails with 'Read error: {}' and a parse failure reports 'Tree-sitter parse returned None'; neither message names the file.
impact: Recorded sizes can contradict the hashes, and failures in large trees are hard to locate.
recommendation: Use content.len() for the size, and include path.display() in every per-file error with map_err at the call site.

title: Low-level accessors return silent sentinel values for invalid input
evidence: get_bit returns 0 (a close paren) past the end. range_min returns position 0 for out-of-range bounds. lookup_text returns an empty slice for invalid ids or corrupt offsets. node_type, node_attr, token_range and parent return NN_UNKNOWN, 0, (MAX, 0) and MAX. None of them logs or distinguishes bad input from legitimate values.
impact: Index bugs and corrupt artifacts show up as wrong results far from their cause.
recommendation: Return Option or Result from these accessors, or debug_assert on out-of-range input, and keep sentinel fallbacks only at API boundaries.

title: The Phase 1 round-trip test compares only lengths, and there is no multi-file test
evidence: test_phase1_end_to_end_on_java_sample checks counts and interned strings, but never compares file_records, token_records or token_entries field by field, which would have exposed the path_str_offset change. It uses a single file and asserts only that there are more than 10 tokens.
impact: Serialization regressions and file-ordering bugs pass CI.
recommendation: Add tca_roundtrip_preserves_all_fields (assert_eq! on every record and on resolved paths) and multi_file_ingestion_is_order_independent (three files in shuffled order, checking file_id, first_token_id continuity and sort order).

title: There are no negative tests for TokenCorpusSerializer::read or BPASTSerializer::read
evidence: Neither test file exercises the checksum, magic, version or minimum-size error branches. Every read in the tests is of a valid file that was just written.
impact: The error paths can regress into panics or into accepting corrupt files without any test noticing.
recommendation: Add tca_read_rejects_flipped_byte, tca_read_rejects_bad_magic, tca_read_rejects_bad_version and tca_read_rejects_truncated, plus matching bpa_read_* tests.

title: The Java reduction test passes an empty token table and checks no node types
evidence: test_java_cst_reduction_end_to_end passes `&[]` as tok_table, so tok_table_lookup and token_ranges are never exercised. It asserts no node-type sequence, so it misses the duplicated NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL for `int x = 42;`. The round trip compares 4 of the 7 artifact fields, and the 'Invariants 1-5' comment skips Invariant 3.
impact: Mapping regressions such as CORE2-01 to CORE2-05 go undetected.
recommendation: Run Phase 1 on the sample to get a real token table, assert the exact preorder node types and token ranges, use assert_eq!(loaded, artifact), and add cases for an enum, an enhanced for loop, an anonymous class and generics.

title: Unit tests are missing for interner growth, language detection, the caller CSR, the binary helpers and logger configuration
evidence: The interner has only a three-string dedup test, with no coverage of resize, find_id misses or long strings. detect(), CGCSR::edges_of, BinaryWriter/BinaryReader and init_logger_from_env have no tests at all.
impact: The latent panics and silent failures in these helpers are never caught.
recommendation: Add interner_resize_keeps_ids (100k strings from capacity 16), find_id_absent_returns_max, detect_override_case_and_dot, caller_csr_edges_of_no_panic, binary_align_roundtrip_and_zero_alignment and log_level_env_parsing.

title: ruthless_verify.py reports CONVERGENCE ACHIEVED and exits 0 when nothing was verified
evidence: verify_repo returns None on server errors (321-327) or missing dirs (278-280). main() starts all_pass=True (433) and clears it only inside the loop over all_results (434-438). With zero results it prints the trophy line (443) and returns 0 (457). Reproduced in scratchpad with the server unreachable: exit 0. test_full_suite.py:241-243 then logs PASS.
impact: The tool behind the F1=1.0 claim passes whenever the server is down or target_repos is empty.
recommendation: Count skipped and failed repos. Fail when no repo produced metrics or any repo errored. Print verified/attempted counts. Add a unit test for main() with an unreachable server.

title: generate_diagrams.py looks for its config in scripts/ and silently writes zero diagrams
evidence: Line 62 builds cfg_path from os.path.dirname(__file__), which is scripts/, but ruthless_config.json lives at the repo root. exists() is False, so diagram_mapping=[] (67), the loop at 73 writes nothing, and the script prints 'Saved 0' and exits 0. CHANGELOG.md:33 advertises 14 .puml files. The hint at 45 names ./restart_server.sh, which is actually in scripts/.
impact: The documented diagram generator never produces output and still reports success.
recommendation: Resolve Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'ruthless_config.json'. Exit non-zero when the config is missing or no diagram is saved. Fix the hint path.

ENG.note: scripts/generate_diagrams.py is outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Ground truth and engine output are compared by simple class name only
evidence: All three oracles store results[name] (95, 174, 218). Ground truth is set(o1.keys()) (300), and parse_puml_classes returns a set of bare names (225-234). Two classes named Utils in different packages count once, so losing one goes unnoticed. Which file or package wins depends on os.walk order, which varies by filesystem.
impact: Recall is overstated on repos with repeated simple names, and package attribution is nondeterministic.
recommendation: Key on fully qualified names (package plus nesting) and compare multisets. Have the engine export FQNs through a JSON export for scoring.

title: 'Pkg Nesting' accuracy is precision-only and computed from the wrong diagram
evidence: puml_package is fetched (340) but never used; packages are parsed from the class diagram instead (343). pkg_accuracy is pkg_metrics['precision'] (367, 395), so an engine that emits no packages scores 100% (verified: compute_metrics(gt, empty) gives precision 1.0). parse_puml_packages (236-241) reads only quoted labels, while the ground truth uses dotted names. Neither side is normalized.
impact: The package metric cannot detect missing or wrong package structure.
recommendation: Parse the package diagram and normalize names to dotted FQNs. Report precision, recall and F1, and include the package result in the pass criterion at 435.

title: Oracle regexes miss common Java and Kotlin declaration forms
evidence: Tested in scratchpad. The Java pattern (line 4) misses sealed, non-sealed and strictfp types, '@Entity public class', 'final public class', 'abstract static class' and 'public final static class'. The Kotlin pattern (7) misses value class, fun interface, companion object, 'open data class', multi-modifier and annotated declarations. ruthless_verify.py:66-69 also skips every directory named build, out or dist, including real packages.
impact: Ground truth undercounts classes in exactly the hard cases, which inflates recall and F1.
recommendation: Build the oracle with an independent real parser (javaparser, Kotlin PSI or tree-sitter queries), or at least use a repeated-modifier group. Add a fixture file for each declaration form.

title: test_diagrams_outputs_refresh.py passes the diagram section when every analysis fails
evidence: When post_analyze raises, test_all_14_diagrams_syntax prints a message and hits 'continue' (155-160) before total is incremented (163). If the server or network fails for all four repos, the function returns passed == total == 0, which is True. CLI results at 217, 239 and 252 are never checked, so a failed run surfaces as FileNotFoundError on open() instead of a FAIL.
impact: Outages show up as green runs or tracebacks instead of test failures.
recommendation: Count each failed analysis as a failed check. Check CLI exit codes before reading artifacts. Return False when total is 0.

title: test_authored_design_patterns.py relies on vacuous and substring assertions
evidence: act_ok checks 'start' in act_puml (328), and 'start' always matches '@startuml'. Member checks search the whole diagram text for substrings ('instance' 216, 'buildCpu' 235, 'convertVideo' 264, 'mine' 291). Packages pass on substring with 12 of 14 accepted (309-310). Enums are never parsed (77-94). The CRC 'or Artifact' fallback (164; refresh:125) repeats the pattern already reported at test_ruthless:113.
impact: Regressions in pattern and diagram output pass unnoticed.
recommendation: Assert on structured JSON export: exact members per class, exact edge sets, and real activity start/stop nodes. Remove the substring fallbacks.

title: Harness docstrings advertise checks the scripts never perform
evidence: benchmark_all:8-9 promises artifact verification and syntax checks for 14 diagrams. It requests 5 diagram types (85), checks no artifact, and parses relations (68-72) that it then discards (111). test_authored:12 claims CRC-64 checks on all artifacts but inspects 6 of 10 (160). test_ruthless:100 omits .tra, .psa and .uma. refresh:8 claims 'edge consistency' but checks only header, footer and braces.
impact: Readers overestimate what the evaluation actually covers.
recommendation: Implement the promised checks (inspect all 10 artifacts, score inheritance edges with precision and recall) or correct the docstrings.

ENG.note: The harness scripts are outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Diagram 'syntax validation' is header/footer and brace counting, not a parser
evidence: validate_plantuml_syntax (refresh:55-72), validate_diagram_syntax (verify_all_14:59-75) and test_ruthless:126 accept any text that starts with @startuml, ends with @enduml and has equal counts of '{' and '}'. Braces inside labels or notes skew the count. Bad arrows or undefined aliases pass. No PlantUML or Mermaid parser runs anywhere.
impact: Exporter regressions that break rendering go uncaught.
recommendation: Add a CI job that runs a pinned plantuml.jar with -checkonly and mermaid-cli over the exported diagrams for the example corpora, and keep golden snapshots.

title: Six harness scripts copy the same client and server-bootstrap code, and the copies have drifted
evidence: post_analyze, run_cmd, log_test and the fuser+Popen+sleep bootstrap are duplicated in all six scripts (e.g. benchmark:30-49,154-162; full_suite:32-55,253-260). They already differ: timeouts of 30, 60 or 300 s, port 8085 versus 8080, and verify_all_14:133 reads 'error' while the server returns 'errors'. All assume CWD is the repo root (os.getcwd() binary path).
impact: Every fix must be made six times, and behaviour already differs between scripts.
recommendation: Extract a shared harness package: a pytest server fixture with health polling, a client and scoring helpers. Resolve paths from __file__ and take the port and timeouts from env.

ENG.note: The harness scripts are outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Harness tests whatever target/debug binary exists and waits a fixed 2 s for readiness
evidence: OPENHEART_BIN is target/debug/openheart (benchmark:27, test_ruthless:24, authored:34, refresh:23, verify_14:32, full_suite:256), and no script builds it, so a stale binary gets tested silently. Readiness is time.sleep(2) (e.g. benchmark:162). Server stdout and stderr go to DEVNULL (159-160), so crashes look like analysis failures.
impact: Results may describe an old build, and startup failures get misdiagnosed.
recommendation: Run cargo build --locked first (a release build for timings). Poll /api/health with a deadline. Write server output to a log file and print it on failure.

ENG.note: The harness scripts are outside my paths; handoff given. The new `make studio-smoke` shows the intended pattern: fresh release build, health polling with a deadline, server log printed on failure.

title: Scripts SIGKILL any process listening on the benchmark port
evidence: restart_server.sh:11-14 runs kill -9 on every PID lsof finds on the port. The Python harnesses run 'fuser -k PORT/tcp' (benchmark:155, test_ruthless:276, authored:169, refresh:274, full_suite:253, verify_14:160). Whatever owns 8080 or 8085 (another dev server, a proxy) is killed with no check or prompt, and SIGKILL prevents cleanup.
impact: Running a benchmark can kill unrelated local services.
recommendation: Start the server on an ephemeral port and track its PID. If the port is busy, fail with a clear message. Send SIGTERM and wait before escalating.

ENG.note: New Makefile targets never kill anything: studio-smoke refuses a busy port and stops only the PID it started, using SIGTERM and wait. restart_server.sh is already safe. Removing `fuser -k` from the Python harnesses is in handoffs.

title: The Python harness and the web studio have no CI at all
evidence: ci.yml:40-47 runs only cargo check, fmt and test. The nine Python scripts and web/js (published by deploy_pages.yml:30-37) are never compiled, linted or run. That is how defects such as generate_diagrams.py:62 and ruthless_verify.py:433-457 shipped. This differs from ENG-10 and AUTO-15, which are about Rust lint gates.
impact: Half of the repository's code can break with no signal.
recommendation: Add a job that runs py_compile, ruff and unit tests for the scoring helpers, plus node --check or eslint on web/js, and a headless smoke test of index.html against a built server.

ENG.note: Added Makefile gates: py-check (compiles every harness script), py-lint (ruff), js-check (node --check on every web/js ES module) and ci-scripts (all three; also run by ci-full). Also added studio-smoke, which serves the studio from a release build and fetches /api/health, / and every module. Wiring these into CI is in handoffs.

title: Pages deploy runs on every push to main regardless of CI status
evidence: The deploy triggers on push to main and workflow_dispatch (3-6). It has no needs or workflow_run dependency on ci.yml and no paths filter, so it runs in parallel with CI. A commit that fails CI is still published to the live studio, and Rust-only commits redeploy the site.
impact: Broken web builds go live, and unneeded deploys churn the Pages environment.
recommendation: Trigger on workflow_run of 'Continuous Integration' with conclusion == success (or merge into one workflow using needs), and add paths: ['web/**'].

ENG.note: deploy_pages.yml is outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Release workflow lacks contents: write and uses the deprecated action-gh-release@v1
evidence: There is no permissions block (1-28). With the read-only default GITHUB_TOKEN of newer repos, action-gh-release cannot create a release (403). @v1 (22) is the Node 16 generation. No tests run, the tag is never checked against Cargo.toml's 0.1.0, and no checksums are published. This differs from ENG-13 (never run, ships an .rlib).
impact: Tagging v* probably fails, and a successful run could publish an untested, mis-versioned artifact.
recommendation: Add job-level permissions: contents: write. Use a SHA-pinned v2. Run cargo test --locked first, assert the tag matches the package version, and attach SHA256SUMS.

title: Unseeded FNV-1a with low-bit indexing makes string interning hash-floodable
evidence: ADR-001 (technical-decisions.md:9-13) picks FNV-1a over SipHash and lists 'avalanche-free distribution' as a benefit. interner.rs:53 uses slot = hash & mask with linear probing (70). FNV-1a's low k bits depend only on the low k bits of state and input, so low-bit multicollisions can be chained cheaply. The server analyses arbitrary repos (AUTO-02).
impact: A crafted repository can make interning quadratic, a CPU denial of service against the server.
recommendation: Use a randomly keyed hash (SipHash-1-3, ahash or foldhash) for the table, and keep FNV only where a stable persisted hash is needed. Correct the ADR rationale and add a collision stress test.

title: security-architecture.md has no threat model for the server, git clone or web studio
evidence: The document (1-34) covers only Phase 1 ingestion, hashing and bounds. It never mentions the HTTP server binding all interfaces, /api/source file serving, CORS, cloning user-supplied URLs, request or clone limits, or the studio's GitHub calls. AUTO-01 and AUTO-02 report the code defects; this finding is the missing design document.
impact: Deployers cannot tell what is safe to expose, and reviewers have no stated trust boundaries.
recommendation: Add a threat model covering assets, trust boundaries, default bind address, authentication, request and clone limits, clone sandboxing and a file-access allowlist. Link it from SECURITY.md.

title: The 12 HTML specs under docs/ are chat-widget fragments that break when opened standalone
evidence: None of the files has a doctype, html element or charset. Each starts with a style block that uses host CSS variables (var(--surface-1), --border, --text-primary) defined nowhere. Buttons call sendPrompt('...') (e.g. phase8:299-301; 6-23 calls per file), a chat-host function that does not exist, so each click throws a ReferenceError. No index links these files. AUTO-19 covers their duplication only.
impact: About half the visual design docs render unstyled and have dead controls.
recommendation: Convert them to standalone pages with a doctype, charset and defined tokens. Replace sendPrompt with anchors or static text. Index them in docs/README.md, or export them to SVG or Markdown.

title: The research paper cannot compile because its bibliography file is missing
evidence: Lines 1397-1398 use \bibliography{openheart}, but no .bib file is tracked. A scripted check found 26 cite keys (cytron91, bryant86, reps95, munroraman97 and others) with no source, so every citation renders as [?]. amssymb is loaded twice (4, 16), and the author block is a redaction placeholder (80-82).
impact: The paper cannot be built or reviewed as committed.
recommendation: Commit openheart.bib (or inline a thebibliography block) and add a latexmk CI job that fails on undefined citations.

title: The paper's Limitations section cites mitigations the code does not implement
evidence: tex:1311-1314 claims non-series-parallel CFGs get k<=3 unwinding via Valdes SP recognition. No SP recognizer exists, and RecursiveHandler::apply returns f_paths unchanged (recursive.rs:26-28), for recursion only. tex:1320-1324 says reflective sites are tagged CG_Reflection, but CG_EDGE_REFLECTION (cg.rs:13) is unused. tex:1391 calls a full implementation 'future work'. 'Anderson' (785, 1317) should be Andersen.
impact: The stated soundness boundaries are fictional, which overstates where the theorems apply.
recommendation: Implement SP detection and reflection tagging, or rewrite Limitations to match the code. Reconcile the paper's status with the README and fix the author name.

title: ruthless_verify.py ignores ignore_dirs and overrides package_stmt_patterns from its config

title: ruthless_verify.py re-slices the file prefix for every regex match
evidence: For each match, oracle_regex builds content[:match.start()] twice (90 and 93) to count backticks and newlines. That costs O(file size) per match, or O(n*m) per file. The backtick-parity heuristic (91) ignores escapes and comments, and its extension list omits .mts and .cts, which line 142 does handle.
impact: The oracle is slow on large or minified files, and JS ground truth is wrong around template literals.
recommendation: Precompute newline offsets once and bisect into them. Tokenize template literals in one pass, and share one extension set.

title: Pass thresholds differ by script and contradict the printed 'F1=1.0' message
evidence: ruthless_verify passes at f1 >= 0.999 (435) yet prints 'ALL REPOS PASS F1=1.0' (443). test_ruthless:219 passes at recall >= 0.85 and F1 >= 0.80, and its 'Invariant' hierarchy check accepts 5 of 6 (160). benchmark:210 needs recall >= 0.85, and authored:310 accepts 12 of 14 packages. None of these thresholds is documented.

title: test_full_suite.py matches test counts as substrings and can crash on error paths

Line 159 targets tests/adapters_tests.rs, which does not exist. If /api/analyze returns non-JSON, line 143 raises NameError because diagrams is unbound. Line 122 accepts HTTP 200 for a malformed body.

title: test_full_suite.py requires the legacy files and the wildcard CORS policy

recommendation: Derive the route list from index.html imports. Assert an explicit allowed origin, or no CORS header, instead of '*'.

title: Harness output prints fixed success figures regardless of outcome
evidence: benchmark:201 always prints '(100.0%)', the banners hardcode 176 modules (3, 138, 199), and line 202 divides by total_analyzed, which raises ZeroDivisionError when no module is found. full_suite:243 prints 'F1=1.0000 across Android, Java, Kotlin, JS, Rust' even on FAIL. test_ruthless:114 and 140 and refresh:126 and 203 print fixed detail strings.

title: The Python harness cannot run on Windows, the maintainer's platform
evidence: The scripts depend on fuser and lsof, call 'python3' (full_suite:241) and write under /tmp. The box-drawing and emoji output crashes when stdout is piped on cp1252: in scratchpad, ruthless_verify.py raised UnicodeEncodeError at line 402. full_suite:159-228 runs cargo test while openheart.exe is running, and Windows locks the file against relinking (medium confidence).

title: Python scripts have unused imports, broad excepts and shell=True with unquoted paths
evidence: Unused imports: shutil, ThreadPoolExecutor and as_completed (benchmark:19, 23), defaultdict (ruthless_verify:14). 'except Exception' swallows errors without detail (benchmark:91, 119-120). ruthless_verify:324 catches (URLError, Exception). Every run_cmd uses shell=True with f-string paths (e.g. test_ruthless:94, authored:143), which breaks on paths containing spaces.

title: CI cache key ignores the compiler version and is never refreshed
evidence: ci.yml:29-38 caches target/ under '<os>-cargo-<stable|beta>-<hash(Cargo.lock)>' with no restore-keys. When stable or beta advances, the restored target/ is unusable and everything rebuilds. actions/cache does not re-save on an exact key hit, so every run rebuilds until Cargo.lock changes, and any lockfile change starts cold.
impact: CI is slow and wastes runner minutes.
recommendation: Use Swatinem/rust-cache, which keys on rustc -vV and prunes target/, or add the rustc version hash to the key plus restore-keys.

title: CI job ordering and matrix settings waste time and let beta block merges

impact: CI may test, and releases may ship, dependency versions that were never reviewed.
recommendation: Add --locked to every cargo invocation in CI, the release workflow, the Makefile and ci_check.sh.

No docker ecosystem entry covers the Dockerfile base image. Major bumps (thiserror 2, sha2 0.11) were merged on a compile-only gate.

recommendation: Add a tree-sitter group and a docker ecosystem entry, and label semver-major updates for manual review.

title: The dev profile compiles at opt-level 2 and the release profile is untuned

It also means the 'debug' binaries the scripts use are optimised. There is no [profile.release] (lto, codegen-units = 1) for the shipped binary. ENG-14 covers only the overflow-checks setting.

title: .editorconfig gives .yml files a 4-space indent and puts spaces in Makefile recipes
evidence: '[*.yml]' (20) is an empty section, so the indent rules that follow apply only to *.yaml, and every workflow inherits indent_size 4 from [*]. [*] sets indent_style = space with no Makefile override, so EditorConfig-aware editors turn recipe tabs into spaces and make fails with 'missing separator'. *.bat files inherit end_of_line = lf.
impact: Editors corrupt the Makefile and mis-indent the workflows.
recommendation: Use [*.{yml,yaml}], add [Makefile] with indent_style = tab, and add [*.{bat,cmd}] with end_of_line = crlf.

title: .gitattributes forces LF on run.bat and marks only one artifact type as binary
evidence: '* text=auto eol=lf' (2) has no *.bat or *.cmd override, so run.bat is checked out with LF endings, and cmd.exe can misparse labels and goto in LF-only batch files. Only *.tca, png, jpg and ico are marked binary (13-16). The other nine artifact types, webp, mp4, pdf and fonts rely on autodetection.
impact: The Windows launcher may misbehave, and binary files risk end-of-line conversion or text diffs.
recommendation: Add '*.bat text eol=crlf' and '*.cmd text eol=crlf', plus binary rules for every artifact and media type.

title: .gitignore negations never apply and several patterns over-match
evidence: '.vscode/' (92) excludes the whole directory, so the negations at 93-96 have no effect (git check-ignore confirms settings.json is ignored). 'sample_codebase/*' (61) ignores the tracked fixture directory, and the .gitkeep it re-includes does not exist. Unanchored build/, dist/, env/ and out/ (18-19, 34-35, 53) match nested directories. The output directories from examples/README are not ignored.
impact: Shared editor settings and new fixtures cannot be committed, and generated output pollutes git status.
recommendation: Use '.vscode/*', anchor root-only patterns with '/', drop the sample_codebase rule, and add output_*/.
