title: security-architecture.md calls CRC-64 tamper protection and misstates the interner bounds
evidence: Lines 16-20 present CRC-64 as 'Tamper Protection', but an attacker can simply recompute a CRC, and the SHA-256 digests written in ingestion/mod.rs:56-97 are never re-verified. Line 27 says u16 lengths prevent unbounded allocation. In fact interner.rs:99 truncates tokens over 64 KiB and line 67 then never matches them, so each occurrence is stored again. ENG-17 covered only lines 11-12, 26 and 34.
impact: Readers assume tamper evidence that does not exist, and long tokens bloat storage.
recommendation: Call it corruption detection or add a keyed MAC. Verify the SHA-256 digests on load. Store full token text or reject oversize tokens explicitly.

title: README and codebase-guide list artifact magic headers that do not exist
evidence: README.md:113-124 and codebase-guide.md:272-283 list TCA\0, BPA\0, SSA\0 and so on. The code uses 'TOKCORP\x01', b'BPAST\0\x01\0', 'SSA1', b'OPENHPSA' and b'OPENHUMA'. u64 magics are written little-endian (binary.rs:40-41), so the STA, CFA, CGA and TCA bytes appear reversed on disk. CFA_MAGIC contains '0' where its comment says \0, and phase2 spec:946 shows a 15-digit hex magic.
impact: Anyone who writes a reader or file-type detector from these docs gets it wrong.
recommendation: Define magics as byte arrays written verbatim, generate the table from the constants, and fix the source comments.

title: Docs claim CRC-64 on all ten artifacts, but .scpg uses CRC-32 and inspect skips verification
evidence: README.md:59 says all 10 phases produce CRC-64 verified artifacts, and 10_phase_pipeline_overview.md:85 says Phase 10 verifies CRC-64. The .scpg writer uses per-section CRC-32 (serializer/mod.rs:22, 111). 'inspect' on a .scpg prints 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' without checking any checksum (main.rs:469-474). The help text (main.rs:56) lists 6 inspectable types, although inspect handles 10.
impact: Integrity guarantees are overstated, and the inspect output is misleading.
recommendation: Verify the section CRCs in inspect, print a factual status, and correct the docs and help text.

title: Docs give contradictory token and traceability record layouts
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:53 describes the sort_key as 48/24/8 bits, which is 80 bits in a u64; the code packs 16/24/16 plus a reserved byte (token.rs:121-124). traceability:29 calls the key u48, and line 36 gives a '10-byte' backward-index entry whose fields sum to 9 bytes (the real entry is 16). succinct_structures.md:121-122 says 12 and 10 bytes, where both are 16. The UMLLink struct in traceability:57-68 does not match tra/types.rs:99-109.
impact: Contributors who write readers or review invariants work from wrong layouts.
recommendation: Keep one layout reference generated from the const asserts and link every doc to it.

title: The 'cache-line aligned' TokenRecord and 'hardware-friendly' CRC claims are inaccurate
evidence: ADR-003 (technical-decisions.md:25-29), CHANGELOG.md:50 and overview.md:9 call the 16-byte TokenRecord cache-line aligned. It is repr(C) with 8-byte alignment (token.rs:136-145), and the .tca token table is only 8-byte aligned, so a record can straddle two cache lines. ADR-004 (33-37) calls the CRC 'fast hardware-friendly', but crc64_ecma is a bit-at-a-time loop (serializer.rs:16-29).
impact: The ADRs' performance rationale does not describe the actual implementation.
recommendation: Use #[repr(C, align(16))] with 64-byte section alignment, or reword the claim. Switch to a table-driven (slicing-by-8) CRC.

title: overview.md and architecture.md define the layers as both disjoint and strict subsets
evidence: overview.md:37-51 and architecture.md:35-56 define V as a disjoint union of five layers and then assert V_tok ⊂ V_syn ⊂ V_bb ⊂ V_sym. That is impossible for disjoint non-empty sets, V_ssa is left out, and the docs derive O(1) projection from it. The paper's caption (tex:485-491) reinterprets ⊂ as 'anchored'. traceability:17-20 also mislabels phases 3, 4 and 5.
impact: The formal model is self-contradictory as written.
recommendation: Replace the subset chain with anchoring functions into token ranges, state the O(1) claim as a property of the stored arrays, and fix the phase labels.

title: architecture.md lists ROBDD and BP operations that do not exist
evidence: architecture.md:119 says the ROBDD layer uses complement edges, but ROBDDNode (node.rs:44-58) has no complement bit; flag bits 2-15 are reserved. architecture.md:106 and succinct_structures.md:32-34 promise O(1) findopen, findclose and enclose over the BP bitstring. No such primitives exist, and first_child and next_sibling live on the builder's arrays (builder.rs:58-71).
impact: Readers credit the engine with algorithms it does not have.
recommendation: Remove these claims, or implement the operations with tests.

title: succinct_structures.md uses the wrong probe-count formula and a wrong baseline size
evidence: Line 81 gives E[probes] = 1/(1-α) = 4 for linear probing at α = 0.75, but that is the uniform-hashing bound. Knuth's linear-probing costs at that load are about 2.5 probes for a hit and 8.5 for a miss. The pointer-AST baseline at lines 40-41 ({u32, u64, u64, u64, u32}) takes 40 bytes with natural alignment, not 32.
impact: The document's complexity and memory comparisons are off.
recommendation: Use ½(1+1/(1-α)) for hits and ½(1+1/(1-α)²) for misses, and recompute the baseline with alignment.

title: The Phase 2 spec understates its sparse-table size by about 140 MB
evidence: Lines 967-969 compute Σ_{k=0}^{20}(2M-2^k) × 4 B as about 20 MB. The sum is roughly 39.9M entries, or about 160 MB. The 20 MB figure feeds the totals at 933, 971 (45.75 MB) and 1003 (92 MB peak). phase1 spec:675 calls tree-sitter 'GLL, linear', but it is GLR. BENCH-03 measured the code; this finding is about the spec's own arithmetic.
impact: The design document's own memory budget is wrong.
recommendation: Fix the arithmetic. If the budget matters, specify an RMQ structure with O(n) words, such as a block decomposition.

recommendation: Add docs/format/ generated from the constants, with a format-version changelog, and mark the plans as superseded.

title: The scoring helpers have no unit tests
evidence: compute_metrics (247-270), parse_puml_classes and parse_puml_packages (225-241), the three oracles, and parse_class_diagram (authored:66-122) have no tests. Unit tests would have caught the empty-set, duplicate-name, threshold and zero-repo defects found in this pass.
impact: Metric bugs flow straight into published numbers.
recommendation: Add pytest tests: test_compute_metrics_empty_produced, test_compute_metrics_empty_truth, test_parse_puml_classes_generics_and_stereotypes, test_oracle_regex_sealed_and_annotated, test_main_fails_when_no_repo_verified, test_pkg_metric_uses_recall.

title: The ADR log covers four micro-decisions and leaves out the major ones
evidence: The file has ADR-001 to ADR-004 (FNV-1a, token_id, TokenRecord, CRC), with no status, date, alternatives or consequences. No record exists for the single-crate layout, the hand-rolled HTTP server, the unsafe BDD arena, the tree-sitter 0.20 pin, little-endian u64 magics, or the web studio's separate regex extractor.
impact: Reviewers cannot see why the risky choices were made or when to revisit them.
recommendation: Adopt a MADR template and record the major decisions, including the options that were rejected.

title: Empty then/else and loop bodies become dead ends that the builder wires to EXIT
evidence: Each builder connects a branch or body to its join, update block or header only if current_block moved or the entry block has statements. For `if (c) {}`, `while (c) {}` or `for (n = head; n.next != null; n = n.next) {}` the entry block keeps no successor, so the sink loop adds an edge to EXIT. `if (c) {} else { return; }` leaves the join unreachable, and all later code is pruned.
impact: The true branch of an empty body appears to leave the method, loops lose their back edge, and following code can vanish.
recommendation: Always connect the final block of a branch or body, even when empty, to the join, update block or header, and delete the emptiness heuristic. This is separate from FLOW-01, which covers the try/do-while pending-edge path.

title: Def extraction ignores ++/--, compound and chained assignments, and multi-declarator lists
evidence: update_expression maps to NN_UNARY_EXPR and reaches the default branch, so `i++` is only a use. NN_ASSIGN_EXPR pushes the LHS as a def without checking the operator, so `s += i` misses the read of s. `a = b = 0` never visits the inner assignment. `int a = 1, b = 2;` yields one def. `o.f = v` and `a[i] = v` define the access node itself.
impact: Loop counters and accumulators are never redefined, so φs at loop headers cannot appear even after FLOW-04's keying is fixed.
recommendation: Walk expressions recursively in evaluation order. Treat ++/-- and compound assignment as a use plus a def, recurse into nested assignments, emit one def per variable_declarator, and model stores as heap writes plus uses of the base and index. This differs from FLOW-04, which is about identity keying.

title: Use extraction stops one operand deep and skips declaration initializers
evidence: For NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL only direct NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR children count, but the initializer sits under the nested variable_declarator, so `int y = a + b;` records no uses. For assignments and binaries, operands are pushed as raw nodes without recursion: `x = foo(a)` and `(a + b) * c` record the call or binary node id as a variable and miss a and b.
impact: Most real uses are never seen, so liveness, pruned φ placement and def-use chains stay empty even after keying is fixed.
recommendation: Recurse into every operand subtree and declarator initializer, and emit uses only for identifiers that resolve to variables. Add unit tests for each expression shape. This differs from FLOW-04 (identity) and FLOW-16 (granularity).

title: No entry definitions for parameters, this, captured variables or fields
evidence: Parameters are NN_PARAM_DECL children of the declaration and are never placed in a block. ENTRY is empty, and rename_dfs starts from an empty VersionStack. Uses with no reaching def are silently dropped (`current_ver != u32::MAX`), and φ args get u32::MAX. SSA_FLAG_IS_PARAM_DEF, IS_FIELD_DEF, IS_RETURN_VAL and IS_CONST are never set anywhere.
impact: Parameter-to-use flows, which taint and null analyses need, cannot exist even after FLOW-04 is fixed.
recommendation: Emit version-0 defs in ENTRY for each parameter, `this` and captured variables (optionally fields too), with the flags set. Use an explicit undefined version instead of u32::MAX, and count undefined uses.

title: Non-variable identifiers and nested closure bodies are counted as uses/defs of the enclosing statement
evidence: Every NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR counts as a use: method names in `foo(x)`, selectors in `a.b`, break/continue labels, enum case labels and lambda parameters. The default branch also recurses into lambda, anonymous-class and local-class bodies inside a statement, so their assignments are credited to the enclosing block. Phase 4 also builds separate CFGs for those same lambdas.
impact: Spurious liveness and defs. Closure side effects appear to run at creation time and are attributed twice.
recommendation: Classify identifier roles (variable, member name, label) through the symbol table. Stop recursion at NN_LAMBDA_EXPR, class declarations and anonymous class bodies, and model captures explicitly.

title: φ order and SSA numbering depend on HashMap iteration order
evidence: place_phi_functions iterates `var_defsites: HashMap<u32, HashSet<u32>>` and seeds each worklist from a HashSet; both follow per-process RandomState order. pending_phis order drives phi_by_block, which assigns φ ssa_ids before each block's ordinary defs, so every later id shifts between runs.
impact: Once φs exist, .ssa bytes, ssa_hash links and downstream ids are not reproducible from run to run.
recommendation: Use BTreeMap/BTreeSet, or sort variables and def sites before placement. Add a test that runs Phase 5 twice and byte-compares the .ssa output.

title: φ operands are recorded as anonymous u32::MAX uses in the def-use CSR
evidence: When rename_dfs fills φ arguments, it pushes u32::MAX into the reaching def's use list instead of the φ's ssa_id or block, and stores arg_ssa_id = u32::MAX when no def reaches. Ordinary uses store the statement node, repeated once per occurrence. DefUseCSR documents none of these conventions.
impact: Def-use walks cannot continue through φ-functions, and every consumer has to special-case the sentinels.
recommendation: Record φ uses as the φ's ssa_id (or as a tagged entry), dedupe per statement, use an explicit undefined def, and document what use_adj contains.

title: Switch case-label detection marks every case group as default
evidence: build_switch counts a group as labelled only when its first child is NN_LITERAL or NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR. The Java reducer drops switch_label (unlisted kind, `_ => Drop`), so the first child is a statement and has_default is set for every group. Qualified constants such as Color.RED, constant expressions and patterns would also be read as default. Labels are never recorded.
impact: After FLOW-02's body loss is fixed, switches without a default still lose their selector-to-exit edge, and case values are gone.
recommendation: Keep switch_label (and switch_rule) in the adapter, detect `default` explicitly, record every label of a group on the Switch edge, and suppress fall-through for arrow rules. This differs from FLOW-02 (dropped body) and FLOW-08 (switch expressions).

title: Catch bodies collapse into one opaque statement because the catch parameter is dropped
evidence: The Java adapter does not map catch_formal_parameter, so the reducer drops it. In build_try the first child of NN_CATCH_CLAUSE is then the body block: it goes in as a single statement through add_stmt_to_current, next_sibling() is None, and the body is never dispatched. resolve_catch_type always sees a block and returns u32::MAX.
impact: Even after FLOW-01 is fixed, returns, throws and branches inside catch blocks produce no edges, and the catch variable is never defined.
recommendation: Keep catch_formal_parameter as NN_PARAM_DECL, or find the body by node type instead of position. Dispatch the block and define the catch variable. This differs from FLOW-07 (exception-edge semantics).

title: Enhanced-for loop variable is defined once in the pre-header
evidence: build_enhanced_for adds both the loop-variable node and the iterable to the block before the header. The header holds no statement, and neither the per-iteration assignment nor the implicit iterator()/hasNext()/next() calls appear anywhere.
impact: SSA sees one def outside the loop (no φ and no per-iteration def), and the call graph misses the Iterator calls.
recommendation: Keep the iterable in the pre-header. Add a synthetic hasNext condition to the header and the variable def (next) at the top of body_entry, and emit the implicit call sites. This is separate from FLOW-03's child-selection bug.

title: while(true) gets a spurious exit edge, inconsistent with for(;;)
evidence: build_while always adds a header-to-exit False edge, so `while (true) { ... }` without a break has a path out of the loop and the code after it stays reachable. build_for omits the False edge when there is no condition, so the two infinite-loop forms produce different CFGs and post-dominator trees.
impact: Infeasible exit paths distort post-dominance, the CDG and PSA summaries for common worker and server loops.
recommendation: Fold literal true conditions in while and do-while into an unconditional edge, as for(;;) already does. Optionally add a constant-condition pass. This is constant folding, not the label or short-circuit issues in FLOW-08.

title: Expression-bodied lambdas, field initializers and instance initializers get no CFG
evidence: Phase 4 handles only method, constructor, static-init and lambda symbols, and it needs an NN_BLOCK child. `x -> x.foo()` is skipped as if it were abstract. Field initializers and instance-initializer blocks have no function-like symbol at all. FLOW-02 covers dropped constructor bodies; these are different constructs.
impact: Code in these places has no CFG, SSA or block mapping, so calls inside them have no block context.
recommendation: Build a one-block CFG for expression lambdas. Synthesize per-class <init>/<clinit> CFGs from field initializers and initializer blocks, and splice them into constructors. This differs from FLOW-12, which covers the call-graph side.

title: Points-to allocation seeding can never fire
evidence: Seeding requires `bpa.node_type(rec.def_stmt) == NN_NEW_EXPR`, but def_stmt is the enclosing block statement (for `Foo f = new Foo();` it is NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL), never the new-expression itself. pts therefore stays empty, and resolve_1cfa's fallback has the same dead test.
impact: The only points-to constraint that is implemented can never trigger, so receiver-based resolution never adds anything.
recommendation: Record the defining RHS expression in SSARecord (or in a side table) and seed allocations from it. This differs from FLOW-11, which covers missing constraint kinds and merged ids.

title: Lambda creation sites become lambda-to-lambda self-loops marked self-recursive
evidence: find_enclosing_method starts at the call node itself, so for an NN_LAMBDA_EXPR site the caller is the lambda's own SK_LAMBDA symbol. resolve_dynamic step 1 returns the same lambda. The edge is lambda-to-lambda, Tarjan classifies every lambda as SELF_RECURSIVE, and the enclosing method gets no edge to its lambda.
impact: Every lambda is reported as recursive, and method-to-lambda relationships are missing from the call graph and SCC data.
recommendation: For lambda and method-reference sites, start the caller search at parent(node), emit a creation edge from the enclosing method, and model invocation through the functional-interface method. This differs from FLOW-05, which is about the callee side.

title: call_site_id no longer equals vector position after an unstable sort
evidence: Ids are assigned in AST pre-order, then `sites.sort_unstable_by_key(|s| s.caller_sym)` reorders the vector. TRA's BICsEntry, documented as indexed by call_site_id, and cs_span both use vector position as the id. The unstable sort can also put one caller's sites out of source order, and sequence diagrams take their message ordinals from that order.
impact: TRA call-site ids point at the wrong CGA sites, and diagram message order can differ from source order.
recommendation: Sort stably by (caller, node) and assign ids after sorting, or keep pre-order. Assert call_sites[i].call_site_id == i in assert_invariants.

title: CGCSR::edges_of panics on the caller CSR
evidence: edges_of checks `end <= adj.len()` but then slices `edge_types[start..end]`. caller_csr is built and deserialized with `edge_types: Vec::new()`, so edges_of panics with an out-of-range slice for any method whose CSR offset is non-zero. Nothing calls it yet, but it is public API.
impact: The first who-calls-me query through this public accessor crashes the process.
recommendation: Also check edge_types.len() and return an empty kind slice, or store caller edge kinds; separate types for the two CSRs would be cleaner. Add a unit test that calls caller_csr.edges_of.

title: .cga deserializer pre-allocates from untrusted counts
evidence: deserialize calls Vec::with_capacity(n) for every count read from the file: call sites, CSR arrays, the edge map, points-to and SCCs. CRC-64 is not a MAC, so a crafted file passed to `openheart inspect` with call_site_count = 0xFFFFFFFF asks for about 112 GiB and aborts the process before any read error is returned.
impact: Denial of service against `inspect` or any loader that opens a foreign .cga file.
recommendation: Before allocating, bound each count by the remaining bytes divided by the record size (or grow the vectors incrementally), and reject counts that contradict method_count.

title: classify_call never emits INTERFACE and dispatches super calls virtually
evidence: The INTERFACE test compares the resolved method symbol's kind with SK_INTERFACE, which a method can never have; it should test the declaring type. `super.m()` receivers (NN_SUPER_EXPR) are not checked, so super calls are VIRTUAL and go through CHA to overrides. Final methods and classes are never devirtualized.
impact: Edge kinds are wrong, and super calls gain spurious override targets.
recommendation: Check the parent type's kind for INTERFACE, classify super calls as SPECIAL, and use DIRECT for final, private and static targets. This differs from FLOW-05, which is about the wrong target symbol.

title: Hot-loop trace logging is always formatted and flushed to two log files
evidence: Phases 4-6 emit one format!-built log line per call site and about eight per function. log_event writes every level to both the persistent and session files under a mutex, with two write_all and two flush calls, whatever the console level. The CLI enables both files (main.rs:129).
impact: Millions of flushed writes and unbounded log growth on large codebases.
recommendation: Gate formatting behind a level check or a macro, filter file output by level, keep per-site and per-function messages at trace, and stop flushing on every line.

title: More quadratic scans in Phases 4-6 that FLOW-13 does not list
evidence: resolve_1cfa scans every symbol per allocated type and every SSA record of every function per virtual site. points_to scans all φ records for each φ def. find_block_for_stmt searches functions linearly per site. analyze_loops allocates and sweeps n flags per back edge. DF and CDG dedupe with Vec::contains/any, and every throw clones the exception stack.
impact: O(sites×records), O(φ²) and O(back_edges×n) costs on large inputs.
recommendation: Pre-index symbols by (parent, name), SSA and φ records by id per function, and functions by sym_id. Dedupe with bitsets or hash sets, and compute loops in one loop-nesting-forest pass.

title: No heap or field SSA (Memory SSA)
evidence: Only local identifiers are versioned. Field and array accesses have no memory versions, SSA_FLAG_IS_FIELD_DEF is never set, and calls carry no may-def or may-use of heap state.
impact: Flow through fields, arrays and object state, which is most Java data flow, is invisible to SSA, IFDS and slicing.
recommendation: Add Memory SSA (heap φs per alias class from points-to), or field-based SSA for this.f accesses, plus may-def/may-use summaries at call sites.

title: Add golden CFG tests for each statement builder
evidence: tests/cfg_tests.rs only checks that counts are non-zero and that idom[0] == 0. No test checks the edges produced by build_if, build_while, build_for, build_enhanced_for, build_switch, build_break/build_continue or build_return/build_throw.
impact: The empty-body, edge-type and switch defects above all pass CI.
recommendation: Add test_cfg_if_empty_then_reaches_join, test_cfg_while_empty_body_backedge, test_cfg_for_update_backedge, test_cfg_switch_no_default_exit, test_cfg_break_in_switch_in_loop and test_cfg_return_single_stmt. Each should assert the exact (from, to, type) edge list for a small Java snippet.

title: Add unit and property tests for the graph algorithms
evidence: The only analysis test is a 4-node diamond. compute_idom_cooper on loops, compute_dominance_frontiers at loop headers, analyze_loops on nested loops, compute_post_idom and CDGBuilder::build have no tests.
impact: Regressions in dominance, post-dominance and the CDG go undetected.
recommendation: Add test_idom_nested_loops, test_df_loop_header_contains_self, test_analyze_loops_nested_depth, test_post_idom_diamond and test_cdg_if_else_labels, plus a proptest that checks Cooper idom and DF against brute-force dominance on random graphs.

title: Add SSA construction tests
evidence: tests/ssa_tests.rs only asserts total_ssa_vars >= 1. extract_stmt_vars, LivenessAnalysis::compute, place_phi_functions and rename_function have no direct tests, and determinism is never checked.
impact: SSA can stay entirely φ-free without any test failing.
recommendation: Add test_extract_vars_increment_compound_initializer, test_liveness_loop_counter, test_phi_at_if_join_and_loop_header, test_rename_phi_args_match_preds, test_param_entry_defs and test_phase5_output_deterministic (run Phase 5 twice and compare bytes).

title: Add call-graph and SCC tests
evidence: tests/cg_tests.rs only asserts method_count > 0 and that SCCs exist. Nothing checks specific edges, call_site_id ordering, lambda handling, CHA over overrides, Tarjan classification, Tarjan's output order (which PSA relies on) or CGCSR::edges_of.
impact: The self-loop, id-mismatch and panic defects all pass CI.
recommendation: Add test_cg_main_calls_helper, test_call_site_id_equals_index, test_lambda_not_self_recursive, test_cha_override_targets, test_tarjan_self_mutual_and_reverse_topo_order (on a synthetic adjacency) and test_caller_csr_edges_of_no_panic.

title: Branch edge types are inconsistent across loop and switch builders
evidence: The do-while taken branch is typed LoopBack, so that branch has a False edge with no True partner. A switch's no-match edge is typed False. for(;;) types its unconditional header-to-body edge True. CFGEdgeType has no way to mark an edge as both True and a back edge.
impact: CDG, PSA and diagram consumers that key on True/False see malformed conditional branches.
recommendation: Separate branch polarity from a back-edge flag. Use True/False for do-while, a Switch/Default kind for the no-match edge, and Uncond for for(;;).

title: Empty-statement then-branch drops the condition or swaps branches
evidence: The reducer drops `;`, so `if (c) ;` has a single child and build_if returns before recording the condition, which loses its side effects. `if (c) ; else f();` has children [c, f()], so f() is wired as the True branch and there is no else. FLOW-03 covers the matching while/for cases.
impact: Rare, but it silently inverts branch semantics.
recommendation: Select children by tree-sitter field (consequence/alternative), recorded as a node attribute, or keep an empty-statement node.

title: return and throw register both the expression and the statement
evidence: build_return and build_throw add the child expression and then the enclosing statement node to the same block. extract_stmt_vars recurses into the statement and visits the expression again, so `return x = y;` creates two SSA defs, uses are recorded twice, and the block's statement lists overlap.
impact: Duplicate SSA records and use entries, plus overlapping statements in traceability.
recommendation: Add only the statement node (or only the expression plus a terminator marker), and do it the same way in every builder.

title: assert statements and ternary expressions are treated as straight-line code
evidence: NN_JAVA_ASSERT_STMT and NN_TERNARY_EXPR fall through to add_stmt_to_current, so the assert's conditional AssertionError throw and the ternary's two arms never become branches. FLOW-08 covers && / || and switch expressions but not these two.
impact: Branch points and exceptional exits are missing from the CFG and CDG.
recommendation: Lower assert to `if (!cond) throw` (optionally behind an -ea flag), and lower ternaries to diamond sub-CFGs once an expression IR exists (FLOW-16).

title: Pending-exit list is global and is flushed or drained at inconsistent points
evidence: pending_exits is a single unscoped list. build_if drains all of it, including edges an enclosing construct left pending, and routes them to its own join. Loops flush outer pending edges into the header and body pending edges as LoopBack. No builder flushes when it creates then_entry or case_entry. All of this is latent today because add_pending_exit is never called (FLOW-01).
impact: The obvious fix for FLOW-01, emitting pending exits, would misroute edges across constructs.
recommendation: Scope pending edges per construct (a stack of frames, or have each builder return them), and flush only at the construct's own continuation block.

title: CDG labels every non-False dependence TRUE and has no ENTRY augmentation
evidence: cd_type is CD_EDGE_FALSE only for CFGEdgeType::False, so Switch, Except, Return, LoopBack and Uncond dependences are all labeled TRUE, and dedupe keeps only the first label per target. There is no ENTRY-to-EXIT augmentation edge (the builder's intended one is dead code), so top-level statements have no controlling node.
impact: Switch-case and exceptional dependences cannot be told apart from true-branch dependences.
recommendation: Add CD labels for switch cases (with the label index) and for exceptional edges, and add the standard START-to-STOP edge before building the CDG. This differs from FLOW-09, which is about wrong post-dominators.

title: 1-CFA results replace CHA instead of refining it; a missing symbol falls back to name_id 0
evidence: For a virtual call, any non-empty 1-CFA target set is returned and CHA is skipped, so a receiver with only partial points-to (assigned from a parameter on another path) loses targets. When the target symbol is missing, name_id defaults to 0 and matches every method whose name id is 0.
impact: Unsound under-approximation once points-to works, and spurious targets when an id is bad.
recommendation: Use points-to only to filter CHA candidates, and only when the set is known to be complete. Return no targets when the symbol is missing.

title: CHA and 1-CFA keep bodiless interface methods as concrete targets
evidence: Targets are filtered with `modifiers & ABSTRACT == 0`, but ABSTRACT is set only when the source text contains the `abstract` keyword. Implicitly abstract interface methods pass the filter and become call targets next to their implementations. FLOW-12's name-only and downward-only points are different.
impact: Call edges point into declarations that have no body, inflating fan-out.
recommendation: In the filter, treat a method with no NN_BLOCK body, or an interface method that is neither default nor static, as abstract.

title: Duplicate caller-to-callee pairs keep only the first edge kind
evidence: callee_adj_lists dedupes by callee and keeps the etype of the first site seen. A caller that reaches the same callee both directly and virtually shows only one kind in callee_csr.edge_types. FLOW-19's every-symbol span is a different issue.
impact: Edge-kind data depends on the order of call sites.
recommendation: Treat the per-site edges as authoritative, and store an OR-ed kind mask or one entry per kind in the CSR.

title: Artifact readers skip version and structural validation
evidence: The CGA, CFA and SSA readers accept any format_version. CGA does not check offsets.len() == method_count+1, monotonic offsets, adj ids < method_count, SCC member ranges or trailing bytes. CFGArtifact hard-codes format_version 1 instead of using a constant like SSA_VERSION or CGA_FORMAT_VERSION.
impact: Stale or malformed artifacts load without error and can make later consumers panic.
recommendation: Reject unknown versions, validate CSR and SCC invariants after loading, and define CFA_VERSION.

title: Magic comments do not match the bytes on disk, and .cfa u32 arrays are unaligned
evidence: CFA_MAGIC is written little-endian as 00 00 01 00 30 41 46 43, not the commented ASCII CFA prefix, and 0x30 is the character '0', not NUL. CGA_MAGIC is written as 00 00 00 01 00 41 47 43. In .cfa, the idom u32 array follows the u8 edge_types array with no padding, so a zero-copy mmap reader would read misaligned data.
impact: External readers written from the comments will not recognize the files, and future mmap readers will hit misalignment.
recommendation: Define the magics as byte arrays and write them verbatim, as .ssa already does with SSA1. Pad to 4 bytes after u8 arrays.

title: Artifact writes are not atomic and buffer the whole file in memory
evidence: All three serializers build the complete file in a Vec, doubling peak memory, then truncate and rewrite the destination in place with File::create or fs::write. There is no temp file, fsync or rename. SSASerializer also throws away every write Result with `let _ =`.
impact: An interrupted run leaves a truncated artifact, and large projects pay a high peak-memory cost.
recommendation: Stream through a BufWriter with an incremental CRC, write to path.tmp, fsync, then rename. Propagate write errors.

title: Misleading algorithm names, invariant logs and missing Phase 6 timer
evidence: Anderson is a misspelling of Andersen. resolve_1cfa filters by receiver allocation and is not call-string 1-CFA. Phase 6 logs Invariants 1-4 as asserted after three checks, and logs a count mismatch as Invariant 1 verified. Invariant 2 cannot fail, because find_method_name_token never returns u32::MAX. Phase 6 skips PhaseTimer, so its duration is never reported.
impact: Names and logs overstate what is implemented and verified.
recommendation: Rename (AndersenPointsTo, resolve_by_receiver_alloc), report the mismatch as a warning, implement or drop the missing invariant, and use PhaseTimer.

title: Phase 4-6 invariant checks are mostly vacuous, yet any failure aborts the whole run
evidence: The unique-EXIT and idom-defined checks hold by construction. The Single Assignment check only confirms that sequentially allocated ssa_ids are unique, and Invariant 3 compares a single offset. Nothing checks edge ranges, entry/exit degree, CSR monotonicity or that defs dominate uses. Any failure returns Err for the whole program, so the server fails the request.
impact: The checks miss real defects, while a single odd function would sink an entire analysis.
recommendation: Add meaningful invariants (defs dominate uses, CSR consistency) and run them in tests. In production, log and skip the offending function instead of aborting.

title: Silent integer truncation in metrics, versions and offsets
evidence: cyclomatic is cast `as u16` and wraps above 65535; this is the cast, not FLOW-17's formula issues. SSA versions are u16 incremented with `*ver += 1`, so they panic in debug builds or wrap in release after 65,536 defs. Directory offsets in .cfa and .ssa are u32 and wrap beyond 4 GiB.
impact: Wrong metrics or panics on generated or very large code.
recommendation: Use checked or saturating arithmetic with error paths, and widen the version, count and offset fields.

title: Liveness fixpoint stops silently after 100 iterations
evidence: The backward fixpoint loop runs while `changed && iter_count < 100` and logs nothing when the cap ends it. Pruned φ placement then reads partially converged live_in sets. This is a correctness concern, separate from FLOW-13's cost concern.
impact: Silent under-approximation and missing φs on pathological CFGs.
recommendation: Use a worklist over reverse RPO without an arbitrary cap (it terminates on its own), or log an error and fall back to minimal SSA when the cap is hit.

title: Recursive AST walks in CFG construction and def/use extraction
evidence: dispatch_stmt recurses through build_if and the other builders for every nested statement, two frames per else-if level. extract_stmt_vars recurses through nested expressions such as fluent call chains. Neither has a depth limit. FLOW-14 covers recursion over CFG size, not these AST-depth walks.
impact: Deep else-if chains or generated code can overflow the stack in Phases 4-5.
recommendation: Use explicit work stacks, or enforce a depth limit with a graceful fallback. Phase 2's reducer uses the same recursive pattern.

title: Core type docs overstate layouts and leave sentinels undocumented
evidence: SSARecord is described as Cache-Aligned but has no repr or align attribute, and the fixed-size CallSite, CallEdge and SCCRecord have no repr(C). CFGEdgeType::from maps unknown bytes to Uncond without error. BasicBlock's u32::MAX/0 token sentinel for empty blocks is undocumented, and TRA maps it to token 0.
impact: Readers rely on layout guarantees that do not exist, and corrupt edge bytes go unnoticed.
recommendation: Add repr(C) with size asserts or drop the claims, implement TryFrom for CFGEdgeType, and document every sentinel.

title: IFDSResults taint tuple means different things to its producer and its consumer
evidence: ifds.rs stores (ssa_id, 1), where the u16 is a taint-source id. PSA feasibility reads the same u16 as a block id and treats every branch in block 1 as complex whenever any taint fact exists. IFDSResults documents neither field. FLOW-10 covers the stub logic itself, not this contract.
impact: PSA misclassifies block-1 branches and ignores tainted branches in all other blocks.
recommendation: Document the tuple and store the def block (or use a struct with named fields), and have PSA look up blocks through SSARecord.

title: Dead code and unused results across Phases 4-6
evidence: The ENTRY-to-EXIT fallback condition is always false, because the entry-to-first_real edge always exists. pred_lists, the _succs parameter, PendingPhi.target_ssa, block_phi_map, live_out, the returned ipdom, site_to_targets, MOD_ABSTRACT and the CallEdge type are never used. `receiver.is_none()` is unreachable, because a method_invocation always has a name child.
impact: Readers are misled about what is actually computed, and the work is wasted.
recommendation: Delete each item or wire it up (for example, persist ipdom and use block_phi_map).

title: No block-merging pass, so CFGs carry many empty pass-through blocks
evidence: Every if creates a join block, and every loop and switch an exit block. ENTRY always flows into a separate first block. Chains of single-predecessor, single-successor blocks are never merged, and edges are stored twice: in `edges` and in the succ/pred CSR.
impact: Inflated block counts and memory, plus noisier diagrams and metrics.
recommendation: Add a compaction pass that merges straight-line block chains while keeping ENTRY and EXIT, and build the CSR without keeping the edge list.

title: Pruned blocks that still contain statements are discarded silently
evidence: Compaction keeps only RPO-reachable blocks and drops the rest without logging anything. Statements lost to builder bugs (FLOW-01, FLOW2-01) or to genuinely dead code disappear without a trace.
impact: Construction bugs that delete code are hard to detect, and unreachable code cannot be reported.
recommendation: Count and log (or record in the artifact) pruned blocks that held statements, and fail tests when a non-synthetic block is pruned unexpectedly.

title: Add zero-copy CFG accessors and cache per-statement def/use sets
evidence: get_succs is duplicated in liveness.rs and renaming.rs, and each copy, like get_dominance_frontier, allocates a Vec on every call. extract_stmt_vars runs three times per statement. Liveness uses HashMap<u32, HashSet<u32>> keyed by dense block ids.
impact: Avoidable allocation and hashing in the hottest SSA loops.
recommendation: Add FunctionCFGData::succs/preds/df(b) returning &[u32], compute def/use once per statement into a side table, and use Vec-indexed bitsets for live-in and live-out.

title: Add serializer robustness tests
evidence: The round-trip tests compare header counts only. No test covers truncated files, unknown versions, huge counts or the byte-level magic layout.
impact: The allocation DoS and format drift go unnoticed.
recommendation: Add test_cga_rejects_huge_counts_without_alloc, test_cga_truncated_returns_err, test_readers_reject_unknown_version and test_magic_bytes_layout. Once the readers decode functions (FLOW-18), add full payload-equality round trips.

title: Phase10Stage::run panics on I/O failure instead of returning Result
evidence: src/scpg/mod.rs:53-55 wraps SCPGSerializer::write in .expect("Phase 10: Failed to write unified .scpg binary file"). Its callers return Result and use ?/map_err for every other phase: SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute (src/core/pipeline.rs:151, 223) and cmd_analyze (src/main.rs:101, 243). The spec declares -> Result<OpenHeartEngine> (docs/plans/phase10.md:302). The written file is never re-opened to validate it.
impact: A read-only output dir, full disk or locked file aborts the CLI or a library caller instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Return io::Result<OpenHeartEngine> (or a typed error) and propagate it with ? in pipeline.rs and main.rs. Optionally re-open the file with OpenHeartEngine::open to validate it, and pass a PipelineArtifacts-style struct instead of 10 positional parameters.

title: scpg_hash changes on every run, so it is not a content fingerprint
evidence: bpa.tca_hash is crc64 of the whole .tca file (src/ast/mod.rs:48). The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() (src/ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84), file mtimes (:115) and paths as given (:93-101). That hash, the link hashes derived from it, and tra.hashes.tca_hash (crc of Debug(file_records), which includes mtime_ns, hash_chain.rs:36) all feed compose_scpg_hash (serializer/mod.rs:124-134).
impact: Identical sources get a new scpg_hash on every run, so cross-run caching, staleness checks and 'hash unchanged' incremental semantics cannot work.
recommendation: Hash content only: keep timestamps, mtimes and absolute paths out of link hashes (for example, use sorted content_sha256 plus relative paths), or give each artifact a deterministic content hash. Add a test that builds the same sources twice and asserts equal scpg_hash. This is distinct from SCPG-13's header timestamp field.

title: Two incompatible scpg_hash definitions (Phase 7 links vs Phase 10 header)
evidence: Every UMLLinkRecord and ClassRecord stores tra.hashes.scpg_hash, which is crc32_ieee of the XOR of 6 Phase-7 hashes (src/tra/uml_link/hash_chain.rs:43-44, src/tra/builder.rs:41, src/uma/structural/class_diagram.rs:316). The .scpg header and OpenHeartEngine::scpg_hash use an XOR-fold of 9 different inputs (src/scpg/serializer/integrity.rs:29-38). StaleDetector::is_stale tests record.scpg_hash != current (src/tra/delta/invalidation.rs:10-11).
impact: Checking links against the engine or .scpg hash, which is the documented staleness protocol, flags every link as stale.
recommendation: Define one canonical scpg_hash function, compute it once, and stamp it into links, class records and the header, or rename one value (for example tra_chain_hash). Add a test asserting header.scpg_hash == tra.uml_links[0].scpg_hash on a fresh build.

title: Phase 10 never verifies that the nine input artifacts come from the same build
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:124-134 only XORs hashes. Checkable link invariants are ignored: bpa.tca_hash == sta.tca_hash (src/ast/mod.rs:48, src/symbol/serializer.rs:43), sta.bpa_hash == cfa.bpa_hash (src/cfg/mod.rs:31), cfa.sta_hash == cga.sta_hash (src/cfg/mod.rs:30, src/cg/mod.rs:46) and ssa.cfa_hash == psa.cfa_hash. docs/plans/phase10.md:526 claims 'Strict hash-chain integrity across all 9 artifacts'.
impact: A stale .cga or .psa combined with fresh upstream artifacts produces a .scpg and an engine that silently mix inconsistent graphs.
recommendation: Before writing, compare each artifact's recorded upstream hashes with its siblings (or recompute them from bytes) and return InvalidData naming the broken link. Add a test that passes a CGA built from other sources and expects an error.

title: Query cache key ignores the artifacts passed with each call
evidence: OpenHeartEngine::is_reachable and backward_slice take cga, sta and ssa on every call (src/scpg/api/mod.rs:51-72), but QueryKey holds only query_type, the ids and self.scpg_hash (src/scpg/query/mod.rs:46-50, 70-74). The engine stores no artifacts and never checks that the supplied ones match its hash. This differs from SCPG-10 (hash toggle) and SCPG-14 (key strength).
impact: Querying with a rebuilt or different CGA returns answers cached from the earlier graph, and mismatched artifacts are accepted silently.
recommendation: Let the engine own or borrow its artifacts and drop the per-call parameters, or add an artifact fingerprint to QueryKey and reject artifacts whose link hashes disagree with the engine or header.

title: Header source_hash is always zero, so a stale .scpg cannot be detected
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:146 writes [0u8; 32] as source_hash. The spec defines it as SHA-256 of sorted per-file SHA-256s (docs/plans/phase10.md:24) and claims it 'detects out-of-date SCPG' (:549). Ingestion already computes per-file content_sha256 (src/ingestion/mod.rs:55-58) and a source_tree_hash (:93-97) that it writes into the .tca. Nothing reads the field.
impact: Consumers cannot tell whether a .scpg matches the current sources, so they may serve a stale graph.
recommendation: Compute SHA-256 over the sorted (relative path, content_sha256) pairs from tca.file_records, write it at offset 16, and add an is_up_to_date(sources) check that OpenHeartEngine::open and the CLI can use.

DOCS.note: phase10.md defines source_hash (SHA-256 of sorted path/digest pairs) and notes the zeros; checklist marks it not implemented; code handed off

title: Comment and whitespace edits are classified as needing no rebuild, which leaves positions stale
evidence: RebuildPlanner::classify returns RebuildScope::None when is_comment_or_ws_only is set (src/scpg/incremental/mod.rs:11-12), following docs/plans/phase10.md:384 'token positions unchanged'. Adding a blank line or a comment shifts the line/col of every later token (TCA sort keys) and of the TRA spans. apply_delta still changes the hash for None (:28), contradicting phase10.md:400.
impact: Once this is wired up, navigation and click-to-source point at wrong lines after any comment edit, and no-op edits flush the caches.
recommendation: Add a PositionsOnly scope that re-lexes the file and re-indexes TCA/TRA spans without rerunning the semantic phases. Keep None only for edits that move no offsets, and leave the hash unchanged for None. Fix the spec as well.

DOCS.note: phase10 classify spec gains a PositionsOnly scope (re-lex and re-index spans), None only for offset-free edits, and an unchanged hash for None; code handed off

title: Engine exposes only 2 of the specified queries; the other query modules have no callers
evidence: OpenHeartEngine and QueryEngine route only is_reachable and backward_slice (src/scpg/api/mod.rs:51-72, src/scpg/query/mod.rs:39-83). SliceEngine::forward_slice, ImpactAnalyzer::impact_set, NavigationEngine::from_source and ROBDDQueryEngine::path_count/cyclomatic have no caller anywhere (grep). Spec section 10.7 (docs/plans/phase10.md:444-516) lists callers_of, callees_of, subtypes_of, find_symbol, stats, to/from_source and more.
impact: Most query code cannot be reached through the public API, is uncached, and is untested. This is the in-process gap, separate from SCPG-19's interop point.
recommendation: Add engine methods for forward_slice, impact_set, to_source/from_source, path_count/cyclomatic, callers_of/callees_of (via CGCSR), subtypes_of/supertypes_of (STA th_edges) and find_symbol(qualified name), routed through QueryEngine with typed keys. Add one test per method.

title: End-to-end SCPG test checks only output prefixes and a constant banner
evidence: tests/scpg_tests.rs:131-165 asserts starts_with("classDiagram"), contains("@startuml") and summary.contains("Generated all 14 UML Diagram Types"). That banner is a fixed prefix that generate_summary always emits (src/scpg/diagram/mod.rs:27-29). Nothing checks for SystemCompleteTest, the entryPoint->workerA->workerB chain, or the name field. This differs from SCPG-12's x || !x lines.
impact: Exporters, reachability and slices could return empty or wrong content and the test would still pass.
recommendation: Resolve method ids by name from sta. Assert is_reachable(entryPoint, workerB) and !is_reachable(workerB, entryPoint), check slice contents and the class name and members in each export, and compare the summary counts with the uma lengths.

title: No tests for the .scpg format: section CRCs, header fields, malformed files
evidence: Only the magic, the directory length and scpg_hash are asserted (tests/scpg_tests.rs:113-116). No test calls get_section, crc32, compose_scpg_hash or SectionLayoutPlanner, and none passes MemoryMappedSCPG::open a truncated, wrong-magic or huge-section_count file (grep over tests/ and src/scpg).
impact: Format regressions and the loader panics noted in SCPG-07 ship undetected.
recommendation: Add these tests: crc32_known_answer ('123456789' -> 0xCBF43926), scpg_section_crc_roundtrip, scpg_header_fields (version, section_count, language_count, source_hash), open_rejects_truncated, open_rejects_bad_magic, open_rejects_huge_section_count, compose_hash_changes_per_input and layout_has_11_distinct_sections.

title: Query engine, cache, incremental planner and most query modules have no tests
evidence: src/scpg has no #[cfg(test)] module or #[test] function. tests/ never references QueryEngine, LRUQueryCache, ImpactAnalyzer, ROBDDQueryEngine, forward_slice, from_source, RebuildPlanner, IncrementalEngine, or OpenHeartEngine::open/is_reachable/backward_slice (grep).
impact: Cache invalidation, eviction and every query except one smoke call are unverified.
recommendation: Add unit tests on small hand-built CGAs: cache_hit_and_hash_invalidation, cache_capacity_eviction, engine_cached_matches_uncached, impact_set_handles_cycles, forward_slice_depth_limit, from_source_nested_ranges, robdd_unknown_symbol, classify_table, apply_delta_hash and engine_open_roundtrip.

title: Surgical test advertises inheritance, dispatch and recursion but asserts none of them
evidence: The fixture (tests/surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:23-88) has Dog extends Animal, fetch->speak/breathe, main->fetch and a recursive count(). The assertions (:575-626) only bound-check ids and CSR lengths. Nothing checks for a TH_EXTENDS Dog->Animal edge, a SELF_RECURSIVE SCC for count or a fetch->Dog.speak edge, and header counts are not compared with vector lengths.
impact: Wrong call-graph or hierarchy output passes the main 'surgical' inspection test.
recommendation: Look up symbols by name and assert the expected TH edges, the call edges (including the virtual target), the SCC class of count, and that header counts match vector lengths for sta, cfa, ssa and cga.

title: Composite hash arguments are shifted one phase upstream and omit CGA, PSA and UMA content
evidence: compose_scpg_hash names its parameters tca_hash..psa_hash (src/scpg/serializer/integrity.rs:18-28). src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:124-134 passes a token count as tca_hash, bpa.tca_hash as bpa_hash, sta.bpa_hash as sta_hash, ..., uma.tra_hash as uma_hash and psa.cfa_hash as psa_hash. No argument covers the .cga, .psa or .uma bytes, and the header has no generator-version field.
impact: A changed analyzer that produces a different call graph, ROBDDs or UML from the same inputs keeps the same scpg_hash.
recommendation: Give each artifact its own content hash, pass the nine values to the matching parameters, mix in a generator/format version, and derive the 32-bit key with a real hash. This is distinct from SCPG-14's point that XOR is weak.

title: A poisoned query mutex silently turns into 'unreachable' and empty slices
evidence: src/scpg/api/mod.rs:52-56 returns false when self.query.lock() fails, and :67-71 returns Vec::new(). After any panic inside a query that holds the lock, every later reachability query answers false and every slice is empty, with no error or log. This differs from SCPG-14's lock-contention point.
impact: After one panic, every later answer is plausible but wrong.
recommendation: Recover with lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) and clear the cache, or return Result<_, QueryError>. Log the poison event.

title: language_count header field is hardcoded to 1
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:149 writes 1u32 as language_count whatever the input. tca.file_records carry a language_id per file, and LangId defines Java, Kotlin and eight more (src/core/types/token.rs:6-18). docs/plans/phase10.md:27 specifies 'number of distinct source languages ingested'.
impact: Mixed Java and Kotlin projects are recorded as single-language, so the header metadata cannot be trusted.
recommendation: Count the distinct non-Unknown language_id values in tca.file_records and write that number. Add a test with one .java and one .kt file that expects 2.

title: The .scpg write is non-atomic, unsynced and fully buffered in memory
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:40-165 assembles the whole file in one Vec; the string table is copied by to_vec() at :62 and again into file_buf. Then :167 calls fs::write, which truncates in place with no temp file, rename or fsync. docs/plans/phase10.md:296-345 describes a streamed BufWriter. This is the writer side, unlike SCPG-07's loader checks.
impact: A crash or a concurrent reader mid-write sees a truncated .scpg, and peak memory doubles once sections carry real data.
recommendation: Stream sections through a BufWriter into a temp file, seek back to patch the header and directory, call sync_all, then rename over out_path. Drop the intermediate to_vec copies.

title: classify() trusts three independent booleans and resolves conflicts to the cheapest scope
evidence: SourceDelta has three independent flags: is_comment_or_ws_only, is_method_body_only and is_type_decl_changed (src/scpg/incremental/delta.rs:12-17). classify (src/scpg/incremental/mod.rs:10-20) checks them in order. So method_body_only plus type_decl_changed gives Behavioral instead of Structural, and comment_only plus anything gives None. Nothing validates the combination.
impact: A caller that sets several flags gets an under-scoped rebuild and stale structural data.
recommendation: Replace the bools with a ChangeKind enum, or a bitset resolved to the widest scope. Add a table test (classify_resolves_conflicts_to_widest_scope) covering all 8 combinations.

title: Query-type codes are magic numbers that contradict the spec; params_crc is not a CRC
evidence: src/scpg/query/mod.rs:47 uses query_type 0 for CFL, and :71 uses 2 with the comment '// SLICE_BWD'. The spec assigns SLICE_FWD=2 and SLICE_BWD=3 (docs/plans/phase10.md:241). Both slices pack params as root<<32|depth, so a forward-slice cache numbered per the spec would collide with backward-slice entries. src/scpg/types.rs:47 calls the packed value params_crc.
impact: Adding a forward-slice cache per the spec would return backward-slice results, and the field name misleads readers.
recommendation: Add a #[repr(u8)] enum QueryType that matches the spec and use it in QueryKey. Rename params_crc to params_key, or hash serialized parameters as documented.

title: EngineBuilder cannot build anything and duplicates SCPGPipelineBuilder
evidence: src/scpg/api/builder.rs:5-35 holds output_dir, cache_capacity and enable_mmap with two setters. It has no build() or open(), no setter for enable_mmap, and no code reads any field. It is public API (src/scpg/mod.rs:16). SCPGPipelineBuilder (src/core/pipeline.rs:97-114) does the real work and defaults to temp_dir instead of ./scpg_out. This is broader than SCPG-14's cache-capacity point.
impact: A public configuration path does nothing, and the two builders have conflicting defaults.
recommendation: Implement EngineBuilder::build() and open(path) honoring cache_capacity and enable_mmap (adding with_mmap), or remove it and keep a single builder with a documented default output directory.

title: Engine export methods ignore engine state, expose only class diagrams, and hide errors
evidence: export_mermaid, export_plantuml, export_json, export_xmi and summary (src/scpg/api/mod.rs:74-117) never use self; callers pass uma/sta/tca. Only class diagrams are exposed, while main.rs and the server call UniversalDiagramEngine::export_diagram directly. export_xmi takes &[ClassRecord], unlike the others. export_json turns a serde error into "{}" (:112). The scpg_hash, query and mmap fields are pub.
impact: There are two parallel export APIs, failures produce silent '{}' output, and callers can desynchronize scpg_hash from the file.
recommendation: Expose export(format, diagram_type) that delegates to UniversalDiagramEngine using engine-held artifacts, return Result<String, ExportError>, and make the fields private behind accessors.

title: Dead code and a capacity-0 edge case in the query layer
evidence: QueryResult::Count, StringList, SymbolList and Json (src/scpg/types.rs:54-58) are never constructed. LRUQueryCache::invalidate (src/scpg/query/cache.rs:38-41) has no caller. LRUQueryCache::new(0) still caches one entry, because put clears and then inserts (cache.rs:31-35). QueryResult does not derive PartialEq, which makes tests clumsy.
impact: Unused API suggests features that do not exist, and capacity 0 cannot disable caching.
recommendation: Remove the unused variants or wire them to real queries, call invalidate from the incremental path, treat capacity 0 as disabled, and derive PartialEq on QueryResult.

title: CFL search keeps a redundant pair state and an unreachable final check
evidence: The first tuple element is always source (src/scpg/query/cfl.rs:18-19, 28-29), so the HashSet<(u32,u32)> is just a visited set. Every inserted pair is queued and the loop returns when u == target (:22-24), so summary.contains(&(source, target)) at :34 is always false. source == target returns true for any id, even one absent from the graph (:11-13).
impact: Readers are misled into thinking summary edges exist, and any id, even an unknown one, reaches itself.
recommendation: Use a HashSet<u32> or bitset visited set, return false after the loop, and validate ids or document reflexivity. This is separate from SCPG-09's algorithm point.

title: Slice traversals scan the whole site_to_edge_map for every visited symbol
evidence: backward_slice scans every cga.site_to_edge_map entry for each popped symbol to find callers (src/scpg/query/slice.rs:28-32), and forward_slice does the same for callees (:64-68). That is O(V·E). The CGA already has caller_csr/callee_csr indexed by symbol id, with edges_of() (src/core/types/cg.rs:127-137; src/cg/mod.rs:110). SCPG-09 and SCPG-15 cover only CFL and impact.
impact: Slices on large call graphs become quadratic and hold the engine's global mutex the whole time.
recommendation: Use cga.caller_csr.edges_of(sym) and cga.callee_csr.edges_of(sym) for O(degree) neighbor lookup, or build a reverse adjacency once per CGA. Note that the CSR omits out-of-range external callees.

title: from_source ignores columns and ordering; to_source returns only the first link
evidence: from_source filters on line_start <= line <= line_end (src/scpg/query/navigation.rs:24) and ignores columns. It returns matches in uml_links order (outer class before inner method), not innermost first. to_source returns the first link with the given sym_id (:10). Callers must supply an internal u16 file_id; there is no lookup by path. This goes beyond SCPG-15's complexity point.
impact: Navigating from an editor position to the diagram cannot find the innermost entity, and entities on the same line cannot be told apart.
recommendation: Take (file, line, col), test full (line, col) containment, sort by span size ascending, and add a path-to-file_id lookup. Test: a method nested in a class on one line returns the method first.

title: ROBDD lookups return a fabricated 1 for unknown or non-function symbols
evidence: path_count and cyclomatic end in .unwrap_or(1) (src/scpg/query/robdd.rs:10-12, 17-19). A class id, an unknown id, or a function missing from the PSA therefore reports 1 path and complexity 1, the same as a real straight-line method. max_path_len, unwind_depth and PathMetrics are not exposed. This is separate from SCPG-15's O(1) claim.
impact: Metrics and rankings silently treat missing data as the simplest possible code.
recommendation: Return Option<u64>/Option<u16> (or Result) and let callers decide. Add accessors for max_path_len, unwind_depth and path_metrics.

title: Sections are unaligned, and count widths vary without type metadata
evidence: Sections are appended back to back with no padding (src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:53-121), so everything after the variable-length StringTable starts at an arbitrary offset. PathSummaries writes psa.total_nodes as u64 (8 bytes, :103-107), while the other count sections write u32. Directory entries have no element size, count, flags or compression field (src/scpg/types.rs:36-42).
impact: Zero-copy typed views and the claimed hot/warm/cold page grouping are impossible.
recommendation: Align each section to 8 bytes and the hot/warm/cold boundaries to pages, add elem_size, elem_count and flags to directory entries, and bump SCPG_FORMAT_VERSION.

title: StringTable section omits the interner's offset index
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:62 writes only tca.interner.get_storage_bytes(), that is, u16-length-prefixed strings (src/ingestion/interner.rs:95-102). The offsets array (interner.rs:23, get_offsets at :123) and the string count are not written, so resolving a text_id needs an O(n) scan from the start.
impact: The only section with real content cannot support the O(1) name lookups that diagrams and navigation need.
recommendation: Write the count and a u32 offsets array before the storage blob (or as their own section) and document the layout. Test: round-trip the interner and compare lookup_text for every id.

title: Header and directory layout is duplicated as magic offsets, with no codec or checksum
evidence: The writer appends fields in order (src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:142-163); the reader hardcodes byte ranges 0..8 through 60..64 (src/scpg/mmap/mod.rs:26-62). SCPGHeader and SectionDirectoryEntry have no to_bytes/from_bytes, and SCPGSectionType has no TryFrom<u32>. SCPG_SECTION_COUNT (types.rs:6) is not tied to ordered_sections(), and a mismatch panics at copy_from_slice (:165). Header and directory have no checksum.
impact: A layout change on one side silently breaks the other, and corruption in the header or directory goes undetected.
recommendation: Add to_bytes/from_bytes for SCPGHeader and SectionDirectoryEntry using named offset constants. Derive the section count from the layout array with a const assert, add TryFrom<u32> for SCPGSectionType, and store a header+directory CRC in the reserved bytes.

title: Bitwise CRC-32 is duplicated and slow, and breaks the CRC-64 convention
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/integrity.rs:3-16 and src/tra/uml_link/hash_chain.rs:12-25 are identical bit-at-a-time CRC-32 loops (8 iterations per byte). The output is correct (0xCBF43926 for '123456789'). Every other artifact uses crc64_ecma, and README.md:59 says all phases produce 'CRC-64 verified binary artifacts'.
impact: There are two copies to maintain, and both run about 8x slower than a table-driven CRC on full-size sections.
recommendation: Keep one table-driven (or slicing-by-8) CRC in core and reuse it in TRA and SCPG. Either switch the .scpg sections to CRC-64 or correct the README.

DOCS.note: README 'CRC-64 verified' claim corrected; security doc and ledger record the CRC-32 hash chain; CRC dedup handed off

title: Debug output of MemoryMappedSCPG prints the entire file
evidence: #[derive(Debug)] on MemoryMappedSCPG (src/scpg/mmap/mod.rs:9-14) includes the private bytes: Vec<u8>. So {:?}, for example in an expect or unwrap message or a log line, prints every byte of the .scpg as a decimal list.
impact: Logs and panic messages grow to megabytes once sections hold real data.
recommendation: Implement Debug by hand so that it prints only the header, the directory and bytes.len().

title: Documented SCPG magic number disagrees with the constant, and the magic embeds a version
evidence: SCPG_MAGIC = u64::from_le_bytes(*b"SCPG\x00\x01\x00\x00") = 0x0000010047504353 (src/scpg/types.rs:3), but docs/plans/phase10.md:21 documents 0x5343504700010000. The mismatch error prints the little-endian value (src/scpg/mmap/mod.rs:30). The 0x01 byte in the magic duplicates format_version.
impact: Readers implemented from the spec reject valid files, and any version bump forces a change to the magic.
recommendation: Document the on-disk bytes ('SCPG\0\x01\0\0') rather than a u64 literal, print the magic as bytes in the error, and keep versioning in format_version only.

DOCS.note: phase10.md documents the magic as on-disk bytes, explains the LE/BE literal mismatch, and keeps versioning in format_version only; printing the magic as bytes in errors handed off

title: Cache hits deep-clone results
evidence: LRUQueryCache::get returns self.entries.get(key).cloned() (src/scpg/query/cache.rs:27), and QueryEngine::backward_slice stores res.clone() (src/scpg/query/mod.rs:81). Every Slice hit therefore copies the whole Vec<u32>. docs/plans/phase10.md:275-289 claims O(1) cached complexity.
impact: Large cached slices cost an O(n) allocation per hit, made while the global lock is held.
recommendation: Store results as Arc<[u32]> or Arc<QueryResult> and hand out clones of the Arc.

title: Query answers lack witness paths, distances and edge-kind filters
evidence: is_reachable returns only a bool (src/scpg/query/cfl.rs:10); impact_set and the slices return flat sorted Vec<u32> (src/scpg/query/impact.rs:31-33, src/scpg/query/slice.rs:42-44). The site_to_edge_map tuples carry no edge kind, although callee_csr.edge_types exists (src/core/types/cg.rs:120-124). So no query can exclude REFLECTION or DYNAMIC edges or report the call chain.
impact: Users cannot see why A reaches B, cannot verify results, and cannot tune precision.
recommendation: Return an optional witness path (from a BFS parent map), per-node distance for slices and impact, and accept a CG_EDGE_* mask on all graph queries.

title: Surgical test prints 'ALL FIELDS MATCH' after comparing only lengths
evidence: The CGA round-trip compares call_sites, sccs and points_to_table only by len() (tests/surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:550, 557, 559). The TRA round-trip compares only scpg_hash, uml_links.len() and sym_span.len() (:563-565). Both then print 'ALL FIELDS MATCH' (:560, :566). CallSite, SCCRecord, PointsToEntry and TraceabilityArtifact all derive PartialEq.
impact: Field-level serializer corruption, such as a wrong call_type or swapped spans, passes while the log claims full equality.
recommendation: assert_eq! on call_sites, sccs and points_to_table, and assert_eq!(tra, tra_rt). Otherwise, reword the message to say what was actually checked.

title: Surgical pipeline test stops at Phase 7
evidence: The test runs only Phases 1-7 (tests/surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:101-519). PSA, UMA and SCPG are never built, dumped or round-tripped, and only CGA and TRA are deserialized back. It ends with 'TOTAL PIPELINE OUTPUT ... across 7 binary artifacts' and 'ALL SURGICAL INSPECTIONS PASSED' (:676, :686).
impact: Phases 8-10 have no dump-level or round-trip coverage in the pipeline inspection test.
recommendation: Extend the test through Phase8Stage, Phase9Stage and Phase10Stage, round-trip .sta/.cfa/.ssa/.psa/.uma/.scpg with their readers, and assert cross-phase links such as psa.cfa_hash == ssa.cfa_hash.

title: Surgical test output is nondeterministic, slightly wrong, and floods CI logs
evidence: Node-type counts come from a HashMap sorted only by count (tests/surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:153-160), so ties print in random order. The BP size line computes node_count*2/8, which floors (:149). Slicing scc_members (:504-506) panics before the SCC assertion at :597 can run. CI runs cargo test with --nocapture (.github/workflows/ci.yml), which prints every symbol, block and CSR array.
impact: Dump diffs are noisy, the size line under-reports, and failures show an index panic instead of a message.
recommendation: Break ties by name, use div_ceil(8), use .get(range) with an assertion message, and put verbose dumps behind an environment variable.

title: SCPG test hand-rolls the 10-phase harness in one monolithic test
evidence: tests/scpg_tests.rs:24-107 and tests/surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:90-519 each wire up the phases by hand instead of using SCPGPipelineBuilder (src/core/pipeline.rs). All Phase 10 checks sit in one test behind nine phases. The JSON check depends on serde's pretty-print spacing ("diagram_type": "class", scpg_tests.rs:162).
impact: Test wiring can drift from the real pipeline, one upstream failure hides every Phase 10 result, and the string match is brittle.
recommendation: Build a shared fixture with SCPGPipelineBuilder, split the checks into focused tests, and parse the JSON with serde_json::from_str before asserting on fields.

title: Phase 10 log lines and module docs describe behavior that does not exist
evidence: src/scpg/mod.rs:57-60 logs 'Merged all 9 artifacts into unified .scpg file', and :64 logs 'production engine bootstrapped & ready', although the engine holds no mmap and no artifacts. src/scpg/serializer/integrity.rs:1 names an 'IntegrityVerifier' that verifies nothing. src/scpg/api/builder.rs:1 promises a fluent builder that builds nothing. SCPG-02 covers the missing content itself.
impact: Users and maintainers are told that features exist, and the logs mislead debugging.
recommendation: Reword the logs and docs to describe what is actually written (counts and the string table) until the features land, then update them together.

title: Package diagrams mix segment names with full paths, adding stray root packages
evidence: Pass 1 gives each package symbol a one-segment name_id and puts the full path only in custom_package_names (src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:543-556). PlantUML inserts resolve_name(pkg.package_sym_id), i.e. the segment, into all_pkg_paths next to full class paths (plantuml.rs:658-671), so `package com.example.app` renders com→example→app plus stray roots `example` and `app`. Mermaid emits Pkg_com, Pkg_example and Pkg_app beside Pkg_com_example_app (mermaid.rs:908-933).
impact: Every multi-segment package produces duplicate, disconnected packages, which misrepresents the architecture in both formats.
recommendation: Resolve package records through sta.custom_package_names (the full path), build one tree from full paths in both exporters, and add a test asserting that `package a.b.c` yields exactly one root.

title: Primitive and JDK member types render blank or 'Unknown' in every format
evidence: Primitive type ids are sentinels 0xB000_0000+ (src/symbol/adapter/java.rs:21-29) and java.lang/java.util stubs are 0xC000_0000+ (src/symbol/std_library/java_stubs.rs:8-21), but SymbolTableArtifact::symbol only indexes symbol_records (src/symbol/serializer.rs:37-39). So `int count` renders `+count : ` in PlantUML (plantuml.rs:338-346), an empty type in JSON (json.rs:208-209), and `+count Unknown` / `+run() Unknown` in Mermaid (mermaid.rs:700-735). Stubbed supertypes such as Exception also drop out.
impact: int, String, List, void and other common member types are missing or wrong in class, object and composite diagrams.
recommendation: Add a shared type-name resolver that maps primitive and stub sentinel ids to names (or persist stub records in .sta), use it in every exporter, and test rendering of int, String and void.

title: Interaction overview resolves scenario_name (an interner id) as a symbol id
evidence: The UMA builder stores `scenario_name: entry_sym_rec.name_id` (src/uma/behavioral/sequence_diagram.rs:156), but plantuml.rs:1160 and mermaid.rs:1312 call resolve_name(sta, tca, seq.scenario_name), which looks up an unrelated symbol. The gallery labels the App() scenario 'generateSRSWithProgress' (web/diagrams/interaction.mmd:2 vs sequence.mmd:3) and shows three 'Scenario_Unknown' subgraphs (interaction.mmd:6,10,14). PlantUML drops scenarios whose bogus lookup comes back empty.
impact: Every scenario in PlantUML and Mermaid interaction overviews is mislabeled or silently dropped.
recommendation: Use tca.interner.lookup_text(seq.scenario_name), or store the entry symbol id explicitly in the record. Document what the field holds in uma/types.rs, and test that the label equals the entry method name.

title: Collection-typed fields never yield associations to their element type
evidence: A `List<Order>` field's type_sym_id is the List stub taken from the type-ref's first token (src/symbol/passes/pass4_members.rs:41-58), and UMA hardcodes is_collection: 0 (src/uma/structural/class_diagram.rs:215). The stub is unresolvable (SCPGX2-02), so PlantUML (plantuml.rs:474-478), JSON (json.rs:349-355) and the association_syms Mermaid uses (class_diagram.rs:253-265) all drop the edge. clean_type_name's generic parsing (json.rs:93-112) never sees type arguments. SCPG-18 covers arrow kinds; here the edge is missing entirely.
impact: One-to-many relationships, the backbone of domain models, are missing from every class diagram.
recommendation: Record element/type-argument symbols for fields upstream. Emit an association or aggregation with multiplicity * to the element type in every exporter, and remove the dead generic parsing.

title: PlantUML class diagram keeps only one relationship per ordered class pair
evidence: edges_by_pair is keyed by (src,dst) (plantuml.rs:451). extends/implements use insert (462, 469) and fields use or_insert_with (490-492), so `class Decorator implements Component { Component inner; }` keeps `..|>` and loses the association. An inner-class `+--` (499) also overwrites a field association. JSON (json.rs:368) and Mermaid (mermaid.rs:633) keep both edges, so the formats disagree.
impact: Decorator/Composite/Proxy structures (is-a plus has-a) lose the has-a edge in the default PlantUML output.
recommendation: Key edges by (src, dst, kind), or keep a Vec of relations per pair, and emit each distinct relation. Add a Decorator fixture test expecting both `..|>` and `-->`.

title: Method return types are drawn as associations, and JSON doubles field edges
evidence: UMA adds method return types to association_syms (src/uma/structural/class_diagram.rs:267-279). Mermaid draws `-->` for each one (mermaid.rs:761-768), and JSON adds 'association' edges (json.rs:385-405) that are deduped only per kind. A final field therefore gets both a composition and an association, and a field of a List-named class gets both an aggregation and an association. PlantUML ignores association_syms, so formats disagree. In UML, using a type as a return type is a dependency, not an association.
impact: Mermaid and JSON class diagrams overstate structural coupling and show contradictory relation kinds for a single field.
recommendation: Separate structural relations (fields) from usage relations (signatures) in UMA, render usage as a `..>` dependency, and dedupe per (src, dst) keeping the strongest kind.

title: JSON detects aggregation by substring of the target class name
evidence: json.rs:356-361 marks a field edge as aggregation when raw_target contains "List", "Set" or "Array". Real java.util types resolve to "" (SCPGX2-02) and only declared project classes pass json.rs:354, so the test only ever fires as a false positive: fields typed Listener, Settings, Asset, Dataset or PlayList become `o--`. PlantUML uses is_collection only (plantuml.rs:483). SCPG-18 is about missing detail; this is a wrong classification.
impact: Common project types get the wrong UML relationship in the JSON IR and the web studio.
recommendation: Delete the substring test and derive aggregation from real collection/element-type data shared by all exporters (see SCPGX2-04).

title: Unresolved types and constructors render inconsistently; JSON invents Object/void
evidence: Constructors keep type_id u32::MAX because pass 4 skips SK_CONSTRUCTOR (src/symbol/passes/pass4_members.rs:44-50). PlantUML prints a dangling `+Foo() : ` (plantuml.rs:353-361). Mermaid prints `Unknown` (mermaid.rs:722-728). JSON substitutes `Object` for fields and `void` for returns (json.rs:208-212, 234-238), so constructors appear to return void while real void methods (sentinel id) get an empty type.
impact: Members show invented or contradictory types, and the three formats disagree about the same member.
recommendation: Model an unknown type as None: omit it in text formats, emit null in JSON, and render constructors without a return type (or as «create»).

title: Name-based 'primitive/system' filters silently drop user-defined classes
evidence: PlantUML drops classes named String, Object, Class, Integer, Long or Boolean (plantuml.rs:229-235, 292, 455). Mermaid drops Unknown, Entity, String, Object and args (mermaid.rs:542-560, 642, 747), and DiagramUtils adds List/Map/Set/Optional (common.rs:59-91). JDK and primitive types never resolve to these names (SCPGX2-02), so the filters only ever remove user classes, such as a JPA or ECS `Entity`, together with their edges.
impact: Legitimate project classes and their relationships disappear without warning, and differently in each format.
recommendation: Filter by symbol kind or id range (SK_EXTERNAL, stub and primitive sentinels) in one shared helper, never by simple name.

title: The external actor splits into two entities and loses its actor role
evidence: Lifelines resolve EXTERNAL_ACTOR_ID to "ExternalActor" (plantuml.rs:173-175), but messages hardcode "Actor" (plantuml.rs:1047-1049, mermaid.rs:1207-1212, json.rs:590-595). The gallery has an isolated actor node part_ExternalActor (web/diagrams/sequence.json:6) and a participant part_Actor (sequence.json:42) that carries every message. Mermaid never declares an `actor`. A real class named Actor merges with it. SCPG-06 covers PlantUML alias validity.
impact: Sequence and communication outputs show a dangling actor and a fake participant, and real `Actor` classes collide with it.
recommendation: Use one reserved id and label (e.g. __external_actor) everywhere, declare it as an actor in PlantUML and Mermaid, and give it kind 'actor' in JSON.

title: Mermaid 'Unknown'/'Empty' sentinels make every empty-name guard dead
evidence: resolve_name returns "Unknown" (mermaid.rs:499-507) and sanitize never returns "" (it returns "Empty", 533-534). So checks such as `safe_field == ""` (697, 702, 719, 724), `!from_name.is_empty()` (1215, 1255-1258) and `!scenario.is_empty()` (1313) never fire. The gallery shows `Actor->>useState: Unknown()` (sequence.mmd:93), communication.mmd:48 and three Scenario_Unknown subgraphs; PlantUML and JSON skip these instead.
impact: Unrelated unresolved lifelines, methods and types collapse into one shared 'Unknown' entity, and Mermaid disagrees with the other formats.
recommendation: Return Option<&str> from resolve_name, skip unresolved symbols or give them unique ids (sym_<id>), and remove the sentinel strings.

title: Sequence exports misrepresent call structure and lose scenario identity
evidence: PlantUML emits a synthetic `return` and deactivate straight after every call (plantuml.rs:1055-1064), so nested calls look sequential. Mermaid emits no returns or activations at all (mermaid.rs:1217-1220). All three ignore message_kind, ordinal and combined_fragments. JSON message edges carry only a label (json.rs:643-651), with every scenario merged and no scenario id or order field.
impact: Readers cannot see call nesting, message kinds, or which scenario a JSON message belongs to.
recommendation: Build call trees from caller→callee nesting, emit activations and returns at the correct depth, map message_kind to arrow styles, render fragments, and add scenario_id and ordinal to JSON message edges.

title: Communication diagrams are built wrongly in all three formats
evidence: PlantUML links obj_ aliases that are never declared (plantuml.rs:1106-1111), so PlantUML draws them as classes. Numbering is the per-scenario index, so almost every link reads "1:" (web/diagrams/communication.puml).
