Self-calls are dropped (plantuml.rs:1102, mermaid.rs:1259), and there is one link per message instead of a message list per link. The JSON communication diagram is the sequence IR with a new name (json.rs:1660-1669); the gallery communication.json is byte-identical to sequence.json.
impact: Communication output lacks real objects, meaningful sequence numbers, recursion and per-link message aggregation.
recommendation: Declare objects, aggregate messages per link, use hierarchical numbering (1, 1.1) derived from call nesting, keep self-links, and build a dedicated JSON communication IR.

title: Empty-data fallbacks fabricate interactions
evidence: With no sequences: communication chains the first four classes with numbered messages (plantuml.rs:1117-1144, mermaid.rs:1275-1299); interaction overview invents 'Class Flow' partitions (plantuml.rs:1173-1188, mermaid.rs:1331-1352); timing invents state changes (plantuml.rs:1224-1246); JSON sequence invents execute() calls (json.rs:656-690). The fallback also pairs filtered class_names[i] with uma.classes.get(i), mislabeling methods (plantuml.rs:1131, mermaid.rs:1286).
impact: Exactly when analysis finds nothing, diagrams present invented messages as if they were results.
recommendation: Emit an explicit empty diagram with a note such as "no interactions found" instead of synthetic content.

title: JSON IR emits duplicate node ids for same-named functions and components
evidence: Activity partition, start, step and stop ids come from the sanitized function name (json.rs:890, 908, 936, 999). Use-case ids come from class plus method name (json.rs:1302), and component ids are not deduped (json.rs:1062). Overloads such as add(int)/add(String), or the same method name in two classes, produce duplicate ids and ambiguous edges. Mermaid already keys activities by function_sym_id (mermaid.rs:1136). This differs from SCPG-04, which covers same-named types.
impact: Graph consumers such as the web studio merge or reject nodes, and activity flows interleave.
recommendation: Derive ids from symbol ids (e.g. act_<sym>_<block>), dedupe them, and check IR invariants (unique ids, edges pointing at existing nodes) before serializing.

title: Diagram-type keys and aliases differ by format; JSON silently falls back to the class diagram
evidence: PlantUML and Mermaid accept exact keys only (plantuml.rs:93-103, mermaid.rs:400-410). JSON accepts aliases (state, state_machine, use_case, cg, composite_structure, interaction_overview) and returns the class diagram for anything else (factory.rs:181-207), and its export_all keys differ ("state", factory.rs:245). Driven by the server's list (src/adapters/server.rs:640-662), this produces duplicate state/statemachine.json and use_case/usecase.json files with no matching .puml or .mmd.
impact: A typo returns the wrong diagram with no error, the gallery holds duplicate files, and export_all maps cannot be joined by key.
recommendation: Introduce a DiagramType enum with FromStr and aliases shared by every factory, return an error for unknown types, and expose the supported types per format.

title: Exporter interfaces receive only uma/sta/tca, so IR diagrams cannot use CFA/SSA/CGA/PSA
evidence: DiagramExporterFactory::export_diagram (factory.rs:50-56), PlantUMLDiagramStrategy::export (plantuml.rs:18-23) and MermaidDiagramStrategy::export (mermaid.rs:1631-1636) take only uma, sta and tca. The CDG exporters ignore even those (plantuml.rs:1378-1382, mermaid.rs:1559-1563). This API shape is the root cause behind the templated CFG/DFG/CDG/call-graph/ROBDD views that SCPG-01 reports.
impact: Real compiler-IR diagrams cannot be produced without breaking the public trait.
recommendation: Pass an AnalysisContext (uma, sta and tca plus optional cfa, ssa, cga, psa and tra) through factories and strategies, and return a Result with 'artifact missing' errors.

title: Package dependencies use only field and return types, and are labelled «imports»
evidence: plantuml.rs:723-754 and json.rs:482-516 build package edges from field types and method return types only, ignoring extends/implements, parameters, locals, calls and imports. Both label the edges <<imports>> (plantuml.rs:763, json.rs:527), which in UML means a PackageImport, not a usage. Mermaid's package diagram emits no dependencies at all (SCPGX2-19).
impact: Layering violations through inheritance, parameters or calls never appear, and the dependency semantics are mislabelled.
recommendation: Aggregate class-level dependencies (supertypes, members, parameters, call-graph edges) into weighted package edges, labelled «use» or «import» as UML defines them.

title: Mermaid package diagram is flat and edge-less; the dead nested renderer would hide com/org
evidence: export_package_diagram (mermaid.rs:900-935) emits one flat subgraph per name, with no hierarchy and no dependency edges, unlike PlantUML and JSON. The nested renderer PkgNode::render (188-258) is unreachable and would skip any root named com, org, java or kotlin (SYSTEM_ROOT_PACKAGES, 12-15, 193). Package resolution also differs: this diagram uses resolve_pkg_name_from_sym (937-953), the class diagram uses resolve_sym_package (426-487).
impact: Mermaid users get no package structure, and reviving the dead renderer as-is would hide most Java packages.
recommendation: Render nested subgraphs and dependency edges from full paths, drop the SYSTEM_ROOT_PACKAGES filter, and use a single package resolver.

title: Mermaid duplicate-package disambiguation hardcodes frontend/backend and is not unique
evidence: Four copies of the same logic (mermaid.rs:107-121, 211-225, 287-301, 562-583) suffix a duplicated leaf name with F or B when the root contains "frontend" or "backend", and otherwise with the root's first letter. com.a.util and com.b.util both become util_C, so namespaces still collide and find_node_path (100-141) returns the first match. The id also uses the unsanitized name. mermaid.rs:719 hardcodes skipping methods named Override or annotation.
impact: Same-named packages under one root merge, and project-specific heuristics leak into a general tool.
recommendation: Disambiguate with the full sanitized path (as DiagramUtils::resolve_container_pkg_id does), generate ids in one place, and remove the name hacks.

title: Raw identifiers become Mermaid ids without reserved-word handling
evidence: Sequence and communication lines start with the bare sanitized lifeline name (mermaid.rs:1218, 1264). Mermaid treats `end` and statement keywords such as style, click or subgraph specially in flowcharts, and words such as note, loop, alt, box or title in sequence diagrams. Lifelines are often lowercase module or variable names (the gallery has backend, srs, null, type, e), and nothing prefixes or quotes them.
impact: A single lifeline named end, style or note can make a whole Mermaid diagram fail to parse.
recommendation: Prefix every Mermaid id (e.g. p_<sym_id>), put names in quoted labels or `participant id as "name"`, and add a test using reserved names.

title: JSON Graph IR has no version or schema, uses free-form kinds, and bloats output
evidence: GraphIR (json.rs:12-65) has no schema_version. Kinds are free strings, and the doc comments (34, 62) list only a subset of emitted kinds (message, transition, manifestation, timing_track, data_node and others); the manifest's 'containment' kind is never emitted. Every node serializes empty fields/methods/instructions/lines arrays and duplicates id, label and name, and `arrow` stores PlantUML syntax. Classes without a package go into an invented pkg_default (133-134), and is_domain_tier is simply nest_level==0 (173).
impact: Consumers cannot validate against or evolve with the IR, and files are inflated (sequence.json is 144KB for 46 nodes).
recommendation: Add schema_version and a published JSON Schema, use serde enums for kinds, skip empty fields, and drop the PlantUML arrow strings and the synthetic default package.

title: No unit or property tests cover the exporter logic
evidence: There is no #[test] under src/scpg/diagram, and the integration tests only assert headers and substrings (tests/design_pattern_architecture_tests.rs:62-89, tests/strategy_diagram_tests.rs:41-118). Untested functions include JSONExporter::clean_type_name, all three sanitize variants, PlantUMLOptimizer::optimize, both export_package_diagram implementations, export_interaction_overview_diagram and JSON IR integrity.
impact: Regressions such as stray packages, mislabeled scenarios and duplicate ids ship unnoticed.
recommendation: Add test_package_diagram_no_stray_roots, test_interaction_scenario_label, test_json_ir_unique_ids_and_edge_targets (all 19 types), test_primitive_member_types, test_clean_type_name_generics, test_optimizer_keeps_inheritance, test_mermaid_reserved_lifelines, test_type_aliases_consistent and test_decorator_has_both_edges.

title: Mermaid interaction overview ids collide across scenarios, and there are no flow edges
evidence: Nodes are named Disp_<method> and subgraphs Scenario_<name> (mermaid.rs:1315-1325). The gallery puts Disp_component_name in two subgraphs and repeats Scenario_Unknown three times (web/diagrams/interaction.mmd:6-15). No edges connect the interaction uses, so there is no control flow, unlike a UML interaction overview.
impact: Mermaid moves shared nodes into one subgraph, scenarios lose messages, and the diagram shows no ordering.
recommendation: Scope ids by scenario index (s<i>_m<j>) and connect consecutive interaction uses; add decision/fork nodes once real control data exists.

title: Mermaid activity diagram leaves the start node unconnected and ignores node/edge kinds
evidence: mermaid.rs:1138-1141 emits Start_<id> with no edge to act.start_node (web/diagrams/activity.mmd:3). Every node is a rectangle whatever its node_kind (1143-1155), and edges ignore guard_text_id, is_back_edge and edge_kind (1157-1162).
impact: Activity diagrams lack an entry flow, decision diamonds, loop back-edges and guards.
recommendation: Connect Start to start_node, map NODE_KIND_* to Mermaid shapes ({} for decisions, (( )) for finals), and label or style back-edges and guards.

title: PlantUML output hard-codes a dark theme
evidence: theme_header (plantuml.rs:119-166) is prepended to every diagram: transparent background, #e5e5e5/#ffffff text, and a CSS-style font list `"Space Grotesk", "Segoe UI", sans-serif` that PlantUML probably reads as one font name. Mermaid's theme_init (mermaid.rs:1947-1949) is never called, so the formats differ. There is no `hide empty members`, even though most gallery classes are empty (class.puml).
impact: Rendered with stock PlantUML on a white page, the text is nearly invisible, and each file carries about 2KB of boilerplate.
recommendation: Make theming an export option (default none, or `!theme`), emit `hide empty members`, and theme Mermaid consistently or not at all.

title: Free-text labels go through the identifier sanitizer
evidence: Activity labels are passed to sanitize (plantuml.rs:970, mermaid.rs:1153, json.rs:935), so text like `x = foo(a, b)` becomes `x___foo_a__b_`. These labels are quoted text, so they need format-specific escaping (quotes, brackets, newlines, `;` in PlantUML actions), not identifier mangling.
impact: Once real statement labels arrive, activity nodes become unreadable.
recommendation: Add per-format label-escaping helpers for PlantUML and Mermaid, separate from id sanitizing, and keep the raw text in JSON.

title: Profile diagram uses wrong UML notation and invents metaclass links
evidence: PlantUML draws `X --|> Class : <<extends>>` for every annotation and pattern (plantuml.rs:833, 856-858), a generalization to an implicit class; UML profiles use an Extension (filled arrowhead) to a «metaclass». Strategy and Observer are hard-wired to extend 'Interface', an annotation named Singleton collides with the pattern alias, and the fallback invents an <<entity>> stereotype (plantuml.rs:871, mermaid.rs:1051).
impact: Profile output is notationally wrong and implies JPA-style entities that do not exist.
recommendation: Declare metaclasses, use extension notation, drop invented stereotypes, and show which classes apply each annotation.

title: pattern_kind is truncated from u16 to u8
evidence: `dp.pattern_kind as u8` (plantuml.rs:838, mermaid.rs:1022) maps 0x0103 to 3 (Factory). The .uma loader accepts any u16, so corrupted or future values are misclassified instead of ignored.
impact: Corrupted or newer .uma files produce wrong pattern stereotypes.
recommendation: Match on the u16 value directly (or u8::try_from, skipping on error), and define pattern kinds as an enum.

title: Package-resolution loops hang on cyclic parent_sym chains
evidence: plantuml.rs:243-252, mermaid.rs:440-455 and mermaid.rs:942-951 follow `curr = sym.parent_sym` until u32::MAX, with no visited set or depth limit. A corrupt or hostile .sta with a self-parent or a cycle makes every diagram export loop forever.
impact: A malformed symbol table hangs CLI or server diagram export, a denial of service.
recommendation: Bound the walk (depth at most symbol_count, or a visited bitset) and check parent_sym chains for cycles when loading .sta.

title: Mermaid resolve_name leaks memory through Box::leak
evidence: mermaid.rs:504-506 returns `Box::leak(custom.clone().into_boxed_str())` when a symbol's interned name is empty or "Unknown" but it has a custom package name. Each call leaks a fresh allocation for the life of the process, resolve_name runs in loops, and the server exports per request. Normal pass-1 package symbols have names, so the path is mostly latent.
impact: When this path is hit, the long-running server's memory grows without bound.
recommendation: Return Cow<'a, str>, or tie the lifetime to sta as PlantUML's resolve_name does.

title: Mermaid edge placement and package fallback are super-linear
evidence: For every relationship, find_node_path runs two full-tree DFS passes that allocate an id per node (mermaid.rs:780-797, 100-141), plus linear child scans calling sanitize (162-165), giving O(R·P). resolve_sym_package scans all custom_package_names and file_records for each class without a package parent (464-483), giving O(C·(P+F)). Factories rebuild exporters and their 19 boxed strategies on every call (factory.rs:85, 95, 116, 126).
impact: Class-diagram export slows sharply on repositories with thousands of packages and relationships.
recommendation: Precompute package-id→path and file-id→package maps once per export, cache exporters in the factories, and write with `write!` into one buffer.

title: PlantUML name fallback borrows a nearby token's text for unnamed symbols
evidence: When a symbol's interned name is empty, resolve_name (plantuml.rs:182-203) returns the first non-keyword identifier within 20 tokens of first_token_id, such as the type in `new Runnable() {...}` or a lambda parameter. JSON reuses this resolver, while Mermaid prints 'Unknown'.
impact: Anonymous classes, lambdas and initializers take the names of unrelated types or variables and collide with real classes.
recommendation: Generate explicit names (Outer$1, lambda$<line>, <clinit>) from symbol kind and position, shared by all exporters.

title: DiagramGenerator/DiagramRenderers names and summary text misstate what they do
evidence: generate_summary (mod.rs:25-31) reports "Generated all 14 UML Diagram Types" but only counts records. render_all_14_diagrams (renderers.rs:8-25) renders nothing; it reuses classes.len() for composite/profile/use-case, components.len() for deployment and sequences.len() for communication/interaction/timing, and generate_summary picks stats by position ([0],[8],[10],[9]). The text is exposed via scpg/api/mod.rs:115-116.
impact: The API summary claims work that never happens and reports misleading counts.
recommendation: Rename to diagram_input_counts, return a typed struct, and word the summary as input counts.

title: Module and section doc comments claim properties the code lacks
evidence: plantuml.rs:1-2 says "100% Dynamic ... Formal UML 2.5 Compliance", and its sections say "(100% Symbol-Grounded)" over templated views. mermaid.rs:2 says "Zero hardcoded constants or fallback strings". json.rs:1-2 says "Strongly-Typed ... from in-memory Rust AST", but kinds are strings and no AST is used. export/mod.rs:1 omits Mermaid. plantuml.rs:37 and mermaid.rs:344 say 14 strategies while 19 are registered, and plantuml.rs:14 lists 'strategy' and 'decorator' as diagram types.
impact: The docs mislead maintainers and users about fidelity and coverage.
recommendation: Rewrite the doc comments to state each diagram's real data sources and limitations.

title: Dead code hidden by #[allow(dead_code)], unused parameters and redundant checks
evidence: mermaid.rs:12-29 blanket-allows dead code. PkgNode::render (188-258), sort_children_and_edges (174-186), resolve_pkg_name (510-520) and theme_init (1947) are unreachable, and package_path_by_sym is always empty (599). Parameters `_bpa_bytes` (plantuml.rs:240), `_tca` (mermaid.rs:939, common.rs:106) and `_options` (plantuml_optimizer.rs:42) are unused. Redundant checks include `!text.is_empty() && text != ""` (plantuml.rs:179), sanitize's empty branch (222-226) and repeated `== "" || is_empty()` (mermaid.rs:815, 843, 1083).
impact: Dead code obscures which paths matter and invites reviving broken logic.
recommendation: Remove the allow attributes and dead items, drop unused parameters from public APIs, and run clippy with -D warnings on this module.

title: DiagramUtils has latent bugs that would surface if exporters are moved onto it
evidence: resolve_name maps both u32::MAX (unresolved) and u32::MAX-1 to "Actor" (common.rs:21-23), so unresolved types would render as Actor. resolve_sym_package treats scope_kind 1 as a package scope (common.rs:118), but 1 is ScopeKind::Class (src/core/types/symbol.rs:151-158), so it never matches. It also scans all symbols per level and uses the Vec position as a symbol id (120-124). SCPG-17 flagged the helpers as unused, not these defects.
impact: Moving exporters onto these helpers (the natural SCPG-17 fix) would bring in wrong names and failed package lookups.
recommendation: Fix the helpers before adopting them: only MAX-1 is the actor, resolve packages via parent_sym/custom_package_names, and add unit tests.

title: PlantUMLOptimizer drops inheritance edges it claims to preserve
evidence: Non-inheritance cross-package edges are grouped and their (src,dst) pairs added to suppressed_edges (plantuml_optimizer.rs:49-79). The next loop drops any unbundled edge whose pair is suppressed (85-88), which includes the inheritance edge for that pair. Bundling also turns relations into package-to-class lines (105), such as a package composing a class. This is a latent defect in the unused optimizer, beyond SCPG-17's note that it is dead.
impact: If enabled, `A extends B` disappears whenever A also references B across packages.
recommendation: Suppress by (src, dst, rel_op) or exempt inheritance from suppression, honour the thresholds, and add a unit test.

title: Sequence and timing participant order follows HashMap iteration
evidence: UMA builds lifelines with lifelines_map.into_values() (src/uma/behavioral/sequence_diagram.rs:153), and the exporters emit seq.lifelines in that order (plantuml.rs:1034-1043, json.rs:558-587, timing plantuml.rs:1206-1211) instead of ordering by first message. This adds sequence and timing participants to SCPG-13's list of nondeterministic outputs.
impact: Participant columns reorder between runs, which defeats diffs and golden tests.
recommendation: Order lifelines by first appearance in the messages (actor first) inside the exporters, or sort them upstream.

title: Nested classes are rendered with three different relationship meanings
evidence: PlantUML uses the nesting connector `+--` (plantuml.rs:499). Mermaid draws a composition `*--` (mermaid.rs:775). JSON emits kind "composition" with arrow "+--" (json.rs:332-341), although web/diagrams/manifest.json defines a 'containment' kind.
impact: Mermaid and JSON report nesting as composition, and the formats disagree.
recommendation: Emit a distinct containment relation in every format: `+--` in PlantUML, a note or dedicated style in Mermaid, and 'containment' in JSON.

title: Record and annotation types lose their kind
evidence: PlantUML maps STEREOTYPE_RECORD and STEREOTYPE_ANNOTATION to a plain `class` with no stereotype (plantuml.rs:307-313). JSON maps both to kind "class" with "<<class>>" (json.rs:191-203). Mermaid labels records but not annotations (mermaid.rs:662-668). UMA does produce annotation classes (src/uma/structural/class_diagram.rs:184).
impact: In two of the three formats, records and annotation types look like ordinary classes.
recommendation: Emit `annotation X` and `class X <<record>>` in PlantUML, <<annotation>> in Mermaid, and record/annotation kinds in JSON.

title: Mermaid package tree collapses repeated consecutive segments
evidence: navigate_to_path (mermaid.rs:52-56) and insert_package_path (83-88) stop recursing when the next segment equals the current one ("no self-nesting"). So com.example.example.service stops at com.example, and classes from the deeper packages land in the wrong namespace.
impact: In projects with repeated segment names, classes are merged into a parent package.
recommendation: Remove the equality guard, since a segment nested under an equally named parent is valid.

title: Package ids and labels are generated inconsistently
evidence: The class diagram keeps empty segments (plantuml.rs:381-411) while the package diagram skips them (684-686). Aliases replace only . / - (419, 704, 761), so `a.b` and `a_b` collide on pkg_a_b, and JSON ids replace only '.' (json.rs:159, 456). The class diagram captions nested packages with the full path (421), the package diagram with the leaf (705-708).
impact: Rare id collisions or dangling dependency arrows, and package captions that differ between views.
recommendation: Generate package ids in one helper from normalized segment lists (escaping underscores), and caption packages with the leaf name everywhere.

title: Design-pattern results are rendered without confidence and one pattern per class
evidence: Class diagrams show only class_rec.design_pattern (plantuml.rs:315-328, mermaid.rs:670-683), a single value that each detector overwrites upstream (src/uma/patterns/mod.rs:53-161). uma.design_patterns, which carries confidence 0..100, is used only for profile stereotype names (plantuml.rs:836-861). Roles such as Subject vs Observer and thresholds are never shown.
impact: Low-confidence detections look certain, and a class in several patterns shows only one.
recommendation: Render every detection from uma.design_patterns with its confidence (e.g. «Singleton 92%»), and add an export threshold option.

title: No DOT, GraphML or ELK export
evidence: DiagramFormat offers only PlantUML, Mermaid, XMI and JSON (factory.rs:17-22). Graphviz DOT is the usual format for CFG, call-graph and BDD views, and GraphML or ELK JSON feed graph tools such as yEd, Gephi and Cytoscape; none is supported. This differs from SCPG-19, which covers code-intelligence formats (SCIP/LSIF/LSP).
impact: Compiler-IR graphs cannot be laid out by mature engines or analyzed in standard graph tools.
recommendation: Add DOT and GraphML exporters driven from the JSON Graph IR, so one model feeds every format.

title: Exporters do not check that uma, sta and tca belong together
evidence: Every entry point (factory.rs:314-339, plantuml.rs:93-117) accepts any artifact triple. Symbol ids from a stale .uma are resolved against a newer .sta/.tca with no hash comparison, even though UMA carries tra_hash and class records carry uml_link.scpg_hash (src/uma/types.rs:255-267).
impact: Mixing artifact generations silently produces diagrams with wrong names.
recommendation: Validate the hash chain (or a shared corpus hash) before exporting, and return an error on mismatch.

title: Git credential prompt freezes the whole server
evidence: server.rs:429-437 runs git clone via Command::output() with the inherited environment, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, no askpass override and no timeout. GitHub answers HTTPS clones of nonexistent or private repos with 401, so git prompts for a username on the controlling TTY (run.sh/run.bat) or Git Credential Manager opens a GUI on Windows. Differs from SRV-04: an indefinite hang, not slowness.
impact: One mistyped repo URL blocks every client until someone answers the console prompt.
recommendation: Spawn git with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, GIT_ASKPASS/SSH_ASKPASS set to a no-op, -c credential.helper=, ssh BatchMode, stdin null, and a wall-clock timeout that kills the child. Test: cloning a nonexistent GitHub repo fails within the timeout.

title: Clones run with the operator's git credentials (confused deputy)
evidence: The clone (server.rs:429-437) inherits the server user's credential helpers, ~/.git-credentials and SSH agent. Any page can POST a private repo URL the developer can access (CORS * at server.rs:327), then read the files from ./target_repos via /api/source (server.rs:211). Differs from SRV-02: even a strictly validated https://github.com/owner/repo URL leaks private code.
impact: Any website can exfiltrate a developer's private repositories while the studio is running.
recommendation: Clone in an isolated credential context: HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to an empty temp dir, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, -c credential.helper=, ssh disabled, anonymous https only; make private-repo access an explicit opt-in token. Test that a private repo URL fails.

title: A panic in any request or phase kills the server process
evidence: start() calls handle_connection on the main thread (server.rs:40-42) with no catch_unwind and no worker thread. Phases 1-9 run inline (server.rs:527-617) and contain asserts and unchecked slicing (src/ast/builder.rs:180, src/ast/mod.rs:58-59). run.sh launches a dev build, where debug_assert! is active (token.rs:122).
impact: One unusual or crafted repository terminates the service for everyone and leaves temp dirs behind.
recommendation: Run each request on a worker thread, or wrap it in catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe. Turn panics into logged 500 responses and keep accepting. Test: a handler that panics returns 500 and the next request succeeds.

title: Server directory walkers follow symlinks (loops, exponential traversal, escapes)
evidence: collect_files (server.rs:777-804) and walkdir_find::visit (server.rs:345-347) recurse on path.is_dir(), which follows symlinks, and git checks symlinks out on Linux and macOS. Links a->. plus b->. give about 2^40 traversals before ELOOP. A link to / walks the host filesystem. One loop link re-collects every file about 40 times. Differs from SRV-01 (direct path read).
impact: One public repo can hang the serial server, duplicate classes, or pull host files outside the clone into the analysis.
recommendation: Use DirEntry::file_type()/symlink_metadata and skip symlinks, or canonicalize and require targets under the repo root. Track visited (dev, inode) pairs and cap depth and file count. Tests: fixture with self-loop links and a link to an outside directory.

title: Symlinked source files are read through to devices and host files
evidence: collect_files keeps any entry with a code extension without checking that it is a regular file (server.rs:805-884), and ingestion follows the link in fs::metadata/fs::read (src/ingestion/mod.rs:51-54). A cloned Evil.java -> /dev/zero grows memory until OOM. X.java -> /etc/... pulls host files into results and, via walkdir_find, into /api/source. The CLI has the same gap (main.rs:90-95).
impact: One public repository can crash the server with OOM or expose host files through analysis output.
recommendation: Accept only regular files using DirEntry::file_type() without following links, or canonicalize and require targets inside the repo. Cap per-file size before reading. Test: a symlink to /dev/zero is skipped.

title: Clone cache keyed only by the URL's last path segment
evidence: repo_url maps to ./target_repos/<last segment> (server.rs:393-399), and an existing directory is reused (server.rs:460-465) without checking owner, remote, branch or commit. alice/utils and bob/utils share one directory. Clones are never refreshed. A clone interrupted by restart_server.sh kill -9 is later treated as complete. Differs from SRV-07 (fallback when the dir is missing).
impact: Users silently receive another owner's code, stale code, or a partial checkout reported as success.
recommendation: Key the cache by normalized host/owner/repo plus resolved commit, and verify git remote get-url origin. Clone into a temp dir and rename atomically on success. Refresh or expire entries. Test: two owners with the same repo name get different analyses.

title: restart_server.sh SIGKILLs every process using the port, including clients
evidence: lsof -t -i:${PORT} (restart_server.sh:11) matches sockets whose local or remote port is 8080. That includes browsers, IDEs and any app connected to a remote :8080 service or proxy, and all of them are killed with kill -9 (line 14) without confirmation. Both make server and make serve run it (Makefile:39-44).
impact: Starting the dev server can force-kill unrelated applications and lose unsaved work.
recommendation: Select listeners only (lsof -t -iTCP:$PORT -sTCP:LISTEN) and check that the process is openheart or cargo. Send SIGTERM and wait before SIGKILL, and ask before killing any other process.

ENG.note: restart_server.sh already selects only LISTEN sockets, stops only openheart processes (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and refuses to touch anything else. The Makefile `server` target only calls that script on Unix, and on Windows it starts without killing anything.

title: Docker builder toolchain is likely too old for the locked dependencies
evidence: Dockerfile:2 pins rust:1.80-slim. Cargo.lock pins sha2 0.11.1 (digest 0.11.3, hybrid-array 0.4.15) and getrandom 0.4.3; these release lines use edition 2024 and need Rust 1.85 or later. Cargo.toml has no rust-version, and CI tests only stable and beta (ci.yml:19). Differs from SRV-11: the image cannot be built at all.
impact: docker build fails while compiling dependencies, even after the CMD in SRV-03 is fixed.
recommendation: Pin a current toolchain image by digest, declare rust-version in Cargo.toml, and add MSRV and docker-build CI jobs.

ENG.note: rust-version 1.88 is declared, with a comment that dependency upgrades must raise it. The Dockerfile is already on rust:1.88-slim-bookworm. Digest pinning and the MSRV/docker CI jobs are in handoffs.

title: Server collects ~60 extensions the pipeline cannot parse
evidence: collect_files accepts py, rs, go, c/cpp, sh, sql, rb, php, asm and more (server.rs:807-867). AdapterRegistry registers only Java, Kotlin (parsed with the Java grammar) and JavaScript, and sends every other language to a JavaScript-grammar fallback (registry.rs:24-57, kotlin.rs:29-30). The suite's own target, the OpenHeart repo (scripts/test_full_suite.py:129), is mostly Rust, Python and JS.
impact: Shell, SQL, C and Python files are tokenized as JavaScript, which pollutes results and wastes time on polyglot repos.
recommendation: Collect only extensions that have a registered adapter (query AdapterRegistry), make the set configurable, and report skipped-file counts in stats. Test: a repo with Foo.java and build.sh yields only Foo.

title: Directory and test-name heuristics drop production sources
evidence: collect_files skips directories named build, out, dist, vendor, target, test, tests, spec or specs at any depth (server.rs:771-803). It also drops files whose lowercase stem ends in test or tests (server.rs:875-881). Real packages such as com/android/build and org/springframework/test disappear, and classes Contest, Latest and Greatest are dropped, while FooIT and FooSpec tests are kept.
impact: Common Java and Android projects silently lose packages and classes from their diagrams.
recommendation: Exclude build outputs only at module roots (next to build.gradle/pom.xml) and treat only src/test* and src/androidTest* as test roots. Use explicit, case-aware test-name patterns and make filters configurable. Tests: a package named build and a class Contest are kept.

title: CLI and server select different files for the same repository
evidence: main.rs:76-99 includes hidden dirs (.gradle, .idea), build/ and generated sources, test sources and Gradle .kts scripts, and matches extensions case-sensitively. server.rs:764-890 lowercases extensions, skips hidden, build and test dirs and test-named files, and adds ~57 non-JVM extensions.
impact: The CLI and the web studio report different classes, hashes and diagrams for the same input.
recommendation: Move discovery into one library function with an options struct (include/exclude globs, test policy) and use it from both entry points. Test that both select the same files for a fixture tree.

title: CLI scan aborts or double-counts on symlinks and unreadable entries
evidence: collect_source_files recurses via p.is_dir(), which follows symlinks, and propagates every read_dir and entry error with ? (main.rs:84-96). A self-referential link re-collects files until ELOOP, and then the whole analyze fails with 'Failed to scan directory'. A single permission-denied subdirectory also aborts the run.
impact: openheart analyze fails outright, or counts sources twice, on repos with symlinks or unreadable folders.
recommendation: Skip symlinked dirs (or dedupe by canonical path), warn and continue on per-entry errors, and dedupe the final list. Test: a temp tree with a loop link yields each file once.

title: Hand-built JSON responses are invalid for common error strings
evidence: Phase 1-6 error branches insert the raw error string (server.rs:530-604), and ingestion errors contain Debug-quoted paths (src/ingestion/mod.rs:52). The no-sources branch embeds target_dir.display() (server.rs:495-502), which on Windows contains sequences like ./target_repos\FractalAndroid. escape_json_str leaves other control characters unescaped (server.rs:701-707). Node's JSON.parse rejects all three cases.
impact: Clients get a parse error instead of the failure reason; on Windows every missing-sources error is unparseable.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json (json! or Serialize structs), including error paths, and delete escape_json_str. Test: each error branch's body parses with serde_json::from_str.

title: Status codes and error schema do not reflect outcomes
evidence: /api/analyze always answers 200, even for a missing repo_url, malformed JSON or phase failures (server.rs:252-253, 374-382). respond_json labels every non-200 code 'Not Found' (server.rs:321-325). Malformed request lines get no response (server.rs:61-64), and wrong methods get 404 instead of 405. Phase errors also omit the session_id and logs that other errors include.
impact: Clients and monitors cannot detect failures reliably and must parse response bodies.
recommendation: Have handlers return a status plus a typed body: 400 for bad input, 502 for clone failure, 500 for phase errors, 405 with Allow. Use a complete reason-phrase table and one error schema. Add per-route status tests.

title: repo_url is extracted by splitting on quotes, not by parsing JSON
evidence: process_analyze_request takes the fourth quote-delimited token after the first "repo_url" (server.rs:367-370). Emulation shows {"repo_url":null,"branch":"main"} yields 'branch'. A nested {"meta":{"repo_url":...}} key wins over the top-level one. Escaped quotes truncate the value, and \/ escapes are passed to git unchanged.
impact: Valid JSON payloads clone or analyze the wrong repository.
recommendation: Deserialize into a typed AnalyzeRequest {repo_url, branch, diagram_types} with serde_json and return 400 on schema errors. Tests for null, nested and escaped inputs.

title: Session temp directory leaked on every error or panic path
evidence: tmp_path is created at server.rs:506-513 but removed only at server.rs:693. The early returns for Phase 1-6 failures (server.rs:527-605) and any panic skip cleanup, leaving corpus.tca, ast.bpa and other artifacts in the system temp directory.
impact: Every failed analysis leaks disk space indefinitely.
recommendation: Hold the directory in tempfile::TempDir (promote tempfile from a dev-dependency) or a Drop guard so cleanup runs on every path. Test: a forced Phase 1 failure leaves no openheart_sess_* directory.

title: On Windows the temp dir is not deleted while corpus.tca is still mapped
evidence: stage_input owns a MemoryMappedFile of corpus.tca (server.rs:539-546) and lives until process_analyze_request returns, but remove_dir_all runs earlier (server.rs:693). Windows refuses to delete a file with a live mapped view, and let _ = hides the failure.
impact: Under run.bat, even successful analyses leave their artifacts in %TEMP%.
recommendation: Drop stage_input before cleanup (put the pipeline in its own block) and log cleanup errors. Add a Windows CI test that the session dir is gone after a request.

title: Server swallows I/O failures that the CLI treats as fatal
evidence: Artifact reads use fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default() (server.rs:536, 556, 581, 593, 609). The .sta write result is discarded (server.rs:569), and diagram dir and file writes are ignored (server.rs:638, 671-689). main.rs:154-226 propagates the same failures with ?. Stale web/diagrams files also survive a failed export. Differs from SRV-13 (duplicated orchestration).
impact: Empty buffers feed hash links and later phases, and the UI shows a previous repo's diagrams while reporting success.
recommendation: Propagate errors with ? into an error response through a helper shared with the CLI. Delete stale outputs before writing, and list failed exports in errors. Test: an unwritable diagram dir yields an error status.

title: Synchronous /api/analyze runs longer than the studio's 2.5 s fetch abort
evidence: Nothing is written until the clone and the whole pipeline finish (server.rs:241-253, 732-761). The main studio aborts the fetch after 2500 ms (web/index.html:862) and switches to the in-browser engine. The server keeps cloning and analyzing, with no cancellation, job id or progress endpoint. Differs from SRV-04: this is a protocol mismatch, not only throughput.
impact: The main UI never uses the native backend for real repositories, yet each attempt still blocks the server.
recommendation: Make analysis asynchronous: POST returns 202 with a job id, GET /api/jobs/{id} returns status, progress and result, and DELETE cancels. Stop the work when the client disconnects. Test the job lifecycle.

title: /api/source misses trigger full recursive walks of all roots
evidence: When the direct path misses, walkdir_find scans five roots on every request (server.rs:208-223). That includes ./target_repos with every .git objects directory, because hidden dirs are not skipped (server.rs:342-361). It collects all matches instead of stopping at the first, and caches nothing. Differs from SRV-01 (access control).
impact: Every source-view click walks all cached clones, stalling the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Resolve sources from the analysis file table (file_id to repo-relative path) or an index built after each analysis. Skip .git and stop at the first exact match.

title: /api/source returns an arbitrary or wrong file for common names
evidence: walkdir_find returns matches in read_dir order and the first one is served (server.rs:215-217). Duplicate basenames (Main.java, Utils.java across packages or repos) therefore resolve nondeterministically. Matching strips .java/.kt from both names (server.rs:350-354), so Foo.java can resolve to Foo.kt or to an extensionless file named Foo.
impact: The editor shows source from a different class or repository than the node that was clicked.
recommendation: Look files up by repo-relative path from the traceability data. If a basename fallback stays, require exact names, scope it to the active repo, sort candidates, and return 409 with the candidates when ambiguous.

title: /api/source query parsing and percent-decoding are incomplete
evidence: Only %2F, %20 and %2B are decoded (server.rs:96-112). The editor sends encodeURIComponent output (editor.js:160), which also produces %24, %5C, %3A, %26, %25 and UTF-8 sequences, so Outer$Inner.java, Windows backslash paths and non-ASCII names never resolve. Values are cut at a second '=', '+' is not decoded to a space, and lowercase %2f is ignored. Differs from SRV-01.
impact: Source view fails for Windows-produced paths and for many legitimate file names.
recommendation: Decode with a real percent or form decoder (the percent-encoding or form_urlencoded crate) and split pairs with split_once('='). Tests for $, backslash, UTF-8 and '=' inside values.

title: /api/supported-languages advertises languages that are not supported
evidence: server.rs:82-85 lists java, python, typescript, javascript, cpp, rust and go, and omits kotlin. Only Java, Kotlin (via the Java grammar) and JavaScript adapters exist (registry.rs:24-39, kotlin.rs:29-30); every other language falls back to the JavaScript grammar.
impact: Clients are told Python, Rust, Go and C++ work, and get JavaScript-grammar garbage instead.
recommendation: Generate the list from AdapterRegistry with an accuracy or maturity flag per language, and include Kotlin with its caveat.

title: No write timeout: a client that stops reading blocks the server
evidence: handle_connection sets only a read timeout (server.rs:47). write_all for large bodies blocks indefinitely once the peer's receive window fills, both in serve_file (server.rs:310-311) and for analyze and source JSON in respond_json (server.rs:333). Differs from SRV-06, which concerns read timeouts.
impact: One slow or malicious client holding a large response stalls all other requests indefinitely.
recommendation: Call set_write_timeout (for example 10 s), treat a timeout as an aborted connection, and bound the total time per connection.

title: No Host-header validation enables DNS rebinding
evidence: handle_connection never inspects the Host header (server.rs:54-77), so it serves any hostname that resolves to it. A rebinding domain gets same-origin access to /api/analyze and /api/source even after CORS * (SRV-05) is removed.
impact: Restricting CORS alone will not stop malicious websites from reaching the local server.
recommendation: Reject requests whose Host is not in an allowlist (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], configured names) with 421 or 403, and add tests.

title: Credentials embedded in repo_url are logged, echoed and persisted
evidence: The raw URL is printed to stdout (server.rs:384), returned in the response logs (server.rs:387-390, 423-426), and saved by git in ./target_repos/<name>/.git/config. Users commonly paste https://user:token@github.com/... for private repos. Differs from SRV-15 (paths and git stderr).
impact: Personal access tokens leak into terminals, API responses and on-disk clone metadata that /api/source can read.
recommendation: Reject URLs that contain userinfo, or redact it before logging and echoing and strip it from the clone's remote config. Sanitize control characters in logged URLs.

title: GitHub tree/sub-directory URLs are mapped to wrong paths
evidence: For https://github.com/o/r/tree/main/sub/dir, repo_name becomes 'dir' (server.rs:393-398), and the sub-path probe looks for ./target_repos/r/tree/main/sub/dir (server.rs:407-414), which never exists. git is then asked to clone the tree URL, which fails. Non-GitHub URLs split into parts such as 'https:' and an empty string.
impact: Branch or sub-directory URLs, a common way to point at part of a repo, always fail or land on the fallback repo.
recommendation: Parse owner, repo, optional ref and sub-path. Clone owner/repo with --branch <ref> and analyze <clone>/<subpath>. Tests for tree URLs, trailing slash and .git.

title: ./target_repos grows without bound
evidence: Every distinct repo name is cloned into ./target_repos (server.rs:428-437) and never evicted. There is no quota, no per-clone size limit and no cleanup endpoint. Differs from SRV-04 (per-request limits): this is storage that accumulates across requests.
impact: Long-running or exposed servers run out of disk, and basename walks get slower over time.
recommendation: Add an LRU cache with total-size and age limits, per-clone size checks (--filter=blob:limit plus a post-clone size check), and an admin cleanup command.

title: A lone verbosity flag panics the CLI
evidence: main.rs:491 checks args.len() < 2 before flags are stripped. After args.retain (main.rs:499, 505), 'openheart --verbose' or 'openheart --trace' leaves only the program name, and main.rs:508 reads args[1], panicking with index out of bounds. Differs from SRV-10: a crash, not dropped flags.
impact: A trivial invocation crashes with a Rust panic instead of printing usage.
recommendation: Strip flags first, then check how many arguments remain (or adopt clap). Test: running with only --trace prints usage and exits 2.

title: inspect reports 'CRC-64 VERIFIED VALID' without verifying
evidence: For .tca and .bpa, cmd_inspect only compares the magic, then prints the verified line (main.rs:373-389) without calling the readers that check the CRC (ingestion/serializer.rs:175-193, ast/serializer.rs:72-86). It prints the compiled-in TCA_VERSION and a hard-coded '1' instead of the file's version. .scpg section CRC32s are never checked (scpg/mmap/mod.rs:17-79), and deserializer errors are discarded (main.rs:481-484).
impact: Corrupted artifacts are certified as valid, which misleads integrity checks and bug triage.
recommendation: Call TokenCorpusSerializer::read and BPASTSerializer::read, verify .scpg section CRCs, print the file's version, and surface the underlying error. Test with a byte-flipped .tca.

title: Requested diagram types and branch are ignored; web_repo config is dead code
evidence: Clients send diagram_types (web/index.html:869, api.js:34-37), but the server reads only repo_url (server.rs:366-372) and always computes everything. WebRepoConfig {branch, selected_diagrams} and UmlDiagramType (web_repo.rs:8-90) are never used. The module doc promises fetching logic and calls a HashSet-based enum a 'Bitmask' (web_repo.rs:1-8). Differs from SRV-02 (validate_url).
impact: Branches and tags cannot be analyzed, unrequested diagrams waste work, and the public API is misleading.
recommendation: Parse a typed request into WebRepoConfig: pass branch to git --branch, parse diagram names with FromStr for UmlDiagramType, and export only the selected diagrams. Otherwise delete the module, and fix the docs. Test: requesting only class returns only class.

title: Monolithic connection handler with no Request/Response abstraction
evidence: handle_connection (server.rs:46-290) mixes socket I/O, request parsing, an if/else route chain, query parsing and business logic. Handlers write straight to TcpStream, and process_analyze_request returns preformatted JSON strings.
impact: Routes cannot be unit-tested without sockets, and every fix touches one 250-line function.
recommendation: Introduce Request and Response types and a route table whose handlers are pure functions, or adopt a small HTTP crate (tiny_http, axum). Add per-route unit tests.

title: Server is hard-wired to CWD-relative paths with no configuration
evidence: The web root 'web' (server.rs:78, 257-258), ./target_repos (server.rs:399, 428), the ./examples roots (server.rs:122-123, 209-210) and the web/diagrams output (server.rs:637) all resolve against the process CWD. OpenHeartServer holds only a port (server.rs:22-29). When started from another directory, every page returns 404 and nothing is logged at startup.
impact: Running the installed binary outside the repo root, or as a service, silently breaks the studio and the clone cache.
recommendation: Add a ServerConfig (bind address, web_root, cache_dir, output_dir, limits) read from CLI or env, validate paths at startup, and default to executable-relative or XDG directories.

title: Dockerfile PORT and HOST environment variables are ignored
evidence: Dockerfile:43-44 sets PORT=8080 and HOST=0.0.0.0, but the port comes only from argv (main.rs:532-537) and the bind host is hard-coded (server.rs:32). Nothing reads either variable. Differs from SRV-14 (.env.example knobs).
impact: On platforms that inject PORT (Cloud Run, Heroku, Render), traffic goes to a port the app never binds.
recommendation: Read PORT and HOST (or OPENHEART_PORT and OPENHEART_BIND) in main, with CLI flags taking precedence, or remove the ENV lines.

title: Security doc presents CRC-64 and SHA-256 as tamper protection
evidence: docs/security-architecture.md:16-20 titles the section 'Tamper Protection', but CRC-64 is unkeyed and anyone can recompute it. The stored SHA-256 digests are written (serializer.rs:77, 109) but never re-verified. Ingestion also hashes one read of each file and tokenizes a second read (mod.rs:53, 111). Differs from SRV-14.
impact: Users may treat artifacts as tamper-evident when they only detect accidental corruption.
recommendation: Reword the section as corruption detection, or add an HMAC or signature and verify source hashes on load. Hash and tokenize the same buffer.

title: Security docs omit the network-facing server and clone path
evidence: docs/security-architecture.md:9-34 covers only ingestion, hashing and bounds, and line 33 says there are no local path assumptions, although server.rs:119-214 hard-codes paths. SECURITY.md:26 lists only the parser, interner and tree-sitter as components. Binding, CORS, authentication, git cloning and cache storage are not documented.
impact: Operators have no guidance on the most exposed attack surface, and reporters may treat it as out of scope.
recommendation: Add a threat model for the HTTP server and clone adapter (trust boundaries, defaults, hardening, safe deployment) and list both as in-scope components.

title: SCPG query engine and XMI exporter are unreachable from CLI and API
evidence: OpenHeartEngine exposes is_reachable, backward_slice and export_xmi (scpg/api/mod.rs:51-83). main.rs uses the engine only for scpg_hash (main.rs:243-337) and has no query subcommand. The server never builds the engine and has no query routes. Neither entry point exports XMI (main.rs:281-309, server.rs:663-691).
impact: The advertised query engine and XMI output cannot be used without writing Rust code.
recommendation: Add 'openheart query <scpg> reachable|slice ...' and a --format xmi option, plus /api/query/* endpoints backed by one engine per session. Test each command.

title: Predictable temp path; pre-existing dirs accepted; create errors ignored
evidence: tmp_path is temp_dir()/openheart_sess_<unix nanos> (server.rs:506-512). let _ = fs::create_dir_all (server.rs:513) accepts an existing directory or symlink and ignores failures. On shared hosts, artifacts can therefore be written into a location an attacker created in advance; otherwise later phases fail with confusing errors.
impact: Other local users can tamper with intermediate artifacts on multi-user machines.
recommendation: Create the session dir with tempfile::Builder (random name, exclusive create, mode 0700) and propagate errors.

title: Non-UTF-8 sources are reported missing and may be substituted
evidence: Candidates are read with fs::read_to_string (server.rs:201, 217). A Latin-1 or Windows-1252 Java file fails with InvalidData, and the loop moves on to other candidates or the basename walk. It may serve a different file with the same name, or return 404 'not found on server disk'.
impact: Projects in legacy encodings cannot show source, or show the wrong file.
recommendation: Read bytes and decode lossily (or detect the encoding), and tell 'unreadable' apart from 'not found' in the response.

title: Whole-file reads with no size cap in /api/source and static serving
evidence: /api/source loads any matched file into a String and JSON-encodes it (server.rs:201, 217, 227-232). serve_file reads whole files with fs::read (server.rs:303), with no streaming and no Range support.
impact: Large files (logs, bundles, binaries in clones) cause memory spikes and multi-megabyte responses.
recommendation: Enforce a maximum source size and return 413 above it, stream static files with io::copy, and support Range requests.

title: Hard-coded demo paths baked into /api/source
evidence: direct_candidates hard-codes ./target_repos/FractalAndroid/ and nine design-pattern package directories under two roots (server.rs:119-198), plus fixed search roots including ./web (server.rs:208-214). All 24 strings are formatted on every request. Differs from SRV-01: maintainability, not access control.
impact: Behavior depends on one developer's local layout, and unrelated repositories are probed.
recommendation: Remove the hard-coded candidates and resolve paths relative to the analyzed repo root recorded for each session.

title: Version, health and capability endpoints are hard-coded
evidence: /api/health always returns online, 'OpenHeart SCPG v0.1.0' and plantuml:true (server.rs:80), although the server renders nothing. /api/version hard-codes 0.1.0, build 'production' and release_date 2026-08-22 (server.rs:93), and main.rs:32 repeats v0.1.0. /api/patterns and /api/supported-diagrams are hand-copied lists (server.rs:86-91). The module doc advertises Telemetry, which does not exist (server.rs:2).
impact: Reported versions drift from Cargo.toml, debug builds claim to be production, and health never reflects failures.
recommendation: Use env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), cfg!(debug_assertions) and a build-time git SHA, and derive the lists from the engine. Make the health check test git availability and writable dirs.

title: HTTP/1.1 framing gaps: no Connection: close, abrupt close, absolute-form
evidence: Responses are HTTP/1.1 with Content-Length but no 'Connection: close' (server.rs:305-307, 326-328), yet the socket is closed after one request. Unread request bytes are dropped without shutdown or drain, so the kernel may send RST and destroy the response. Absolute-form targets (GET http://host/path) fall through to 404 (server.rs:254).
impact: Keep-alive clients and large POSTs see sporadic connection resets, and proxy-style requests fail.
recommendation: Send Connection: close (or implement keep-alive), shut down the write half and drain input briefly before closing, and accept absolute-form targets.

title: Every CLI command creates log files in the current directory
evidence: main.rs:488 calls init_logger_from_env, which opens ./openheart_persistent.log (append) and ./openheart_session.log (logger.rs:110-112), even for help, inspect and server. analyze then re-initializes into OUTPUT_DIR (main.rs:129), leaving stray files in the CWD. The server appends all pipeline logs to the CWD files for its whole lifetime, with no rotation.
impact: Repos fill up with log files, read-only CWDs fail silently, and server log files grow without limit.
recommendation: Enable file logging only for analyze and server, with an explicit --log-dir and size-based rotation. Keep help and inspect console-only.

title: Combined or misplaced flags become positional arguments
evidence: When both --trace and --debug or -v are given, the else-if at main.rs:497-506 strips only --trace. 'openheart analyze src --trace --debug' therefore uses '--debug' as OUTPUT_DIR and creates a directory with that name. 'openheart analyze --help' treats '--help' as the source path.
impact: Output lands in surprising locations and errors are confusing.
recommendation: Strip every recognized flag independently and keep the highest verbosity. Support -h/--help per subcommand and reject unknown dash-prefixed arguments.

title: Command output goes through the logger and can be silenced
evidence: inspect results and the analyze summary are printed with log_info (main.rs:311-342, 354-475). OPENHEART_LOG=warn or off (logger.rs:98-107) suppresses them, so openheart inspect prints nothing and exits 0.
impact: Users and scripts lose the command's main output when they lower log verbosity.
recommendation: Print results to stdout directly (optionally as --json) and keep the logger for diagnostics.

title: analyze reports success when diagram export fails and keeps stale files
evidence: main.rs:258 and 289-307 discard create_dir_all and fs::write errors with .ok() and ignore export_diagram returning None. main.rs:311-341 then logs 'SUCCESS' and 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' unconditionally. Diagram files from earlier runs in the same OUTPUT_DIR remain and look current.
impact: Users and CI do not notice missing or stale diagrams.
recommendation: Collect export failures, warn per file, and remove stale outputs first. Exit non-zero, or print a partial-success summary.

title: Artifact bytes depend on how the source path was spelled
evidence: cmd_analyze passes paths exactly as given or joined (main.rs:104-111, 151), and ingestion interns them into the .tca (ingestion/mod.rs:137-138). 'analyze ./src', 'analyze src' and an absolute path therefore produce different .tca bytes, CRC hash links and SCPG hashes. Absolute paths also embed the user's home directory.
impact: Hashes are not reproducible across machines or invocations, and local paths leak into shared artifacts.
recommendation: Store paths relative to the source root with forward slashes and record the root separately. Test that ./src and src give the same SCPG hash.

title: CLI usage text misdescribes inputs, outputs and checks
evidence: print_usage says analyze scans '.java source files' (main.rs:41), but .kt and .kts are included (main.rs:80). It promises 14 UML diagrams as *.puml and *.mmd, but 19 types and .json files are written (main.rs:53, 260-308). inspect lists six artifact types and CRC-64, though .tra/.psa/.uma/.scpg are handled and .scpg uses CRC32 (main.rs:55-56). server claims PlantUML rendering, which does not exist (main.rs:59).
impact: Users get wrong expectations about what the tool accepts and produces.
recommendation: Generate help from the real argument definitions (clap) and correct each description.

title: Usage errors exit 0 or print to stdout
evidence: Running with no arguments prints usage and exits 0 (main.rs:491-494). 'Error:' messages for missing arguments and unknown subcommands use println! (main.rs:512, 526, 545), while fatal errors use eprintln! (main.rs:552).
impact: Scripts cannot detect misuse, and error text ends up in captured stdout.
recommendation: Print errors to stderr and exit with status 2 for usage errors.

title: Startup banner prints an unusable or wrong address; IPv4-only bind
evidence: start() prints the requested address (server.rs:32-38), so port 0 is announced as ':0' instead of listener.local_addr(). The printed http://0.0.0.0:PORT (also restart_server.sh:20) is blocked by current Chrome and cannot be reached on Windows. Only 0.0.0.0 is bound, so clients that resolve localhost to ::1 first fail or retry.
impact: Startup output is confusing, and connections are slow or fail on IPv6-first hosts.
recommendation: Print local_addr() and a browsable http://localhost URL, and support a configurable bind address including [::].

title: Accept errors are silently discarded and can spin the CPU
evidence: listener.incoming().flatten() (server.rs:40) drops accept errors with no logging or backoff. A persistent error such as EMFILE makes the loop spin at full CPU.
impact: Failures stay hidden, and the CPU is burned when file descriptors run out.
recommendation: Match each Result, log errors, and back off on resource-exhaustion errors.

title: Header and body sent in separate writes with Nagle enabled
evidence: serve_file writes the header and the body in two write_all calls (server.rs:310-311) on a socket without set_nodelay. A small body can wait for the client's delayed ACK of the header segment, which takes up to 40 ms on Linux and 200 ms on Windows.
impact: Each static asset may gain latency, which adds up on the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Write header and body from one buffer (or one BufWriter flush) and/or call set_nodelay(true).

title: Static file serving gaps (MIME, charset, decoding, directory index)
evidence: Only js, css, svg and html get a content type (server.rs:274-284), so .png, .ico, .json, .puml, .mmd and .mjs are served as application/octet-stream. '; charset=utf-8' is appended even to binary types (server.rs:306). Extension checks are case-sensitive, request paths are not percent-decoded (server.rs:256), and directories do not resolve to index.html.
impact: MIME types are wrong (module scripts with .mjs fail), and files with spaces or Unicode names cannot be served.
recommendation: Use a complete MIME map and add charset only for text types. Percent-decode the path and then re-validate it, and serve index.html for directories.

title: No caching validators or compression
evidence: serve_file and respond_json send no ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control or Content-Encoding headers (server.rs:305-307, 326-328). index.html (79 KB), style.css (42 KB) and large analyze JSON are re-sent uncompressed on every load.
impact: Page loads are slower and transfers larger on a server that is already single-threaded.
recommendation: Add ETag and Last-Modified with 304 handling, set Cache-Control per asset class, and gzip responses above a size threshold when Accept-Encoding allows.

title: PlantUML diagrams generated twice; alias types written redundantly
evidence: The 14 PlantUML diagrams are built with PlantUMLExporter::export_* (server.rs:620-634) and again by diag_engine.export_diagram in the 21-type loop (server.rs:640-672). That loop also includes the aliases use_case and state, which write duplicate JSON files. The comment says 19 diagram formats (server.rs:636), and escaping allocates five strings per diagram (server.rs:701-707).
impact: CPU and memory are wasted on large repositories, and the comment is misleading.
recommendation: Generate each diagram once into a map and reuse it for both the files and the response. Handle aliases in routing instead of writing duplicate files.

title: Traceability payload is truncated and mislabeled
evidence: Only the first 10 uml_links are returned, with no total (server.rs:710). 'tid' carries link.sym_id (server.rs:724-725), but the viewer labels the column TOKEN ID (viewer.js:114, 123). A missing file record gets an invented file_<id>.kt name (server.rs:717). Symbol name and sym_kind are left out, and the same list is shown for every projection.
impact: Users see an incomplete and mislabeled traceability matrix.
recommendation: Return paginated links with a total and rename the field to sym_id. Add the symbol name, kind and repo-relative path, and filter per diagram type.

title: Session id is a seconds timestamp; no real SCPG hash is returned
evidence: session_id is sess_<unix seconds> (server.rs:376-380, 733-737), so it collides within the same second and is not tied to any stored session. The server neither runs Phase 10 nor returns any hash, so the studio shows the timestamp's last 8 digits as 'SCPG 0x... Verified' (web/index.html:890-891). This adds to SRV-13's missing Phase 10.
impact: The UI's 'verified hash' badge is made from a clock value.
recommendation: Use random unique ids, and return the real scpg_hash (or the TRA composite hash) as an explicit field.

title: validate_url silently rewrites names and accepts plaintext http
evidence: validate_url accepts http://github.com (web_repo.rs:99) and deletes '..' and backslashes instead of rejecting them (web_repo.rs:111-112), so 'o..x/repo' validates as owner 'ox'. Any characters (?, #, %, spaces) pass, a '.git/' suffix is kept, and the host match is case-sensitive. Tests cover only the happy path (web_repo.rs:126-133). Differs from SRV-08 (index panic).
impact: Once wired in, it could clone a different repository than requested, over a transport open to man-in-the-middle attacks.
recommendation: Parse with a URL parser, require https and host github.com (case-insensitive), validate owner and repo against [A-Za-z0-9._-], and reject rather than rewrite. Add a test for each case.

title: HTTP server and git shell-out compiled into the library crate
evidence: lib.rs:1 exports pub mod adapters (server and web_repo), and Cargo.toml defines no features. Every library consumer therefore compiles an HTTP server that spawns git and writes to CWD-relative directories.
impact: Embedders who only need the analysis engine get a larger attack surface and longer builds.
recommendation: Move the server into the binary crate, or put it behind an optional 'server' cargo feature.

ENG.note: Declared feature `server` (on by default) and made the openheart bin require it. `make check` also builds the library with --no-default-features. The cfg gating in src/adapters is in handoffs.

title: No request logging or structured observability
evidence: Only ad-hoc println! lines exist (server.rs:35-38, 314, 384), and they bypass the project logger and its levels. There is no per-request line with method, path, status and latency, no request id and no metrics.
impact: Incidents and abuse are hard to diagnose.
recommendation: Log one structured line per request through the logger, and add request ids and an optional metrics endpoint.

title: No graceful shutdown
evidence: start() loops over incoming() forever (server.rs:40-43), with no signal handling or stop flag. SIGTERM or Ctrl-C kills the process mid-clone or mid-write, leaving partial clones, temp dirs and half-written web/diagrams files (fs::write is not atomic, server.rs:671-689).
impact: Cache and output state can be corrupt after a restart.
recommendation: Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM: stop accepting, then finish or abort jobs cleanly. Write outputs to a temp file and rename.

title: No result cache: identical requests rerun the whole pipeline
evidence: Even when ./target_repos/<name> already exists, every request reruns Phases 1-9 and all exporters (server.rs:505-691). Nothing is keyed by commit SHA or source tree hash.
impact: Each repeat view of the same repository costs seconds to minutes.
recommendation: Cache results keyed by repository, commit, engine version and options, and serve the cached JSON and diagrams.

title: No file-count or file-size caps although file ids are 16-bit
evidence: The server passes every collected file to ingestion (server.rs:484-515) with no count or size limit. Ingestion casts file_id to u16 (ingestion/mod.rs:70, 123), and Phase 2 reads file_count as u16 (ast/mod.rs:59). Repositories with more than 65,535 matching files therefore wrap ids silently. Differs from SRV-04: the results are corrupted, not just slow.
impact: Large monorepos give corrupted cross-file results instead of a clear error.
recommendation: Reject or shard inputs above 65,535 files or above a per-file size limit with an explicit error, and make the limits configurable.

title: Expect: 100-continue is not supported
evidence: The server never sends 'HTTP/1.1 100 Continue' (server.rs:241-250). curl (for bodies over 1 KiB) and .NET clients wait up to a second for it before sending the body. The server's second read times out after 500 ms and answers that repo_url is missing.
impact: Larger analyze payloads from standard clients fail for no real reason.
recommendation: Detect Expect: 100-continue and reply 100 before reading the body, or adopt an HTTP library.

title: Redundant and unreachable checks in collect_files
evidence: target, node_modules and build are tested twice (server.rs:771-773 and 779-781). lower_name == '.git' (server.rs:786) can never match, because names starting with a dot are already skipped (server.rs:770). The '_test', '_tests' and == 'test' checks (server.rs:877-881) are already covered by ends_with('test') and ends_with('tests').
impact: Dead conditions hide the actual filtering rules.
recommendation: Replace them with one declarative exclusion set when discovery is unified (SRV2-11).

title: Docker build is not reproducible and copies the wrong inputs
evidence: cargo build runs without --locked (Dockerfile:16, 23). tests/ is copied although the binary build never uses it (Dockerfile:20), which invalidates the layer cache. examples/ is not copied (Dockerfile:40), although /api/source and the demos expect ./examples (server.rs:122-123, 209-210).
impact: The lockfile can drift inside images, rebuilds are slower, and source lookups break in containers.
recommendation: Use cargo build --release --locked --bin openheart, drop COPY tests, and either copy examples or explicitly exclude it, with a documented runtime layout.

title: Launchers open the browser too early, run debug builds and lose fallbacks
evidence: run.sh opens the browser after 1 s (run.sh:33) and run.bat opens it immediately (run.bat:21), while cargo run may still be compiling for minutes. Both use the dev profile (run.sh:34, run.bat:22). If the build fails, exec cargo run (run.sh:34) and goto :eof (run.bat:23) skip the Python fallback.
impact: First-run users see connection errors, get a slower server, and have no fallback when the build fails.
recommendation: Run cargo build --release first and fall back on failure. Poll /api/health before opening the browser, then exec the release binary.

title: Direct-file fallback cannot load the module-based studio
evidence: When neither cargo nor Python is found, run.sh:52-54 and run.bat:51-55 open web/index.html via file://. The page uses ES modules (script type=module, web/index.html:408) and fetches diagrams/*.json, and Chromium browsers block both for file:// origins.
impact: The last-resort launcher shows a broken or empty studio.
recommendation: Open the hosted Pages URL instead, or ship a non-module bundle for file:// use, and print a clear message.

title: run.bat batch-parsing hazards: unescaped ')' in a block, delayed expansion
evidence: Inside the 'where py ... && ( ... )' block, line 36 echoes 'Python launcher (py) detected'. Its unescaped ')' closes the block early, leaving a syntax error once execution reaches line 35. setlocal enabledelayedexpansion (run.bat:2) is unused, but it corrupts paths containing '!' in cd /d "%~dp0" (run.bat:15).
impact: Systems with only the py launcher, or repo paths containing '!', get batch errors instead of the studio.
recommendation: Escape the parentheses as ^(py^), drop enabledelayedexpansion, and test the script with each interpreter combination.

title: run.bat trusts 'where python', which finds the Microsoft Store stub
evidence: run.bat:27 and 43 accept any python or python3 on PATH. On Windows 10/11 without Python, the WindowsApps execution alias is found, python -m http.server exits with 'Python was not found', and goto :eof (run.bat:32) ends the script before the py and direct-browser fallbacks.
impact: Users without Python get nothing instead of the documented fallbacks.
recommendation: Probe with python -c "import sys" and check errorlevel before choosing a branch, and fall through on failure.

title: run.bat is checked out with LF line endings
evidence: .gitattributes:2 forces '* text=auto eol=lf' with no override for *.bat, and the working copy of run.bat contains only LF (checked with od). cmd.exe parses LF-only batch files unreliably, especially label scanning and block parsing.
impact: Windows checkouts can hit intermittent batch failures that are hard to diagnose.
recommendation: Add '*.bat text eol=crlf' and '*.cmd text eol=crlf' to .gitattributes and renormalize.

ENG.note: .gitattributes sets *.bat and *.cmd to eol=crlf. The one-time renormalization of the existing checkout is a git state change and is in handoffs.

title: Python fallback listens on all interfaces and assumes Python 3.7+
evidence: python -m http.server PORT --directory web (run.sh:49; run.bat:31, 39, 47) binds every interface by default. --directory needs Python 3.7+, 'python' can be Python 2 on older systems, and the version is never checked.
impact: The studio is exposed to the LAN, and older interpreters fail with an argument error.
recommendation: Add --bind 127.0.0.1 and check the interpreter version before launching.

title: restart_server.sh misreports when lsof is missing and runs a debug build
evidence: '2>/dev/null || true' hides a missing lsof (restart_server.sh:11), so the script prints 'No existing server process found' and then cargo fails to bind. The script is Unix-only, yet the Makefile targets call it on every platform (Makefile:39-44). It runs cargo run (debug) with an unquoted ${PORT} (line 21).
impact: Diagnostics are misleading, the server runs slower, and make fails on Windows.
recommendation: Check command -v lsof (fall back to ss or fuser), quote variables, and run the release binary.

ENG.note: On Windows, `make server` now skips the Unix-only script and runs the release build directly (`cargo run --release --locked`). On Unix it calls the script, which already detects a missing lsof. Switching the script to a release build is in handoffs.

title: Makefile target hygiene issues
evidence: .PHONY (Makefile:1) is missing release, run and server, and help (Makefile:51-61) does not list run or server. server and serve are duplicate targets (Makefile:39-44). docs uses --open, which fails in headless environments (Makefile:28).
impact: Targets silently stop running if a file with the same name appears, and targets are hard to discover.
recommendation: Complete .PHONY, generate help from the ## comments, drop the duplicate target, and make --open optional.

ENG.note: .PHONY is complete, help is generated from ## comments, there is no duplicate recipe, and --open lives only in the separate docs target.

title: Security doc's input-bounds claims contradict the code
evidence: docs/security-architecture.md:26 says lines and columns are capped. In fact build_sort_key masks the line with 0x00FFFFFF after only a debug_assert (token.rs:122-123), and the walker truncates columns with 'as u16' (walker.rs:59). Line 27 says u16 length headers prevent unbounded allocation, but the interner silently truncates text beyond 65,535 bytes (interner.rs:99-101).
impact: Wrong positions on huge or minified files are neither documented nor expected.
recommendation: Implement saturation or explicit errors, and document the truncation behavior accurately.

title: Security contact address is unverifiable
evidence: SECURITY.md:19 and SUPPORT.md:26 send reports to security@openheart.dev. Nothing in the repository shows that the project controls that domain (it lives under a personal GitHub account), and GitHub private vulnerability reporting has to be enabled separately.
impact: Vulnerability reports may silently go nowhere.
recommendation: Verify the mailbox or make GitHub Security Advisories the primary channel, and state the PGP policy.

title: Package declarations are truncated at segments named data, object, open, sealed, abstract, val, var or fun
evidence: The package parser accepts a segment only if it is not in a keyword list containing data/object/open/sealed/abstract/val/var/fun (496-513), and stops at the first rejected segment (517-518). Simulating lines 470-527: `package org.springframework.data.jpa.repository;` gives "org.springframework"; `com.example.app.data.local` gives "com.example.app". All of these are legal package segments.
impact: Classes in common *.data.* and *.object.* packages get a truncated package symbol, path and file_package_names entry, so package diagrams and qualified names are wrong.
recommendation: Accept any identifier token as a segment and stop only at ';', a newline or unexpected punctuation; better, read package_declaration from the CST. Add test_pass1_package_with_data_segment asserting the full path in custom_package_names and file_package_names.

title: Primitive and JDK-stub type ids are not written to .sta, so int, void, String and List members render with blank types
evidence: Passes 3 and 4 store 0xB000_000x (primitives) and 0xC000_000x (stubs) as type ids. Only builder.symbols is serialized; stub records stay in std_lib.stub_records with name_id u32::MAX, and primitives have no record at all. SymbolTableArtifact::symbol() only indexes symbol_records, so resolve_name returns "" and PlantUML prints `+count : ` and `+getName() : `.
impact: Almost every class-diagram member whose type is a primitive, void or a JDK type loses its type. TH_USES targets also point to ids that are not in .sta.
recommendation: Insert stub and primitive SymbolRecords (with interned names and qual_name_id) into the table when the builder is created, or serialize them as a typed side table that symbol() can read. Replace magic id ranges with an explicit SymbolRef enum. Test resolve_name for int, void and String members after a round trip.

title: TH_EXTENDS vs TH_IMPLEMENTS is guessed from the target's kind, so implements clauses become extends edges
evidence: The AST eliminates the superclass and super_interfaces nodes, so Pass 5 sees bare TYPE_REFs and only emits IMPLEMENTS for class-to-interface pairs. Enums and records implementing interfaces, and classes implementing external interfaces such as Runnable or Serializable, get EXTENDS. The test sample `extends BaseService implements Runnable` produces two EXTENDS edges, and class_diagram keeps the last one, so the superclass shown is Runnable. Lines 64-67 duplicate the else branch, and target kinds are never checked.
impact: Class diagrams show the wrong superclass and apparent multiple inheritance; enums and records lose their realization edges.
recommendation: Keep the clause information: retain the superclass and super_interfaces nodes or tag their TYPE_REFs in NodeAttr, and derive the relation from syntax. In the token scan, use the keyword actually seen. Reject targets that are not type kinds. Add tests for enum, record and external-interface cases.

title: variable_declarator becomes its own SK_LOCAL_VAR, duplicating fields and locals and losing all but one field of `int a, b;`
evidence: A field_declaration yields one SK_FIELD, and each child variable_declarator yields an SK_LOCAL_VAR under it. `private int a, b;` gives a single SK_FIELD named "b" plus locals "a" and "b", so field a never exists. Every local yields two SK_LOCAL_VARs. Declarator symbols are never typed because the type node is a sibling, not a child. This is about symbol count and kind, not the naming problem in SYM-02.
impact: Fields from multi-declarator statements vanish from class diagrams, and SSA and points-to see doubled, untyped locals.
recommendation: Treat each variable_declarator as the declaration: emit one SK_FIELD or SK_LOCAL_VAR per declarator, taking kind and type from the enclosing declaration, and emit no symbol for the wrapper. Test that `int a, b;` produces two SK_FIELD symbols typed int.

title: The token sweep rewrites an existing AST symbol's kind to class, turning parameters into phantom classes
evidence: When a (file, name) pair is already registered, position() picks the first symbol in that file with that name, whatever its kind. Unless it is a method, line 392 overwrites its kind with SK_CLASS or SK_ENUM and makes it the current class. Fallback naming names parameters after their type, so `Outer(Entry e) {}` written before `static class Entry {}` turns the parameter into a class. Unlike SYM-04, this corrupts real symbols rather than inventing new ones.
impact: Diagrams show phantom duplicate classes and enums, and later swept members attach to the converted parameter.
