recommendation: Never let the sweep change AST-derived symbols. Match only class-like kinds, ideally the symbol whose name token is the lookahead token, and skip the sweep for files that have a real AST adapter. Test a nested type used as a parameter before it is declared.

title: Constructor bodies, switch blocks and annotation bodies are dropped before Phase 3, so declarations inside them never become symbols
evidence: The reducer's catch-all `_ => Drop` discards any unlisted node kind together with its subtree. tree-sitter-java 0.20.2 wraps constructor bodies in constructor_body, switch bodies in switch_block and annotation members in annotation_type_body, and none of these is mapped. Locals, lambdas and classes in constructors and switches never reach Pass 1, constructor token ranges stop at the parameter list, and has_new_expr_in_subtree can never find a `new`. SYM-12's list does not include these.
impact: Every constructor looks empty to Phase 3, and composition detection stays impossible even after SYM-08 is fixed.
recommendation: Map constructor_body to NN_BLOCK, and map switch_block, switch_rule and annotation_type_body to Eliminate or to kept nodes. Add a Phase 3 test asserting that a local declared in a constructor becomes an SK_LOCAL_VAR under that constructor.

title: sanitize_th_graph deletes legitimate edges that merely lead into a cycle
evidence: After Kahn's pass, the code deletes the first EXTENDS or IMPLEMENTS edge whose endpoints are both unvisited, but descendants of a cycle are also unvisited. Simulating edges [C→A, A→B, B→A] removes the legitimate C→A first, then A→B, leaving only B→A. Nothing is reported, and every round rebuilds the maps (O(k·E)). This is removal of the wrong edge, separate from SYM-16's tautology point.
impact: Any class that extends a member of a heuristic cycle silently loses its real superclass edge.
recommendation: Compute strongly connected components (Tarjan) and remove only edges inside an SCC, preferring token-heuristic edges over AST edges. Emit a diagnostic for each removed edge and do it in one O(V+E) pass. Add test_sanitize_keeps_descendant_edges.

title: Primitive-typed fields create TH_USES edges and Dependency associations to ids that are not symbols
evidence: For `int count;` the type id is 0xB000_0005. builder.symbol() returns None, and unwrap_or treats it as SK_EXTERNAL, so Pass 5 adds a TH_USES edge to 0xB0000005 and writes a Dependency association to a non-symbol. The owner is never checked to be class-like. has_type_hierarchy_edge counts any relation, so an int field makes a class look like it has a supertype. This differs from SYM-08's constant-folding.
impact: .sta gets bogus dependency edges and associations, and pattern queries misfire on ordinary classes.
recommendation: Skip primitive ids and void before classifying, and treat an unknown symbol as no association. Require the owner to be class-like, and keep dependency edges separate from inheritance edges. Test that a class with only int fields has no TH_USES edges.

title: Members found by the token sweep have no token range, so Pass 4's Kotlin type binding never runs
evidence: fun, val and var symbols are built from SymbolRecord::UNINIT without a first_token_id, so Pass 4 step 2 skips them at lines 67-72 and only ever sees AST symbols. Swept classes get a one-token extent (403-404). With no type_id, Pass 5 never emits TH_USES edges or associations for Kotlin fields. The 25-token window is also not bounded by last_token_id. This differs from SYM-04 and SYM-06.
impact: Kotlin properties and functions are never typed, so Kotlin classes get no associations, and traceability sees wrong extents.
recommendation: Record the first and last token (keyword through end of declaration) and the file for swept symbols, and bound scans by last_token_id. Longer term, parse Kotlin with tree-sitter-kotlin. Test that `class A { val b: B }` gives field b a type_id equal to B.

title: The sweep de-duplicates members per (file, name), dropping members of later classes and overloads
evidence: A fun, val or var symbol is created only if registered_name_ids.insert((file, name)) succeeds, and that set is shared by every class in the file and by class names. If two classes in one file both declare `val id`, only the first gets it. Of two overloads `fun f(a: Int)` and `fun f(a: String)`, one is kept. A factory `fun Foo()` next to `class Foo` is dropped.
impact: Kotlin classes silently lose members, so diagrams and metrics undercount.
recommendation: Identify members by (owner symbol, name, kind, token position), or stop de-duplicating members, and keep class de-duplication separate. Add test_sweep_member_dedup_per_class with two classes that share property names.

title: The sweep names members from the wrong token (type parameters, receiver types, soft keywords)
evidence: The first alphabetic, non-blocklisted token after fun, val or var becomes the name. `fun <T> map()` is named "T" and the extension `fun String.isEmail()` is named "String". `val data: List<X>` skips the blocklisted soft keyword `data` and is named "List"; properties named default, internal, open or by behave the same way. This differs from SYM-02 (AST names) and SYM-04 (fabrication).
impact: Kotlin functions and properties get type names instead of their own names.
recommendation: Skip type-parameter lists and receiver types (`Type.`), and take the identifier immediately before '(', ':' or '='. Do not blocklist soft keywords in name position. Add tests for generic, extension and `data` members.

title: Passes 4 and 5 bind types through a global simple-name map in which the last-created class wins
evidence: Both passes build a HashMap from simple name to symbol over all class-like symbols, overwriting in id order, so the highest id wins. Sweep-fabricated classes are created after all AST symbols and therefore shadow real classes with the same name. Two `Config` classes in different packages collapse into one. The same map is built twice.
impact: Token-level types and supertypes bind to the wrong class across packages, or to fabricated classes.
recommendation: Resolve through the scope graph, imports and package. If a map is kept, store a Vec of symbols per name and pick by the file's package and imports, prefer AST-derived symbols, and build it once in the builder.

title: Java `var` locals are typed as a fabricated external type named "var"
evidence: tree-sitter-java parses the `var` in `var x = new Foo();` as a type_identifier, so it becomes an NN_TYPE_REF. primitive_type_id has no case for it, and lexical, import and stub lookups all fail. Fallback 5 creates an SK_EXTERNAL named "var", and Pass 4 assigns it as the local's type_id.
impact: All inferred-type locals share one bogus type, so type-based analyses such as points-to allocation types are wrong for them.
recommendation: Treat `var` in local, for-loop and lambda-parameter type position as inferred: leave type_id unset or infer it from the initializer (a new expression or literal). Never create an external for it. Test `var x = new Foo();`.

title: Lambda parameters never become SK_PARAM symbols
evidence: Only formal_parameter and spread_parameter map to NN_PARAM_DECL. A lambda's single identifier parameter becomes NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR, and inferred_parameters (`(a, b) ->`) hits `_ => Drop`. So `x -> ...` and `(a, b) -> ...` create no SK_PARAM, count_params gives the lambda 0, and the lambda is named after its parameter. Lambda parameters are not in SYM-12's list.
impact: Most lambda parameters are invisible to scopes, SSA def-use and metrics.
recommendation: Emit NN_PARAM_DECL for a lambda's identifier parameter and for each identifier in inferred_parameters, set param_count, and give lambdas a synthetic name. Test both lambda forms.

title: Blocks do not open scopes, while every leaf declaration does
evidence: Scopes are created only for declaration nodes. Blocks, for, catch, try and switch open none, so `{int x;} {int x;}` and a for-loop variable share the method scope and stay visible after their block. Meanwhile every field, parameter, local and type-parameter list opens its own Block scope, each adding a record and four HashMap entries. This differs from SYM-03 (lookup rules) and SYM-09 (CPU cost).
impact: Once expression names are resolved, shadowing in sibling blocks will resolve wrongly, and memory grows with every declaration.
recommendation: Open scopes for blocks, for, catch, try-with-resources, switch and lambdas, and none for leaf declarations. Store per-scope data in Vecs indexed by scope id, and drop parent_edges, which duplicates ScopeRecord.parent_scope.

title: Project symbols never get fully qualified names
evidence: qual_name_id stays u32::MAX for every AST and swept symbol; only externals and stubs are interned, and package paths live separately in custom_package_names. No `com.example.Foo`, `Outer.Inner` or method signature exists anywhere in .sta, contrary to phase3.md:97. QualifiedNameTable stores each string twice and has no lookup that does not intern. SYM-14 covers positional ids; this is the missing FQN.
impact: There is no stable FQN identity for cross-file resolution, de-duplication, cross-run diffs or benchmark comparison.
recommendation: After package linking, compute FQNs (package + enclosing types + name, plus a parameter-type descriptor for methods) and intern them. Add lookup_id(&str) -> Option<u32> and store each string once. Test the FQN of a nested class.

title: Scope-graph serialization is lossy and its fields mislead consumers
evidence: Only ScopeRecords are written. Per-scope declaration lists, import edges and import mappings are not, import_table_off is always 0, and first_decl/decl_count imply a contiguous id range even though declarations are interleaved. ScopeKind has no Package kind, and at HEAD resolve_sym_package treats scope_kind 1 (Class) as a package scope. This differs from SYM-14, which covers the dropped type_ref_resolutions.
impact: Consumers cannot redo or audit resolution from .sta, and scope-based package lookup misreads the records.
recommendation: Serialize declaration lists in CSR form (offsets plus symbol ids) and import tables with real offsets. Redefine or remove first_decl. Add a Package scope kind or document that packages are not scopes. Add a round-trip test for scope membership.

title: Collection detection matches substrings of the qualified name
evidence: Besides the always-true contains_key("List") reported as SYM-08, the remaining test is qual_name.contains("List"/"Set"/"Map"/"Collection"). EventListener, UserSettings, ObjectMapper, Bitmap, Asset and Playlist therefore count as collections, while Queue, Deque, Iterable, Optional, Stream, arrays and Kotlin MutableList do not. is_collection_type is never consulted and the element type is never captured.
impact: Even after SYM-08 is fixed, non-collection fields will still get aggregation with multiplicity 0..*.
recommendation: Decide by subtyping of java.util.Collection or Map (or an exact FQN set via is_collection_type) plus an array flag, and record the generic element type as the association target.

title: The composition test ignores which field a constructor creates
evidence: is_instantiated_in_constructor ignores _field_sym_id and returns true if any constructor contains any `new`, including `throw new IllegalArgumentException()`, call arguments, and nested anonymous classes or lambdas. Field initializers like `final Engine e = new Engine();` are never examined, and every field re-walks all constructors. This differs from SYM-08, where composition is simply unreachable today.
impact: Once reachable, composition will be reported for every final field of any class whose constructor contains a `new`.
recommendation: Look for assignments whose target resolves to this field (`this.f = new T(...)` or `f = new T(...)`) in constructors and initializer blocks, and check the field's own initializer. Require the created type to be compatible with the field type, and memoize the result per class.

title: There is no Kotlin semantic adapter or Kotlin standard-library model
evidence: Phase3Stage::run always builds JavaSemanticAdapter, whatever each file's language. Kotlin files therefore get Java primitives (Int, Long, Unit and Any are not recognized), Java stubs only (no kotlin.collections List or MutableList), and Java default visibility, although Kotlin defaults to public. SymbolKind has no kinds for object, companion, typealias or property.
impact: Most Kotlin type references become SK_EXTERNAL, and Kotlin visibility and declaration kinds are wrong.
recommendation: Pick a SemanticAdapter per file from its LangId. Add a Kotlin adapter with Kotlin primitives, public by default, implicit kotlin.* imports and built-in type stubs, plus symbol kinds for object, companion and typealias.

title: The documented annotation table and UML metadata section do not exist, and annotations are never recorded
evidence: phase3.md lists a UML METADATA section and a per-symbol ANNOTATION TABLE in .sta, with uml_meta_offset pointing into it. The serializer writes neither, and uml_meta_offset is always 0. No pass records which annotations (@Override, @Entity, @Autowired, @Nonnull) a declaration carries, which is why Pass 1 relies on hardcoded annotation-name lists.
impact: Framework-aware analysis (Spring/JPA stereotypes, @Override checks, nullability for composition) has no data to work from.
recommendation: Resolve the NN_ANNOTATION_USE children of declarations in Pass 3 and store (symbol, annotation type, argument summary) records with an offset index. Serialize them, and either populate uml_meta_offset or remove it from the spec.

title: Phase 3 produces no resolution diagnostics
evidence: Unresolved names silently become SK_EXTERNAL, cycle edges are silently deleted, and sweep conflicts are silently skipped. .sta has no diagnostics section, even though phase3.md:675 says cycles are reported as diagnostics. The only trace is console logging.
impact: Users cannot see what failed to resolve, so resolution accuracy can be neither measured nor improved.
recommendation: Collect structured diagnostics in the builder (unresolved reference with its node, ambiguous name, removed hierarchy edge, duplicate FQN, sweep conflict), serialize them, and print summary counts.

title: No regression tests cover the defects in this list
evidence: No test covers: package `org.springframework.data.x`; sanitize_th_graph with a cycle plus a descendant; enum or record implements and `implements Runnable` in Pass5Hierarchy::run; `int a, b;`; two Kotlin classes sharing member names; a nested type used as a parameter before its declaration; primitive-field associations; deserialize with oversized counts. SYM-13 covers the missing oracle; these are concrete per-function gaps.
impact: Each of these defects can come back silently after it is fixed.
recommendation: Add test_pass1_package_with_data_segment, test_sanitize_keeps_descendant_edges, test_pass5_enum_implements_interface, test_pass5_external_interface_is_implements, test_multi_declarator_fields, test_sweep_member_dedup_per_class, test_param_not_promoted_to_class, test_primitive_field_no_uses_edge and test_sta_deserialize_rejects_huge_counts.

title: STA deserialization allocates memory from untrusted counts and lengths
evidence: Header counts go straight into Vec::with_capacity, and each string length goes into read_exact_bytes, which allocates vec![0; len] before reading. CRC-64 is not a MAC, so a 72-byte file with symbol_count 0xFFFFFFFF and a recomputed checksum requests about 256 GiB. The CLI artifact inspector reaches this code.
impact: A crafted or corrupt .sta aborts the process instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Before allocating, check that count × record size fits in the remaining bytes, cap string lengths by the remaining bytes, and use try_reserve. Fuzz SymbolTableArtifact::deserialize.

title: Deserialization does no semantic validation, and the From<u8> enum conversions silently coerce unknown values
evidence: format_version is read but never compared with STA_FORMAT_VERSION. symbol_id is not checked to equal its index, and parent, child, sibling, type and scope ids are not range-checked. THRelation::from maps any unknown byte to TH_EXTENDS; unknown kinds similarly become SK_EXTERNAL, visibilities Package and scope kinds File. The optional package sections swallow read errors, and trailing bytes are ignored.
impact: A version mismatch or corruption produces plausible but wrong hierarchies instead of a load error.
recommendation: Reject unknown format versions. Implement TryFrom<u8> for these enums and fail on unknown values. Validate id ranges and the exact payload length, and add negative tests.

title: verify_invariants skips range and link checks and the BPA/TCA hash link
evidence: Nothing checks that bpa.tca_hash equals the CRC-64 of tca_bytes, which phase3.md documents as Invariant 4. Invariant 5 checks only that first_token_id is below the token count; it does not check last_token_id, first ≤ last, decl_node, or link and type ids. Invariant 2 covers only methods and fields, and only that the parent is set, not that it is class-like as documented. This goes beyond SYM-16's repair-before-verify point.
impact: Mismatched inputs and dangling links pass verification and reach later phases.
recommendation: In Phase3Stage::run, compare bpa.tca_hash with the hash of tca_bytes. Extend Invariant 5 to full range and ordering checks, validate every link field and the parent kinds required by phase3.md:673, and collect all violations rather than stopping at the first.

title: Per-class diagnostic logging at INFO level on the hot path
evidence: Pass 1 logs every discovered class at INFO ("[DIAG-PASS1] Class Discovered") and the first 100 nodes at DEBUG. log_event writes and flushes both log files whatever the console level, and the format! call runs first regardless. A 10k-class project produces 10k console lines and 20k flushed file writes, and class names pile up in the persistent log.
impact: Large inputs pay for avoidable I/O, the console is noisy, and source identifiers are kept across runs.
recommendation: Remove the DIAG logs, or demote them to TRACE behind a level check (a macro that skips formatting when disabled), and log one summary line per pass.

title: Pass 2 has no handling for static imports or import aliases
evidence: The module doc and phase3.md promise a separate map for static imports. Instead, `import static a.B.c;` is treated as a type import with "static" left inside the qualified name, `import static a.B.*` becomes a wildcard package "static a . B", and Kotlin `import a.B as C` keeps "as C" in the simple name. This differs from SYM-01, which covers imports never reaching Pass 2 and the spacing bug.
impact: Once imports reach Pass 2, static members and Kotlin aliases will resolve to bogus type mappings.
recommendation: Parse imports structurally from tokens, not from a joined string: record a static flag, an on-demand flag and any alias in a per-file import table, with a separate map for static members.

title: Empty or mismatched inputs crash Pass 2 or silently skip discovery
evidence: extract_range_text computes `tca.token_records.len() as u32 - 1`. If the TCA is empty but a mismatched BPA still carries token ranges, this underflows: debug builds panic, and release builds wrap and then index out of bounds. Pass 1 returns before the token sweep when bpa.node_count is 0, so a corpus with an empty AST gets no symbols and no warning.
impact: Mismatched artifacts crash Phase 3, and AST failures silently produce an empty symbol table.
recommendation: Use checked_sub or an is_empty guard, validate the BPA/TCA link first, and run the sweep (or emit a warning) regardless of node_count.

title: ScopeRecord.import_count is a u16 incremented without overflow checks
evidence: add_import_edge and add_import_mapping increment import_count, a u16, with plain `+= 1`. Pass 2 registers every file's imports on the shared root scope, so a project with more than 65,535 import lines overflows: debug builds panic and release builds wrap. Duplicate mappings are counted twice. The bug stays dormant until SYM-01 lets imports reach Pass 2.
impact: Once imports flow, large monorepos can crash Phase 3 in debug builds or serialize wrong counts.
recommendation: Use u32 or saturating_add, count distinct entries only, and register imports on each file's own scope.

title: Passes disagree on which symbol kinds count as types
evidence: SK_ANNOTATION_TYPE is missing from registered_name_ids, from package linking and from both name maps, so annotation types stay under their module and never become package members. SK_ENUM is included in Pass 5's AST step but not its token step, so a swept Kotlin `enum class X : I` gets no supertype. Each pass hard-codes its own list.
impact: Annotation types are missing from packages, Kotlin enums lose their interfaces, and future kinds will drift between passes.
recommendation: Add one SymbolKind::is_type() helper and use it everywhere, and include annotation types in package linking.

title: Modules, lambdas, initializers and type-parameter lists are named after their first identifier
evidence: Modules, lambdas, static initializers and type-parameter lists fall through to the generic naming fallback. A module is named after its first package segment ("com"), a lambda after its parameter or first body token, and a static initializer "static" (missing from the exclusion list). `<K, V>` becomes a single symbol named K. These names are added to scope declarations. SYM-02 covers members, parameters and class headers; these are different declarations.
impact: .sta and diagrams carry misleading names, and lexical lookups see spurious entries.
recommendation: Use synthetic names (the file stem, `lambda$N`, `<clinit>`), keep them out of name lookup, and emit one SK_TYPE_PARAM per type parameter.

title: Instance initializer blocks are never recognized
evidence: The adapter handles NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT, but the Java reducer maps every block, including an initializer block in a class body, to NN_BLOCK. SK_INSTANCE_INIT is therefore never produced, and locals declared inside `{ ... }` initializers get the class as parent and live in the class scope.
impact: Initializer code is attributed to the class itself, and its locals look like class-scope declarations.
recommendation: Emit NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT when a block's parent is class_body, and give it a method-like scope.

title: Several SymbolRecord fields are never filled in
evidence: type_param_count, flags and uml_meta_offset are always 0. def_node always equals decl_node, even for abstract and interface methods that have no body. Records carry no file id, so consumers decode it from first_token_id, which swept, package and external symbols do not have. AssociationDetector reads bit 0x08 of flags as an array flag that nothing ever sets.
impact: Record bytes are wasted, and array fields, generic arity and a symbol's file are unavailable.
recommendation: Set type_param_count and array/varargs flags from the AST, set def_node only when a body exists, store a file_id in the _reserved field, and define named constants for the flag bits.

title: The modifier and visibility model cannot carry half of SymbolModifiers or Kotlin visibility
evidence: NodeAttr has room for only 8 modifier bits, so DEFAULT, STRICTFP, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, DEPRECATED, SYNTHETIC and RECORD_COMPONENT can never be set. There is no Kotlin internal visibility and no bits for open, override, data, suspend or lateinit. default_visibility(kind) is not told the enclosing kind, so interface members cannot default to public. This differs from SYM-15, where extraction never runs at all.
impact: Even once extraction is fixed, default methods, varargs, sealed hierarchies and Kotlin visibility are lost.
recommendation: Carry modifiers in a wider attribute or a side table, add an Internal visibility and Kotlin modifier bits, and pass the enclosing kind to default_visibility.

title: Layout comments misdescribe the records, the magic number and the hierarchy encoding
evidence: SymbolRecord is called "cache-aligned" but is plain repr(C) with 4-byte alignment. UMLAssociationRecord is called 28 bytes but is 32 in memory; only the serialized form is 28. The type hierarchy is described as CSR but is written as a flat 9-byte edge list. The STA_MAGIC comment says "STA\x00\x01", but little-endian write_u64 puts 00 00 00 01 00 41 54 53 on disk. The u16::MAX "many" multiplicity is undocumented.
impact: External readers of the .sta format and maintainers get wrong expectations.
recommendation: Add align(64) or drop the alignment claim, and add const size assertions. Fix the CSR comments or implement CSR. Write the magic as a byte string, and add a MULT_UNBOUNDED constant.

title: Dead or redundant code not covered by SYM-17
evidence: The fallback SK_MODULE can never be created, because any non-empty AST yields a module as symbol 0. `if lookahead > 0` is always true, and next_bytes is looked up twice. The SK_INTERFACE branch duplicates the else branch. crc64_checksum stays 0 after build() and serialize() never sets it. name_index costs 8 bytes per symbol, but nothing ever looks names up with it, despite phase3.md's O(log n) lookup claim.
impact: Noise, wasted bytes, and an artifact field that misleads readers.
recommendation: Delete the dead branches. Either set crc64_checksum or remove it. Add a binary-search lookup over name_index or stop writing it.

title: A second, unused PatternDetector shares the uma type's name and has wrong rules
evidence: symbol::uml_meta::PatternDetector is never called, yet `pub use uml_meta::*` re-exports it under the same name as uma::patterns::PatternDetector. Its is_singleton treats a class with no declared constructor, which has an implicit public one, as having no public constructor. Its is_factory flags any method returning an interface, including the List, Map and Set stubs. SYM-17 covers only is_observer's name lookup.
impact: The duplicate name makes the API confusing, and switching this detector on would mislabel most classes.
recommendation: Delete the module, since uma owns pattern detection, or rename it and fix the implicit-constructor and interface-return rules.

title: Building the artifact clones all builder data, and serialization trusts cached counts
evidence: build() clones every vector and map instead of moving them out of the builder. serialize() writes the cached count fields but iterates the public vectors, so editing a vector after build produces a header that does not match the payload, under a valid CRC. All builder fields are public, and append_child does not set the child's parent_sym.
impact: Peak memory roughly doubles at the end of Phase 3, and corrupt artifacts or inconsistent symbol trees are easy to produce.
recommendation: Make build() consume the builder, compute counts from vector lengths at write time, and make the fields private behind methods that keep parent and sibling links consistent.

title: Name extraction allocates a lowercase string per token and over-filters identifiers
evidence: For every token in each method, field and local window, extract_name_token allocates text.to_lowercase() just to compare it against keyword lists. Because the match ignores case, it also rejects real identifiers such as Default, Final or Native.
impact: Every declaration pays extra allocations, and capitalized identifiers occasionally get wrong names.
recommendation: Compare exact-case bytes, or reuse interned keyword ids as the sweep does.

title: The round-trip test compares only header fields
evidence: After deserialize, the test compares only the magic, counts and hashes. It never compares symbol records, scope records, hierarchy edges, associations, qualified names or the package maps, and never serializes twice to check that the bytes are identical.
impact: Serializer bugs such as wrong field order or a missing section would still pass.
recommendation: Derive PartialEq for SymbolTableArtifact and TypeHierarchyEdge and assert full equality after the round trip. Also assert that two serialize() calls give identical bytes.

title: The unit tests skip the code they are named after
evidence: test_pass5_hierarchy_acyclicity never calls Pass5Hierarchy::run or sanitize_th_graph; it only runs verify_invariants on hand-made edges. Both unit tests use an empty TokenCorpusArtifact, so name extraction, the sweep, package parsing and the Pass 4/5 token scans never execute. The integration test asserts no names, types or hierarchy edges.
impact: Most of the logic in Passes 1, 4 and 5 has no test coverage.
recommendation: Build fixtures from real source through Phases 1 and 2, and assert concrete names, kinds, parents, type ids and edges. Add a direct test of sanitize_th_graph.

title: Dependency edges come only from field types, and TH_CREATES is never emitted
evidence: THRelation::TH_CREATES is defined, but no pass produces it, and TH_USES edges come only from field types. Parameter types, return types, local and thrown-exception types, and `new T()` expressions produce no dependency edges.
impact: UML dependency arrows and coupling metrics miss most dependencies between classes.
recommendation: Emit TH_USES from method signatures and locals and TH_CREATES from NN_NEW_EXPR targets. De-duplicate per (from, to, relation) and keep these edges separate from inheritance edges.

title: Phase 3 runs single-threaded and re-hashes inputs that Phase 2 already hashed
evidence: All passes run sequentially, and Pass 1 makes one pass over the nodes plus two full token sweeps, although discovery, package parsing and name extraction are independent per file. build() recomputes CRC-64 over the whole TCA and BPA, even though Phase 2 already stored the TCA hash in bpa.tca_hash.
impact: Phase 3 time grows linearly with corpus size, with no parallel speed-up on large projects.
recommendation: Split per-file work across threads (rayon) and merge ids deterministically. Reuse bpa.tca_hash and compare it (see SYM2-26). Fold the package scan into the primary walk.

title: LabelExtractor slices UTF-8 labels by byte and panics on non-ASCII tokens, aborting Phase 9
evidence: `&label_text[..max_chars.saturating_sub(3)]` slices by byte length. It runs for every non-entry/exit block (max 30). node_attr is misused as a token index, so it reads token 0 or op<<12 (e.g. token #86016 for `==` conditions). A token such as 'Bitte geben Sie Ihr Passwört ein', or CJK text, puts byte 27 in the middle of a character (checked in Python), so the slice panics.
impact: Phase 9 crashes on such input. The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind, so a crafted repo sent to /api/analyze is a remote DoS.
recommendation: Truncate on char boundaries (char_indices().nth(n)) and never byte-slice a String. Add test_extract_label_multibyte_truncation with umlaut and CJK tokens. This differs from UML-12, which is about reading the wrong token.

title: Sequence records mix interner name ids and symbol ids, so scenario names resolve to unrelated symbols
evidence: scenario_name is set to entry_sym_rec.name_id, an interner id, yet both exporters call resolve_name(sta, tca, seq.scenario_name), which looks it up as a symbol. Lifeline name_id falls back to a symbol id via unwrap_or(entry_class) and unwrap_or(callee_class), and the actor name_id is a literal 0, which is an arbitrary interned string.
impact: Interaction-overview partitions carry another symbol's name or 'Unknown'. Consumers of .uma cannot interpret the name fields.
recommendation: Store the entry method's sym id, keep name fields strictly interner ids (u32::MAX when unknown), and document each field's id space. Disambiguate overloads. Add test_sequence_scenario_name_is_entry_method.

title: extends_sym keeps only the last TH_EXTENDS edge, so extra super-interfaces and enum/record realizations are lost
evidence: `extends_sym = edge.to_sym` is assigned for every TH_EXTENDS edge, so `interface C extends A, B` keeps only B. Pass 5 emits TH_EXTENDS, not TH_IMPLEMENTS, for enums and records that implement interfaces. So `enum E implements X, Y` gets one generalization and no realization, and which one survives depends on edge order. This differs from UML-08 (multiplicity and association kinds).
impact: Interfaces, enums and records get wrong or missing inheritance arrows, and the result depends on edge order.
recommendation: Keep every generalization in a Vec. Map an edge to a realization when the target is an interface and the source is not, and deduplicate. Add test_interface_multiple_extends_all_kept and test_enum_implements_two_interfaces.

title: Associations skip record-typed targets and all self-references
evidence: The field and return-type association checks match only SK_CLASS, SK_INTERFACE and SK_ENUM (lines 257-260 and 271-274), so SK_RECORD is left out even though records are extracted as classes. Both checks also require type_sym_id != sym_id, so `Node next` or `Employee manager` produce no reflexive association.
impact: Records look disconnected, and linked lists, trees and self-referencing Composites lose their self-links.
recommendation: Use one is_classifier() helper that includes SK_RECORD, and allow reflexive associations. Add test_record_field_association and test_self_association_kept. This differs from UML-08's multiplicity and kind issues.

title: The test-source filter only matches absolute forward-slash paths, so Windows and relative runs include test classes
evidence: Paths are interned with to_string_lossy(), which keeps native separators. The filter only checks contains('/src/test/'), '/src/tests/' and '/__tests__/'. So D:\proj\src\test\FooTest.java on Windows and relative 'src/test/...' paths never match. This differs from UML-05, which is about filters dropping real user types.
impact: The same sources give different class diagrams on Windows and Linux, and for relative and absolute inputs.
recommendation: Normalize separators, match path components (test, tests, androidTest, __tests__), and make the rule configurable. Add test_windows_and_relative_test_paths_filtered.

title: Activity nodes misclassify switch dispatch and exception successors
evidence: A block is a DECISION only when succs_len == 2. A switch selector gets one Switch edge per case group, plus exit, so every switch dispatch becomes an ACTION with three or more outgoing flows. succs_len also counts Except edges, so a try block with one normal and one handler successor becomes a DECISION. swimlane_count is always 1. This differs from UML-12, where guards, loops and labels are not emitted.
impact: Switch-heavy code renders as plain fan-out actions, and try blocks look like conditionals.
recommendation: Classify from edge types: True, False or Switch edges mean DECISION. Handle Except edges separately as exception handlers, and derive swimlanes from the owning class. Add test_switch_block_is_decision and test_try_block_not_decision.

title: Sequence extraction has no size bound, and its u16 ordinals wrap
evidence: For each entry point, a DFS over the entire reachable call graph emits one message per (site, target) pair, with no cap on depth, messages or lifelines. A polymorphic CHA site emits one message per target. ordinal is a u16 incremented with `+= 1`, and the HEAD dev profile sets overflow-checks=false, so after 65,535 messages ordinals wrap silently. This differs from UML-09 (scan cost) and UML-07 (ordering).
impact: Large apps produce scenarios with huge message lists and duplicate ordinals, and memory grows as entry points times call edges.
recommendation: Add configurable per-scenario depth and message caps, collapse polymorphic targets into one message to the declared type, and use u32 ordinals. Add test_sequence_message_cap_respected.

ENG.note: The Cargo.toml part is in place: the dev profile no longer turns overflow checks off, and test pins them on, so u16 ordinal overflow traps. The caps and u32 ordinals in sequence_diagram.rs are in handoffs.

title: Entry-point detection drops protected framework callbacks and promotes bodyless and dead methods
evidence: An entry point is a Public or Package method with no distinct callers. That excludes protected callbacks such as Android onCreate and onResume and Servlet doGet and doPost. It includes package-private methods and every unused getter. CHA skips abstract targets, so abstract and interface methods have no callers and become one-message scenarios. A self-recursive method is never an entry point. There is no handling for main or annotations.
impact: The main framework flows are missing while thousands of trivial scenarios are produced. This differs from UML-07.
recommendation: Rank entry points in this order: main, annotated handlers, overridden framework callbacks of any visibility, then public API with no external callers, ignoring self-loops. Skip bodyless methods. Add test_protected_on_create_is_entry.

title: Call sites with no in-project target are left out of sequence diagrams
evidence: Messages come only from site_to_edge_map entries. Calls into libraries, the JDK or frameworks (JDBC, HTTP, Android) resolve to no symbol, so site_edges.get(..) returns None and nothing is emitted. The only lifeline outside the project is the single caller actor.
impact: Interactions with databases, networks and frameworks, often the point of a sequence diagram, never appear.
recommendation: Emit unresolved sites as messages to an external lifeline per receiver type or package (from call_token or the receiver's SSA type). Add test_library_call_creates_external_lifeline.

title: Composite detection copies the Decorator predicate and never checks for a collection
evidence: Both detectors build parent_types from th_edges and test whether any field's type_id is in it. So any class with a supertype-typed field is reported as both Decorator (85) and Composite (75). has_collection_field_of is never called, and its own test matches any field name ending in 's' or any type name containing 'Set' (Settings, Offset, Asset). This differs from UML-02, which concerns TH_USES edges.
impact: Even after UML-02 is fixed, Decorator and Composite cannot be told apart.
recommendation: Composite: require a collection or array field whose element type is a supertype, plus add/remove/iterate-children methods. Decorator: require a single wrapped field plus delegating overrides. Add tests that tell the two apart.

title: Phase9Stage::run panics when the .uma write fails and cannot return an error
evidence: run() returns a bare UMLMetadataArtifact and calls panic! when UMASerializer::write fails (disk full, permissions, missing directory). SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute returns a Result but cannot pass this error on, and the server process dies. Phases 3 to 6 return Result.
impact: An ordinary I/O error crashes the CLI or server instead of being reported.
recommendation: Return Result<UMLMetadataArtifact, io::Error> and map the error at each call site. Add a test that writes to an unwritable path and expects Err.

title: UMASerializer::read trusts every count and offset, so malformed files panic or abort
evidence: After the CRC check, every read is an unchecked slice (bytes[offset..offset+4]). Vec::with_capacity takes the u32 header counts as-is, so a count of 0xFFFFFFFF overflows capacity or aborts on OOM. format_version is read but never validated, offset is never compared with data_end (which is why UML-10's misparse goes unnoticed), and tra_hash is never checked.
impact: `openheart inspect` crashes on an old-version, truncated or crafted .uma with a recomputed CRC, instead of returning an error. This differs from UML-10's layout bugs.
recommendation: Read through a bounds-checked cursor that returns io::Error, reject unknown versions, cap capacities by the remaining bytes, and require offset == data_end. Add a fuzz test fuzz_uma_read.

title: Much of the .uma schema is write-only: source links, confidence, counts and fragments are never read
evidence: Grepping src/scpg, src/adapters, src/core and main.rs finds no reads of ClassRecord.uml_link, uml_link_node, type_param_count, loop_depth, guard_text_id, is_back_edge, start_node, end_node_count, swimlane_count, combined_fragments, ordinal, uml_link_token, objects, label_texts, the package and component counts and parents, or DesignPatternRecord.confidence. The JSON exporter writes file '<Name>.java' and lines [1] instead of the real uml_link.
impact: Traceability and confidence data never reach users, and the effort spent computing them is wasted and untested.
recommendation: Wire these fields into the exporters and query API (source links, confidence badges, back-edge styling), or remove them from the schema. Add an exporter test asserting that file and line come from uml_link.

title: src/uma has no unit tests
evidence: No #[cfg(test)] or #[test] exists anywhere under src/uma. Phase 9 is exercised only by five end-to-end tests with loose assertions, and none of them would catch the label panic, the extends overwrite, the switch misclassification, the scenario-name confusion or the reader bounds bugs.
impact: Regressions in more than 30 extractor and detector functions go unnoticed.
recommendation: Add unit tests built on small synthetic STA/CFG/CGA fixtures, for example: test_extract_label_multibyte, test_switch_is_decision, test_interface_multi_extends, test_record_association, test_entry_points_protected, test_sequence_message_cap, test_uma_roundtrip_all_sections and fuzz_uma_read.

title: pipeline_accuracy_tests never reaches Phase 9 and locks in the missing constructor CFG
evidence: The 'ruthless line_by_line' test stops at Phase 6 and checks no line numbers. It asserts function_count == 2 although the sources contain three bodies. The Java adapter maps constructor_body through `_ => Drop`, which drops the whole subtree, so constructors get no CFG, no call sites and no activity. The assertion sccs.len() == symbol_count fixes the assumption that every symbol is a call-graph node.
impact: UML output is never checked, and the lost constructor bodies look intended. Constructors get no activity diagrams and their calls never appear in sequence diagrams.
recommendation: Run the test through Phase 9 and assert the OrderService to PaymentProcessor association, the decision and loop nodes in processOrder, and a constructor activity. Expect 3 functions once constructor_body maps to NN_BLOCK.

title: UMA has no use-case, actor or profile records
evidence: The artifact holds classes, objects, activities, state machines, sequences, packages, components and patterns only. Actors are a single EXTERNAL_ACTOR_ID constant, and there is no record for use cases, actor-to-use-case links or profiles, although mod.rs claims to drive all 14 UML diagrams. This differs from UML-03 (stub extractors) and UML-01 (templated exporters).
impact: Use-case and profile diagrams can only be made up downstream.
recommendation: Add a UseCaseRecord derived from ranked entry points and annotations, an ActorRecord for roles and external systems, and a ProfileRecord built from annotation types and stereotypes.

title: Annotation types never reach the class diagram, and the STEREOTYPE_ANNOTATION and SK_LAMBDA arms are unreachable
evidence: The kind filter admits only CLASS, INTERFACE, ENUM and RECORD and skips everything else. The stereotype match below it still handles SK_ANNOTATION_TYPE as STEREOTYPE_ANNOTATION and SK_LAMBDA, so those arms and `_ => continue` can never run. User-declared @interface types are always missing.
impact: Custom annotations, common in Spring and Jakarta code, are absent, and the dead branches mislead maintainers.
recommendation: Let SK_ANNOTATION_TYPE through the filter, drop the SK_LAMBDA arm, and add test_annotation_type_has_annotation_stereotype.

title: The local-type filter is inconsistent: local classes are kept but local records, enums and interfaces are dropped
evidence: A type is skipped when its parent is a METHOD, FIELD, PARAM or LOCAL_VAR unless it is SK_CLASS or SK_LAMBDA. Method-local classes therefore become ClassRecords that no inner_classes list references, while Java 16 local records, enums and interfaces are dropped. Types declared inside lambdas or initializers skip the check entirely.
impact: Class diagrams show stray method-local helper classes and omit equivalent local records.
recommendation: Pick one policy (exclude all local types, or include them flagged as local) and implement it with one is_local_scope check that also covers lambda and initializer parents. Add tests for each local kind.

title: A missing UML link is replaced with a made-up file 0, line 1 location that the tests cannot detect
evidence: When no TRA link exists, the extractor emits file_id 0, lines 1..1 and columns 1..1 with the real scpg_hash. TRA marks an unknown span with (0,0,0,0,0) instead. Invariant 3 in uma_tests only compares scpg_hash, which the fallback copies, so the test passes even when every link is made up.
impact: Traceability points at the first line of the first file instead of saying 'unknown', and the invariant can never fail.
recommendation: Share an explicit sentinel with TRA (file_id u16::MAX, line 0), count fallbacks, and assert in tests that file and line match the class declaration.

title: Methods without a PSA summary get an invented cyclomatic=1 and sat_count=1
evidence: When psa.function_header returns None, the extractor falls back to (1, 1). That happens for abstract and interface methods and for constructors, which have no CFG. The defaults look like real values and flow into the ArchitecturalMetricsVisitor totals and mean_cyclomatic_complexity.
impact: Complexity metrics come out too low, and bodyless methods look like trivial real methods.
recommendation: Mark the value as unknown (a sentinel, or 0 plus a has_body flag) and leave such methods out of averages. Add test_abstract_method_has_no_metrics.

title: Field and method modifiers are truncated from u16 to u8
evidence: `modifiers: child.modifiers as u8` drops bits 8 to 15: DEFAULT, SEALED, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, BRIDGE, SYNTHETIC, DEPRECATED and RECORD_COMPONENT. Today only SEALED is ever set (pass1_discovery.rs:940), so nothing is lost yet, but ClassRecord keeps the full u16 while member records cannot.
impact: Default methods, varargs and deprecation can never be shown once Phase 3 starts setting them, and the loss is silent.
recommendation: Widen FieldRecord and MethodRecord modifiers to u16 and bump the format version, or debug_assert that the high byte is zero.

title: ClassRecord.type_param_count is always 0, and type parameters are never captured
evidence: The extractor copies sym.type_param_count, but every place that creates a SymbolRecord sets it to 0 and nothing updates it. UMA has no field for parameter names or bounds, and no consumer reads type_param_count.
impact: Generic types such as Repository<T> render as plain classes, so UML template parameters are impossible.
recommendation: Count the SK_TYPE_PARAM children in Phase 3, store their sym ids in ClassRecord, and render them as UML template parameters. Add test_generic_class_type_params.

title: Debug diagnostics are logged at INFO, and the kind check is written three times
evidence: '[DIAG-CD]' lines for symbol_count and for every class-like symbol, before any filtering, go through log_info. That is the default console level, and the persistent log is append-only. The same CLASS/INTERFACE/ENUM/RECORD matches! appears at lines 44, 79 and 167, and the third is always true. This differs from UML-09, which is about speed.
impact: Every run floods the console and the persistent log with one line per class, and the redundant code hides the real filter.
recommendation: Demote these lines to trace level or remove them. Compute is_classifier once and delete the redundant block.

title: Activity node indices and counts are truncated to u16
evidence: start_node, from_node and to_node are u32 block ids cast with `as u16`, and node_count and edge_count are `len() as u16`. Past 65,535 blocks, edges wrap silently to the wrong nodes. JVM method-size limits make this rare, but generated or non-JVM code can exceed it. This differs from UML-10, which covers serializer lengths.
impact: Giant functions get corrupt activity graphs instead of an error.
recommendation: Use u32 indices in ActivityEdge and ActivityRecord, or u16::try_from with a logged skip.

title: Activity labels come from a block's first statement, not the branch condition, and always end in '()'
evidence: stmt_node is taken from blk.stmts.first(). For an if, the CFG appends cond_node after the statements before it, so the condition is the last statement of the decision block. LabelExtractor also appends '()' to every label, so assignments and returns would read like calls. The computed label is then thrown away, which wastes one extraction per block.
impact: Once labels are wired up, decision nodes will show unrelated text, formatted as a call.
recommendation: Label DECISION nodes from the last statement (the condition) and actions from their statement kinds. Add '()' only for call nodes, and store the result in label_texts.

title: message_kind stores raw call-graph edge codes, and the entry message reuses call_site_id 0
evidence: message_kind = site.call_type, which holds DIRECT 0, VIRTUAL 2, CONSTRUCTOR 4 and so on, not UML message sorts. The actor message hard-codes kind 0 and call_site_id 0, and 0 is also the first real call site's id. There are no MESSAGE_KIND_* or fragment-kind constants, and no exporter reads message_kind.
impact: Create and async messages cannot be told apart, and call_site_id 0 is ambiguous.
recommendation: Define MESSAGE_KIND sync/async/create/reply and FRAGMENT_KIND constants, map CG_EDGE_CONSTRUCTOR to create, and use u32::MAX for the synthetic entry call site.

title: Behavioral views ignore the class-diagram filters and cover test and excluded classes
evidence: Activities are built for every CFG function, including lambdas and static initializers that have no owning class record. Entry points and state machines are built for every symbol. None of them applies the test-path, blacklist or keyword filters used for ClassRecords.
impact: Lifelines and activities refer to classes the class diagram does not show, and test methods appear as scenarios.
recommendation: Compute the included-class set once in Phase 9, filter every extractor by owning class, and attach the owner sym id to lambda and initializer activities.

title: ClassRecords refer to sym ids that have no ClassRecord of their own
evidence: inner_classes, association_syms, extends_sym and implements_syms keep any child or target of class kind, even when the blacklist, keyword, Binding or test filters dropped that type.
impact: Consumers meet dangling references, so diagrams either draw edges to undefined nodes or silently drop them.
recommendation: After extraction, prune or flag references to types outside the class set, or emit stub records marked external, and check this in finalize().

title: The Builder heuristic counts static self-returning methods, so Singletons and static factories become Builders
evidence: self_returning counts every SK_METHOD whose type_id is the class, with no STATIC check. In uma_tests, UmlMetadataTest has getInstance() (static, returns its own type) and processData(), which gives a ratio of 0.5 > 0.4. It should therefore also be reported as a Builder at confidence 75, next to Singleton.
impact: Classic Singletons and value classes with static of() or valueOf() factories are reported as Builders.
recommendation: Leave static methods out of the fluent ratio, and require two or more instance setters returning this plus a build() method. Assert in uma_tests that UmlMetadataTest is not a Builder.

title: Facade and Adapter count primitive-typed and stub-typed fields as subsystems or adaptees
evidence: The check is `type_id != u32::MAX && type_id != sym_id`. Primitive fields resolve to sentinel ids 0xB000_0000 to 0xB000_0008 and JDK types to stub ids at 0xC000_0000 and above, so they pass. Three separately declared int fields therefore give a Facade at confidence 70. This differs from UML-02, which is about TH_USES edges.
impact: Plain data classes are reported as Facades.
recommendation: Count only fields whose type is an in-project classifier (sta.symbol(type_id) returns a class or interface), ideally one in another package. Add test_primitive_fields_not_facade.

title: Four PatternInspector helpers are never called, and their doc comments do not match the code
evidence: has_private_constructor, has_static_self_reference, has_collection_field_of and has_interprocedural_delegation have no callers anywhere in src or tests. name_matches is documented as 'contains or ends with' but only checks contains. has_collection_field_of promises 'of a given component type' but takes no type. has_interprocedural_delegation is O(E×M) because it uses Vec::contains.
impact: Readers assume structural checks run that never do, and wiring them in later would bring their bugs along.
recommendation: Fix the helpers and wire them into the detectors, or delete them. Correct the doc comments, and use a HashSet for the caller set.

title: Three separate pattern-detection paths, and the pattern-name tables are duplicated
evidence: detect_all hard-codes 11 detector calls. PatternDetectionChain registers the same 11 rules but only a test uses it, so add_rule has no effect on the pipeline. It is named a Chain of Responsibility but runs every rule. Phase 3 has its own, stricter PatternDetector that Phase 9 ignores. Each exporter keeps its own copy of the kind-to-name table.
impact: Results depend on which path is used, the extension point does nothing, and pattern names can drift apart.
recommendation: Make detect_all iterate a PatternDetectionChain, merge or delete the Phase 3 detector, and give all exporters one pattern_name(kind) function in uma::types.

title: .uma writes are not atomic
evidence: The whole file is built in a Vec with no capacity reserved and then written with fs::write straight to the final path. A crash or a full disk mid-write truncates the previous good artifact, and the reader then fails the CRC.
impact: An interrupted run destroys the last valid .uma.
recommendation: Write to a temporary file, fsync, then rename it over the target, and reserve the exact capacity up front.

title: Record size comments disagree with the serialized layout, and the layout is unaligned
evidence: The comments give FieldRecord as 16 bytes but it is serialized as 20. MethodRecord is 20 vs 22, MessageRecord 24 vs 25 and CombinedFragment 12 vs 11. Class headers take 26 bytes, so every later record is misaligned for memory-mapping, and UMLLink line numbers are cut to 24 bits.
impact: A reader written from the comments misparses the file, and zero-copy memory-mapping is impossible.
recommendation: Drive sizes from one layout table (a SIZE constant per record plus static assertions), pad records to 4- or 8-byte alignment, and keep full u32 line numbers. Bump the format version.

title: UMA records use inconsistent id widths, carry redundant fields and lack equality derives
evidence: ActivityNode.guard_text_id is a u16 while every other text id is a u32. Pattern kind is a u8 on ClassRecord and on rules but a u16 in DesignPatternRecord, and evaluate() returns the kind again. ClassRecord has field, method and inner counts that the writer ignores. LifelineRecord.type_sym_id always equals sym_id. Records lack PartialEq, and the artifact lacks Debug and Clone.
impact: Values can disagree or overflow silently, and tests cannot assert_eq records.
recommendation: Use u32 for all ids, derive counts from Vec lengths, derive Debug, Clone and PartialEq, and add a full round-trip equality test.

title: Package records inherit a wrong parent and corrupted sibling chains from Phase 3
evidence: Root packages start with parent u32::MAX, and Pass 1's final sweep reparents them to symbol 0, which is file 0's module. So parent_package_sym of 'com' points at a module. The same sweep appends to symbol 0's chain, whose last child, file 0's last class, is already linked into its package. That package's sibling walk then continues into the root packages and can lose later classes. Phase 9 copies both without checking.
impact: Package hierarchy roots are wrong, and class and subpackage counts are off.
recommendation: Set parent_package_sym to u32::MAX unless the parent is SK_PACKAGE, and count children through parent_sym, as class_diagram does, instead of sibling chains. Add a multi-file package test.

title: Package and component counts disagree with the class diagram and miscount interfaces
evidence: class_count includes types the class diagram filtered out. The skip test at lines 19-24 can never fire, because every package has a custom name, and name_id holds only the last name segment. required_interface_count counts raw TH edges of every relation, not distinct interfaces (despite the TH_USES comment), and only for direct children. provided counts every interface, public or not. The counters are u16, and packages are extracted twice. This differs from UML-14.
impact: The counts are unreliable even as plain containment metrics.
recommendation: Count distinct interface sym ids, treat only public ones as provided, reuse the packages and the filtered class set already extracted, and use u32 counters.

title: The metrics visitor reports an inheritance depth it never computes, and its path-count sum wraps
evidence: inheritance_depth_max is declared and never assigned, so it is always 0. total_sat_path_count adds method.sat_count with +=, while PSA saturates each function's count at u64::MAX, so two saturated methods wrap the total. There are no DIT, NOC, CBO, RFC, LCOM or WMC metrics, despite the 'formal architectural metrics' description.
impact: Metrics offered for research use are wrong or missing.
recommendation: Compute DIT from the extends chains, use saturating_add or u128 for the sum, and add the standard CK metrics, each with a unit test.

title: The attack-surface visitor only matches name suffixes, and neither visitor is wired into the product
evidence: A class counts as a controller only if its name ends in Controller, Endpoint or Resource; @RestController, @Path and @WebServlet are ignored. Protected members are excluded, while members of private nested classes are counted. There is no visit_object, so objects are never visited. Both visitors are used only in design_pattern_architecture_tests.
impact: The attack-surface output is unreliable, and users cannot reach it from the CLI or the server.
recommendation: Use annotation symbols and effective visibility (class and member together), add visit_object, and expose the metrics through the CLI or the query API.

title: Doc comments in Phase 9 promise behavior that does not exist
evidence: The actor module claims to identify 'external actors', but only a constant exists, and it says 'public methods' while also including package-private ones. extract_label says it interns the label but just returns a String. finalize claims every ClassRecord is valid but only checks sym_id in debug builds. chain.rs calls an evaluate-every-rule loop a Chain of Responsibility. The component comment names TH_USES but the code counts every relation.
impact: Maintainers rely on guarantees the code does not give.
recommendation: Correct each comment, or implement the behavior it describes.

title: UMABuilder::finalize checks no invariants in release builds
evidence: The only check is assert!(sym_id != u32::MAX), and it runs only under cfg(debug_assertions). Nothing checks for unique class ids, references to existing records, activity edge endpoints below node_count, increasing message ordinals, or that a pattern's class_sym exists.
impact: Corrupt records like those in UML2-07, UML2-24 and UML2-28 reach disk and the exporters unnoticed.
recommendation: Add an always-on validate() that returns errors and mirrors the §9.7 invariants, and call it from finalize().

title: EXTERNAL_ACTOR_ID is redefined as a literal in the exporters
evidence: Phase 9 defines EXTERNAL_ACTOR_ID = 0xFFFF_FFFE. The exporters redefine it as u32::MAX - 1 and also hard-code `u32::MAX - 1 || u32::MAX` checks in message rendering.
impact: Changing the sentinel in one place silently breaks actor rendering in the others.
recommendation: Export the constant once from uma::types and use it everywhere.

title: Pattern test inputs are not valid Java, and the file headers claim coverage that is not there
evidence: PatternSubject.java, Core.java, Patterns.java and Subsystem.java each declare several public top-level types, which javac rejects. adversarial_trick_tests advertises identical class names across packages, guarded state machines, sequence fragments and adapter delegation, but its inputs contain none of them and nothing asserts them. The other file calls itself a 'Formal Verification Suite'.
impact: The tests exercise code shapes real projects never have, and they overstate coverage.
recommendation: Split the inputs into one public type per file, and either add the advertised cases with exact expected records or correct the headers.

title: uma_tests depends on symbol id 1 and has invariants that cannot fail
evidence: The class under test is fetched with sta.symbol(1), which assumes a fixed symbol numbering. Invariant 2 can never fail, because the extractor only skips CFGs with zero blocks. Invariant 4 (confidence ≤ 100) can never fail either, because every confidence is a literal below 100. This differs from UML-06, which is about the missing ground truth.
impact: The test breaks on harmless renumbering but passes through real regressions.
recommendation: Look the class up by name, assert the exact activity node kinds for processData, and replace the tautological invariants with exact expectations.

title: The 40-line pipeline setup is copied across the test files
evidence: Each test re-implements the Phase 1 to Phase 9 calls with its own temp paths, although SCPGPipelineBuilder, already used in design_pattern_architecture_tests, does the same job. The strategy tests then only check strategy counts and that a class name appears in the output.
impact: A change to any phase signature needs edits in five places, and the weak checks add little UML coverage.
recommendation: Add tests/common/mod.rs with a run_pipeline(files) -> PipelineArtifacts helper and reuse it in every test file.

title: UMA records have no identity that stays stable across runs
evidence: Every record is keyed by dense Phase 3 symbol ids, which shift whenever files are added or reordered. No qualified-name id or content hash is stored. This differs from UML-08, which is about simple-name collisions within a single run.
impact: Diagrams and pattern results cannot be compared across commits or linked from external tools.
recommendation: Store qual_name_id, or a stable hash of the qualified name plus signature, in class, method and pattern records.

title: Phase 9 runs on one thread although the per-class and per-function work is independent
evidence: Classes, activities, sequences and patterns are each extracted in a sequential loop, and the only shared mutation is the final design_pattern assignment. Nothing parallel is used, and there is no rayon dependency.
impact: On large codebases Phase 9 runs on a single core.
recommendation: Parallelize extraction per class, per function and per entry point with rayon's par_iter, then sort the results to keep the output deterministic.

title: The stereotype field cannot express sealed, data, object, companion or value types
evidence: stereotype is a single exclusive u8 with the values NONE, ABSTRACT, INTERFACE, ENUM, RECORD and ANNOTATION. SEALED exists in modifiers but is never mapped, and Kotlin data, object, companion and value classes have no representation.
impact: Kotlin designs render as plain classes, and combinations such as abstract plus sealed are lost.
recommendation: Use a stereotype bitset or list, and map sealed, data, object, companion and value from the modifiers and declaration keywords.

title: The class extractor treats path_str_offset as an interner id, which a disk-loaded TCA does not hold
evidence: The test-file and filename-stem checks look up tca.interner.lookup_text(file_records[fid].path_str_offset). The TCA writer replaces that field with a byte offset into the path section, and the reader skips the path bytes without interning them. Phase 9 currently always receives the in-memory TCA, so the problem is latent.
impact: Running Phase 9 on a reloaded .tca would apply the test and stem filters to unrelated strings.
recommendation: Give TokenCorpusArtifact a file_path(fid) accessor that works in both modes, and use it in class_diagram. Add a test that runs Phase 9 on a reloaded .tca.

title: PNG export always throws ReferenceError (isDarkMode not imported)
evidence: exportPng calls isDarkMode() at graph-canvas.js:1416, but line 16 imports only getTheme, onThemeChange and buildCytoscapeStylesheet. ES modules are strict and isDarkMode is only exported from theme-manager.js:166, so every PNG export click, and the PNG fallback in the SVG export handler, throws.
impact: PNG export never works. The SVG fallback path fails silently with only a console error.
recommendation: Import isDarkMode. Wrap export handlers in try/catch and report failures in the HUD. Use cy.png({output:'blob'}) with downloadBlob instead of data URIs. Add an exportPng smoke test on a tiny graph.

title: Java extends/implements parsing loses or misclassifies inheritance edges
evidence: Regex group 3 starts after the first keyword, so extMatch is always null. Tested in Node: 'class A extends B implements C, D' gives parts ['B  C','D'], so B and C are dropped and D becomes generalization. 'implements Runnable' becomes generalization; 'interface X extends Y' becomes realization.
impact: Imported Java class diagrams show wrong or missing inheritance and realization. The extends/implements fields in the AI export are empty.
recommendation: Capture the extends and implements clauses separately and classify by keyword, not by an I-prefix heuristic. Interface-extends-interface is generalization. Add tests parseSourceFile_extendsAndImplements, _implementsOnly and _interfaceExtends.

title: Kotlin classes, Java records and nested generics are not detected; Kotlin packages not extracted
evidence: Tested misses: 'data class User(val id: Int) : Base() {', 'class Repo(val db: Db) {', 'object S {', 'record Point(int x,int y) {', 'class Foo<T extends Comparable<T>> {'. The package regex needs ';' or '{', so a Kotlin 'package com.x' returns null and the directory path is used. 'class Q {' inside a string literal is matched. record is mapped to interface.
impact: For Kotlin, a target language, and modern Java, classes are missing, package names are wrong and heritage is lost.
recommendation: Strip comments and strings before matching. Allow constructor parentheses, object, data class and ':' supertypes, balance generics, make ';' optional, and map record to class. Better: use tree-sitter WASM or the Rust parser. Add tests for each case.

title: ROBDD terminals both render as FALSE for engine-produced IR
evidence: The loader passes terminalValue: node.id==='1'?1:0 and never passes id. The bundled/Rust ids are bdd_term_0 and bdd_term_1, so isTrue evaluates to 0===1 || ''==='1' || ''.includes('1'), which is false for both terminals. The id.includes('1') heuristic would also flag ids like *_10 as TRUE.
impact: Every Rust-exported ROBDD shows no TRUE terminal, which inverts the meaning of half the paths.
recommendation: Emit an explicit terminal value in the IR and use it, falling back to node.name. Remove the id-substring heuristics. Add test loadGraphIrToCytoscape_robddTerminals: robdd.json must yield one TRUE and one FALSE terminal.

title: Final pseudo-state rendered as an initial state
evidence: The loader passes node.name, and statemachine.json names both state_init and state_final '[*]'. isInitial (name==='[*]') is checked first, so state_final draws as a filled initial circle. isFinal tests the name against 'state_final' and '_final', which can never match.
impact: Bundled and engine state machines show two initial states and no final state.
recommendation: Pass id/kind or an explicit pseudo-state type from the IR and decide initial vs final from it. Add a test that statemachine.json renders exactly one bullseye.

title: Zero metrics coerced to undefined: infeasible paths shown as '1 Canonical SAT'
evidence: The loader uses cyclomatic: x || undefined, idomRank: node.idom_rank || undefined and bddSatCount: node.sat_count || undefined. A sat_count of 0 becomes undefined, so the inspector prints '1 Canonical SAT'. An idom_rank of 0 (entry block) prints 'Parent: …' or 'Root Tier' instead of rank 0.
impact: Unsatisfiable paths are displayed as satisfiable, and the entry block's rank is lost.
recommendation: Use ?? instead of ||. Show 'n/a' when a metric is absent instead of inventing a value. Add a test with sat_count: 0 and idom_rank: 0.

title: Bundled communication.json is a copy of sequence.json; class.json has zero edges
evidence: A Python check showed communication.json == sequence.json (diagram_type 'sequence', 699 message edges). class.json's metadata says total_edges 0, and none of its 120 nodes (17 interfaces) has extends/implements. WEB-10 flagged duplicate ids in class.json, not these problems.
impact: The Communication view shows a 699-edge sequence hairball. The landing class diagram has no relationships, so the Layers panel stays hidden.
recommendation: Regenerate the assets from the Rust exporters. Add a CI check that each file's diagram_type matches its name and that class.json contains relations.

title: Custom projections emit edges whose endpoints are not in the node set; edges silently dropped
evidence: Component nodes are package ids (or comp_<id>) plus interfaces, but the edges reuse raw class-to-class endpoints. Composite, object and communication keep the first 12/12/6 classes but the first 10/10/8 raw edges, whatever their endpoints. The loader drops dangling edges without logging.
impact: Component diagrams of imported code are nearly edgeless, and other projections lose links depending on file order.
recommendation: Lift edges to the projected nodes (class→package/component) and filter edges to the selected nodes before slicing. Log dropped-edge counts. Add a test that projectCustomDiagram('component') keeps inter-package dependencies.

title: Fabrication sites not cited by WEB-02
evidence: WEB-02 cites only the deployment, state-machine and 476-578 ranges. Other invented content: object slots '= [active]'; profile stereotypes; sequence messages Execute()/ResultAck; activity steps; use cases 'Manage & Use X' with fake actors; communication 'dispatch()'; interaction refs; fallback members id:String/execute(); stub classes; default entry/do/exit; saturated_paths 1; fake imports; ${name}.java file names; lines [1,5,10]; default timing slices.
impact: Fixing only the ranges WEB-02 cites leaves most of the invented content in place.
recommendation: Treat all of these sites as part of the WEB-02 fix. Show 'not available from in-browser analysis' empty states and never synthesize names, members, files or line numbers.

title: In-browser package hierarchy flattened and every package labelled DOMAIN
evidence: buildGraphIr emits every package with is_domain_tier:true, nest_level:0 and parent:null. The loader therefore labels each one 'DOMAIN: COM.EXAMPLE.APP.SERVICE' and the layout treats all as roots. With directory-fallback names the labels become 'SRC.MAIN.JAVA…'.
impact: Package nesting is lost and every package is mislabelled as a domain tier.
recommendation: Build a package tree by splitting dotted names, set parent and nest_level, and mark only the top tier as domain. Add a test that buildGraphIr nests com.a.b under com.a.

title: Collection-typed fields never produce associations; duplicate parallel edges
evidence: fieldType = type.replace(/[\[\]<>]/g,'') turns List<Order> into 'ListOrder' (checked in Node), which never matches a class, so aggregation edges come only from arrays. Each field of the same type adds another relation, and buildGraphIr never dedupes.
impact: The most common relationship form, collections, is missing, and duplicate edges inflate the counts.
recommendation: Extract generic arguments (List<Order>→Order, Map<K,V>→V), dedupe on (source,target,kind) and record multiplicity. Add tests parseSourceFile_listFieldAggregation and buildGraphIr_dedupesEdges.

title: Explicit /tree/<branch> in the URL is overridden by the repo default branch
evidence: defaultBranch starts as the URL's branch, but the metadata fetch then always assigns meta.default_branch. So github.com/o/r/tree/dev analyzes the default branch. This is distinct from WEB-13, which covers slashed branch names and sub-paths.
impact: Users asking for a specific branch silently get the default branch's code.
recommendation: Consult default_branch only when the URL names no branch, and show the analyzed branch in the HUD. Add a test that /tree/dev uses dev.

title: GitHub ingestion lacks the local path's ignore list; filters are inconsistent
evidence: The local path skips node_modules, target, build, vendor and similar folders; the GitHub path does not, so vendored or minified JS and test fixtures compete for the 30-file sample, which follows alphabetical tree order. The caps differ (30 vs 80). Both accept .py/.go/.c even though only Java/Kotlin-style regexes exist. __MACOSX/._*.java entries are not ignored.
impact: GitHub analyses often sample irrelevant files, and results differ from the same code uploaded as a ZIP.
recommendation: Share one filter and sampling function: ignore list, an allow-list matched to what the parser supports, src/main first, and __MACOSX excluded. Unit-test it.

title: Concurrent imports possible via Enter key, presets and history
evidence: Only btn-import-repo is disabled during importRepo. The Enter handler, preset chips and history items call importRepo/importCustomCodebase with no in-flight guard, and importCustomCodebase disables nothing. A second run starts a second progress interval and a second analysis, and their renderCustomGraphIr calls race.
impact: Duplicate GitHub API usage, interleaved HUD messages, and whichever run finishes last wins the diagram.
recommendation: Use a single import controller with an AbortController and a generation token. Cancel or ignore earlier runs and disable every import entry point while one is busy.

title: Folder drag-and-drop never works; ZIP drop errors are unhandled
evidence: The folder branch relies on files[0].webkitRelativePath, which is set only for <input webkitdirectory>; dropped folders and files have '', so nothing happens. JSZip.loadAsync on drop has no try/catch, so a corrupt ZIP gives an unhandled rejection and no HUD message. The global dragover preventDefault also blocks dropping text into the URL field.
impact: The advertised folder drop silently does nothing, and failed ZIP drops are invisible.
recommendation: Walk directories with DataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry(), reuse the ZIP picker's error handling, show a drop overlay, and let inputs accept text drops.

title: No size limits on ZIP or folder ingestion (zip bomb or huge file crashes the tab)
evidence: There is no cap on archive size, entry count, per-entry uncompressed size or file size. zipEntry.async('string') and File.text() load whole files into memory on the main thread. A small zip bomb or a multi-GB generated source exhausts memory.
impact: One malicious or oversized upload crashes the tab.
recommendation: Check file.size and each entry's uncompressed size before reading, cap total bytes, skip files above about 1 MB, and do the work in a Worker.

title: Unguarded localStorage access aborts the whole studio when storage is blocked
evidence: localStorage is read and written without try/catch. The typeof guard in theme-manager still evaluates the getter, which throws. With cookies blocked or in a sandboxed iframe, the InteractiveGraphCanvas constructor (index.html:417) throws and the DOMContentLoaded handler aborts. Corrupted values also give NaN px/% labels.
impact: The studio is blank for users who block site storage.
recommendation: Add a safeStorage helper with an in-memory fallback and value validation. Test with a throwing localStorage stub.

title: Global Space and arrow handlers swallow native keyboard behavior
evidence: Space keydown is preventDefault-ed whenever focus is not an INPUT/TEXTAREA, which suppresses Space activation of focused buttons. Arrow keys are preventDefault-ed to pan the canvas until a node is selected, which blocks keyboard scrolling of the tree and code panes. WEB-15 cites only the Alt and wheel handlers.
impact: Keyboard users cannot press buttons with Space or scroll the panes with arrow keys.
recommendation: Make the canvas focusable (tabindex=0) and handle these keys only when focus is inside it. Skip BUTTON, SELECT and scrollable targets.

title: Missing ARIA roles and states on tabs, toggles and icon buttons (WCAG 4.1.2)
evidence: The inspector tabs are plain buttons with no role=tab, aria-selected or aria-controls. The Pan Lock, Radar and Loupe toggles expose no aria-pressed. The +, − and ⊡ buttons have a title but no aria-label. The active diagram button has no aria-current. WEB-15's list does not cover name/role/value.
impact: Screen readers cannot announce which tab, view or toggle is active.
recommendation: Add role=tablist/tab with aria-selected, aria-pressed on the toggles, aria-label on icon buttons, and aria-current on the active diagram.

title: Text colour contrast below WCAG 1.4.3 in both themes and on cards
evidence: Computed ratios: dark --text-faint on --bg-subtle 3.46:1 and on surface 3.86:1; light faint on subtle 4.34:1; light status badge #059669 on #ECFDF5 3.58:1; card placeholder #94A3B8 on white 2.56:1; BDD TRUE white on #10B981 2.54:1. All of this text is 9-11.5px and needs 4.5:1.
impact: Placeholders, meta text, the status badge and BDD labels are hard to read.
recommendation: Adjust the tokens to at least 4.5:1 and add a token contrast check to CI.

title: Word wrap makes code lines overlap and misaligns the line numbers
evidence: .code-line-row and .code-gutter-line have a fixed height of 20px. With .wrap-lines (pre-wrap), a wrapped line overflows into the following rows, and the separate gutter column no longer lines up with the code rows.
impact: Wrap mode shows overlapping, unreadable code with wrong line numbers.
recommendation: Use min-height and render each gutter cell and code line in the same grid row, or number lines with CSS counters.

title: Code viewer race: a slower earlier load overwrites the newer file
evidence: loadFile sets currentFile and then awaits up to 22 sequential fetches. A later call for another file can finish first; the earlier call then overwrites currentContent and re-renders, while the breadcrumbs show the newer file. There is no generation token or AbortController. This is distinct from WEB-12's request storm.
impact: The viewer can show a different file from the selected node.
recommendation: Track a load generation id or AbortController and discard stale results. Test two overlapping loadFile calls.

title: Project Explorer shows fabricated and duplicate files; the badge counts nodes
evidence: Every node without a file gets `${name}.java`, and the tree inserts one row per node with no dedupe. activity.json alone produces six 'start.java' rows, and CFG blocks, actors and BDD gates appear as .java files.
