The badge counts nodes, not files. An empty element list leaves the previous tree on screen.
impact: The Explorer misrepresents the repository's actual files.
recommendation: Build the tree from the real file list (fileCache or the tree API), dedupe by path, omit nodes without a real file, and clear the tree when there are no elements.

title: Hover HUD and minimap tooltip show '<>' or '>' instead of the class name
evidence: textLabel is '<>\nName' and both readers take its first line. The HUD's innerHTML of '<>' is parsed into a '' element and displays '<>'. The minimap's replace(/^<.*?>\s*/,'') turns '<>' into '>' (checked in Node). index.html:649 uses the same pattern and may already be covered by WEB-11.
impact: Hovering any class or interface shows '<>' or '>' instead of its name.
recommendation: Use data.name (or the last line of textLabel) and write it with textContent.

title: AI export reflects the on-screen projection, not the codebase; counts are wrong
evidence: getCodeStructureForAi reads this.cy, i.e. whatever is on screen: the first 12 classes on the object tab, the invented state machine, BDD gates. Every node that is not an interface, enum or abstract (actors, basic blocks, states) is counted in total_classes, and file_path defaults to `${name}.java`. Yet it promises 'complete type contracts'.
impact: The exported LLM context is truncated or invented depending on the active tab.
recommendation: Export from the full Graph IR regardless of the current view, count by real kind, omit unknown file paths, and state the sampling limits in the export.

title: Use-case actors drawn as sequence lifeline boxes
evidence: The loader sends kind 'actor' to generateSequenceLifelineSvg in every diagram, so the three actors in usecase.json render as rectangles labelled <<actor>>. The stick-figure branch of generateUseCaseSvg (isActor) is reachable only from the PUML fallback.
impact: Use-case diagrams break UML actor notation.
recommendation: Pass diagram_type into the loader and choose the renderer by diagram, drawing stick figures in use-case views.

title: Timing tracks show no states and have a non-proportional time axis
evidence: The track is a flat line at y=40. Only the first five instructions are used, only their '@Nms' prefix is printed, and ticks are spaced 80px apart whatever the times. timing.json has nine states per track up to '@280ms: READY', but only @0 to @100ms appear and no state names or level changes are shown.
impact: Timing diagrams carry no state information and a distorted time scale.
recommendation: Parse '@t: STATE', map states to levels, scale x by time, draw step waveforms with labels, and size the width to the time range.

title: Docs pages are chat-widget fragments: no document shell, undefined sendPrompt and CSS tokens
evidence: Six of the seven pages lack a doctype, and five also lack <head>, charset, viewport and title, so they render in quirks mode. 91 onclick='sendPrompt(…)' handlers call a function that is never defined and throw ReferenceError. Host-only variables (--surface-1, --border, --text-accent) and the .sr-only class are undefined, so borders and colours vanish and hidden headings show.
impact: The published docs render unstyled and their interactive elements do nothing.
recommendation: Wrap each page in a full HTML document, define the tokens and .sr-only, replace sendPrompt with local detail panels, and link the docs from the studio.

title: Run in-browser ingestion in a cancellable Web Worker
evidence: Fetching, reading and regex-parsing up to 80 files runs on the main thread inside async loops, with no Worker, cancel button or AbortController. This differs from WEB-05: even linear-time parsing of large files blocks input and painting.
impact: The UI freezes during imports and there is no way to cancel.
recommendation: Move ingestion and parsing into a module Worker that posts progress and supports cancellation, and transfer the Graph IR back.

title: Studio cannot export PlantUML, Mermaid or XMI
evidence: The engine has PlantUML, Mermaid and XMI exporters and the site ships .puml and .mmd files per diagram, but the Export menu offers only state JSON, AI JSON/Markdown, PNG and SVG.
impact: Users cannot take diagrams from the studio into standard UML tools.
recommendation: Add PlantUML, Mermaid and XMI exports for the current view, using backend output or a JS serializer of the Graph IR.

title: Concrete unit tests to add for the defects above
evidence: WEB-08 notes there are no tests. First cases to add: exportPng smoke test; parseRepoUrl (tree/branch, SSH, query); parseSourceFile (heritage, Kotlin, records, List<T> fields); buildGraphIr (nesting, dedupe); loadGraphIrToCytoscape (ROBDD terminals, sat_count 0, null name); generateStateNodeSvg final state; computeDeterministicLayout no-overlap; PUML arrow direction; describeRelationSemantics; projectCustomDiagram edge retention.
impact: Each listed bug can regress silently.
recommendation: Add Vitest with jsdom (or node:test) covering these cases and run them in CI before deploy_pages.

title: files_processed reports discovered files, not parsed files
evidence: stats.files_processed is sourceFiles.length (every discovered file), but only 30 (GitHub) or 80 (local) files are parsed. The HUD shows '(N files, M classes)' as if all were analyzed. WEB-02 cites the hardcoded execution_time, not this count.
impact: Users believe the whole repository was analyzed.
recommendation: Report discovered, sampled and parsed counts separately and warn when results are truncated.

title: Local imports get bogus raw.githubusercontent.com URLs that are fetched on cache miss
evidence: analyzeSourceFiles passes owner=codebaseName and repo='Local', so local classes get raw_url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<folder>/Local/main/<path>. loadFile fetches raw_url whenever the cache misses. setSource skips empty content, so empty files, or sources lost to the sessionStorage quota, send local folder and path names to GitHub.
impact: Local project and path names leak to a third party, and the 404s add latency.
recommendation: Leave raw_url undefined for local sources and cache empty strings (test content == null, not falsy).

title: Selection feedback loop double-loads files and double-selects tree rows
evidence: A tree click runs editor.loadFile(file,[1,5]) and canvas.focusNodeByFile. focusNodeByFile fires onNodeSelectedCallback, which calls fileTree.selectFile twice (646, 674) and loadFile again with different target lines. The two loads run concurrently.
impact: Duplicate fetch storms, flicker and competing line highlights on every click.
recommendation: Separate selecting from notifying. Route all selection through one function that knows its source.

title: File tree selection over-matches and the folder model desyncs
evidence: selectFile highlights every row with the same base name (all Main.java or index.ts files) and smooth-scrolls to each. It expands folders in the DOM without updating node.expanded, so the next click on that folder appears to do nothing. Every diagram switch resets all folders to expanded.
impact: Wrong rows are highlighted and folder toggling feels broken.
recommendation: Match by nodeId or full path only, update the model and re-render, and persist expansion state.

title: describeRelationSemantics labels transitions and control flow as 'association/calls'
evidence: The arrow checks run before the kind checks for message, transition, control_flow and data_flow. Edges default to arrow '-->', so a transition matches arrow.includes('-->') and is described as 'is associated with and calls … (Association)'. The association wording also asserts a call that may not exist.
impact: The AI/LLM export mislabels behavioral and CFG relations.
recommendation: Switch on kind first and fall back to the arrow only when kind is missing. Add a unit test for describeRelationSemantics(a,b,'transition','-->').

title: Expanding a package re-shows filtered edges; edges without a kind ignore filters
evidence: Expand sets children.connectedEdges().style('display','element'), which overrides the Layers filter. getActiveEdgeKinds files edges without uml_kind under 'association', but the filter selects [uml_kind="association"], so those edges cannot be hidden. The edge.layer-hidden class is never used. WEB-11 cites other filter sites.
impact: Hidden relationship layers reappear after expanding a package, and some edges cannot be filtered.
recommendation: Drive visibility through classes (layer-hidden, collapsed-hidden) in one recompute step, and normalize uml_kind when loading.

title: Package collapse hides relations, uses dead sizing code and drifts labels
evidence: Expand writes data width/height from origWidth, but compound package styles never map width or height to data, so that code has no effect. The expanded label '[−] DOMAIN LAYER: X' differs from the initial 'DOMAIN: X', and 'N subpackages' is shown even when the children are classes. Collapsing hides child edges instead of rerouting them.
impact: Collapsing a package hides all of its cross-package relations, and labels become inconsistent.
recommendation: Reroute hidden edges to the collapsed node as aggregated meta-edges with counts, keep labels consistent, and remove the dead sizing code.

title: Standalone-node grid overlaps cards of different sizes
evidence: Standalone nodes are spaced by their own size: x = c*(w+GAP)+w/2 and y = base + r*(h+GAP)+h/2. Class cards range from 290 to 950px wide with varying heights, so neighbours overlap, contradicting the file's 'zero overlapping' claim. layoutModularGridLayout already spaces by max size correctly.
impact: Overlapping cards in package-less, composite and PUML-fallback diagrams.
recommendation: Use the per-column max width and per-row max height. Add a property test asserting that no bounding boxes overlap.

title: Hierarchical layout pins any id containing 'start' or 'init' to rank 0
evidence: isStart is true for kind 'entry' and for any id containing 'start' or 'init' (restart_handler, bb_initialize_cache), so those nodes are seeded at rank 0 even when deep in the graph. id.includes also throws for numeric ids.
impact: CFG and state layouts place mid-graph nodes at the top.
recommendation: Use explicit entry flags from the IR and call String(id) before string tests.

title: PUML fallback parser: stereotypes swallowed, left arrows reversed, many [*] states
evidence: Tested in Node: the name absorbs '<<Entity>>' and 'extends Bar'. <|--, --*, --o and <-- keep source→target order, so arrowheads point the wrong way. Each [*] creates a new state_init_N or state_final_N drawn as a normal state. An unquoted 'package x {' is ignored but its '}' pops the stack. Multiplicities and dotted names do not match.
impact: When a JSON file is missing, the fallback diagrams are structurally wrong.
recommendation: Implement a small PlantUML grammar or remove the fallback and show an error. Add tests for each arrow direction and for [*] handling.

title: Most card types use fixed widths; text overflows and content is silently dropped
evidence: Only class cards size to content (capped at 950px, and 8.5px/char overestimates). State, action, use-case, object, CFG and package cards have fixed widths. CFG cards print 'BASIC BLOCK #<id>' and drop the label when instructions exist. Component and port shapes at x=-4 are clipped by the viewBox. Composite and profile cards silently show only 2-3 fields.
impact: Real names are clipped and information disappears without notice.
recommendation: Measure text (canvas measureText) for every card type, wrap or ellipsize with tooltips, keep shapes inside the viewBox, and show '+N more'.

title: Card SVGs request web fonts that SVG-as-image cannot load
evidence: Cards are data-URI SVG images whose text asks for JetBrains Mono and Inter. An SVG rendered as an image cannot use the page's Google web fonts, so text falls back to local fonts while card widths are estimated for JetBrains Mono.
impact: Typography varies between machines and cards are mis-sized.
recommendation: Embed a subset font with @font-face inside the SVG, or draw labels with Cytoscape text styles.

title: A node with a null name crashes the whole render
evidence: Destructuring defaults apply only to undefined. 'name': null reaches name.length (line 32) or name.endsWith (line 236) and throws, aborting the render. shortName.toUpperCase in graph-loader also throws when a package id or name is not a string.
impact: One malformed node blanks the entire diagram.
recommendation: Coerce with String(name ?? id) in the loader and wrap each card in try/catch with a placeholder card.

title: Magnifier loupe shows the diagram on a black background
evidence: The loupe context is created with alpha:false and cleared with clearRect, which produces opaque black. Cytoscape layer canvases are transparent outside drawn shapes, so the magnified view shows the diagram on black instead of the canvas background, even in light mode.
impact: The loupe is hard to read, especially in the light theme.
recommendation: Fill with the theme's canvas colour before blitting, or create the context with alpha:true.

title: M/L shortcuts ignore modifier keys and swallow Ctrl/Cmd+L
evidence: keydown checks only e.key 'm' or 'l' and calls preventDefault, so Ctrl/Cmd+L (focus address bar) toggles the loupe and Ctrl+M toggles the minimap. WEB-15 flags these as single-key shortcuts, but blocking browser shortcuts is a separate functional bug.
impact: Standard browser shortcuts stop working on the studio page.
recommendation: Return early when ctrlKey, metaKey or altKey is set.

title: Shared HUD status line clobbers errors and results
evidence: More than 15 writers set #hud-status-text. showCanvasNotification resets it to the default hint after 2.5s regardless of later writers, and every hover replaces it. 'Analysis Failed: …' or the import summary vanishes on the next hover, undo or shortcut.
impact: Errors disappear before users can read them.
recommendation: Separate a persistent status line from transient toasts, queue notifications, and keep errors until dismissed.

title: Import renders a class diagram while the sidebar still highlights another tab
evidence: renderCustomGraphIr renders graphIr.diagram_type || 'class' and sets currentGraphType, but neither the sidebar highlight nor localStorage openheart_active_graph changes. Loading a saved state updates the highlight but not localStorage.
impact: After an import the canvas shows a class diagram under an active 'Sequence' tab, and a reload reverts the view.
recommendation: Add one setActiveDiagram(type) function that updates canvas, sidebar and storage together, or render the selected tab's projection after import.

title: Dead preset, inconsistent preset lists, and lossy history dedupe
evidence: The payment-service chip goes to github.com/example/payment-service, a placeholder, and fails. The chips and the dropdown offer different presets. Chips clear the custom-codebase state before the import succeeds; dropdown presets do not. History dedupe drops any entry with the same name, merging different owners' repos.
impact: One visible preset always fails, and preset behaviour depends on where it is clicked.
recommendation: Define presets once in the manifest with verified URLs, dedupe history by id only, and clear state only after a successful import.

title: Startup waits on the manifest fetch; theme applied late (flash of wrong theme)
evidence: The bootstrap awaits fetchManifest, which has no timeout, before any init, and initTheme runs only after the canvas and editor are initialized. Dark-theme users see a light flash, the UI is inert meanwhile, OS theme changes are never observed, and the first auto-detected theme is persisted as if the user had chosen it.
impact: A flash of the wrong theme and an unresponsive UI on slow networks.
recommendation: Set the theme in an inline head script, fetch the manifest in parallel with a timeout, listen to matchMedia changes, and persist only explicit choices.

title: Static HTML placeholders present fabricated status before any analysis
evidence: The page ships with 'SCPG 0x83D202B2 · Verified', a file count of 35, VideoConversionFacade.java, '3 Feasible', 'Block #0 (Entry)', a branch guard, an always-'Synchronized' pill and a 'Cooper Dominators + ROBDD Active · 2026 Production Build' footer. class.json's compiler_hash is 0x83D2D2B2, not the badge value. The static sidebar is replaced at runtime anyway.
impact: Users see invented status before any work has happened.
recommendation: Ship neutral empty states and derive every badge and metric from loaded data.

title: Empty-view placeholder node renders as an unlabelled grey dot
evidence: For empty projections renderGraph inserts a node with kind 'entry', a multi-line label and no svgDataUri. The stylesheet has no generic node rule mapping label to data(label), so Cytoscape draws a default dot with no text. The fallback text also claims 'Compiled Live from Source'.
impact: Empty views show an unexplained dot instead of a message.
recommendation: Show empty states as an HTML overlay rather than a graph node.

title: Saved state embeds card SVGs: bloat, stale theme, and an image-URL load from untrusted files
evidence: Saved state stores every node's svgDataUri, so files are mostly encoded SVG and reload with the old theme's cards. A crafted state can set svgDataUri to any URL that Cytoscape loads as a background image, which works as a beacon; this is not WSEC-04's innerHTML or fetch sink. The $schema URLs point to schemas that are not published.
impact: Large, theme-locked state files, and a third-party image load when opening an untrusted file.
recommendation: Persist the IR plus positions and regenerate cards on load. Accept only data:image/svg+xml. Publish the schemas or drop the $schema fields.

title: Dead and misleading code, and conflicting colour sources
evidence: Unused import generatePackageFolderSvg. normType 'use_case' is unreachable after underscores are stripped. wheelSensitivity is set although user zooming is disabled. 'pan zoom viewport' fires the minimap twice per change. The id 'interactive-canvas' filter and kind.startsWith('cfg') can never match. Theme canvas.* and edges.<kind> tokens are unused and disagree with the manifest (aggregation #F59E0B vs #059669). Export comments are numbered 1-5 then 4.
impact: Maintainers are misled about which values are authoritative.
recommendation: Delete the dead branches and tokens, keep one source of edge colours, and enable ESLint no-unused-vars.

title: Manifest is not authoritative: duplicated in JS, fields ignored, relation kinds missing
evidence: DEFAULT_MANIFEST hand-duplicates manifest.json. file_json, file_puml and layout_engine are never read: renderGraph hardcodes `${graphType}.json`, and the actual layouts differ from the declared ones (communication is circular). The kinds 'call', 'include' and 'extend' are missing and fall back to the default style. The assembly label '(-(0-)' is malformed.
impact: The 'zero hardcoding' claim does not hold, and new relation kinds silently lose their styling.
recommendation: Read file paths and layout from the manifest, generate the default copy at build time, add the missing kinds, and validate against a schema.

title: Unreferenced assets deployed (.mmd files, duplicate JSON, unlinked docs, garbage demo names)
evidence: No JS references the .mmd files, state.json or use_case.json (renderGraph fetches statemachine and usecase). Nothing links web/docs. The workflow uploads all of web/. deployment.json has exporter-garbage node names such as node_Lets and node_terface.
impact: Larger deploys, duplicate sources of truth, and demo data that looks broken.
recommendation: Expose the Mermaid/PlantUML sources and docs in the UI or exclude them from the artifact, and regenerate deployment.json.

ENG.note: web/ and deploy_pages.yml are outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Docs claim Lengauer-Tarjan dominators; the code uses Cooper-Harvey-Kennedy
evidence: The pipeline and architecture pages state Lengauer-Tarjan in O(m α(m,n)), but dominators.rs implements the iterative Cooper-Harvey-Kennedy algorithm, which the phase-4 doc and the studio footer also name. Only phases 1-6 have docs pages; phases 7-10 have none.
impact: Published algorithm and complexity claims do not match the implementation.
recommendation: Correct the algorithm and complexity text and add pages for phases 7-10.

title: Pages workflow: mutable action tags, persisted credentials, no path filter
evidence: checkout@v4, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5 and deploy-pages@v5 are pinned to mutable major tags, not SHAs. checkout keeps persist-credentials at its default. With no paths filter, every Rust-only push redeploys Pages, and there is no post-deploy smoke or link check. WEB-08 covers only the missing test gate.
impact: Supply-chain exposure and unnecessary deployments.
recommendation: Pin actions by SHA (Dependabot can bump them), set persist-credentials: false, add a paths filter for web/** and the workflow file, and add a smoke/link-check step.

ENG.note: deploy_pages.yml is outside my paths; handoff given.

title: No content hashing, so modules can mismatch after a deploy; duplicate theme CSS
evidence: ES modules and CSS are referenced by fixed names with no hash or version. After a deploy a browser can combine a new index.html with cached old modules, or the reverse; this is distinct from WEB-09's meta cache tags. style.css also @imports the two theme files that index.html already links.
impact: Runtime errors right after deploys, and duplicate CSS requests.
recommendation: Add a build step that emits hashed filenames or ?v=<sha> suffixes, and remove the duplicate @imports.

title: Spinner invisible in dark mode; no color-scheme or reduced-motion support
evidence: The spinner is white (border-top #FFFFFF) on .btn-analyze-pill, whose background is --text-main, #F8FAFC in dark mode, so it is invisible. There is no color-scheme declaration, so native scrollbars, the range slider and checkboxes stay light in dark mode. Smooth scrolling, pulses and animated zoom ignore prefers-reduced-motion.
impact: The progress spinner disappears in dark mode, native controls clash, and motion-sensitive users are not accommodated.
recommendation: Draw the spinner with currentColor, set color-scheme per theme, and add a prefers-reduced-motion media query.

title: Head metadata issues: verification meta, apple-touch-icon, brand link
evidence: The google-site-verification meta content is the HTML-file token name rather than a meta-method token. apple-touch-icon points to an SVG, which iOS ignores, although favicon-192.png exists. The brand link href='#' only appends a hash to the URL.
impact: Minor SEO and home-screen icon problems.
recommendation: Remove the meta tag (the file method is enough), use a 180x180 PNG for the touch icon, and link the brand to './'.

title: Orphaned legacy modules contain fake exports and leaks (beyond WSEC-05's security sinks)
evidence: The XMI export writes an empty XMI and toasts 'Exported XMI 2.5 metadata'. Object URLs are never revoked. Pan/zoom listeners are re-added on every render. The trace card picks item type.length % n. The local SVG fallback invents '+ execute()'. The orb's rAF loop never stops, and window.activeTraceabilityList leaks a global.
impact: If revived, these modules produce fake exports and leaks; today they only add weight and confusion.
recommendation: Delete app.js and its module graph, or move it to an archive folder excluded from deploy.

title: Touch pinch and pan are not 1:1
evidence: Pinch zoom is damped (1 + (ratio-1)*0.4), so fingers and content drift apart. Two-finger pan movement is multiplied by panSensitivity*10, which is 5x at the 50% setting. When Pan Lock captures mousedown, one-finger panning falls back to emulated mouse events.
impact: Touch navigation feels inaccurate on tablets.
recommendation: Use 1:1 pinch anchored at the midpoint, ignore the wheel sensitivity for touch, and switch to Pointer Events.

title: Pan Lock says 'Layout locked' but collapse and delete still edit the graph
evidence: The HUD announces 'Layout locked. Pure pan & inspect mode', yet taps in lock mode still collapse and expand packages, and Delete/Backspace still removes the selected nodes.
impact: A mode labelled read-only still changes the diagram.
recommendation: Block structural edits while locked, or rename the mode.

title: Serial GitHub fetches and fragile URL parsing
evidence: Raw files are fetched one by one (30 awaits), and up to six tree requests are tried sequentially. parseRepoUrl rejects git@github.com:o/r.git, keeps '?tab=readme' in the repo name, does not strip www.github.com, and treats gitlab.com/a/b as owner gitlab.com. index.html takes the last path segment as the repo name, so /tree/main yields 'main'.
impact: Imports are slow, and common URL forms cause confusing errors or names.
recommendation: Fetch through a concurrency pool of about 6, parse URLs with URL() and validate the host, and derive the name from the parsed owner/repo.

title: Code viewer re-renders the whole file with per-line regexes and listeners
evidence: render() rebuilds the full file as two HTML strings (one div per line in both gutter and code), runs five regex passes per line and attaches one listener per gutter line. It does this on every load, gutter click and theme change, with no virtualization or size cap.
impact: Opening a multi-thousand-line file freezes the inspector.
recommendation: Virtualize rows, delegate gutter clicks to one listener, cache highlighted lines, or adopt CodeMirror 6.

title: Copy button can stick on 'Copied'; source cache collides on base names
evidence: Two Copy clicks within 1.8s capture the 'Copied' markup as orig, leaving the button permanently on 'Copied', and clipboard errors are swallowed. setSource also caches by base name, so a/Util.java and b/Util.java overwrite each other for bare-name lookups such as the fabricated ${name}.java paths.
impact: A stuck button state, and the wrong file shown for bare-name lookups.
recommendation: Capture the original markup once and clear any pending timer, show clipboard errors, and key the cache by full path only.

title: No node search and no shareable deep links
evidence: There is no search or 'find class' command for the canvas. View state (repo, diagram type, selected node) lives only in storage, never in the URL, so a view cannot be bookmarked or shared.
impact: Large diagrams are hard to navigate and views cannot be shared.
recommendation: Add a search box that highlights matches and zooms to them, and encode repo, diagram and node in location.hash with popstate handling.

title: Call resolution returns the caller itself; the error cascades into SCCs, PSA, entry points, sequence diagrams and queries
evidence: resolve_method_target never compares names. Step 3 matches a declaration's first token, which is never a call token. Step 4 returns the first method whose token span encloses the call, i.e. the caller (resolution.rs:179-238). For `t.helper()` the 'name' token picked is the receiver `t` (call_sites.rs:153-163). Self-edges are kept (cg/mod.rs:88-91,114-127), so every method that makes a call becomes SELF_RECURSIVE (scc.rs:40-47) and loses entry-point status (actor_identification.rs:18-43). call_block is always 0 because blocks hold statements, not call nodes (call_sites.rs:142-151). Field-initializer calls are dropped (call_sites.rs:32-35). cg_tests.rs:79-87 checks only counts.
impact: Every call edge is a self-loop or an override of the caller. The call graph, recursion flags, PSA unwinding, entry points, sequence and communication diagrams, slices, impact sets and reachability queries are therefore wrong for all input.
recommendation: Resolve callees by (name_id, arity, receiver static type), using Phase 3 scopes and the receiver's type_id. Then expand with CHA (Dean et al., ECOOP'95) or RTA (Bacon-Sweeney, OOPSLA'96) over th_edges. Record call_block through a statement-to-block map built in Phase 4. Done = the cg_tests fixture yields exactly main->helper, main->recurse and recurse->recurse. Then score against the CATS/Judge suites (Reif et al., ISSTA'18/'19) and diff against Soot or OPAL output.

title: The five compiler-IR diagrams and several UML views are hard-coded templates; Phase 4-8 data has no path to any exporter
evidence: Exporters receive only (uma, sta, tca) (factory.rs:50-56,314-325), so .cfa, .ssa, .cga and .psa cannot reach any diagram. The JSON cfg/dfg/cdg/callgraph/robdd exporters ignore all inputs and emit OpenHeart's own pipeline ('v0 = load manifest', 'main() -> ingest_sources()') with compiler_hash 0x83D2D2B2 and verified: true (json.rs:1748-2101). PlantUML and Mermaid emit fixed 4-block CFGs, 'var_name: retries', '(amount > 0) -> repository.saveOrder()', and a call chain in HashSet order with a fake SCC loop (plantuml.rs:1253-1450; mermaid.rs:1389-1620). State machines are a 2-state template (state_machine.rs:22-50). Four extractors have empty bodies (communication_diagram.rs:9-11; interaction_overview.rs:9-15; timing_diagram.rs:8-10; composite_diagram.rs:9-11).
impact: Every project receives fabricated CFG, DFG, CDG, CG and ROBDD views labelled verified, so README's 19 derived projections are overstated and users cannot tell real views from templates. The committed Pages demo even cites a nonexistent PipelineControlFlow.java.
recommendation: Pass a read-only AnalysisDb holding all artifacts to every exporter. Render the CFG from cfa.functions (blocks, typed edges, idom), the DFG from the def-use CSR, the CDG from ssa.cdg, the CG from cga.callee_csr plus sccs, the ROBDD from psa.node_arrays, and state machines from type-state facts. Delete the templates; when data is absent, emit an explicit 'no data' node. Lock each diagram with insta snapshots on 3 or more fixtures, and assert that JSON, PlantUML and Mermaid share the same node and edge sets.

title: Kotlin and every non-Java language are parsed by different grammars in different phases; Phase 3 covers this with a raw-token keyword sweep
evidence: Phase 1 parses .kt files with tree_sitter_java (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2 has no Kotlin adapter and falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28,41). Python, Rust, TS, C++ and Go use the JavaScript grammar in both phases (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:29-39,56). Phase 2 then maps JS-grammar nodes onto Java-grammar tokens by (line, col). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (symbol/mod.rs:38), plus a keyword sweep over raw tokens (pass1_discovery.rs:200-460). Symbols from the sweep have no decl_node, so Phase 4 skips them (cfg/mod.rs:55-58). The sweep turns `var`/`val` locals into SK_FIELDs (pass1_discovery.rs:414-450) and never resets current_class_sym per file (pass1_discovery.rs:257).
impact: Kotlin functions found by the sweep get no CFG, SSA, call edges or activity diagram. Kotlin and Java 10+ local variables appear as class fields. Top-level Kotlin functions attach to a class in another file. The multi-language claims rest on keyword heuristics.
recommendation: Create one LanguageRegistry (grammar, CST reducer, semantic adapter) keyed by LangId and used by Phases 1-3. Add pinned tree-sitter-kotlin and the other grammars, or reject unsupported extensions with a diagnostic. Remove the token sweep once Kotlin reduction exists. Per-language golden fixtures must assert classes, members and per-function CFG counts, plus a test that no SK_FIELD symbol lies inside a method body.

title: Phase 5 ignores the symbol table: SSA variables are AST node ids, so def-use chains and phi functions are empty by construction
evidence: Phase5Stage::run takes `_sta` and never uses it (ssa/mod.rs:34). Liveness treats each declaration node as its own variable (`let sym_id = node`, liveness.rs:134) and each identifier occurrence as a separate use (liveness.rs:140,160). Renaming looks up `vstack.top(u)` under the use node but pushes versions under the def node (renaming.rs:150,165). As a result no use ever finds a reaching definition, and pruned phi placement never sees a definition live-in (placement.rs:37-61). IFDS facts are placeholders: any literal child means 'nullable' and a nested method declaration means 'taint' (ifds.rs:58-78). The processOrder fixture needs phi(status), yet the test asserts only total_ssa_vars >= 4 (pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:178).
impact: Def-use chains, phi functions, taint and nullable facts, points-to seeds and PSA feasibility inputs are empty or meaningless for every function, while the run summaries report SSA statistics as if they were real.
recommendation: Resolve each NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR to a SymbolId through the Phase 3 scope graph (export a reference-to-symbol table, see E2E-14). Key liveness, phi placement and renaming by SymbolId for locals, parameters and this-fields. Use Braun et al., 'Simple and Efficient Construction of SSA Form' (CC 2013), or Cytron et al. with symbol-level variables. Done = the processOrder fixture yields phi(status) at the if-merge and at the loop header, and non-empty def-use chains for status and attempt.

title: No typed ID discipline: ids from one space are read as another at six phase boundaries
evidence: AST node ids stored in SSARecord.orig_sym_id are looked up as symbol ids by points-to (points_to.rs:31) and by the object diagram (object_diagram.rs:16,27). Per-function ssa_ids (renaming.rs:124,159) key a global points-to table (cg/mod.rs:71-78) and are matched across all functions (resolution.rs:152-154). Phase 8 reads IFDS 'taint source 1' as a block id (ifds.rs:25 vs feasibility.rs:88-93). It also uses ssa_id as a BDD variable index that collides with edge variables (feasibility.rs:122). Exporters pass scenario_name, which is a name_id, as a symbol id (sequence_diagram.rs:156; plantuml.rs:1160; mermaid.rs:1312). ssa_bi.rs:13-24,35 derives block bases from max(def_block)+1, unlike bi_blk (blk_bi.rs:12-27).
impact: Object diagrams, points-to sets, #SAT path counts, interaction-overview titles and phi source spans silently refer to unrelated entities. The compiler cannot catch any of it because every id is a bare u32.
recommendation: Introduce newtypes TokenIdx, NodeId, SymbolId, TextId, FuncId, BlockId{func,local} and SsaId{func,local}, with no implicit conversions. rust-analyzer does the same with la_arena::Idx<T> and salsa interned ids. Store a per-function block-offset table in .cfa and use it wherever global block ids are formed. Done = cargo check rejects the call sites above, and a test asserts that every object-diagram type_sym_id is a class symbol.

title: Traceability stops at Phase 9: exporters ignore UMLLink spans and fabricate file names and line numbers
evidence: Phase 7 computes exact (file_id, line, col) UMLLinkRecords, and Phase 9 copies them into ClassRecord.uml_link (class_diagram.rs:304-319). No exporter under src/scpg reads uml_link, uml_link_node or uml_link_token. The JSON IR the studio loads sets file to '<Name>.java' and lines to [1, 5, 10] (json.rs:267-268; also 580-581, 671-672, 733-734) and hard-codes 'OpenHeartEngine.java' (json.rs:1447). The editor requests /api/source by that guessed name (editor.js:160-161). The server then matches it by file stem across fixed example folders (server.rs:109-224). NavigationEngine::to_source and from_source are linear scans (navigation.rs:9-27).
impact: Click-to-source is wrong for Kotlin files, files with several classes, nested classes and duplicate names, and it always highlights lines 1, 5 and 10. The O(1) source-to-diagram traceability claim therefore fails at the UI.
recommendation: Attach a source anchor to every diagram node and edge: root-relative path, start/end line and column, and token range, taken from ClassRecord.uml_link and MessageRecord.uml_link_token. Serve sources by (session, file_id), never by name. Make to_source an O(1) index (uml_links is already sorted by sym_id) and from_source an interval-tree lookup. Done = for each fixture class, the JSON anchor equals the declaration position reported by JavaParser or javac.

title: No two runs produce identical artifacts or diagrams: timestamps, mtimes, HashMap order and raw path strings leak into outputs
evidence: .tca embeds SystemTime::now() and per-file mtimes (ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84,115; ingestion/mod.rs:62-67). .bpa embeds the .tca CRC (ast/serializer.rs:31), so every later link hash changes on each run. .sta serializes two HashMaps in iteration order (symbol/serializer.rs:169,180). .scpg embeds a timestamp (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136-140). The TRA hash is taken over Debug output that includes mtimes (hash_chain.rs:36). Iteration order also leaks: HashSet-to-Vec relations (class_diagram.rs:300-301), lifelines via into_values (sequence_diagram.rs:153), JSON packages, edges and edge ids (json.rs:148,445,518), call-graph edges in HashSet order (plantuml.rs:1432; mermaid.rs:1605), and phi order (placement.rs:37). Invocation path strings are stored verbatim (ingestion/mod.rs:137-138).
impact: Results cannot be reproduced or diffed, golden tests are impossible, the committed web/diagrams change on every run, and all UMLLinks look stale after a rebuild. README's 'deterministically derives' claim is false.
recommendation: Use BTreeMap or IndexMap, or sort, before every serialization and export. Drop wall-clock timestamps from artifacts (or honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) and keep mtimes out of hashes. Store root-relative POSIX paths (camino, path-slash). Add a CI job that runs analyze twice, once from another working directory and with shuffled discovery order, and requires byte-identical outputs (cmp or diffoscope, as reproducible-builds.org recommends).

title: Four separate pipelines (CLI, server, test builder, browser) give different results for the same repository
evidence: The CLI analyzes .java/.kt/.kts files, tests included (main.rs:76-99). The server takes 58 extensions and drops test and build dirs and *Test files (server.rs:770-884). It never calls Phase10Stage yet reports 'All 10 phases verified' (server.rs:619-699), and it swallows IO errors with unwrap_or_default (server.rs:536-609). It ignores the client's diagram_types (api.js:36 vs server.rs:366-372) and writes into the git-tracked web/diagrams shared by every session (server.rs:636-691). SCPGPipelineBuilder, the only path the tests use, writes graph.scpg instead of unified.scpg and ignores diagram_formats (pipeline.rs:100,143-148,168). The browser engine regex-parses only the first 30 files and uses a random compiler_hash (github-engine.js:102,576). The Dockerfile runs `openheart serve`, which main.rs rejects (main.rs:532,544; Dockerfile:49).
impact: The same repository gives different classes and diagrams depending on entry point. Tests and the F1 harness validate paths the CLI does not run. Concurrent sessions overwrite each other's diagrams, and the Docker image exits at startup.
recommendation: Expose one library entry point, Pipeline::run(&AnalysisConfig) -> Result<AnalysisOutputs, PipelineError>, with include/exclude globs, languages and formats. Call it from the CLI, the server and the tests, and delete the copies. Have the server write per-session directories served under /sessions/{id}/ and never touch web/. Add a contract test asserting byte-identical CLI and server outputs for a fixture, fix the Dockerfile CMD, and regenerate the Pages demo from the engine in CI.

ENG.note: Unifying the pipelines is src work. `make docker-smoke` now catches the broken Dockerfile CMD.

title: Most computed IR is never consumed, and the persisted artifacts cannot be reloaded: .scpg stores counts and .ssa reads back empty
evidence: SCPGSerializer writes a 4- or 8-byte count for 10 of 11 sections and real bytes only for strings (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:56-108). OpenHeartEngine holds a hash and an empty cache (scpg/api/mod.rs:29-45). SSASerializer::read returns no functions (ssa/serializer.rs:167-205). The CDG, def-use CSR, dominators, dominance frontiers, loop info, points_to_table and the TRA bi_ast/bi_blk/bi_ssa/bi_cs/cs_span indexes have no consumer outside their own modules except inspect printing their lengths (main.rs:397,435-439). Phase 9 computes activity labels and discards them (activity_diagram.rs:82-93), and label_texts is never filled (uma/types.rs:282). Artifact files are re-read only to compute CRCs (main.rs:154-226).
impact: Nothing can be queried, resumed or diffed from disk. The 'unified memory-mapped SCPG' and its compression figures describe a file with no data, and most Phase 4-8 work cannot change any output.
recommendation: Make .scpg the real database: store each section as a schema-versioned, zero-copy encoding of its artifact (rkyv, FlatBuffers or Cap'n Proto), memory-mapped, with section CRCs verified on open. OpenHeartEngine::open must answer queries with no in-memory artifacts, as a CodeQL database or Joern's persisted flatgraph CPG does. Add a test that fails when an artifact field has no consumer, plus an e2e test that analyzes, reopens the .scpg and runs a slice and a reachability query.

title: Error handling is inconsistent across phases: global aborts on local faults, silent skips, panics, and invariants met by editing data
evidence: One unreadable file or a None parse aborts Phase 1 (ingestion/mod.rs:51-54,111,117), and one odd function aborts Phases 4 and 5 (cfg/mod.rs:84; ssa/mod.rs:81). Yet Phase 2 silently skips files it cannot read or parse (ast/mod.rs:141-154). Phases 7-10 return no Result and panic or assert instead (tra/mod.rs:42-44; tra/builder.rs:67-130; psa/mod.rs:153-155; uma/mod.rs:97-99; scpg/mod.rs:53-55). The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind (server.rs:40-42). Invariants are met by editing data: empty blocks map to token 0 (blk_bi.rs:17-21), orphans are moved under symbol 0 (pass1_discovery.rs:622-627), and hierarchy cycles are deleted (pass5_hierarchy.rs:218). thiserror is a dependency but is never used, and error JSON interpolates Debug paths (server.rs:530-533).
impact: Large repositories fail completely on one bad unit, or degrade silently. One panic stops the server for every user, and real resolution bugs stay hidden. The CLI prints 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' even when diagram writes fail (main.rs:289-341).
recommendation: Define a StageError enum with thiserror. Make every stage return Result and record per-file Diagnostics (file, phase, kind, message) in a diagnostics table, as CodeQL extractors do, continuing past local faults. Turn invariant checks into reported errors, never data patches. Run each server request under catch_unwind or in a worker pool, and build every response with serde_json. When a run is degraded, exit non-zero and report the skipped files and failed functions.

title: Name blocklists silently drop real user classes, and the F1 = 1.0 oracle excludes the same names
evidence: ClassDiagramExtractor drops any class named in a 188-entry list that includes Entity, Configuration, Error, Value, Root, Context, Logger, Table, Singleton and Scanner, plus repo-specific names such as HomeScreen, INVESTOR and OpenHeart (class_diagram.rs:346-538). It also drops names ending in 'Binding', ALL_CAPS names, and lowercase names that differ from the file stem (class_diagram.rs:107-164). ruthless_verify.py removes every name in ruthless_config.json 'keywords' from its regex ground truth (ruthless_verify.py:88). 184 of the engine's 188 suppressed names are in that list. The harness compares only class-name sets parsed from the server's class PUML (ruthless_verify.py:317-350).
impact: Ordinary domain classes vanish from every diagram. The published F1 = 1.0 is partly true by construction, covers one projection (class names) on one path (the server), and says nothing about members, relations, CFGs or call graphs.
recommendation: Delete the name blocklists and filter only by symbol kind and origin (library vs project source). Build independent oracles: javac/JDT or Spoon for classes, members and hierarchy; kotlinc PSI for Kotlin; Soot or OPAL for call edges. Report precision and recall per relation (classes, fields, methods, extends/implements, associations, call edges, CFG blocks) on a public corpus such as Qualitas.class, XCorpus or Defects4J subjects. Run it through the CLI entry point, and publish the scripts and numbers.

ENG.note: Blocklists and oracles are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: Blocklist dropping real classes is documented in status.md, uml_derivation and the paper; blocklist removal and oracle handed off

title: End-to-end tests have no semantic oracle, so cross-phase defects pass CI
evidence: scpg_tests.rs:120 asserts `is_reach || !is_reach`, and line 128 asserts `to_src.is_some() || to_src.is_none()`. cg_tests.rs:79-87 checks only that counts survive serialization, although its fixture has known edges (main->helper, recurse->recurse). pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs asserts total_ssa_vars >= 4 (line 178) and sccs.len() == symbol_count (line 222) instead of phi placement or call edges. design_pattern_architecture_tests.rs:72-89 asserts only that 19 strings exist and contain '@startuml'. CI runs cargo check, fmt and test only (.github/workflows/ci.yml). There is no clippy, no golden-output, no determinism and no CLI end-to-end job.
impact: Every defect above survives a green build. Refactors cannot be checked against known-correct outputs, and the benchmark claims have no regression evidence behind them.
recommendation: Add 10-20 small Java and Kotlin golden fixtures with hand-verified symbols, call edges, CFG block and edge counts, phi sets and diagram node and edge sets, checked with insta snapshots. Run the real binary with assert_cmd. Add cargo-mutants to measure test strength, proptest for id-width and ordering invariants, clippy -D warnings, and the determinism job from E2E-07. Done = one injected regression per phase fails CI.

title: Phase 2 re-reads and re-parses every file and re-derives token ids by position; the two token-id spaces match only by accident
evidence: Phase 2 ignores the in-memory TokenCorpusArtifact, then re-reads each path stored in the .tca and re-parses it (ast/mod.rs:136-155). Phase 1 had already read every file twice (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111), and its SHA-256 is never re-checked. Nodes are matched to tokens by (file, line, col), falling back to any token on the same line, possibly one before the node (reducer.rs:95-117). Columns wrap in Phase 1 (`as u16`, walker.rs:59) but saturate in Phase 2 (reducer.rs:56). Phase 1 ids follow allocation order (first_token_id, token_entries), while Phases 2-10 index the sorted token_records. path_str_offset is an interner id in memory (ingestion/mod.rs:138) but a byte offset on disk (ingestion/serializer.rs:93-101).
impact: Front-end cost roughly doubles. A file edited mid-run, or a line longer than 65,535 columns, silently misaligns AST token ranges, so names, spans and links attach to the wrong tokens. A reloaded .tca resolves the wrong paths.
recommendation: Parse once: build the BP AST in the same CST walk that emits tokens, recording each leaf's token index directly, or keep each tree_sitter::Tree in memory between phases. If any phase re-reads a file, verify its SHA-256 first. Keep a single TokenIdx space (the sorted index) and assert in finalize that allocation order matches it. Give path_str_offset the same meaning in memory and on disk.

title: Phase 3 drops its resolution indices at the boundary, so later phases rescan symbols linearly without name resolution
evidence: SymbolTableBuilder holds node_to_symbol, type_ref_resolutions and per-scope import maps (symbol/builder.rs:24-30; scope_graph/mod.rs:15-16). SymbolTableArtifact carries none of them (symbol/serializer.rs:13-34,41-75), and scopes are written with import_table_off = 0 and no import table (symbol/serializer.rs:124-136). The Java reducer drops import_declaration and package_declaration (`_ => Drop`, ast/adapter/java.rs:129). Pass 2 therefore never sees a Java import (pass2_imports.rs:20-28), and Pass 1 rescans raw tokens for `package` (pass1_discovery.rs:464-575). All files share one import scope (pass2_imports.rs:15-18). Phase 6 rescans every symbol for each ancestor of each call (call_sites.rs:70-91; resolution.rs:185-235).
impact: Later phases cannot resolve receiver types or imported names, which is a root cause of E2E-01 and E2E-04. Call extraction costs O(calls x depth x symbols) on large repositories.
recommendation: Export from Phase 3, as CSR arrays in .sta, the maps node->symbol and reference site->resolved symbol and type, plus per-file import tables. Model them on CodeQL's binding relations or Kythe ref edges keyed by VNames. Keep import and package declarations as NN_IMPORT and NN_PACKAGE nodes in Phase 2, give every file its own scope, and have Phase 6 resolve calls through these tables in O(1) per site.

title: The provenance hash chain is inconsistent and partly decorative; each run has two different scpg_hash values
evidence: Phase 7 hashes Debug-formatted file records as tca_hash. It uses crc(file count) as bpa_hash, sta.bpa_hash ^ sta.tca_hash as cfa_hash and crc(call_site_count) as cga_hash (hash_chain.rs:36-41), then re-checks the same XOR (tra/builder.rs:97-109). Phase 10 uses a different XOR whose first input is the token count (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:124-134; integrity.rs:29-38). In it, ssa.cfa_hash and psa.cfa_hash cancel, because both are CRCs of the same .cfa bytes (ssa/mod.rs:41; psa/mod.rs:77). PSA stores the STA hash as ssa_hash (psa/mod.rs:78), and the .scpg source_hash is zeroed (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:146). inspect reports 'VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa without checking either (main.rs:373-388).
impact: UMLLinks carry a different hash from the .scpg header, so StaleDetector (invalidation.rs:10-12) would flag everything. CFG changes cannot alter the composite hash, and stale or mixed artifacts go undetected.
recommendation: Define provenance once. Every artifact header stores a BLAKE3 or SHA-256 digest of its canonical payload, the digests of its declared inputs and the engine version, like Bazel action keys, Nix derivations or SLSA/in-toto provenance. Loaders verify the input digests. Compute scpg_hash as a Merkle root over sorted (artifact, digest) pairs, never by XOR, and make inspect verify every checksum it reports.

title: Cross-phase id fields are narrowed to u8/u16 without checks, and exporters silently keep only the first 3-12 items, with different caps per format
evidence: file_id is u16 (core/types/source.rs:11; token.rs:121-124), so with more than 65,536 files sort keys collide and Phase 1 aborts (ingestion/builder.rs:49-56). SSARecord.def_block is truncated to u8 (core/types/ssa.rs:43) yet read as a block id by TRA and PSA (ssa_bi.rs:20,35; feasibility.rs:115-119). The phi orig_sym_id is written as u16 (ssa/serializer.rs:113), SymbolSpanRecord lines are u16 (tra/types.rs:76-84; sym_span.rs:38-40), and tokens and strings are capped at 65,535 bytes (walker.rs:54; interner.rs:99-101). Exporters keep only the first N items, and N differs by format: activity take(6) in PlantUML vs take(8) in Mermaid, and CFG take(4) vs take(3) (plantuml.rs:958,1262; mermaid.rs:1131,1397).
impact: Methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines and repositories over 65,536 files produce wrong spans, wrong block attribution or aborts. Diagrams of large projects omit most content, and what they omit differs by format.
recommendation: Use u32 for every cross-phase id and convert with checked try_from, recording a diagnostic on overflow. Replace silent take(N) with configurable limits applied identically in every format, and record 'shown/total' in diagram metadata. Add proptest-generated large inputs to CI: a 300-block method, a 70k-line file and a synthetic 70k-file tree.

title: No incremental recomputation: ids are positions in the whole corpus and the incremental engine is a stub
evidence: IncrementalEngine::apply_delta rebuilds nothing and returns `current_hash ^ 0x0101_0101` (scpg/incremental/mod.rs:26-34). RebuildPlanner relies on booleans supplied by the caller, and StaleDetector is never called (tra/delta/invalidation.rs:10-12). Every id is a position in the whole corpus: token indices are global sort positions, AST ids are preorder positions in one forest, and symbol ids follow discovery order (symbol/builder.rs:68). Editing file k therefore renumbers every id after it. Per-file SHA-256 is computed (ingestion/mod.rs:56-59) but never used as a cache key.
impact: Every edit forces a full 10-phase rebuild, which rules out IDE and incremental-CI use, and no result can be reused or diffed across versions.
recommendation: Make the file the unit. Ids become (FileId, local), with FileId interned from the root-relative path, and Phases 1-3 are cached per file, keyed by content SHA-256 plus engine version. Model cross-file phases as Salsa queries (the salsa crate, as in rust-analyzer) with revision-based invalidation and early cutoff. Use stable item ids like rust-analyzer's AstId or CodeQL TRAP keys. Done = editing one method body re-runs Phases 1-5 for that file only, shown with a benchmark.

title: Phase 8 inverts the SCC order it says it needs and never uses callee summaries
evidence: Tarjan's algorithm in scc.rs:63-104 emits an SCC only after its callees, so its output is already callee-first. Phase 8 iterates cga.sccs.iter().rev(), which is caller-first, while its comment claims the opposite (psa/mod.rs:98-104). FunctionROBDDBuilder::build receives only the function's own CFG and SSA (psa/construction/mod.rs:47-52), so the advertised callee-summary composition (psa/mod.rs:23-24) does not exist. The recursion flag comes from E2E-01's self-loop SCCs (psa/mod.rs:106), and RecursiveHandler only sets depth 3 (recursive.rs:26-28).
impact: Path summaries are purely intraprocedural, and unwind_depth = 3 is set on nearly every method that makes a call. Any future summary composition would read callee summaries before they are computed.
recommendation: Iterate Tarjan's output in emitted order (callee-first), and test that each callee's summary exists before its caller is processed. Then either implement summary composition, splicing callee path counts in at call blocks with bounded unwinding inside SCCs (Sharir-Pnueli or Reps-Horwitz-Sagiv summary edges), or drop the interprocedural claims and the CGA dependency.

title: Compiler-IR diagrams are constant templates, and the CDG hard-codes the paper's PaymentService example
evidence: json.rs:1748-2100: the CFG, DFG, CDG, call-graph and ROBDD exporters take `_uma,_sta,_tca` and return fixed nodes describing OpenHeart itself ("v0 = load manifest", "compute_idom", "x2: ASTAcyclic"). plantuml.rs:1271-1283 emits the same 4-block diamond for every function; 1355-1363 hard-code `var_name: retries`. plantuml.rs:1387-1390 and mermaid.rs:1566-1570 hard-code "(amount > 0)" and "repository.saveOrder()", which is the PaymentService fixture in research_paper_theorems_tests.rs:107-112. plantuml.rs:1432-1446 chains HashSet-ordered nodes as "CHA/1-CFA dispatch" and adds a "Tarjan SCC cycle <<Recursive>>" self-loop on every input. No exporter reads CFA, SSA, CGA or PSA.
impact: 5 of the 19 advertised projections show the same picture for any codebase; on unseen or renamed code only the labels change. The fabricated call-graph edges are also nondeterministic across runs because they follow HashSet order.
recommendation: Pass the CFGArtifact, SSAArtifact, CallGraphArtifact and PathSummaryArtifact into the exporters and render from them: CFG from the successor CSR plus the idom tree, DFG from the def-use CSR and PhiRecords, CDG from CDGCSR, call graph from callee_csr with SCC membership, ROBDD from psa.node_arrays. Sort all output. Done = insta golden tests on about 10 hand-labelled functions (if, loop, switch, try, recursion), plus a test that template literals ("retries", "saveOrder") never appear for an unrelated fixture.

title: Ground truth was co-edited with the tool: a shared 184-name exclusion list hides misses and phantoms
evidence: 184 of the 188 names in class_diagram.rs:346-538 (applied at 163) also appear in ruthless_config.json:59-92. They include real class names such as Entity, Configuration, Root, Table, Scanner, Value, Update, HomeScreen, INVESTOR and OpenHeart. The oracle removes them from ground truth (ruthless_verify.py:88) and from tool output (232). The tool's placeholder names SystemNode, Node_0..2 and Unknown (config:73) are erased before phantoms are counted. Commit 660e282 added HomeScreen, INVESTOR, Root, Table and Scanner to the oracle in the same commit that edited the tool filter. Experiment: on examples/huge_enterprise_src the oracle returns 11 classes and omits `interface Entity`, which the tool also drops, so the omission cannot lower F1.
impact: F1 = 1.0000 measures agreement after both sides delete their disagreements; any class the tool mishandles can be fixed by adding it to the list. On an unseen domain (JPA Entity, Table, Value) the lost classes are invisible to the metric.
recommendation: Make the oracle independent and frozen. Derive ground truth from language front-ends (JavaParser with SymbolSolver or `javac -Xprint`, Kotlin PSI, Python `ast`, TypeScript compiler API, rustdoc JSON), exclude only keywords from the language spec, and never filter tool output before scoring (report filtered names as a separate column). Add a CI rule rejecting PRs that change the oracle config and the extractor together. Done = F1 recomputed on a pinned held-out corpus with the shared list removed.

title: The deployed Live Studio fabricates results for user repos: regex on 30 files, template diagrams, random 'verified' hashes
evidence: Without a backend, which is the GitHub Pages default (index.html:908-935), github-engine.js regex-parses only `sourceFiles.slice(0, 30)` (103, 291). When nothing matches it invents `id: String` and `execute(): void` members (144-145). It reports `execution_time_ms: 280` (164), a `Math.random()` compiler_hash with `verified: true` (576-577), and `lines: [1, 5, 10]` for every class (526). graph-canvas.js:277-575 draws 17 views from fixed templates ("Client Workstation", "ResultAck", "Ready / Idle", "Administrator", "@0ms: Idle", "InitializeContext()", "var_isValid"). The HUD shows "SCPG 0x… · Verified" built from the session id (index.html:919-920). The offline SVG draws "+ execute()" on every class (api.js:122-123).
impact: Every Live Studio visitor sees the same invented behavioral and IR diagrams, labelled as compiled and verified. For an unseen repository only the class names differ, and files after the first 30 are silently ignored.
recommendation: Either run the real pipeline in the browser (compile the crate to WASM with wasm-bindgen and use web-tree-sitter grammars) or relabel the mode "regex class outline (preview)" and render only the class and package views. Delete the templates, fake members, random hashes and fixed timings, and show "requires engine" for the other views. Done = a Playwright e2e test on a fixture repo asserting that no template strings appear and that the reported file count equals the parsed file count.

title: F1 compares two keyword scanners on simple class names; non-Java languages use the wrong grammar
evidence: Scoring is the set intersection of simple class names parsed from the class diagram (ruthless_verify.py:247-254, 342-348). Relations and members are not scored, the package score is precision only (395), the promised 3-oracle cross-check is not implemented (299-303), and empty vs. empty scores 1.0 (252-253). Kotlin is parsed with tree-sitter-java (kotlin.rs:30). Python, TS, Rust, C++ and Go fall back to tree-sitter-javascript (registry.rs:34-38; Cargo.toml has only those two grammars). Their classes therefore come from the keyword-plus-uppercase-token sweep (pass1_discovery.rs:249-455), which is the same heuristic as the oracle regexes (ruthless_config.json:2-45). server.rs:83-84 still advertises python, typescript, cpp, rust and go.
impact: The README claim "F1 = 1.0000 across Java, Kotlin, Python, Rust, TypeScript, C++" is tautological. The Phase-1 tokens plus the Pass-1 sweep alone can satisfy it, so it says nothing about the AST, symbol resolution, CFG, call graph or relations.
recommendation: Score at relation level with fully-qualified identities: classes, members with signatures, generalization/realization/association edges and package membership. Report micro- and macro-averages with bootstrap 95% CIs, per language. Add real grammars (tree-sitter-kotlin, -python, -typescript, -rust, -cpp, -go) with semantic adapters, or withdraw the language claims. Done = a per-language scorecard generated in CI from a pinned corpus.

title: GoF detection is keyed on class-name substrings; the structural detectors that exist are never called
evidence: factory.rs:17 is name-only (`contains("factory")` gives 90). state.rs:18 fires on "state" or "strategy" (85). strategy.rs:20-21 gives 95 from the name; adapter.rs:21-22, facade.rs:18-19 and composite.rs:28-29 accept the name alone; builder.rs:33 checks `ends_with("Builder")`. mod.rs runs State (101-112) before Strategy (140-151), so PaymentStrategy is rendered «State» (plantuml.rs:315-320). The query.rs:78-132 helpers and the structural detectors in symbol/uml_meta/patterns.rs:20-137 have no callers. Simulation: the name predicates label 8 example classes; after neutral renaming 6 lose their label, and only Builder and Decorator have structural fallbacks.
impact: Labels disappear under renaming or non-English naming and appear on names like StatementParser and SessionFactoryBean. The bundled Factory Method (Logistics), Observer (NewsAgency.attach; observer.rs:25-29 requires "listener") and Template Method (DataMiner; template_method.rs:32 requires a protected method) examples are missed.
recommendation: Detect roles structurally and behaviourally over SCPG facts. Options: similarity scoring on generalization/association/invocation matrices as in Tsantalis et al. (TSE 2006), or Datalog rules (Soufflé, or Rust ascent/crepe) using the call graph and points-to: Decorator forwards to a field typed as its supertype, Observer iterates an observer collection, Template Method calls abstract primitives. Names may only nudge confidence. Done = a rename-invariance test passes and P/R are reported on P-MARt.

title: The structural checks that do exist are wrong: Singleton on any self-reference, Composite identical to Decorator, Facade counts primitives
evidence: singleton.rs:20-34 returns confidence 100 if any field is named "instance" or typed as the class itself, with no static, private-constructor or accessor check; `class Node { Node next; }` qualifies. composite.rs:22-24 is identical to decorator.rs:21-23 (a field typed as a supertype), so CondimentDecorator is also reported as Composite (75). Real composites are missed: `List<Component>` fields resolve to the erasure head List, because pass3_types.rs:26-36 resolves a type from its first token. facade.rs:11-14 counts fields whose type_id is not u32::MAX, but primitive ids are 0xB000_000x (java.rs:21-29). By static trace, Computer (4 fields) and UserAccount (3 fields) therefore become Facade (70).
impact: Confident false positives on linked structures, trees and plain entities or DTOs, while true composites are missed. Precision on real code will be far below the reported confidences.
recommendation: Wire in the stricter Singleton detector that already exists in symbol/uml_meta/patterns.rs:20-59 (private static self field, public static accessor, no public constructor). Keep generic type arguments in the symbol table. Require a Composite field whose element type is a supertype, plus add/remove methods and iteration delegation via CGA. Define Facade as public methods calling at least 2 distinct subsystem packages, ignoring primitives and JDK types. Done = per-detector unit tests with positive and negative fixtures (linked list, JPA entity, DTO, wrapper).

title: Most UML behavioral views and the XMI export are templates or empty stubs presented as derived
evidence: state_machine.rs:10-64 claims IFDS typestate but leaves `_ssa` unused; it turns every class with a method into a 2-state machine. The exporters add invented states and actions "Uninitialized", "Active", "onInit()", "executeWork()" and "cleanup()" (plantuml.rs:1005-1016; json.rs:758-853). The timing, communication and interaction extractors have empty bodies. Use-case actors are classes whose names end in Controller/Client/App/Main/Service/Facade, and use cases are the first 3 methods of the first 6 classes (plantuml.rs:886-946). Fallbacks invent `execute()` chains (json.rs:656-690), an "OpenHeartEngine" composite (1436-1493) and `X.jar` nodes (1161-1217). Activities emit `if (eval_branch)` with no endif (plantuml.rs:972). XMI writes only `name="Class_{id}"` (xmi.rs:13).
impact: About half of the "14 UML 2.5 diagrams" carry no program-specific information and look structurally the same on any input. The XMI cannot be imported meaningfully into any UML tool, and invalid PlantUML (an unclosed if) gets through.
recommendation: Ship only projections with a real derivation and mark the rest experimental. Derive state machines from enum or state fields and guarded assignments, using typestate over the existing IFDS solver. Derive use cases from framework entry points (@RestController/@*Mapping, Android components) via the call graph. Drop the timing view unless clock or thread events are modelled. Export full UML2 XMI (names, attributes, operations, generalizations) and validate it with Eclipse UML2. Done = golden tests per exporter, and PlantUML `-checkonly` passes.

title: Traceability in the delivered UI is fabricated, and source lookup is overfit to the example corpus
evidence: Every JSON class node gets `file: "{Name}.java"` and `lines: [1, 5, 10]` (json.rs:267-268), although ClassRecord carries a real UMLLink; other views use `lines: vec![1]` (581, 672, 734, 1394, 1472). /api/source first tries hard-coded example-pattern folders and ./target_repos/FractalAndroid (server.rs:119-198). It then returns the first basename match under ./examples before ./target_repos (207-223), so a user's Application.java can resolve to examples/big_project_src/.../Application.java. If that also fails, editor.js:209-213 synthesizes a Java file with invented method bodies (227-500) and highlights lines in it. server.rs:717 falls back to the name `file_{id}.kt`.
impact: The "O(1) bidirectional traceability" claim fails in practice: Kotlin and TS files, inner classes and multi-class files jump to the wrong file or line, sometimes into example code or synthesized source.
recommendation: Emit the real span (file path from tca, line/col start and end from tra.uml_links) on every node and edge. Serve sources only by a manifest-relative path validated against the analysed tree. Remove the example-directory probes and synthesizeSourceFromNode. Done = a property test asserting that, for every node, the cited file and line contain the declared identifier, plus e2e tests on Kotlin and TypeScript fixtures.

title: Hard-coded name deny-lists and suffix rules silently drop real user classes
evidence: class_diagram.rs:161-165 discards any class whose name ends in "Binding" or appears in a 188-entry list (346-538) that mixes keywords with domain names: Entity, Value, Configuration, Root, Table, Scanner, Context, Update, Insert, Error, Logger and others. The PlantUML view also skips user classes named List, Map, Set, Optional or Character (common.rs:59-91; plantuml.rs:292). The server drops any file whose stem ends in "test", such as Contest.java or Latest.java (server.rs:875-881). Pass 1 rejects classes named Map, Set, Array, Function or Promise (pass1_discovery.rs:356-370). The bundled examples/huge_enterprise_src/enterprise/bank/core/Entity.java, implemented by BaseModel, is dropped.
impact: Common domain models (JPA Entity, Table and Value, Android *Binding classes, a game Map class) lose classes and edges without warning, and FIT-02 ensures the benchmark never notices.
recommendation: Filter by origin, not by name. Library stubs already carry first_token_id and decl_node = u32::MAX (java_stubs.rs:127,140), and unresolved types are SK_EXTERNAL. Exclude generated code by configurable path globs, and identify test sources from build metadata (Gradle/Maven sourceSets, Cargo targets) instead of filename suffixes. Done = a fixture with classes named Entity, Table, Map, Contest and FooBinding appears complete in every exporter.

title: Identity is the simple class name end to end; same-named classes merge, and the benchmark cannot see it
evidence: PlantUML declares `class {SimpleName}` with no FQN alias (plantuml.rs:330-333) and keys class_by_name and edges by simple name (443-470). JSON node ids are simple names (json.rs:258). Pass 4 binds types through class_name_to_sym, a map keyed by simple name (pass4_members.rs:18-32, 108). The oracle is a dict keyed by simple name (ruthless_verify.py:95) and the PUML parser returns a set, so both sides collapse duplicates. Experiment: for a toy tree with a/Config.java and b/Config.java the oracle reports one class. adversarial_trick_tests.rs:7 claims "disambiguation of identical class names", but its fixtures contain no duplicates.
impact: In real repositories (java-design-patterns declares App in nearly every module; Spring apps have many Config and Application classes), members and edges from different packages are merged or misattributed while F1 stays unchanged.
recommendation: Use the FQN (package plus enclosing types) or the symbol id as node identity in every exporter, with display aliases (`class "Config" as a.Config`). Resolve types only via the scope graph and imports, and score benchmarks by FQN. Done = a fixture with three Config classes in different packages yields three nodes with correct edges in PlantUML, Mermaid and JSON.

title: A missing or failed repository is silently replaced by another repo and reported as success
evidence: When ./target_repos/<name> is absent and `git clone` fails, process_analyze_request takes the first directory in ./target_repos (server.rs:467-482). It analyses that directory and returns `"status":"success"` with the log "All 10 phases verified" (696-699). The payment-service preset (index.html:93, 1155) points at https://github.com/example/payment-service, which can only succeed through this fallback. Benchmark scripts gate on status and syntax only (verify_all_14_uml_diagrams.py:132-149), so a missing dataset produces green results computed on the wrong code.
impact: A typo, a private repo or an absent dataset returns another project's diagrams under the requested name. Published benchmark numbers can come from the wrong repository without any warning.
recommendation: Fail closed: return an error status (and HTTP 4xx) when the requested repository cannot be materialized. Include the resolved path and commit SHA in every response. Benchmark scripts must assert that the analysed SHA equals the pinned SHA from a dataset manifest. Done = an integration test where an unknown repository yields an error and no diagrams.

ENG.note: server.rs, web/index.html and the benchmark scripts are outside my paths; handoff given.

title: Benchmark scripts cannot fail on wrong content; several checks are hard-wired to pass
evidence: The PlantUCD "stress test" never calls OpenHeart and logs `True` per batch (test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:248-260). CRC checks pass on `"Artifact Type" in out` or `"Artifact" in out` (same file :113; test_authored_design_patterns.py:164; test_diagrams_outputs_refresh.py:125). Meanwhile `inspect` prints "CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID" for .tca and .bpa after comparing only the magic bytes (main.rs:372-388). verify_all_14_uml_diagrams.py:59-121 accepts any "-->" or "partition " line, which the templates always emit. benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py exits 0 on failure (210-215) and special-cases GHobbits→GenHobbits (63-64). test_full_suite.py:243 prints a literal "F1=1.0000 across ... repos".
impact: The suites report 100% regardless of semantic correctness. Breaking any analysis phase leaves every script green, so the scripts provide no evidence for the README claims.
recommendation: Make every check falsifiable by comparing with labelled expectations. Validate diagrams by rendering them (`java -jar plantuml.jar -checkonly`, mermaid-cli `mmdc`). Make inspect call the CRC-verifying deserializers and print the computed checksum. Exit non-zero on any failure and delete dataset-specific renames. Done = a seeded-fault run (corrupt one .tca byte, break the dominator pass) turns the suite red.

title: Rust tests are mostly existence and round-trip checks; obvious ground truth is unused and the 'adversarial' cases are tuned to name matching
evidence: adversarial_trick_tests.rs:259-262 passes if any one of four patterns is found, and every fixture class has the pattern in its name (79-166). The diamond, duplicate-name and state-machine cases promised in the header (1-12) are never asserted. cg_tests.rs encodes main→helper, main→recurse and recurse→recurse (23-37) but asserts only `method_count > 0` and `!sccs.is_empty()` (79-81). pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:142 asserts function_count == 2 for three bodied callables, although cfg/mod.rs:45-48 includes constructors; this looks like current output frozen as truth. φ-nodes are printed but never asserted (surgical_pipeline_dump_test.rs:341-361). The "Theorem 5.6" test checks only `contains("@startuml")` (research_paper_theorems_tests.rs:173-203).
impact: Wrong CFGs, missing call edges, misplaced φ-nodes and the fabricated diagrams all pass. By approximate classification, about half of the 284 assertions are existence, syntax, round-trip or format checks, and src/uma, scpg, cfg, ssa, cg and symbol have no unit tests.
recommendation: Add oracle-backed tests modelled on cfg_tests.rs:120-128 (hand-derived idom and DF): exact CFG and φ expectations per construct, and exact call-edge sets and SCCs, cross-checked against SootUp or WALA on the same Java fixtures. Write pattern fixtures with neutral names. Run cargo-mutants in CI and enforce a mutation score (for example at least 70% on src/cfg, src/ssa and src/cg). Done = the mutation report is published and the thresholds are enforced.

title: Design-pattern detection and class relationships are never scored against labels
evidence: The "Ground Truth: ... Pattern" checks score only class-name recall on java-design-patterns modules (test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:168-226). The "Deep Semantic Design Pattern Verification" (test_authored_design_patterns.py:200-294) checks hand-listed example class names, inheritance edges and raw substrings such as "instance", "getInstance" and "mine". It never reads a «Pattern» stereotype or uma.design_patterns. benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:111 parses the ground-truth relations and then discards them (`gt_classes, _ =`). As far as I know, its "official architect" .urm.puml oracle is generated by the dataset's urm-maven-plugin; I could not verify this offline.
impact: The precision and recall of the GoF detectors, and of every relation in the class diagram, are unknown. The README's pattern-detection claims have no measurement behind them.
recommendation: Score role-level pattern instances on labelled corpora: P-MARt (Guéhéneuc), the DPB benchmark (Arcelli Fontana et al.) and Percerons, and compare with published detectors such as Tsantalis DPD. Add relation-level scoring keyed by FQN, using the .urm.puml edges the script already parses. Report per-pattern P/R/F1 with confidence intervals. Done = a per-pattern table produced in CI and tracked across releases.

title: Headline numbers are unmeasured or unreproducible (128×, the F1 table, the CI badge, test counts)
evidence: "128× Memory Compression" (README.md:54) divides 32 MB of pointers by the 250 KB topology bitstring only; the same derivation totals 9.65 MB, which is 3.3× (docs/succinct_structures.md:37-47). There is no benches/ directory and no criterion harness. The F1 table (docs/overview.md:100-111) cannot be reproduced: target_repos/ is gitignored, no URLs, commit SHAs or result files are committed, and CI (ci.yml) runs only cargo test. The "CI passing" badge is a static shields.io image (README.md:10). README.md:164 claims 22 integration tests; tests/ contains 29.
impact: Readers cannot check any headline claim, and the badge stays green even when CI fails.
recommendation: Publish a benchmark manifest (repo URL, commit SHA, licence) and commit machine-readable results. Add criterion benches that measure serialized artifact bytes and resident memory against a pointer baseline (for example a tree-sitter Tree or a JavaParser AST heap) and report the measured ratio. Use the workflow status badge and generate README numbers from CI artefacts. Done = `make bench` reproduces every README number.

ENG.note: Benches, README and docs are outside my paths. .gitignore does not block committing a benchmark manifest or result JSON. Handoff given.

DOCS.note: 128x, F1 table, static badge and test counts removed; benchmark manifest and result requirements in status.md §7; benches and CI handed off

title: Build an independent, oracle-backed benchmark harness for each pipeline phase
evidence: Today the only external oracles are a regex class scanner (ruthless_verify.py:61-100) and the class names from .urm.puml files. Nothing beyond class discovery (symbols, CFG and dominators, SSA, call graph, points-to, traceability spans) has a reference to compare against. There is no dev/test separation, so heuristics are tuned on the same repositories that are reported.
impact: Without per-phase references and a held-out set, benchmark-grade status cannot be demonstrated, and overfitting will recur as heuristics are added.
recommendation: Create a bench/ directory containing: a pinned corpus (Defects4J, XCorpus or Qualitas subsets, spring-petclinic and java-design-patterns at fixed SHAs); adapters exporting reference outputs into one FQN-keyed JSON schema (JavaParser with SymbolSolver for symbols and relations; SootUp, WALA or OPAL for CFG, dominators and CHA/RTA call graphs; Doop for points-to; the Judge suite for call-graph soundness); per-artifact scorers; a test split run only at release; and a CI scorecard that fails on regression.

title: Add metamorphic rename-invariance and mutation testing to catch overfitting automatically
evidence: Results depend on how identifiers are spelled throughout. name_matches uses substring contains (query.rs:30-38), use-case actors and pattern labels use suffix rules (plantuml.rs:897-903), and the deny-list filters by exact name (class_diagram.rs:346-538). No test applies a semantics-preserving transformation and checks that the output is unchanged, and no mutation testing measures whether the assertions can fail at all.
impact: Name dependence and fixture tuning come back silently with each new heuristic, and weak tests cannot be told apart from strong ones.
recommendation: Add a metamorphic suite using tree-sitter or JavaParser rewriting: consistently α-rename classes, methods and packages to random identifiers, reorder declarations, split or merge files and insert dead code. Assert that analysis outputs are equal modulo the renaming, and generate fixtures with proptest. Run cargo-mutants nightly and publish the mutation score. Done = the rename-invariance suite passes on examples/ and the GoF fixtures.

title: Every non-Java language is parsed with a foreign grammar, silently
