evidence: Cargo.toml:8-10 ships only tree-sitter-java and tree-sitter-javascript. src/ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31 returns `tree_sitter_java::language()`, yet its map targets tree-sitter-kotlin kinds that the Java grammar never emits ('simple_identifier', '?:', '!!' at :35,57). Both registries fall back to a JavaScript-grammar adapter for any unregistered LangId (src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39,56; src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:20-28,41). The AST registry has no Kotlin entry, so a .kt file is lexed as Java in Phase 1 and re-parsed as JavaScript in Phase 2 (src/ast/mod.rs:141-143). Python, TS, Rust, C++, Go, Swift, C# and the server's extra extensions (.sh, .sql, .asm; src/adapters/server.rs:805-866) all become JavaScript. Nothing in src/ calls has_error or is_missing.
impact: For every advertised non-Java language the parse tree is mostly ERROR nodes. Symbols, CFGs, SSA, the call graph and all diagrams are therefore artifacts of mis-parsing; for Kotlin, tokens and AST even come from two different grammars. Users get no warning.
recommendation: Ship real grammars (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng, -python, -typescript/tsx, -rust, -cpp, -go) after moving to tree-sitter 0.24+. Put them behind one registry with no JavaScript fallback; unsupported files are skipped with a diagnostic. Record per-file ERROR/MISSING node ratios (Node::has_error, Node::is_missing) in the .tca file record and the API response, and flag or exclude files above a threshold. Done = a per-language conformance corpus that parses with zero ERROR nodes, asserted in CI.

ENG.note: Needs new grammars in [dependencies] and new adapters/registries in src. Exact dependency and call-site changes are in handoffs.

title: Kotlin token heuristics run on every file and invent members and inheritance, including in Java
evidence: src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:200-456 ('Secondary Token-Level Discovery Sweep for Kotlin & Multi-Lang') never checks the language. After any fun/val/var token, the next alphabetic token within 10 becomes a member of current_class_sym (:414-453); there is no scope check and no per-file reset (:257). src/symbol/passes/pass5_hierarchy.rs:76-157 treats any ':' or 'extends' before '{' as a supertype. A Python port of both loops (C:/Users/AHMAD_~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--Repos-OpenHeart/31873741-1e3a-46df-bb5d-a94a867cbe24/scratchpad/lens/sweep_sim.py) produces these results. Java `var sum` and `int val = compute()` give fields sum and compute; `@Import({Repo.class, Mailer.class})` gives a phantom class Mailer. Kotlin local vals become fields, `fun <T>` gives a method T, and `fun String.shout` gives a method String. `Repo<T extends BaseEntity>` and `data class Order(val c: Customer)` give bogus extends edges. The CLI also feeds build.gradle.kts files to the sweep (src/main.rs:79-93).
impact: Modern Java code (`var` since Java 10, generic bounds) and nearly every Kotlin file get phantom fields and methods and false generalizations in class, package and pattern output. The name-only F1 harness cannot see phantom members or duplicate classes.
recommendation: Delete the sweeps and derive Kotlin declarations from tree-sitter-kotlin-ng through a real lowering. Interim steps: run each heuristic only when the file's language is Kotlin (tca.file_records[fid].language_id); track brace depth to reset current_class_sym per file and at depth 0; skip type-parameter and constructor-parameter lists in Pass 5; and set first_token_id on sweep-created symbols (pass1_discovery.rs:439-446) so Pass 4 (pass4_members.rs:60-71) can give them types. Add the snippets above as regression fixtures.

title: Phase 9 drops real classes through a repo-tuned name blocklist that the F1 oracle mirrors
evidence: In src/uma/structural/class_diagram.rs:346-538, `is_reserved_keyword` (188 names, applied at :163) mixes language keywords with framework and application names: 'Context' (:468), 'Entity' (:418), 'Configuration', 'Root', 'Table', 'Error', 'Update', 'Logger', 'Singleton', 'HomeScreen' (:519), 'INVESTOR', 'OpenHeart'. The extractor also rejects names with characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_] (:98-101), ALL_CAPS names (:107), lowercase-initial names unless they equal the file stem (:157), test paths (:136) and names ending in 'Binding' (:162). Of the 119 entries that are not language keywords, 115 also appear in the ruthless_config.json 'keywords' list. ruthless_verify.py:88,172,216,232 strips that list from both the ground truth and the output.
impact: The State/Strategy participant Context, a JPA Entity, and any class named Error, Root, Table or Logger vanish from every diagram and from pattern detection. The benchmark cannot see the loss, by construction.
recommendation: Remove name-based rejection from Phase 9. Filter only by symbol kind and provenance (declared in an analyzed source file, versus stub, external or annotation). Annotation names are already tagged TokenType::Annotation; keep framework vocabularies in per-language data files, off by default. Decouple the oracle from the engine (no shared lists), and add fixtures with classes named Context, Entity, Error, Größe and $Proxy that must appear.

ENG.note: The class_diagram.rs blocklist and the oracle config are outside my paths.

title: Import, package and module semantics are dead or based on Java strings; types are joined by simple name
evidence: The Java reducer has no import_declaration or package_declaration arm (`_ => Drop`, src/ast/adapter/java.rs:129), so Pass 2 never sees a Java import. For other languages, src/symbol/passes/pass2_imports.rs:27-37 tests starts_with("import ") on space-joined tokens (:63). Kotlin `import kotlin.math.max` therefore yields the key ' max', and the JS `import` keyword is an anonymous token that never reaches the corpus. `wildcard_imports` (src/symbol/scope_graph/resolver.rs:57) is never called. Cross-file Java types fall back to SK_EXTERNAL (pass3_types.rs:86). Passes 4-5 and the PlantUML exporter then re-join by simple name, last insert wins (pass4_members.rs:32, pass5_hierarchy.rs:33, src/scpg/diagram/export/plantuml.rs:442-447). Packages come only from a 'package' token scan (pass1_discovery.rs:464-573).
impact: Same-named types in different packages, modules or languages (com.a.User vs com.b.User, Kotlin User vs TS User) are merged in types, inheritance and associations. Python, TS and Rust module structure never reaches package diagrams.
recommendation: Replace Passes 2-3 with a real scope-graph resolver (van Antwerpen et al.), for example tree-sitter-stack-graphs rule sets (Java, Python, TypeScript and JavaScript exist; vendor them if upstream is archived). Add per-language module resolvers: Java/Kotlin packages and file facades, Python packages with __init__ and relative imports, ES modules with tsconfig paths, Rust mod trees. Key every symbol by qualified name and forbid simple-name HashMaps. Done = same-name, two-package fixtures per language with exact edges.

title: Phases 3-9 ignore the stored language and hardcode JVM semantics for every file
evidence: The language id is read only in Phases 1-2 (src/ingestion/mod.rs:112; src/ast/mod.rs:73,141). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (src/symbol/mod.rs:38) and loads only Java stubs (src/symbol/builder.rs:45; java_stubs.rs:119). The symbol model is the JVM's: SymbolVisibility{Package=0,...} (src/core/types/symbol.rs:79-80), STRICTFP and BRIDGE flags (:65,70), and a package-private default for types (src/symbol/adapter/java.rs:125-133). Call kinds mirror invokestatic/invokespecial/invokevirtual (src/cg/call_sites.rs:93-122). Allocation is recognized only as NN_NEW_EXPR (src/cg/points_to.rs:30; associations.rs:98). In src/symbol/uml_meta/associations.rs:40, stubs.contains_key("List") is always true, so every association saved in .sta is an Aggregation (the exporters ignore these records and re-join by name).
impact: Visibility, dispatch, points-to, composition and entry points are wrong or empty for non-JVM languages, and partly for Kotlin, which has no `new`. The dispatch model cannot express C++ non-virtual calls or Rust static dispatch.
recommendation: Store a lang_id on every symbol (SymbolRecord._reserved) and add a per-language LanguageSemantics profile. It covers: a visibility model mapped to UML (internal, pub(crate), fileprivate) with defaults; a dispatch policy (Joern-style STATIC/DYNAMIC plus receiver-type recovery); an allocation recognizer (a call whose callee resolves to a type); the exception model; collection types; entry points; and data-driven stubs (JDK ct.sym, typeshed, lib.d.ts). Fix associations.rs:40 to test the field's own type.

title: The generic adapter is unsound even for JavaScript, the only other real grammar
evidence: src/ingestion/adapter/generic.rs never overrides include_anonymous (default false, src/ingestion/adapter/mod.rs:14-16). As a result, src/ingestion/walker.rs:42 drops every anonymous leaf: '(', '{', ';', '=', 'class', 'import'. Pass 1 names a method by the last identifier before '(', '{' or ';' within 16 tokens (src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:696-745), so JS methods and fields get a body identifier as their name. src/ast/adapter/generic.rs has no identifier or type_identifier arm, so there is no NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR or NN_TYPE_REF; SSA uses (src/ssa/liveness.rs:139-161), type refs and call names are all empty. Kinds are matched by substring (:107-116) without an is_named() check, so the anonymous 'class' and 'function' keywords (:35,50) likely create nested duplicate declarations. encode_attrs returns 0 (:120-121), and a println! runs in the hot path (:26-28).
impact: JavaScript class diagrams show wrong member names and probably duplicate classes. The JS data-flow graph, call graph and type relations are empty or point back at the caller. TypeScript, Python and Rust inherit all of this through the fallback.
recommendation: Retire the generic adapter. Give each language an explicit lowering keyed on tree-sitter field names (child_by_field_name: name, body, condition, parameters, superclass) that classifies only named nodes; take names from the name field, not from token scans. Generate exhaustive match tables from each grammar's node-types.json and fail CI on any unmapped named kind. Remove the println!.

title: Position and identifier model is byte- and ASCII-based; one long line aborts Phase 1
evidence: src/ingestion/walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps, in the sort key's 16-bit column (src/core/types/token.rs:121-124). On a line longer than 65,535 bytes, a later token can collide with an earlier, non-adjacent one. The dedup handles only adjacent keys (src/ingestion/mod.rs:140-154), so finalize fails with 'Invariant 2 Violation' (src/ingestion/builder.rs:49-56). The server collects .js files from everywhere except a few directory names (src/adapters/server.rs:764-866), for example a committed javadoc jquery-*.min.js. src/ast/reducer.rs:56 saturates the column instead of wrapping it. Sources are parsed as raw bytes with no BOM or charset handling. Identifier checks need an ASCII first byte (pass1_discovery.rs:687,714,766,803), and class_diagram.rs:98-101 rejects non-ASCII and '$' names.
impact: One minified or generated file aborts the server's analysis of a whole repository. Unicode identifiers (legal in Java, Kotlin, Python, JS, Rust and Swift) and '$' names disappear. Columns are UTF-8 bytes, not the UTF-16 units editors use.
recommendation: Anchor tokens on u32 byte offsets and derive line/col lazily from a line index. If the packed key stays, widen columns to u32 and break ties globally by token_id. Skip and report minified or generated files using linguist-style rules (line length, .min.js, generated-file headers). Transcode non-UTF-8 input (BOM sniffing, encoding_rs), use Unicode XID rules (unicode-ident crate) for identifiers, and expose UTF-16 columns to the web studio and LSP clients.

title: Advertised language support is not backed by code
evidence: README.md:60 claims F1 = 1.0000 'across Java, Kotlin, Python, Rust, TypeScript, and C++'. src/adapters/server.rs:84 advertises python/typescript/javascript/cpp/rust/go, but not kotlin. CHANGELOG.md:32 claims multi-language support 'across all 10 compilation pipeline phases without hardcoded dependencies'. ROADMAP.md:27 ticks multi-language support while :127 leaves the C++/Rust/Go adapters open. docs/codebase-guide.md:86 cites Java/Kotlin/Rust stubs, but only java_stubs.rs exists. src/main.rs:41 says .java while :79-93 also accepts .kt/.kts. The paper (docs/openheart_research_paper.tex:735-741, 1326-1330) claims scope graphs and stubs at language boundaries. The Pages studio's 'AST parsing' (README.md:57) is a regex that requires '{' (web/js/github-engine.js:291) and invents classes from file names (:383-397). docs/overview.md:102-113 lists no Python, TS or C++ repository.
impact: Users and reviewers are misled about what the engine can analyze. Benchmark-grade status needs a truthful statement of support derived from tests.
recommendation: Publish a per-language capability matrix generated from conformance tests. Rows are languages; columns are parse, symbols, imports, CFG, SSA, call graph and each diagram. Use tiers: Tier 1 (full pipeline), Tier 2 (outline via tree-sitter tags.scm), unsupported. Serve /api/supported-languages from the registry. Withdraw the F1 claim until an independent benchmark exists, and label the web studio's regex mode in the UI.

DOCS.note: README, CHANGELOG, ROADMAP, codebase-guide (Java-only stubs), overview and paper corrected; capability matrix added; server endpoint, CLI help and studio label handed off

title: The multi-language F1 benchmark is circular, name-only and not run in CI
evidence: ruthless_verify.py builds its ground truth from regexes in ruthless_config.json. The '.rs' rule, for example, is 'struct|enum|trait' followed by a name, which is the same keyword-then-identifier heuristic as the engine's sweep (src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:249-288). compute_metrics (ruthless_verify.py:247-270) compares sets of class names parsed from the PUML (:225-234). Phantoms that share a real name, members, relations and packages (printed but outside the pass rule at :435) are never scored. The harness needs a live server and ./target_repos, and CI runs only cargo test (.github/workflows/ci.yml:47). All 16 tests/*.rs files write .java fixtures only (e.g. tests/pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:27-28); no test exercises the Kotlin or generic adapters.
impact: F1 = 1.0000 cannot be falsified for non-Java languages and cannot detect the defects in LANG-02, LANG-03 and LANG-06. Regressions in any language ship unnoticed.
recommendation: Use independent oracles for each language: SCIP indexers (scip-java including Kotlin, scip-python, scip-typescript) or compilers (javac -Xprint, kotlinc, Python ast, the TypeScript compiler API). Score symbols, members, supertypes, associations, packages and call edges separately with precision and recall. Pin a multi-language corpus (e.g. XCorpus or Qualitas for Java plus popular Kotlin/Python/TS repos at fixed commits) and gate CI on it with snapshot tests (insta).

title: No language-neutral IR: a Java-shaped AST with no node roles is the contract for every phase
evidence: ASTNodeType (src/core/types/ast.rs:6-68) is about 52 Java constructs (NN_INSTANCEOF_EXPR, NN_METHOD_REF, NN_RECORD_DECL). It has no kinds for imports or namespaces, free functions, decorators, with/defer, match arms, await or comprehensions. The 'Language Specific (Java Extensions)' range 0x80-0x84 (:62-67) is not namespaced, and nodes store no language id (src/ast/builder.rs:147-161). Tree-sitter field roles are discarded, so CFG lowering guesses each child's role from the number of children (src/cfg/stmts/for_stmt.rs:117-127). For Java `for (; i < n; )`, the condition is taken as the initializer and no exit edge is added (:167-169). unpack_operator_id returns Assign for every operator (src/core/types/ast.rs:224-232).
impact: Every language has to pretend to be Java. Constructs with no Java equivalent are dropped or lowered wrongly, and guessing roles by position breaks even Java. This is the root cause of LANG-01 through LANG-06.
recommendation: Add a Unified IR between the parse tree and Phase 3. It needs a closed core set of node kinds (Module, TypeDecl{class|interface|trait|struct|enum|record|object}, Function{method|ctor|async|generator}, Loop{kind}, Match, Try, With, Call{dispatch}, Alloc, Member, Name, Import). Each node carries a role byte (cond, then, else, init, update, body, callee, receiver, arg, name, type, super), a full operator id and a (lang, kind) extension pair, plus a file-to-language table. Lower per language as Joern's x2cpg frontends and Semgrep's AST_generic-to-IL do. Share CFG/SSA/dataflow code across languages through a language signature, as CodeQL's shared libraries do. Migration: .bpa v2 with roles, lower Java first and switch CFG/SSA to roles; then add Kotlin/Python/TS frontends; finally delete the token heuristics.

title: The adapter and registry design forces 25+ file edits per new language
evidence: Two language-id registries disagree: src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:19-42 has Kotlin, while src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:16-31 has TS/Rust/Generic. `ext_map` is written but never read (registry.rs:46-48); detect() is a separate hardcoded match (:59-83). File selection differs yet again in src/main.rs:79-93, src/adapters/server.rs:790-881 (which drops '*test' stems such as Latest.java and any /spec package), web/js/github-engine.js:89 and ruthless_config.json. Each file is parsed twice, and Phase 2 re-reads it from disk without checking the stored SHA-256 (src/ast/mod.rs:142). PatternDetectionChain and SCPGPipelineBuilder are used only by tests, and the pipeline is copied by hand (main.rs:150-255, server.rs:526-620). tree-sitter is pinned to 0.20 (Cargo.toml:8).
impact: Adding Python today touches 25+ files across all ten phases: Cargo.toml, both registries, the core type enums, the symbol adapter, stubs and passes 1-5, cfg/stmts, ssa/liveness, cg, uma, four exporters, main.rs, server.rs, the tests, the verifier and the web engine.
recommendation: Make one LanguageFrontend trait and registry the single source of truth. It defines: id; dialects (ts/tsx, kts); extensions plus shebang or linguist-style detection; grammar; token classifier; lowering to the IR; LanguageSemantics; name-binding rules (TSG); and stub data. Parse each file once and hand the tree to Phase 2. Drive the CLI, the server, /api/supported-languages and the verifier from the registry, and run every entry point through SCPGPipelineBuilder. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25 (LanguageFn). Done = adding a language means one module plus fixtures.

ENG.note: The unified LanguageFrontend registry is src work.

title: Design-pattern detection and exporters rely on Java and Spring naming habits
evidence: A Singleton is a class with a field named 'instance' or 'getinstance' (src/uma/patterns/singleton.rs:20-28). A private constructor is found by matching '<init>' (query.rs:86). A Composite is a class with a field name ending in 's' (query.rs:112). A Factory is a name containing 'factory' (factory.rs:17), an Observer has add*/register*Listener methods (observer.rs:25-29), and a Builder has the 'Builder' suffix (builder.rs:33). Use-case actors are classes ending in Controller, Service, App, Main or Facade, copied in json.rs:1246, mermaid.rs:1075, plantuml.rs:897 and visitor.rs:253. Three different Java primitive-type lists exist (src/scpg/diagram/common.rs:59, mermaid.rs:542, plantuml.rs:229). A missing return type prints 'void' (json.rs:237), and Kotlin `object` becomes a plain SK_CLASS (pass1_discovery.rs:278).
impact: Patterns are inferred from names rather than structure. Non-Java idioms (Kotlin object, Python __new__, Rust OnceLock) are missed, and ordinary classes that happen to follow the naming convention are flagged as patterns. Diagrams print Java conventions for other languages.
recommendation: Detect patterns from language-neutral structural facts: a static field of the class's own type, a non-public constructor, an accessor returning the class's own type, delegation through the call graph. Add per-language idiom providers (Kotlin object/companion, Python __new__, Rust static OnceLock). Put type and visibility rendering in one formatter that knows each language's semantics. Route uma/mod.rs:70 through PatternDetectionChain so rules are pluggable, and score against P-MARt or DPB ground truth.

title: No polyglot model: Java-Kotlin interop and language boundaries are not represented
evidence: Android and other JVM repos mix Java and Kotlin in one module, yet SymbolRecord has no language, binary name or JVM descriptor (src/core/types/symbol.rs:96-117). Kotlin file facades (FooKt), @JvmName/@JvmStatic, and the mapping from properties to getters (`user.getName()` calls Kotlin `name`) are not modelled. Call targets are matched by token position (src/cg/resolution.rs:178-239). Java `native` is never recorded (src/ast/adapter/java.rs:149-157 sets only static, final and abstract), so the JNI boundary stubs the paper promises (docs/openheart_research_paper.tex:1326-1330) cannot exist.
impact: In mixed JVM projects, the most common real polyglot case, cross-language calls and type uses are lost or bound only through coincidental simple names.
recommendation: Model the JVM languages in one namespace keyed by binary names and descriptors, as CodeQL does (its Kotlin extractor writes into the Java database schema) and Joern does (kotlin2cpg emits the same CPG as javasrc2cpg). Synthesize Kotlin facade classes and accessor aliases. Add explicit boundary nodes for JNI native, Kotlin external, FFI/ctypes and gRPC/OpenAPI stubs. Done = a mixed Java/Kotlin fixture with call and type edges in both directions.

DOCS.note: Paper multi-language paragraph rewritten (boundary nodes, JVM namespace, impl lacks native/binary names); ROADMAP polyglot item; code handed off

title: The token types are Java-centric and doc comments are never classified
evidence: No adapter emits TokenType::CommentDoc. Java maps block_comment and comment to CommentBlock (src/ingestion/adapter/java.rs:46-48), and the generic adapter maps comment to CommentLine (src/ingestion/adapter/generic.rs:46). The default TokenFilter keeps doc comments but drops block comments (src/core/types/source.rs:31-40), so Javadoc, KDoc and JSDoc never reach the corpus. The 'language-specific' TokenType range holds only Java variants (src/core/types/token.rs:64-68), two of which are never produced. The Java keyword list (java.rs:60-66) lacks sealed, permits and non-sealed, so include_anonymous (:75-77) drops them. The generic adapter maps any alphabetic kind, such as string_fragment, to Keyword (generic.rs:53-54).
impact: UML notes drawn from documentation and doc-aware queries are impossible. New language-specific tokens would collide in the 0x80 range, which is not split by language.
recommendation: Classify doc comments per language in the frontend (/**, ///, //!, Python docstring nodes). Key token extensions by (language, kind). Generate token maps from each grammar's node-types.json and fail CI on unmapped leaf kinds.

title: Unsound unsafe in BDDLibrary: reads through a stale slice after Vec reallocation (use-after-free)
evidence: BDDLibrary::apply, apply_not and restrict (mod.rs:84-86, 100-102, 120-122) build `read = slice::from_raw_parts(self.nodes.as_ptr(), len)` and also pass `&mut self.nodes`, into which make_node pushes (unique_table.rs:65). A push at capacity reallocates and frees the buffer that `read` points to. After that, apply.rs:104 recurses and reads `nodes[..]`, apply.rs:138-139 reads fn_.hi and fn_.var after a recursive call, and restrict.rs:68 reads fn_.var after recursion. The SAFETY comment ('never reallocates ... pre-cleared the cache') is false. A model of the code using Rust's Vec growth policy counts 6 stale reads for one if/else and 110 for eight.
impact: Undefined behaviour on almost every function with a branch. Depending on allocator reuse, results range from nondeterministic ROBDDs and path counts to out-of-bounds panics in restrict or heap corruption. Dev builds can also panic in the canonicity check (construction/mod.rs:126-133).
recommendation: Remove the unsafe. ROBDDNode is Copy, so pass only `&mut Vec<ROBDDNode>` and copy each node by value before recursing (`let n = nodes[f as usize];`), or move to an established BDD crate (biodivine-lib-bdd, oxidd) that has node limits. Add a Miri CI job (`cargo +nightly miri test psa::bdd`): the existing canonicity_after_construction test already reallocates mid-apply. Add #![deny(unsafe_code)] everywhere except core/io/mmap.rs. Done when psa has no unsafe and Miri is clean.

title: Server reads arbitrary files and analyzes arbitrary directories named in requests (no confinement, wildcard CORS, 0.0.0.0)
evidence: The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32) and sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (306, 327). /api/source tries the raw `file`/`path` query value first (96-121, 200-205): `?file=/etc/passwd` or `?file=C:/Users/u/.ssh/id_rsa` returns the file, and `?file=/dev/zero` makes read_to_string grow until OOM. In /api/analyze, a repo_url ending in `/..` analyzes the server's working directory (393-399), and `a/./../../../../home/u/proj` reaches any directory through parts[2..] (407-414). The URL goes to git clone unvalidated and without `--` (429-437), and a failed clone silently analyzes another user's repository instead (467-482). validate_url (web_repo.rs:97-119) is never called, and it panics itself on `https://github.com/owner`.
impact: Any host on the LAN, or any web page a developer opens (because of the wildcard CORS), can read arbitrary files, exhaust the server's memory, turn arbitrary directories into diagrams, and receive another user's repository results.
recommendation: Serve /api/source only from an allow-listed root, using canonicalize() plus starts_with() as the static route already does (254-272). Accept regular files only (check symlink_metadata) and cap read size (File::take). Bind 127.0.0.1 by default, drop the wildcard CORS and require a token. Parse repo_url with the url crate and accept only https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>. Name each checkout by a hash, pass `--` and `-c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always` to git, and never fall back to another repository.

title: Exponential path enumeration in compute_max_path_length makes Phase 8 hang on common methods
evidence: compute_max_path_length (psa/construction/mod.rs:153-173) is a DFS with no visited set and no memo. It pushes every successor with depth+1 until depth >= block count, so it enumerates every path, and build() calls it for every function (line 116). k sequential `if (c) x++;` statements give 2^k paths, because if_stmt.rs:30-72 builds cond->then->join plus cond->join. A port of the loop counts 5.2M stack pops at k=20 and about 5.5e12 at k=40. Protobuf-generated mergeFrom/writeTo methods, with one `if (hasX())` per field, hit this routinely, and so do loops whose bodies branch.
impact: Phase 8 does not terminate on ordinary large methods. The CLI hangs, and a single POST to the single-threaded server stops it from serving anyone.
recommendation: Compute the longest acyclic path in O(B+E): remove back edges (analyze_loops already finds them), order the resulting DAG topologically and relax each edge once; report loops through unwind_depth. Give every per-function analysis a step budget, in the style of CUDD's node and time limits, that degrades to 'unknown' with a diagnostic. Add regression tests: 64 sequential ifs, and a loop with 10 inner branches, must each finish in under 100 ms.

title: Server turns every panic, abort or hang into a remote outage (single-threaded inline pipeline)
evidence: start() runs handle_connection inline on the main thread (server.rs:40-42). There are no workers and no catch_unwind anywhere in src/. Sockets get a 500 ms read timeout but no write timeout (47). /api/analyze clones the repository and runs all ten phases synchronously, with no time or memory limit (241-253, 366-762). Consequences: a panic (ROB-05), a stack-overflow abort (ROB-08) or a hang (ROB-03) kills or wedges the service; each idle socket stalls it for 500 ms; a client that never reads blocks write_all forever. run.sh:34 serves the dev profile, where the debug_assert at token.rs:122 panics on a 16 MB file of newlines. Dockerfile:49 runs `serve`, which main.rs:544 rejects, so the container exits immediately.
impact: Every robustness defect in the analysis code becomes an unauthenticated one-request kill or hang of the default deployment, and any legitimate large analysis blocks all other users.
recommendation: Run each analysis as a job in a child process, or at minimum on a worker thread with catch_unwind and a 256 MB stack, under wall-clock and RSS limits (setrlimit, or Job Objects on Windows), with a bounded queue that returns 503 when full. Replace the hand-rolled loop with hyper/axum plus tower (TimeoutLayer, RequestBodyLimitLayer, ConcurrencyLimitLayer) and set socket write timeouts. Change the Docker CMD to `server 8080` and smoke-test the image in CI. Done when the ROB-03 and ROB-05 repros return an error and the server keeps serving.

title: Byte-index slicing in LabelExtractor panics on non-ASCII text, and labels come from the wrong token
evidence: extract_label truncates with `&label_text[..max_chars.saturating_sub(3)]` (label_extraction.rs:33-35). activity_diagram.rs:89 passes 30, so byte 27 must fall on a char boundary. The text is token_records[bpa.node_attr(stmt)] (line 23), but node_attr is the packed visibility/modifier/operator word (java.rs:177, ast.rs:209-213), which is 0 for expression and return statements. As a result, nearly every block label is token 0 of the whole corpus. If token 0 is at least 28 bytes with a multi-byte char spanning byte 27, Phase 9 panics with 'byte index 27 is not a char boundary'. Examples: the first file starts with an identifier of 16 'ç' characters, or with Cyrillic or CJK text.
impact: A deterministic Phase 9 panic. It is rare in Java-only CLI runs (token 0 is usually `package`), plausible for non-English Python/JS files ingested by the server, and trivially crafted: a one-file repository sent to /api/analyze kills the server. Every activity label is also wrong.
recommendation: Truncate on char boundaries (`s.char_indices().nth(n)`, str::floor_char_boundary once stable, or unicode-segmentation for graphemes), and ban raw string slicing with clippy::string_slice. Derive labels from bpa.token_range(stmt).0 instead of node_attr. Add proptest and fuzz corpora with Unicode identifiers (legal in both Java and Kotlin) and CJK or emoji literals.

title: 16-bit column in sort keys: one line longer than 64 KB aborts the whole repository run
evidence: walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps. build_sort_key packs file (u16), line (u24) and col (u16) into one key (token.rs:121-124), and the duplicate counter only separates consecutive equal keys (ingestion/mod.rs:140-155). Two tokens on one line at columns c and c+65,536 therefore get the same key, and finalize returns 'Invariant 2 Violation (Injectivity)' (builder.rs:49-55). A port of this logic finds 2,232 duplicate keys in a single 70 KB line. The server also ingests .js files (server.rs:816), so a committed jquery.min.js under src/main/resources/static fails the analysis, and long generated Java/Kotlin lines do the same. reducer.rs:56 clamps the column instead of wrapping it, so Phase 2 lookups disagree with Phase 1.
impact: A single minified or generated file makes the entire run fail with no partial output. A file with more than 16,777,215 lines (line & 0xFFFFFF) has the same effect.
recommendation: Identify tokens by (file_id u32, byte_offset) or by a per-file ordinal, and keep line and column in separate u32 tables, as tree-sitter's Point does. If packing stays, saturate and flag instead of wrapping. Turn the injectivity check into a per-file diagnostic that skips the offending file rather than failing the run. Add boundary tests: a 70 KB line, a 16.8M-line file, and minified JS.

title: Packed u8/u16 fields silently truncate at realistic sizes, corrupting SSA, PSA, traceability and UMA data
evidence: With overflow checks off, narrowing casts wrap silently. SSARecord.def_block is a u8 (core/types/ssa.rs:25,43), so block numbers of 256 and above alias. feasibility.rs:115-119 then matches on `block_id & 0xFF`, and ssa_bi.rs:17-35 builds global block offsets from the truncated maxima, which shifts every later function. Span lines are cast `as u16` (sym_span.rs:38-40, cs_span.rs:32), and so is file_id (ingestion/mod.rs:70,123). PSA maps edges beyond 65,535 to var 0 (psa/ordering/mod.rs:40-55), and its condition variables are ssa_id&0x3FFF, which collide with edge variables (feasibility.rs:122). SCC sizes, UMA counts and token lengths are also cast `as u16` (cg/scc.rs:38, uma/serializer.rs:39-40, walker.rs:54, interner.rs:99).
impact: SSA, path-count, traceability and UML data come out wrong, with no error, for methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines and repositories over 65,535 files. Those are exactly the inputs a benchmark contains.
recommendation: Widen on-disk fields to u32 (or LEB128 varints) behind a format-version bump. Replace every narrowing `as` with u16::try_from mapped to a typed error, or to an explicit saturate-and-diagnose. Deny clippy::cast_possible_truncation. Give BDD condition variables their own index space. Add CI boundary tests: a 257-block method, a 65,536-line file, 65,536 synthetic files and a 70 KB token.

title: Unbounded native recursion on input-controlled depth causes stack-overflow aborts that cannot be caught
evidence: Recursion depth follows the input in at least eleven places with no limit: CST walks (walker.rs:32-77, reducer.rs:8-93), statement nesting including else-if chains (cfg/stmts/mod.rs:28-65), expression trees (liveness.rs:124-169), block-graph DFS (rpo.rs:7-17, loops.rs:29-46, postdom.rs:24-33, cdg.rs:37-48), dominator-tree renaming (renaming.rs:103-211), Tarjan over the call graph (cg/scc.rs:63-105), and BDD apply (depth equals n_vars). classify() receives the current depth but ignores it (java.rs:26). A left-associative concatenation of N literals has CST depth of about N. Everything runs on the main thread, which has a 1 MiB stack with MSVC on Windows and 8 MiB on Linux.
impact: Generated code with thousands of concatenated literals, long else-if chains, huge straight-line methods or deep call chains aborts the CLI or the server. On Windows a few thousand levels likely suffice (frame sizes are estimates).
recommendation: Make tree walks iterative using TreeCursor (goto_first_child, goto_next_sibling, goto_parent) or explicit stacks. Use iterative Tarjan (Pearce 2016) and iterative DFS for RPO and SSA renaming. Wrap any remaining recursion in stacker::maybe_grow, as rustc's ensure_sufficient_stack does. Run the pipeline on a thread with an explicit large stack, and enforce a nesting limit that emits a diagnostic. Add tests with 100,000-level nesting to CI on both Windows and Linux.

title: select1 returns the root when a superblock has no 1-bits, corrupting AST navigation on long else-if chains
evidence: select1 (rank_select.rs:86-108) binary-searches the cumulative superblocks array for target_rank and starts scanning at idx-1. When a 512-bit superblock holds only close parens (512 or more consecutive closes, such as the tail of a long else-if chain), adjacent entries are equal. Rust's binary_search then returns the last equal index, the scan starts after the target, and the function returns 0. A port of build/select1 run on an else-if model produces a wrong answer from about 400 branches, depending on alignment. first_child() (builder.rs:58-66) then reports node 1 as a child of that leaf, so walkers such as extract_stmt_vars (liveness.rs:162-169) can re-enter the root subtree without bound.
impact: Generated dispatch code gets wrong first_child, next_sibling, depth and LCA answers, and therefore wrong CFG and SSA facts. In the plausible worst case the recursion is unbounded and ends in a stack-overflow abort.
recommendation: Choose the superblock with `superblocks.partition_point(|&c| c < target) - 1`, or adopt a tested implementation (sucds, vers-vecs, or rank9/select9 from Vigna 2008). Add proptest checks that compare rank1, select1, first_child and next_sibling against a naive pointer tree, on random BP strings and on adversarial long runs of opens and closes.

title: Source discovery follows symlinks with no cycle, file-type or root checks, and one bad file aborts the run
evidence: collect_source_files (main.rs:84-96), collect_files (server.rs:764-804) and walkdir_find (server.rs:342-361) recurse whenever Path::is_dir() is true, and is_dir() follows symlinks. None of them keeps a visited set, caps depth or confines paths to the repository root. A cloned repo containing `a -> .` and `b -> .` makes traversal exponential. `Big.java -> /dev/zero` passes the extension filter, and fs::read (ingestion/mod.rs:53) reads until memory runs out. `x -> /` ingests the host filesystem. Per-file failures are fatal: a dangling symlink fails fs::metadata (ingestion/mod.rs:51-52), and the CLI's `?` (main.rs:85-86) turns one ENAMETOOLONG from a self-link into 'Failed to scan directory'.
impact: Malicious repositories, and merely messy ones (dangling links are common), hang the run, exhaust memory or abort the whole analysis. The server can also be steered into reading outside the clone.
recommendation: Use the ignore crate (ripgrep's walker) with follow_links(false), same_file_system(true), max_depth and .gitignore support. Accept only entries where symlink_metadata() reports a regular file and the canonicalized path lies under the repository root. Cap per-file size (configurable, e.g. 8 MiB) with File::take. Record per-file errors as diagnostics and continue, as ruff and rust-analyzer do.

title: Artifact readers trust header counts and offsets, and inspect reports integrity it never checks
evidence: The readers check a CRC-64, which any attacker can recompute. After that they index `buf[offset..offset+4]` without checking how many bytes remain: TRA (tra/serializer.rs:174-280), PSA (psa/serializer.rs:201-245, including `pos = metrics_offset` taken from the file), UMA (uma/serializer.rs:272 onward) and BPA (ast/serializer.rs:118-171). Short files therefore panic. Counts from u32 headers go straight into Vec::with_capacity (symbol/serializer.rs:240, cg/serializer.rs:158, ingestion/serializer.rs:254,296), so large counts abort on a multi-GiB allocation. scpg/mmap/mod.rs:52-62 reads section_count entries unchecked, and get_section computes `start + byte_length` (86-90), which can wrap. inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa files without checking anything (main.rs:373-389).
impact: `openheart inspect`, the documented validation tool, panics or aborts on small crafted files and claims integrity it never verified. Library users who load artifacts inherit the same crashes.
recommendation: Parse through one bounds-checked cursor: a Reader that returns Err on short reads, or zerocopy, binrw or scroll. Check `count <= remaining / record_size` before allocating, and use try_reserve and checked_add for offsets. Make inspect verify the CRC for every artifact type and report the real error. Add cargo-fuzz targets for each format, seeded with real artifacts. Done when 24 hours of libFuzzer finds no crash.

title: No work or memory budgets, and several phases scale super-linearly on realistic large inputs
evidence: Nothing bounds per-function or per-run work. Switch constraints perform k(k-1)/2 BDD applies (constraints.rs:122-127), each of which clears the apply cache (bdd/mod.rs:78). edge_index_of is a linear scan on every lookup (rpo.rs:106-108). The CFG CSR build is O(blocks x edges) (cfg/builder/mod.rs:150-172). close_node walks every ancestor (ast/builder.rs:163-175). CHA rescans every symbol per call site (cg/resolution.rs:84). The RMQ stores n(log n+1) u32 values (rmq.rs:28-48), about 0.9 GB for 10M BP bits. Each source is read three times and parsed twice, with no size cap or tree-sitter timeout (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; tree_sitter.rs:17-24). OPENHEART_MAX_MEMORY_MB in .env.example is never read.
impact: Giant switches in JavaCC- or ANTLR-generated code, deep nesting and 1M-LOC repositories make phases quadratic or memory-bound. That is a DoS on the server and contradicts the 128x compression claim.
recommendation: Index edges with a HashMap<(u32,u32),usize> or CSR offsets, and build the CSR by counting sort. Encode exactly-one constraints with a linear sequential counter, and keep a persistent computed table with a per-function node budget (CUDD style). Precompute subtype closures for CHA. Replace the sparse table with a range min-max tree (Navarro-Sadakane) or a block-decomposed RMQ using O(n) bits. Parse each file once, and implement the documented memory limits plus Parser::set_timeout_micros.

title: Phase 2 re-reads sources by a lossy path and silently drops files it cannot re-read or re-parse
evidence: Phase 2 does not reuse Phase 1's bytes or parse trees. It decodes paths from the .tca (ast/mod.rs:85-99), then re-reads and re-parses each file inside nested `if let Ok` blocks that have no else branch and no log (141-153). Phase 1 stored the paths with to_string_lossy (ingestion/serializer.rs:94, ingestion/mod.rs:137), so a Latin-1 file name becomes U+FFFD and the re-read fails silently. A file edited between phases is parsed from different bytes than it was tokenized from, and tok_table_lookup (reducer.rs:95-117) then binds nodes to the nearest token on the same line. Phase 1 itself hashes one read (mod.rs:53) and tokenizes a second one (mod.rs:111).
impact: Files silently disappear from the AST, CFG and UML output while their tokens remain, and token ranges can point at the wrong tokens. Nothing tells the user or a benchmark harness.
recommendation: Read each file once into an immutable snapshot (bytes plus content hash) shared by all phases, and reuse the Phase 1 tree or store byte offsets in the .tca. Carry paths as OsString or raw bytes (OsStrExt, os_str_bytes) instead of lossy strings. Emit a per-file diagnostics list in every artifact and API response.

title: Error model is panic or abort-the-run: I/O panics, release-mode asserts, and per-unit failures that fail everything
evidence: Phases 7-10 return artifacts rather than Result, and they panic on I/O failure (tra/mod.rs:42-43, psa/mod.rs:153-154, uma/mod.rs:97-98, and an expect at scpg/mod.rs:53-55). Invariants are enforced with release-mode assert!/assert_eq! (tra/builder.rs:66-131, ast/builder.rs:180-207, jump_table.rs:23-29). In the other direction, one function that fails a CFG or SSA invariant aborts the whole run through `?` (cfg/mod.rs:84, ssa/mod.rs:81), and so does one unreadable file (ingestion/mod.rs:51-54). Locks are taken with lock().unwrap() (logger.rs:82,145; ingestion/mod.rs:136,174).
impact: A full disk or a read-only output directory crashes the CLI with a backtrace and kills the server. One unusual function or file throws away the results for the entire repository.
recommendation: Thread one thiserror enum (already a dependency) through every Phase*Stage::run. Turn per-function and per-file invariant failures into a diagnostic plus a skipped unit, optionally wrapped in catch_unwind per unit, and keep the partial artifacts. Reserve assert! for genuinely impossible states. Enforce clippy deny(unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, indexing_slicing) on non-test code in CI.

title: Overflow checks are disabled in every profile, and there is no fuzzing, Miri or sanitizer coverage
evidence: Cargo.toml:21-23 sets `overflow-checks = false` for the dev profile, and release has them off by default. So neither the tests nor the `cargo run` deployment ever detect the wraps listed above. CI runs only check, fmt and test (ci.yml:41-47), with no clippy, Miri, sanitizers or fuzzing. There is no fuzz/ directory, and the tests use fixed small corpora; adversarial_trick_tests.rs is a single pattern set. By contrast, tree-sitter is fuzzed continuously in OSS-Fuzz, rust-analyzer ships cargo-fuzz parser targets and a parser step limit, and ruff runs libFuzzer targets on its parser and formatter.
impact: Miri, overflow-checked tests and fuzzing would find the use-after-free, panics and truncations in this report within hours. Without them these bugs will keep coming back.
recommendation: Remove the override and add a release-checked profile (overflow-checks = true) for CI. Add cargo-fuzz targets for three entry points: arbitrary bytes as .java/.kt through the in-process pipeline with a time limit, each artifact reader, and the HTTP handler. Run them nightly with a cached corpus. Add a Miri job for psa::bdd, proptest for rank/select and the BDD algebra, and generators for boundary sizes (64K files, lines and columns).

title: Hand-rolled server JSON breaks on error text and control characters, and session temp directories leak
evidence: Error responses splice messages into JSON without escaping (server.rs:529-533, 543, 550-553, 601). Ingestion errors embed `{:?}`-formatted paths that contain quotes and backslashes (ingestion/mod.rs:52,54), and lines 496-502 insert target_dir.display(), derived from the attacker-chosen repo name, unescaped. escape_json_str (701-707) handles only backslash, double quote, newline, carriage return and tab, so any other control character in a file name corrupts success responses too. The early returns at 527-605 skip remove_dir_all (693), leaking one openheart_sess_* directory per failed request.
impact: Clients get JSON parse errors instead of diagnostics, and repeated failing requests gradually fill the temp volume.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json::json! (already a dependency) and a typed error body. Hold the session directory in a tempfile::TempDir (move tempfile out of dev-dependencies) so that every exit path cleans up, and cap total temp usage per job.

title: Phase 8 longest-path DFS enumerates every CFG path: exponential hang on ordinary methods
evidence: psa/construction/mod.rs:153-173 compute_max_path_length pops (block, depth) and pushes every successor with depth+1 (line 168), with no visited or memo set. The only cut is depth >= bound, where bound = block count (158), and acyclic paths never reach it. It runs for every function (mod.rs:116, via psa/mod.rs:129). A Python model of if_stmt.rs block shapes (scratchpad lens/scale_model.py) costs exactly 4·2^k pops for k sequential ifs: k=22 gives 16.8M pops and k=40 gives 4.4·10^12. Loops turn it into walk enumeration up to length n.
impact: Any method with roughly 35+ independent branches (serializers, toXContent, validators) never finishes Phase 8, so the CLI run and the server request hang. Remotely triggerable through POST /api/analyze.
recommendation: Replace the DFS with DAG dynamic programming. Drop the back edges already found by analyze_loops, iterate blocks in RPO, and compute len[v] = 1 + max(len[p]) in O(B+E). Count paths the same way (cnt[v] = Σcnt[p], saturating or log2/BigUint) instead of relying on #SAT for metrics. Add a 64-sequential-if regression test with a 1 s budget, and a per-function work budget for any remaining enumeration.

title: Phase 6 scans the whole symbol table per call site and per AST ancestor: O(C·S·depth)
evidence: For each call node (cg/call_sites.rs:23-64), find_enclosing_method scans all sta.symbol_records at every ancestor (70-90; loop at 73). classify_call→resolve_method_target runs up to three full scans (resolution.rs:185, 212, 225). extract_receiver_ssa scans every SSA record of every function (call_sites.rs:129-140), and find_block_for_stmt does a linear function find plus stmts.contains (143-145). Resolution repeats resolve_method_target, and resolve_cha rescans all symbols and all TH edges per visited subtype (resolution.rs:84, 95). The 1-CFA fallback rescans all SSA records (152).
impact: At 1M LOC, ~1.2M call sites × ~1.1M 64-byte symbols × ~10 scans is ~10^13 record visits: hours to days single-threaded. CHA from heavily-subclassed bases multiplies the cost further.
recommendation: Build the indexes once in O(N): enclosing_fn[pre_idx] in a preorder sweep (as Pass 1's sym_id_by_node does), def_stmt→ssa_id and stmt→block maps, a dispatch index HashMap<(type, name_id, arity), SmallVec<method>>, and a subtype CSR. CHA/RTA per site then costs O(|subtypes|) with memoized (type, selector) results, as in the OPAL and SootUp call-graph builders (seconds at rt.jar scale). Then parallelize site resolution with rayon.

title: Sequence extraction rebuilds a map of all call edges per entry point and scans all call sites per visited method
evidence: uma/behavioral/sequence_diagram.rs:23-27 runs extract_for_entry for every entry point, meaning every public or package method with zero fan-in (actor_identification.rs:12-41). Each call rebuilds site_edges from the whole cga.site_to_edge_map (87-93). For every method popped in the DFS it iterates all cga.call_sites (109-110), although the sites are already sorted by caller (call_sites.rs:66). The DFS (99-151) has no depth or message cap and follows the full transitive closure, then truncates message_count to u16 (158).
impact: O(EP·|E| + EP·R·C): tens of thousands of entry points × millions of edges is ~10^11 operations before any DFS work. Once call resolution is fixed, closure-sized message lists per entry point risk OOM.
recommendation: Build a caller→sites CSR once (a binary-search slice over the sorted call_sites). Use BFS with a depth bound of 3–5 and a message cap, and memoize per-method callee summaries. Generate sequences lazily for the entry points a user requests instead of for all of them, and store counts as u32. Expected cost: O(Σ capped messages).

title: Phase 3 resolves most type references with a full symbol-table scan (O(R·S)), plus other quadratic loops
evidence: pass3_types.rs:108-120 get_or_create_external linearly scans builder.symbols for an existing SK_EXTERNAL. Externals sit after all Pass 1 symbols, so every lookup walks the full table. It runs for every reference not found lexically (75, 88), which includes all cross-file types, because NN_MODULE is a declaration and each file's classes live in their own module scope (symbol/adapter/java.rs:35). Other quadratic spots: pass1_discovery.rs:373 position() per class-keyword token; builder.rs:120 add_th_edge linear dedup, called per field (pass5_hierarchy.rs:182); resolver.rs:20-21 per-scope scans with a string re-compare (pass3_types.rs:56-58).
impact: About 1M lookups × 1.1M records ≈ 10^12 visits at 1M LOC, roughly 20 minutes to 2 hours for one pass. TH-edge deduplication adds O(E²).
recommendation: Keep a HashMap<qual_name_id, sym_id> for externals, a HashMap<(package, name_id), sym_id> for top-level types (which also handles same-package resolution), a per-scope HashMap<name_id, SmallVec<sym_id>> (interned ids make string compares unnecessary), and a HashSet<(from, to, rel)> for TH edges. Model it on rust-analyzer's per-file ItemTree plus DefMap, or on javac's Symtab. Expected cost: O(R+S).

title: Unbounded recursion on the 1 MB main thread: deep CST, CFG, dominator, BDD or call-graph inputs abort the process
evidence: Recursion depth grows with the input in: ingestion/walker.rs:32-71 and ast/reducer.rs:8-68 (CST depth; long + chains and else-if chains nest one level per term); cfg/stmts/if_stmt.rs:34,49; rpo.rs:7, loops.rs:29, postdom.rs:24 and ssa/cdg.rs:37 (DFS depth ≈ block count); ssa/renaming.rs:103-192 (dominator-tree depth, 12-argument frames); liveness.rs:165; bdd/apply.rs:103-104,137-138 and sat_count.rs:79 (≈ variable count); cg/scc.rs:63-85 (Tarjan). Everything runs on the main thread (main.rs, server.rs:40-41), whose default stack is 1 MB on Windows/MSVC and 8 MB on Linux.
impact: A stack overflow aborts the process rather than panicking. The CLI or the HTTP server dies on one deep generated file (JFlex/ANTLR output, huge initializers) with no partial output, and an attacker can kill the server through /api/analyze.
recommendation: Convert these routines to explicit-stack iteration: TreeCursor goto_first_child/goto_next_sibling/goto_parent loops, (node, child_idx) DFS frames, Pearce's iterative SCC (petgraph::algo::tarjan_scc), and an iterative apply with an ITE cache. As a stopgap, run the pipeline on std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(512<<20). Add stress tests: a 100K-term concatenation, a 20K-branch else-if chain and a 50K-block method.

title: Fixed-width ids overflow at scale: u16 file ids, u8 block ids, u16 counts
evidence: ingestion/mod.rs:70,123 cast file_id with `as u16`, and token.rs:121 packs 16-bit file ids into sort keys. File 65,536 wraps onto file 0, and the key collisions trip Invariant 2 (ingestion/builder.rs:52), which aborts Phase 1. core/types/ssa.rs:25,43 stores def_block as (def_block & 0xFF) as u8, so the global block offsets in tra/backward/ssa_bi.rs:17-35 are wrong for every function after one with more than 256 blocks. Also truncated: SCC size as u16 (cg/scc.rs:38), orig_sym_id & 0xFFFF on disk (ssa/serializer.rs:113), line numbers as u16 (sym_span.rs:38-40), UMA counts as u16 (sequence_diagram.rs:158).
impact: Phase 1 fails outright beyond 65,535 files (monorepos such as intellij-community with testData), and traceability and artifacts are silently corrupted on ordinary large code (methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines).
recommendation: Widen ids, counts and line numbers to u32, and split sort_key into (file_id: u32, byte_offset: u32) or a u128. Replace every `as uN` on a length with uN::try_from(..)? returning a typed error. Add generated tests: 70K files, 300-block methods, 70K-line files, and .ssa/.uma round-trips.

title: SSA liveness and renaming are quadratic per method: per-occurrence variable ids give O(blocks × uses) live sets
evidence: liveness.rs:124-174 extract_stmt_vars uses AST node indices as variables: definitions are declaration or LHS nodes (134, 150) and uses are individual identifier occurrences (140, 160). A use never matches a definition, so it is never killed and flows to every upstream block. The sets are HashMap<u32, HashSet<u32>>, cloned per block per round (82-83) for up to 100 rounds (64). renaming.rs:117 save_depths copies the whole per-variable map at every dominator-tree node, and restore_to (210; version_stack.rs:29-37) walks it again. extract_stmt_vars runs three times per statement (liveness:44, placement:29, renaming:146).
impact: Per method, time and memory are O(B·U) and O(B·V). Giant generated methods reach 10^7–10^8 set entries (GBs), which means minutes per method or OOM.
recommendation: Resolve identifier uses to declaration symbols first, number variables densely per function, and compute liveness with fixedbitset/bitvec over a reverse-RPO worklist (O(B·V/64)). Alternatively, adopt the SSA construction of Braun et al. 2013, which needs neither liveness nor dominance frontiers. Make renaming pop only the definitions pushed in each block, and memoize per-statement use/def lists.

title: The 'succinct' AST costs about 210–236 B/node, roughly 45× the documented 4.65 B, and select1 scans bit by bit
evidence: ast/rmq.rs:24-51 builds a full sparse table (Vec<Vec<u32>>, log n levels over 2N bits) plus excess as Vec<i32> and log2 as Vec<usize>. jump_table.rs:16 stores one u32 per bit, and the preorder arrays add 17 B/node. A model of these formulas (scratchpad lens/scale_model.py) gives 209 B/node at 1M nodes and 1.09 GiB at 5M nodes (≈1M LOC), of which 852 MiB is the RMQ table. serializer.rs:183-184 rebuilds the table on every read, and rank_select.rs:100 implements select1 as a get_bit loop. docs/overview.md:119 and architecture.md:107 claim 4.65 MB per 1M nodes.
impact: The AST alone exceeds 1 GB at 1M LOC. Every first_child/next_sibling call (10^7–10^8 calls across Phases 3–6) costs hundreds of cycles. The README's 128× compression and O(1) navigation claims are contradicted.
recommendation: Add a subtree_size (or close-position-by-preorder) array beside parent_map so navigation is O(1) without select. Replace the sparse table with a Navarro–Sadakane range-min-max tree, or Fischer–Heun block RMQ in 2n+o(n) bits. Use Rank9/Select9 or Elias–Fano from the sucds or vers-vecs crates. Publish B/node figures measured with dhat or peak-RSS benchmarks.

DOCS.note: Docs now state the measured-free Theta(n log n) layout and the linear select1; succinct rewrite handed off

title: ROBDD engine: use-after-realloc UB in apply, no node budget or GC, O(E²) edge lookups, no-op O(n²) sifting
evidence: psa/bdd/mod.rs:84-86 builds `read` from self.nodes.as_ptr() and then lets apply push into the same Vec; the comment claims it 'never reallocates'. The Vec starts at length 2, so growth during the lo recursion leaves the hi recursion (apply.rs:103-104) reading freed memory. There is no node or time limit, and dead intermediate nodes are serialized (into_nodes). rpo.rs:106-107 edge_index_of is a linear search, called per predecessor and successor (O(E²)). sifting.rs:56-79 swaps only the ordering table, so node_count never changes. constraints.rs:122-123 builds pairwise at-most-one constraints (O(k²) applies).
impact: Heap UB on ordinary functions, producing silently wrong summaries or crashes. Time and memory are unbounded on wide switches and large methods, and .psa files are bloated with garbage nodes.
recommendation: Index self.nodes after each push instead of holding raw slices, or adopt biodivine-lib-bdd, or Sylvan/CUDD via FFI. These give GC, real dynamic reordering, a bounded computed table and node limits. Precompute a HashMap<(from, to), edge_idx>. Encode exactly-one constraints with a sequential-counter ladder. Cap each function at about 1M nodes and record 'unknown' past it. Run Miri on the BDD tests in CI.

title: Single-threaded pipeline that reads every file three times and parses it twice
evidence: Cargo.toml has no rayon or any other parallelism crate, and core/pipeline.rs:170-225 and main.rs:150-254 run the phases strictly serially. Phase 1 reads each file twice (ingestion/mod.rs:53, 111) and parses it with a single Parser (108); the Mutex-wrapped interner (105) is never shared across threads. Phase 2 re-reads and re-parses every file (ast/mod.rs:142-143). Kotlin is parsed with the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:30) and then with the JavaScript fallback, because no Kotlin AST adapter is registered (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Phases 4, 5, 8 and 9 loop over functions serially.
impact: Uses one core and pays twice the front-end parse cost. Kotlin-heavy repos pay wrong-grammar error recovery twice. About 8–12× of the available throughput on 16 cores goes unused.
recommendation: Parse once and emit tokens plus the reduced BP AST in the same walk. Run rayon par_iter over files with a per-thread tree_sitter::Parser (map_init), discover files with the ignore or jwalk crate, and merge per-file interners (or use lasso::ThreadedRodeo). Assign token ids from per-file counts plus a prefix sum. Use par_iter over functions in Phases 4, 5 and 8 and over classes in Phase 9; ruff and Biome use this per-file model.

ENG.note: Parallelising needs rayon plus pipeline code in src. Handed off; adding the dependency on its own would leave it unused.

title: No incremental or persistent reuse: .scpg is a stub, the delta engine is a no-op, and global ids renumber on every edit
evidence: scpg/serializer/mod.rs:56-108 writes 4-byte counts for 10 of 11 sections (e.g. line 59); only StringTable (62) carries data. MemoryMappedSCPG::open (scpg/mmap/mod.rs:18) uses fs::read rather than mmap, and no query can be served from the file. scpg/incremental/mod.rs:28 'applies' a delta by XOR-ing the hash. Token, preorder and symbol ids are corpus-global, so tra/delta/mod.rs:28-39 invalidates every symbol after the first changed token. main.rs keeps nine artifacts plus six raw byte copies alive until exit.
impact: Every run and every server request is a cold full rebuild, and peak RSS is the sum of all phases (several GB at 1M LOC). The 'O(1) incremental delta update' marked done in ROADMAP.md:116 does not exist.
recommendation: Use stable file-local ids such as (file_id, local_idx) or rust-analyzer-style AstIds. Cache per-file Phase 1–5 outputs keyed by BLAKE3(content + config), as ruff's cache does, and express cross-file phases as Salsa queries. Persist real CSR sections with zero-copy views (rkyv, zerocopy or bytemuck over memmap2) so open() can answer queries. Drop each phase's inputs once they are consumed.

DOCS.note: ROADMAP and traceability doc mark persistence and incremental reuse as planned, with prerequisites (stable ids, per-file caches); code handed off

title: HTTP server runs analyses synchronously on a single-threaded accept loop with no budgets, queue or cache
evidence: adapters/server.rs binds 0.0.0.0 (32) and handles connections one at a time on the accept thread (40-41). /api/analyze (252) runs git clone (429), all ten phases (506-617) and every exporter inside the request, with no timeout, cancellation, CPU or memory budget, or input-size cap. Output goes to the shared web/diagrams directory (637), so sessions overwrite each other. The response is assembled with format! through a five-pass .replace escaper (701-707). Nothing is cached by repo and commit.
impact: One large or adversarial repository (see SCALE-01 and SCALE-05) blocks or kills the service for everyone, including /api/health. Throughput is one analysis at a time, and every repeat request recomputes everything.
recommendation: Move to axum/hyper on tokio and run jobs on a bounded worker pool (spawn_blocking or rayon). Return 202 with a job id, and stream progress over SSE. Enforce per-job wall-clock and work budgets through cancellation tokens checked inside phase loops. Use per-job output directories, an artifact cache keyed by (repo URL, commit SHA), and streaming serde_json responses.

title: No scale benchmarks, perf CI or release tuning; published performance figures are unmeasured
evidence: The largest in-repo corpus is examples/test_patterns_codebase, at 451 lines. There is no benches/ directory, no criterion dependency, and no stress input in tests/. Cargo.toml defines only [profile.dev] (opt-level 2), with no [profile.release] tuning. scripts/benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:27 drives target/debug/openheart with a 60 s timeout (48) on small modules. docs/overview.md:115-124 quotes '~1 ns' and '~0.5 ns' lookups and 4.65 MB per 1M nodes with no harness behind them. CI runs only check, fmt and test.
impact: None of the superlinear cliffs in this report could have been caught, and the project cannot be credibly compared with Joern, CodeQL, SootUp or OPAL.
recommendation: Add criterion (or iai-callgrind) per-phase benchmarks over generated inputs: sequential ifs, deep concatenations, 10K-case switches, 50K-block methods, 70K files. Add a macro harness on pinned commits of guava, spring-framework, elasticsearch and intellij-community that records wall time, peak RSS and artifact bytes, with a CI regression gate (for example bencher.dev). Set lto="fat", codegen-units=1 and panic="abort" in the release profile, and use mimalloc.

title: Logger writes every level, including trace, to two unbuffered files from hot loops
evidence: core/logger.rs:124-159 gates only the console output by level (136). Every call still takes a global Mutex (145), formats a timestamped line (147), and write_all+flushes it to two unbuffered File handles (149-157); callers' format! arguments are built eagerly. Hot callers: a trace per call site (cg/call_sites.rs:57); per-function trace and debug lines (cfg/mod.rs:78,86; ssa/mod.rs:47,83,114; placement, renaming, liveness, cdg, ifds); INFO per function in Phase 8 (psa/mod.rs:131); INFO per class (pass1_discovery.rs:151; class_diagram.rs:56). The persistent log is append-only and never rotated.
impact: At 1M LOC this produces millions of lines, roughly 0.5–1 GB of logs and tens of seconds of syscalls per run, heavy console output on Windows, and a persistent log that grows without bound.
recommendation: Use tracing with EnvFilter, whose macros check the level before formatting, and tracing-appender non_blocking with rolling, size-capped files. Downgrade per-element INFO and DIAG lines to trace, or aggregate them into per-phase counters. Open the session and persistent logs only when requested.

title: Bitwise CRC-64 recomputed 19 times over re-read artifacts, whole-file buffers, and duplicate token tables
evidence: ingestion/serializer.rs:16-29 computes CRC-64 bit by bit (8 iterations per byte), and integrity.rs and hash_chain.rs compute CRC-32 the same way. main.rs re-reads .tca, .bpa, .cfa, .ssa and .tra (154, 163, 180, 192, 226) only so later phases can re-hash them: TCA, BPA, STA and CFA are hashed three times each (ast/mod.rs:48; symbol/serializer.rs:42-43; cfg/mod.rs:30-31; ssa/mod.rs:41; cg/mod.rs:45-46; psa/mod.rs:77). Serializers build the whole file in a Vec first, and SymbolTableArtifact::build clones every builder table (symbol/serializer.rs:64-71). TCA stores token_records and token_entries as identical copies (builder.rs:30-31).
impact: At 1M LOC this means gigabytes of bitwise CRC (seconds to tens of seconds) plus redundant I/O, a 2× memory spike per phase, and a TCA of 32 B/token instead of 16.
recommendation: Hash once while streaming through a BufWriter with an incremental hasher, and pass the digest forward in memory. Use a SIMD CRC (crc64fast-nvme or crc-fast), or xxh3 (xxhash-rust) for integrity and BLAKE3 for content addressing. Move builder tables instead of cloning them. Drop the duplicate backward table, since token_id order already equals sort order.

title: Query engine scans every call edge per worklist pop instead of using the CSR it already has
evidence: scpg/query/cfl.rs:27 iterates the whole cga.site_to_edge_map for each dequeued node, and impact.rs:24 and slice.rs:28,64 do the same. Each query is therefore O(V·E), although Phase 6 already builds callee_csr and caller_csr (cg/mod.rs:149-176). The 'CFL' query is plain reachability. cache.rs:32 clears the entire 'LRU' cache when it fills. tra/forward/sym_span.rs:60 walks back over every record in the file, so forward_sym_query is O(symbols in file), not the documented O(log N + k).
impact: On a multi-million-edge call graph, interactive reachability, impact and slice queries cost up to ~10^11 steps, which defeats the real-time traceability pitch.
recommendation: Traverse callee_csr/caller_csr with a bitset visited set, O(V+E). Use Reps–Horwitz–Sagiv tabulation for genuine CFL or IFDS queries. Replace the cache with the lru crate (or a CLOCK cache). For span stabbing queries, use parent-chain or nested-interval lookups or an interval tree, O(log N + depth).

title: Remaining quadratic helpers: per-function CSR builds, adjacency dedup, per-class TH scans, O(depth) node closes
evidence: cfg/builder/mod.rs:150-151 and 165-166 build the successor and predecessor CSRs by scanning all edges for every block, O(B·E) per function. cg/mod.rs:118-124 deduplicates adjacency with .any/.contains, O(Σdeg²), and sizes the CSR and Tarjan by all symbols (110). class_diagram.rs:283 and the pattern detectors (query.rs:42, strategy.rs:15, composite.rs:16, decorator.rs:15) scan all th_edges for each class. loops.rs:63-81 allocates and sweeps n entries per back edge. frontier.rs:25 and cdg.rs:77 deduplicate with Vec::contains. ast/builder.rs:166 walks the open stack on every close.
impact: Each is tolerable on small inputs but superlinear on giant generated methods, hub methods and 10^5-edge hierarchies, costing seconds to minutes each at 1M LOC.
recommendation: Build CSRs by counting sort (degree count, prefix sum, fill) in O(B+E). Deduplicate with sort+dedup or a HashSet, and size arrays by method count. Build one TH out-edge CSR shared by all extractors. Mark loop bodies with bitsets in a single pass, use bitsets for DF/CDG membership, and delete close_node's ancestor loop, since the reducer already returns merged ranges.

title: Web studio's in-browser ingestion samples 30–80 files sequentially and reports them as the whole repo
evidence: web/js/github-engine.js:103 takes sourceFiles.slice(0, 30) (local folders: slice(0, 80) at line 200) and fetches them one at a time with await (112). It then reports files_processed: sourceFiles.length (161, 253) and a hard-coded execution_time_ms: 280 (164). The api.github.com calls (54, 71) are unauthenticated, so they hit the 60-requests-per-hour limit, and the truncated flag of the recursive=1 tree is ignored. graph-canvas.js:681-684 disables textureOnViewport and hideEdgesOnViewport. uml-layout.js:373,382 runs nodes.find per component and a queue.shift BFS, O(N²) in the worst case.
impact: For a 1M-LOC repo the browser analyzes under 1% of the files while reporting all of them, and large graphs render without any level of detail.
recommendation: Ship the Rust engine as WASM in a Web Worker, using web-tree-sitter grammars. Fetch a single codeload tarball, stream-decompress it with fflate, cache it in OPFS, and report true counts and timings. For large graphs, add package-collapsed level of detail, worker-side ELK.js layout, and Cytoscape's viewport texture and edge hiding, or switch to a WebGL renderer such as sigma.js above 10K nodes.

DOCS.note: README, architecture and getting_started state that the studio analyses a sample through the unauthenticated API; studio code handed off

title: Exporters emit monolithic, unpartitioned diagrams and recompute shared indexes 57 times
evidence: PlantUMLExporter::export_class_diagram (plantuml.rs:274) and JSONExporter (json.rs:121) put every class and edge into one document. main.rs:281-309 runs 19 diagram types × 3 formats serially, and each call recomputes the package maps (json.rs:132-146; mermaid.rs:602-650). Behavioral views take arbitrary samples (.take(6) at plantuml.rs:925,958 and mermaid.rs:1102). JSON is written with to_string_pretty (factory.rs:208). Mermaid's default maxTextSize of 50,000 characters and PlantUML's 4096-px image limit reject diagrams with thousands of classes.
impact: At around 15K classes the class, package and component outputs are tens of MB and cannot be rendered, and the behavioral samples are not representative.
recommendation: Partition output by package or module: one package-dependency overview plus a drill-down diagram per package. Aggregate edges, building on plantuml_optimizer's bundling, and enforce node and edge caps with summary nodes. Compute the class, package and name indexes once per run, export the formats in parallel with rayon, and emit compact JSON.

title: SSA produces no φ-functions or def-use edges for any input; the SSA tests check only counts and CSR shape
evidence: Variable identity is the AST node index: liveness.rs:134-135 does `let sym_id = node; defs.push(sym_id)`, while uses push identifier-node ids (139-141, 159-160). Phase5Stage ignores `_sta` (ssa/mod.rs:34). A def node never equals a use node, so placement.rs:45 `is_live_in(y, var_sym)` is never true (no φ), and renaming.rs:150 `vstack.top(u)` never hits (empty def-use). points_to.rs:31 and object_diagram.rs:16 then call `sta.symbol(orig_sym_id)` on that node index. ssa_tests.rs:84-92 and pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:179-202 assert only counts and CSR shape; the uniqueness check holds by construction.
impact: Phase 5 output (φ, def-use, versions) is empty or meaningless for every program, which corrupts points-to, slicing, DFG and object diagrams. Deleting φ placement entirely would still pass the whole suite.
recommendation: Key SSA on resolved symbol ids, and introduce newtypes (NodeId, SymId, SsaId) so this ID-space confusion fails to compile. Add oracle tests: `int x=0; if(c) x=1; return x;` must yield exactly one φ(x) at the join, with two args, and the return's use must chain to it. A loop counter must get versions 0..2. Add proptest over generated structured programs asserting every use is dominated by its unique reaching def (Cytron et al. 1991). The φ count must equal a naive iterated-dominance-frontier reference keyed by symbol.

title: Call resolution returns the enclosing method, so the call graph is mostly self-loops; no test asserts a single edge
evidence: resolve_method_target (resolution.rs:179-238) never matches by name. Step 1 needs def_node == call_node. Step 3 needs a method whose first_token_id equals the call-site token, but method symbols take their declaration's first token (pass1_discovery.rs:178). Step 4 returns the first method whose token range encloses the call, which is the caller. Edges become (caller, caller) (cg/mod.rs:87-93), and Tarjan classifies nearly every calling method SELF_RECURSIVE (scc.rs:40-48). cg_tests.rs:79-87 asserts method_count>0, non-empty SCCs and round-trip counts; the surgical dump (575-626) only range-checks ids.
impact: Call edges, recursion classes, PSA unwind depths, CFL reachability, slicing and sequence/communication diagrams are wrong for ordinary code. Dropping or reversing every edge would also pass the suite.
recommendation: Add golden edge-set tests: for the cg_tests fixture, assert edges == {main→<init>, main→helper, main→recurse, recurse→recurse}, with SCC class SELF only for recurse. Add a property: a self-edge exists only if the body syntactically calls its own name with matching arity. Add a nightly differential job on pinned repos comparing against a CHA call graph from SootUp or WALA (or the JavaParser symbol solver), with edge precision/recall thresholds that fail CI.

title: The HTTP server has zero tests; /api/source serves arbitrary files and /api/analyze runs git clone on unvalidated input
evidence: The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32). /api/source reads the decoded `file` query verbatim as a path (109-124, 200-205), so `?file=/etc/passwd` or `..%2F..%2F` paths return file contents. /api/analyze passes repo_url straight to `git clone` (429-437). WebRepoFetcher::validate_url is never called, its only test is the happy path, and it panics on `https://github.com/owner` because of `parts[1]` (web_repo.rs:111-112). A failed clone silently analyses the first directory in target_repos and still reports success (467-482). Error JSON is interpolated unescaped (530-533). No test touches any route.
impact: Any network peer can read files readable by the server user. Results can silently come from the wrong repository, and unescaped error text produces invalid JSON. No regression net exists.
recommendation: Refactor routing into a pure `fn handle(req: &[u8], ctx: &Ctx) -> Response` and add table-driven tests. Traversal payloads (absolute, `..`, `%2e%2e`, `C:\\`) must return 403/404. repo_url must match ^https://github.com/[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+$ and never start with `-`. A failed clone must return an error, and every response body must parse with serde_json. Add a cargo-fuzz or proptest target over arbitrary request bytes (no panics), plus an integration test on 127.0.0.1:0. Bind 127.0.0.1 by default.

title: Succinct-tree LCA is wrong on most queries and select1 breaks on deep nesting; the tests use 3-node and 6-bit toys
evidence: rmq.rs:89-95 returns rank1(min)-1, minus 1 more if min is a close paren. For Root(A(A1,A2),B), lca(A1,B) returns A1, not Root. An exact Python port disagreed with a naive parent-walk LCA on 3,699 of 6,000 random queries. ast_tests.rs:63-79 tests only Root(C1,C2), the one shape where the formula holds, and 'Theorem 5.1' (research tests 133-135) checks only bit length. select1 (rank_select.rs:92-95) assumes which duplicate binary_search returns, which std leaves unspecified. With nesting deeper than ~1,024, Rust 1.83+ returns the last equal entry and select1(1100) = 0, not 1099. first_child and next_sibling depend on it (builder.rs:58-87).
impact: The public BPASTArtifact::lca and the 'O(1) LCA' theorem are wrong for typical ASTs. Deeply nested generated code (long else-if chains) can mis-navigate the AST and corrupt CFGs, depending on the toolchain version.
recommendation: Add proptest suites over random and path-shaped trees (up to 5,000 nodes, depth ≥ 1,100 to force all-zero superblocks). Named invariants: rank1(i) == naive popcount; select1(rank1(i)) == i on 1-bits; match_pos is an involution; lca == naive parent-walk LCA; first_child, next_sibling, subtree_size and depth agree with parent_map. Fix lca with the Navarro–Sadakane form: parent(node opening at rmq(open u, open v)+1). This passed 10,000/10,000 against the oracle. Fix select1 with partition_point(|&s| s < k) - 1.

title: BDDLibrary reads through an unsound raw slice that dangles when the node Vec grows; no Miri or sanitizer job
evidence: apply, apply_not and restrict build `read = slice::from_raw_parts(self.nodes.as_ptr(), len)`, then pass `&mut self.nodes`, which make_node pushes onto (bdd/mod.rs:84-95, 100-109, 120-131; unique_table.rs:64-66). Any reallocation leaves `read` dangling. The SAFETY comment's claim that clearing the cache bounds allocations does not hold. Construction calls apply once per CFG block (construction/mod.rs:84-87), so growth is routine. HashMap growth can also reuse the freed buffer. Unit tests build at most about 8 nodes, and CI runs no Miri or AddressSanitizer.
impact: Undefined behaviour in Phase 8. Reads of freed memory can silently corrupt BDDs, sat_count and path metrics, or crash, depending on allocator and platform. No current test can observe it.
recommendation: Remove the unsafe: read nodes via all_nodes[f as usize] (ids below len are never mutated), or use an index-stable arena. Add a nightly `cargo +nightly miri test psa::` job, a proptest that builds BDDs with more than 10^4 nodes from random formulas, and an `-Zsanitizer=address` test run. Set `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` crate-wide, allowing it only in core/io/mmap.rs with documented invariants.

ENG.note: Added `make miri` and `make asan`, both nightly and filtered by UNSAFE_FILTER (default psa::). Removing the unsafe slice and adding #![deny(unsafe_code)] are handed off.

title: `_ => Drop` silently deletes constructor bodies and other constructs, and a test pins the defect as expected
evidence: The Java reduction table ends with `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129), and Drop discards the whole subtree (reducer.rs:17). constructor_body is unmapped, as are try_with_resources_statement, switch_rule, explicit_constructor_invocation, generic_type, array_type and enum_constant. CFG construction needs an NN_BLOCK child (cfg/mod.rs:59-74), so every constructor gets no CFG, SSA or activity record, and its calls (super(...), new) disappear. pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:142 asserts function_count == 2 for fixtures with three bodies (OrderService constructor, processOrder, execute), which pins the bug.
impact: Constructors, try-with-resources blocks and Java 14+ arrow switches vanish from all downstream analyses and diagrams. The suite currently rewards keeping it that way.
recommendation: Add a grammar-coverage test that loads tree-sitter-java's node-types.json and asserts every named kind has an explicit decision, with Drop allowed only for an allow-list of trivia. Add a token-coverage invariant: every non-trivia token in a method or constructor body lies in some kept node's token range. Add fixtures for constructors, try-with-resources, switch rules, records and enums, and correct the assertion to 3.

title: IFDS, CDG, liveness, points-to, SCC, post-dominators and loops have zero semantic tests; 'IFDS' is a local pattern match
