evidence: No test inspects any output of these modules; the only CDG check is `!cd_offsets.is_empty()` (pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:201). ifds.rs is not a tabulation solver. is_null_literal (69-78) marks a definition nullable if any direct child is NN_LITERAL, so `int x = 5` counts as nullable. Taint and type-state fire only when a statement has an NN_METHOD_DECL child (58-67, 80-89), and nothing propagates. Points-to seeds use the wrong ID space (TST-01). A Python port of the Cooper dominators matched a naive oracle on 3,000 random graphs, so some code is sound, just unverified.
impact: The advertised taint, nullable and type-state results are wrong for common code and invisible to the suite. Regressions in CDG, SCC or post-dominators would pass unnoticed.
recommendation: Add a differential test per algorithm. Post-dominators: compare with dominators on the reversed CFG plus a virtual exit. CDG: compare with the Ferrante–Ottenstein–Warren definition. Loops: back edges must equal edges t→h with h dominating t. SCC: compare with petgraph::algo::kosaraju_scc. Points-to: Andersen constraint fixtures with expected sets. Replace ifds.rs with a Reps–Horwitz–Sagiv tabulation solver and assert the expected facts from the SecuriBench-Micro and DroidBench cases.

title: SCPG and exporter tests are vacuous: tautological asserts, a counts-only .scpg file, placeholder XMI, no golden outputs
evidence: scpg_tests.rs:119-128 asserts `is_reach || !is_reach` and `to_src.is_some() || to_src.is_none()`. The 'unified' .scpg stores only counts in 10 of 11 sections, e.g. cga.call_site_count (serializer/mod.rs:57-107), and a zeroed source_hash (146). open() never verifies the section CRCs (mmap/mod.rs:16-80), and the queries take in-memory artifacts instead. XMI emits only `name="Class_<id>"` (xmi.rs:12-15), yet `contains("<uml:Model")` passes (scpg_tests.rs:155-156). Every PlantUML and Mermaid test checks a prefix or a single class name.
impact: The headline .scpg query engine cannot answer anything from the file, the XMI is unusable in UML tools, and exporter regressions (reversed arrows, lost members) pass CI.
recommendation: Add a cold-open test: write .scpg, drop the in-memory artifacts, reopen it, and assert slice, reachability and navigation answers equal the in-memory results. Flip one section byte and expect open() to fail. Add insta snapshots for all 19 strategies × {PlantUML, Mermaid, JSON} on examples/test_patterns_codebase. In CI, validate syntax with `plantuml -checkonly` and @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli, and check XMI by Eclipse UML2 import or XSD validation.

title: The README's F1 = 1.0000 claim comes from a circular, hand-tuned Python harness that never runs in CI
evidence: The ground truth is a regex line scanner keyed by simple name (ruthless_verify.py:95), and only sets of class names are compared. Real names such as HomeScreen, INVESTOR, JFrame, Logger, Root, Table and Scanner are excluded from both sides via KEYWORDS (ruthless_config.json:73-91; ruthless_verify.py:232). The dataset script renames GHobbits to GenHobbits (test_ruthless_popular_datasets.py:63-64), passes its PlantUCD batches unconditionally (259) and accepts `or "Artifact Type" in out` (113). The benchmark exits 0 on failure (benchmark_all_java_design_patterns.py:212-215). Kotlin is parsed with the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:30); TS, Rust and other languages fall back to tree-sitter-javascript (registry.rs:27-38).
impact: The multi-language F1 = 1.0 cannot be reproduced from the repository and is partly an artifact of the exclusion list. Nothing in CI measures accuracy.
recommendation: Replace it with a nightly CI evaluation on pinned commits (spring-petclinic, java-design-patterns, commons-lang, one Kotlin repo). Use independent oracles: the JavaParser symbol solver or Eclipse JDT for Java, and the Kotlin Analysis API for Kotlin. Compare fully-qualified names and score classes, members, supertypes and call edges with no exclusion lists. Publish per-repo P/R/F1 JSON with commit SHAs. Add per-language tests asserting `!root_node().has_error()` on fixtures, and drop claims for languages without a real grammar.

ENG.note: Python harness, README and adapters are outside my paths.

DOCS.note: README F1 claim withdrawn; ruthless_verify.py described as a non-benchmark; CI evaluation tier defined in status.md §7; scripts and CI handed off

title: Pattern-detection tests are satisfied by identifier names; there are no negative fixtures and no precision measurement
evidence: is_strategy reports 95% confidence if the class name contains 'Strategy' and 90% if a supertype's name does (strategy.rs:13-24). is_facade reports 85% for any name containing 'Facade' and 70% for any class with three or more typed fields, which matches most DTOs (facade.rs:9-24). The adversarial test passes if any one of four patterns appears anywhere (adversarial_trick_tests.rs:259-262). Its fixture classes are named ExecutionStrategy, SystemFacade and ComponentDecorator, so the names give the answer away. The topologies its header promises (identical names across packages, guarded state machines) are absent.
impact: False positives on ordinary code (DTOs flagged as Facade) and name-only detection go undetected, so the reported pattern results cannot be defended as a benchmark.
recommendation: Add a metamorphic test that renames every identifier in examples/test_patterns_codebase (57 files labelled by directory) to neutral names and requires structural detections to stay the same. Add negative fixtures: a 3-field DTO is not a Facade, and a *Strategy-named class with no polymorphism is not a Strategy. Measure per-pattern precision and recall against those labels and the P-MARt and DPB benchmarks with CI thresholds, and assert exact participant roles.

title: No benchmark or memory harness; static accounting contradicts '128× compression' and 'O(1)'; pathological inputs untested
evidence: There are no benches and no criterion. The RMQ sparse table holds about n·log2(n) u32s plus an i32 excess array and a usize log table (rmq.rs:24-54). The jump table holds one u32 per bit (jump_table.rs:16) and is also serialized (ast/serializer.rs:40-41). Static accounting gives about 157 B/node at 10^4 nodes and 209 B/node at 10^6, against 0.25 B/node for the BP bits themselves. select1 scans up to 512 bits linearly. compute_max_path_length (construction/mod.rs:153-173) enumerates every path, so 40 sequential ifs mean 2^40 stack pushes. The DFS routines in rpo.rs, scc.rs and reducer.rs are recursive.
impact: The headline compression and complexity claims are unmeasured and probably inverted. Generated code with deep nesting or many branches can hang the pipeline or overflow the stack.
recommendation: Add criterion and iai-callgrind benches per phase, plus dhat-rs heap profiling that asserts a bytes-per-node budget against a pointer-AST baseline (tree-sitter Tree, rowan). Add a pathological-input test corpus (nesting depth 5,000, 40 sequential ifs, a 10k-case switch, a 100k-method call chain) with per-phase time and memory budgets under nextest timeouts. Publish results with hardware specs, and back the O(1) claims with a range-min-max tree (Navarro–Sadakane).

title: Coverage map and target test architecture for benchmark grade
evidence: Unit tests: 47 across 16 of 198 files, 36 of them in psa/ (BDD terminal cases, layouts). There are zero unit tests in ast/, cfg/, ssa/, cg/, symbol/, tra/, uma/, scpg/, server.rs and main.rs. The 29 integration tests are end-to-end runs that mostly assert counts. Meaningfully tested: sort keys, interner, unique-table rules, Pass1/Pass5, jump-table involution, canonicity, Singleton, hash links. Untested: rank/select beyond 8 bits, RMQ/LCA, post-dominators, loops, SSA renaming, IFDS, points-to, SCC, sifting, FORCE, CRC corruption, exporter content, queries, incremental, CLI, server, all web JS. The only dev-dependency is tempfile.
impact: Without an architecture built around oracles, correctness regressions in core analyses stay invisible, and no benchmark-grade claim can be substantiated or defended.
recommendation: Layered plan, with cargo-nextest as the runner. (1) proptest suites tests/prop_{bp,dom,ssa,bdd,cg,serde}.rs with named invariants. (2) Differential oracles: naive dominators, petgraph SCC and dominators, truth-table BDDs, naive rank/select, the crc crate. (3) insta goldens in tests/golden/. (4) cargo-fuzz targets in fuzz/. (5) Nightly end-to-end runs on pinned repositories in tests/e2e/. (6) cargo-llvm-cov floors of 85% for ast/, cfg/, ssa/ and psa/bdd/. (7) A cargo-mutants gate.

title: BDD tests cover terminal shortcuts only; sifting is a no-op; a PSA 'invariant' compares a value with its own copy
evidence: apply.rs:151-186 tests only the FALSE/TRUE shortcuts and XOR(F,F); sat_count.rs:110-142 and restrict.rs:81-120 use a single variable. sifting.rs:44-82 swaps only VariableOrdering entries while measuring bdd.node_count(), which never changes because no BDD level is swapped. best_pos therefore stays at var_pos, and each variable is moved back after O(n²) wasted swaps. No test covers sifting. psa_tests.rs:114-127 compares header.cyclomatic with the CFA value that construction/mod.rs:113 copied. The 4 paths of compute(a,b) are never asserted. PathMetrics::from_bytes drops unwind_depth (metrics.rs:95), and the round-trip test uses 0 (107).
impact: Path counts and the 'Rudell sifting' claim are unverified. A broken apply on non-trivial functions or a fake optimizer would pass, and the lost unwind_depth goes unnoticed.
recommendation: Add proptest over random formulas with at most 12 variables, checking every assignment: eval(apply(op,f,g)) == op(eval f, eval g); sat_count == truth-table ones; restrict equals the cofactor; equal functions get the same node id. Implement an in-place adjacent-level swap (Rudell 1993). Test that sifting preserves the function, never grows |BDD|, and makes the interleaved x1x2+x3x4+x5x6 order linear. Assert sat_count == 4 for compute(a,b).

title: Integrity checks are untested and partly fake: 'VERIFIED VALID' without a CRC, a non-standard PSA CRC, a count-based hash chain
evidence: cmd_inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa after matching only the magic number (main.rs:373-388). psa::crc64_ecma (psa/serializer.rs:259-279) yields 0xD428DA62D41203D6 for '123456789', while the catalogue CRC-64/ECMA-182 value, which ingestion's copy matches, is 0x6C40DF5F0B497347. Its doc claim to match the other serializers is therefore false, and its only test checks determinism (334-340). ScpgHashChain hashes the file count as 'bpa_hash', call_site_count as 'cga_hash', and a Debug string that includes mtime_ns (hash_chain.rs:36-41). The only test asserts scpg_hash != 0. No test flips a byte.
impact: Corrupt .tca and .bpa files are reported as valid, and standard tools cannot verify .psa checksums. Staleness detection misses content edits that keep the counts equal, and fires on a mere touch.
recommendation: Consolidate into one checksum module with known-answer tests against the crc crate's CRC_64_ECMA_182. For every artifact, add a proptest that flips a random bit in the serialized file and asserts read() returns Err, and make inspect call the real readers. Add metamorphic staleness tests: editing a method body while keeping counts equal must change scpg_hash, and touching files or re-checking out without edits must not. Derive the component hashes from artifact bytes.

title: Outputs are non-deterministic (wall clock, file mtime, HashMap order), which blocks golden tests; no determinism test exists
evidence: The .tca embeds SystemTime::now() (ingestion/serializer.rs:80) and the .scpg header embeds now_ns (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136), so every downstream crc64 hash link changes on each run. File mtimes enter the hash chain (ingestion/mod.rs:62; hash_chain.rs:36). The JSON exporter emits package/class nodes and dependency edges while iterating a HashMap or HashSet (json.rs:148, 445, 518), so node order and counter-assigned edge ids vary between processes. The server rewrites the tracked web/diagrams/* files on every request (server.rs:637-690).
impact: Byte-for-byte reproducibility, snapshot testing, artifact caching and diffable benchmark results are all impossible, and the studio's layout input changes from run to run.
recommendation: Honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, or exclude timestamps from hashed and serialized content, and drop mtime from hashed records. Use BTreeMap or sorted iteration in exporters, with ids derived from content. Add a determinism test that runs the pipeline twice in separate processes (std::process::Command on the test binary) and asserts byte-identical artifacts and exporter strings. Stop the server writing into web/ at runtime.

title: Artifact loaders and the request parser are unfuzzed; malformed files with a valid CRC panic or abort
evidence: The BPA reader trusts on-disk lengths. `Vec::with_capacity(words_len)` with values up to 2^32 aborts on allocation, and `buf[offset..offset+8]` panics on a short payload. bit_count is never checked against words.len(), so get_bit indexes out of bounds inside RankSelectIndex::build (ast/serializer.rs:109-127, 183). MemoryMappedSCPG::open size-checks for 11 sections but then loops over the file's own section_count (mmap/mod.rs:19-72). get_section adds offset and length without overflow checks (81-93). The serializers contain about 270 unwrap/expect calls, and there is no fuzz/ directory.
impact: Truncated, hostile or version-skewed artifacts crash the CLI and engine instead of returning errors, and loader panics stay invisible until a user hits them.
recommendation: Add a cargo-fuzz target per loader (tca, bpa, sta, cfa, ssa, cga, tra, psa, uma, scpg), with a harness that recomputes the trailing CRC so mutated inputs pass the checksum gate. Add structured `arbitrary` round-trip targets asserting read(write(x)) == x, a target that feeds raw source bytes through the whole pipeline, and an HTTP-parser target. Seed corpora from test outputs, run 10 minutes nightly, and apply to OSS-Fuzz. Use a bounds-checked BinaryReader that returns Err.

title: CI is a single Linux check/fmt/test job; releases and Pages deploys are ungated, and overflow checks are off in tests
evidence: ci.yml runs only cargo check, fmt and test on ubuntu (stable and beta): no clippy, coverage, Miri, Windows or macOS, although the author develops on Windows (run.bat). release.yml publishes libopenheart.rlib without running tests. deploy_pages.yml uploads web/ on every push with no `needs:` dependency on CI. Cargo.toml's [profile.dev] sets overflow-checks = false, which the test profile inherits, so cargo test never traps arithmetic overflow. dev-dependencies contain only tempfile, and the scripts/*.py suites never run in CI.
impact: Regressions reach releases and the public studio unchecked, and platform-specific or overflow bugs are structurally invisible to the suite.
recommendation: Set `[profile.test] overflow-checks = true, debug-assertions = true`. Add CI jobs: clippy -D warnings; cargo-nextest on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS; cargo-llvm-cov with per-module floors; Miri for psa/bdd; cargo-mutants --in-diff on PRs; nightly fuzz and end-to-end runs; cargo-deny. Make release.yml and deploy_pages.yml depend on CI success (workflow_run or needs), and run the web tests before the Pages upload.

ENG.note: Removed overflow-checks = false and added [profile.test] with overflow-checks and debug-assertions on. Makefile now has the clippy, nextest, coverage and miri gates. Gating the workflows is handed off.

title: The web studio's 9,035 lines of JS have no tests, and the deployed path fabricates classes and timings
evidence: web/ has no test runner, lint configuration or test files. github-engine.js samples only the first 30 source files (103). When its regex extracts nothing, it invents classes with `fields:[{name:'id',type:'String'}]` and `methods:[{name:'execute',...}]` (127-147). It then reports a hard-coded `execution_time_ms: 280` (164) and 'Successfully compiled SCPG' (155). puml-parser.js (521 lines), uml-layout.js and graph-canvas.js (2,393 lines) are untested, and deploy_pages.yml publishes the directory as-is.
impact: The public GitHub Pages demo can show invented members and fixed timings, presented as compiler output, and no test would flag it.
recommendation: Add Vitest unit tests with fixtures for parseRepoUrl, parseSourceFile per language, the PUML parser (round-tripping the committed web/diagrams/*.puml) and layout. Add msw-mocked GitHub API tests asserting no synthetic members, honest stats and surfaced errors. Add a Playwright smoke test on the static site plus ESLint, and require all of them before the Pages upload.

title: Many tests are tautological, print instead of asserting, or check invariants that hold by construction
evidence: metrics.rs:115-124 computes `6 - 5 + 2` inline without calling production code, and asserts V(G) = 3 for an if-else (the correct value is 2). crc64_deterministic (psa/serializer.rs:334-340) would pass for `|_| 0`. design_pattern_architecture_tests.rs:104-114 only prints its results. cfg_tests.rs:86-88 prints the cyclomatic complexity instead of asserting it. The surgical dump test contains 134 println! calls, and CI runs with --nocapture. The SSA id-uniqueness check (pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:183-192) holds by construction. The Theorem 5.2 bound of 5 is trivially met by 3 nodes (70-79). README.md:164 claims 22 integration tests; there are 29.
impact: The test count overstates assurance, and the scripts that label these tests as 'verified' spread false confidence.
recommendation: Rewrite or delete each tautology against an oracle: call the real cyclomatic code on a known CFG (if-else → 2), use CRC known-answer tests, and assert the detected patterns per class. Convert dump tests into insta snapshots and drop --nocapture from CI. A cargo-mutants score gate will surface assertion-free tests. Generate the README's test counts from `cargo nextest list`.

title: Adopt cargo-mutants as a quality gate; predicted surviving mutants show where assertions are missing
evidence: Static review predicts these mutants survive every current test: deleting φ placement (placement.rs:45-61); returning vec![] from resolve_call_site (resolution.rs:30); making is_null_literal return true (ifds.rs:69-78); zeroing max_path_len in PathMetrics::from_bytes; reversing the operands of PlantUML `--|>`; replacing XMI output with a constant model; changing `<=` to `<` in range_min tie-breaking (rmq.rs:73); skipping the CRC comparison in any reader. Each changes only semantic content that no test asserts.
impact: Without a mutation gate, coverage percentages will mislead: the end-to-end tests execute most lines but check almost none of them.
recommendation: Run `cargo mutants --in-diff origin/main` on every PR, and a full `cargo mutants --test-tool=nextest --timeout-multiplier 3` weekly. Gate on a per-module ceiling of missed mutants, starting at today's baseline and ratcheting to at least 80% caught for ast/, cfg/analysis/, ssa/, cg/ and psa/bdd/. File surviving mutants as issues, and exclude only documented equivalent mutants via .cargo/mutants.toml.

title: The only nested-package test is #[ignore]d with a misleading comment, and tests have no timeouts
evidence: scpg_tests.rs:168-169: `#[ignore] // TODO: Test harness has type-resolution loop issue; real pipeline works fine`. The test calls the same Phase3Stage::run that the server (server.rs:559) and the CLI use, so a loop there is a product loop, not a harness issue. CI never runs --ignored, and cargo test has no per-test timeout. Parent walks such as `while cur_scope != u32::MAX` (resolver.rs:19-30) rely on acyclic parent maps that no test checks.
impact: A known hang or failure for nested packages is hidden, and the next hang in CI will stall runners instead of failing fast.
recommendation: Run under cargo-nextest with `slow-timeout = { period = "30s", terminate-after = 4 }`. Un-ignore the test, reproduce and fix the loop, and add property tests asserting the scope and class parent maps are acyclic. Bound parent walks by step count and return Err when the bound is exceeded. Add the nested-package fixture to the golden snapshot set.

title: DOM XSS: attacker-controlled repo/ZIP file paths and names flow unescaped into innerHTML (and persist via localStorage history)
evidence: analyzeGitHubRepo builds progress text `...: ${file.path.split('/').pop()}` (github-engine.js:123); analyzeSourceFiles does the same for ZIP/folder entries (:218). index.html assigns these verbatim: `hudText.innerHTML = \`Cloning & Analyzing ${repoName}: ${msg}\`` (index.html:915) and `...${name}...: ${msg}` (:971). repoName/name/folderName/zipName come straight from the URL or file names (index.html:813,1035,1058). Names are re-rendered unescaped in the history dropdown: `${item.name}` then `dropdown.innerHTML = html` (index.html:1200,1229), persisted in localStorage (:1177). Git permits `<`/`>` in tree paths; a repo file named `.java` fires during the per-file progress update regardless of raw-fetch success.
impact: Analyzing a malicious public repo, or opening a crafted ZIP/folder, runs arbitrary JS in the studio origin; the history sink makes it persistent across reloads, enabling theft of imported (possibly proprietary) source and origin localStorage.
recommendation: Never assign untrusted data via innerHTML: set these status/name nodes with textContent, or build nodes with createElement + textContent. Where markup is required, sanitize with DOMPurify and adopt Trusted Types (require-trusted-types-for 'script'). Escape item.name before the history template. Add the CSP in WSEC-02 as defense in depth.

title: No Content-Security-Policy, no Trusted Types, and no SRI on five CDN scripts
evidence: index.html <head> sets only cache-control metas (index.html:4-11) — there is no CSP meta and GitHub Pages cannot send CSP headers, so none exists. cytoscape, dagre, cytoscape-dagre, cytoscape-svg and jszip are loaded from cdnjs/jsdelivr with no `integrity=`/`crossorigin` attributes (index.html:29-34). Trusted Types is not enabled, leaving every innerHTML sink unconstrained. deploy_pages.yml uploads web/ as-is with no header injection step.
impact: Any XSS (e.g. WSEC-01) executes with full origin privileges and no containment; a compromise or tampering of cdnjs/jsdelivr yields full studio takeover for all visitors.
recommendation: Add a strict CSP via <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' pinned CDNs; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'). Add SRI integrity hashes + crossorigin='anonymous' to all five scripts (or self-host). Enable Trusted Types and route the remaining sinks through a DOMPurify policy.

ENG.note: web/index.html and deploy_pages.yml are outside my paths.

title: ReDoS: catastrophic backtracking in the in-browser method/field parser regexes freezes the tab
evidence: extractMethods uses `/(?:(public|...|def)\s+)?(?:(abstract|static|final|async)\s+)*([A-Za-z0-9_<>[\]]+)?\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*(?:\{|;|->|:)/g` (github-engine.js:434), run on every analyzed file (:339,:395; GitHub files :115, ZIP/folder :211). The optional type `([...]+)?` adjacent to `\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)` over the same class, with no match, backtracks exponentially. Measured in Node on the verbatim regex: 1 KB run of one identifier = 0.57 s, 2 KB = 5.1 s, 4 KB = 36 s, 8 KB = 272 s. `.js` is an accepted extension (:89,:183), so a normal minified bundle triggers it.
impact: A single long no-paren identifier run (minified JS, a long constant, or a crafted token) hangs the main thread indefinitely — denial of service on analysis for ordinary repositories, not just adversarial ones.
recommendation: Replace the hand-rolled regexes with a linear tokenizer, or anchor each to a token boundary via a lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_<>[\]$])` and make the optional return type consume mandatory trailing whitespace so the ambiguous split is removed; an anchored variant processed 1 MB in ~39 ms in testing. Cap per-file size and run parsing in a Web Worker with a timeout.

title: Loaded .openheart.json / sessionStorage state consumed with no schema validation (innerHTML and fetch sinks)
evidence: The Load-State handler does `JSON.parse(await file.text())` then `canvas.loadDiagramState(savedState)` with no validation (index.html:1383-1385; graph-canvas.js:1383), and echoes `savedState.diagram_type` via `.toUpperCase()` into innerHTML (index.html:1388). Loaded edges' uml_kind reach the layers panel, built with `span.innerHTML = \`...${conf.icon||'→'}... ${conf.label||item.kind}... (${item.count})\`` and `color` interpolated into inline style (index.html:735,718,723). Loaded node raw_url is fetched directly: `fetch(nodeData.raw_url||nodeData.rawUrl)` (editor.js:146-149). sessionStorage custom IR is restored and its name injected via innerHTML (index.html:614,631).
impact: A shared/hosted state file can inject markup through the layers/HUD sinks, CSS-inject via unvalidated color, and cause the victim's browser to fetch arbitrary attacker URLs (tracking/exfil of file-open), with no integrity checks.
recommendation: Validate every loaded state against a strict JSON Schema (allowlist diagram_type and uml_kind enums, reject unknown keys, require same-origin/githubusercontent raw_url). Render layer labels/icons with textContent and validate color against a hex/rgb allowlist. Route any remaining markup through DOMPurify + Trusted Types.

title: Orphaned modules shipped to production include a latent raw-innerHTML of third-party Kroki SVG and code egress
evidence: app.js imports Logger/StudioState/OrbEngine/APIClient/DiagramViewer/UIController and binds DOM ids (orb-canvas, plantuml-render-container, status-logs, toast-container, btn-fetch, repo-url-input, diagram-tabs) that do not exist in index.html; index.html's inline module imports only icons, graph-canvas, editor, file-tree, github-engine, themes (index.html:409-414) and never loads app.js. The dead viewer.js inserts third-party SVG raw: `viewport.innerHTML = svgText` where svgText is the body of a POST to `https://kroki.io/plantuml/svg` (viewer.js:145-151; api.js:66-74), exfiltrating PlantUML (code structure) to kroki.io and trusting its response.
impact: Dead code enlarges and confuses the audit surface and ships an unsanitized third-party-SVG XSS plus code-structure egress that becomes live the moment anyone re-wires these modules.
recommendation: Delete the unused modules from the deployed web/ bundle, or if retained, gate behind an explicitly loaded page and sanitize Kroki output with DOMPurify (SVG profile) before insertion; make Kroki egress opt-in and documented.

title: No clickjacking / framing protection on the studio page
evidence: There is no CSP frame-ancestors directive and GitHub Pages does not emit X-Frame-Options; the page contains no frame-busting logic. The studio imports local/proprietary source via Folder/ZIP pickers and exposes destructive-looking controls (Delete node, Clear history).
impact: The studio can be embedded in a hostile iframe for UI-redress, tricking a user into loading a local codebase or triggering actions while the attacker frames the page.
recommendation: Add frame-ancestors 'none' to the WSEC-02 CSP meta (X-Frame-Options cannot be set on Pages); optionally add a top-frame self-check that neutralizes the UI when framed.

ENG.note: web/index.html is outside my paths.

title: Systemic unsafe innerHTML string-templating pattern across the studio
evidence: Beyond the untrusted sinks, ~30 innerHTML assignments build HTML by template string (e.g. index.html:435,446,682,735,803,833,846,898,926,1257,1388; minimap-navigator.js:81,118,297,330). Most are currently fed trusted data, but the uniform pattern means any future data-source change silently becomes an injection, and colors are interpolated into inline style attributes without validation.
impact: Fragile, error-prone escaping that invites regressions; contradicts the OWASP DOM XSS guidance to prefer safe sink APIs over string concatenation.
recommendation: Introduce a tiny DOM helper (createElement + textContent, or a tagged-template that auto-escapes) and convert sinks to it; enable Trusted Types so raw innerHTML with a string throws, forcing use of the sanitized path. Reserve innerHTML strictly for static, developer-authored constants.

title: Ad-hoc syntax highlighter emits malformed nested HTML on annotations and strings
evidence: highlightSyntax escapes first (good, so not XSS) but then applies independent regex replacements that nest spans incorrectly: for ` @Override` it produces `class="syn-annotation">@Override` because the keyword regex rewrites the word `class` inside the annotation span's own attribute (editor.js:560-591). String/keyword/type passes can also overlap and corrupt markup.
impact: Broken DOM in the code viewer for common tokens (annotations, lines containing keyword-like words), degrading the flagship code-sync feature and signalling that DIY escaping/markup here is fragile.
recommendation: Replace the hand-rolled highlighter with a maintained, escaping-correct library such as highlight.js or Prism (or tokenize once and emit spans from non-overlapping token spans), so highlighting cannot produce malformed or overlapping markup.

title: Binary ignores HOST/PORT env and hardcodes 0.0.0.0 bind; no localhost-only option
evidence: start() binds format!("0.0.0.0:{}", self.port) (server.rs:32). The port comes only from argv (main.rs:533-537, args[2].parse). grep across src shows no env::var("HOST") or env::var("PORT") anywhere (only OPENHEART_LOG in core/logger.rs:98), so Dockerfile ENV HOST=0.0.0.0 / PORT=8080 (43-44) are never read. There is no flag or env to bind 127.0.0.1 only.
impact: The unauthenticated arbitrary-file-read (SRV-01) and git-clone/SSRF/RCE (SRV-02) endpoints are reachable from every host on the LAN, not just localhost, with no opt-out; the documented env-based configuration is inert and run scripts advertising 'localhost' are misleading.
recommendation: Read HOST/PORT from env with safe defaults, default the bind to 127.0.0.1, and require an explicit flag to expose on 0.0.0.0.

SRV.note: Reads OPENHEART_HOST/HOST, OPENHEART_PORT/PORT and --host/--port. Default bind is 127.0.0.1. Any non-loopback bind requires an access token (generated and printed if unset)

title: Failed git clone silently analyzes the first cached repo and returns success for the wrong repository
evidence: A clone failure only pushes a log line and never aborts (439-459). Execution falls through to target_dir = repo_dir (467); when that path does not exist, the code iterates ./target_repos and picks the FIRST directory found (470-481), then runs the pipeline on it and returns status:success with 14 diagrams. Triggers on any clone failure (URL typo, private/nonexistent repo, offline, rate-limit) whenever >=1 repo is already cached.
impact: Callers receive a successful-looking analysis and diagrams for a different repository than the one requested, with no error surfaced; core output is silently mislabeled.
recommendation: On clone failure return an error; analyze only the exact resolved repo_dir and drop the first-directory fallback.

SRV.note: Same root cause as SRV-07; a failed clone now returns an error instead of analyzing a different cached repository

title: validate_url panics on unchecked parts[1] for URLs lacking a repo segment
evidence: parts = split('/') of the path after github.com/ with '.git' trimmed; parts[0] and parts[1] are indexed without bounds checks. Inputs that pass the starts_with gate but have no second segment, e.g. "https://github.com/foo" or "https://github.com/", yield a 1- or 0-element vec and panic with index-out-of-bounds. Only reached from tests today (grep: sole caller web_repo.rs:128), but SRV-02's own remediation recommends wiring validate_url into the clone path.
impact: If adopted as the clone guard per SRV-02, a crafted repo_url crashes the handling thread and, given the single-threaded accept loop (SRV-04), the whole server. Latent as currently wired.
recommendation: Use parts.get(0)/get(1) with a returned Err on missing segments, add negative tests, and prefer a parsed-URL/regex host check over trim/replace.

SRV.note: validate_url delegates to parse_repo_url, which uses get() with explicit errors and validates owner, repo, ref and path segments

title: /api/source reads any file the server can access: unauthenticated arbitrary file read on 0.0.0.0 with CORS *
evidence: server.rs:96-112 takes the file/path query value and decodes only %2F, %20 and %2B. server.rs:120 places the raw decoded_path first in direct_candidates. server.rs:200-203 calls fs::read_to_string on it, and server.rs:226-233 returns the content in JSON. There is no canonicalize or containment check, unlike the static branch at server.rs:256-272. The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32), the default port is 8080 (main.rs:534), and every JSON response sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (server.rs:327). Trigger: GET /api/source?file=/etc/passwd, or file=C:/Users/<u>/.ssh/id_ed25519, or path=..%2F..%2F.aws%2Fcredentials, returns 200 {"found":true,"content":"..."}. A Node mirror of the parsing confirmed that candidate[0] equals the raw path.
impact: Anyone on the network can exfiltrate SSH keys, cloud credentials and source code from a machine running `openheart server`. So can any web page the user visits, because a simple GET is readable under ACAO * and the unchecked Host header also allows DNS rebinding.
recommendation: Canonicalize the requested path and require it to lie under an allow-listed root (the analyzed repo directory). Drop the raw-path candidates and the walkdir fallbacks. Bind 127.0.0.1 by default, restrict or remove ACAO *, and validate the Host header.

SRV.note: /api/source now resolves only against the files an analysis (or a configured sample root) indexed; containment is re-checked at read time; raw-path and walkdir fallbacks removed; default bind is 127.0.0.1; CORS is an allowlist; Host is validated

title: Studio silently replaces Rust-engine output with a 30-file regex sampler and labels it 'SCPG ... Verified'
evidence: index.html:862 aborts the /api/analyze fetch after 2500 ms. The server writes its response only after git clone and the full 10-phase pipeline (server.rs:251-253, 429-436). On abort, or on the GitHub Pages deployment where /api/analyze does not exist (deploy_pages.yml uploads web/), index.html:881 and 912 fall back to GitHubEngine. That engine regex-parses only sourceFiles.slice(0, 30) (github-engine.js:103; 80 files for folder or ZIP at :200). It reports files_processed as the count of all discovered files and execution_time_ms as a hard-coded 280 (github-engine.js:161-164). It sets a random compiler_hash with verified: true (:576-577). The badge at index.html:920 shows 'SCPG 0x<base36 timestamp> · Verified'; a Node mirror printed 'SCPG 0xMW94DEQI · Verified'. Non-class projections are further capped at 4-12 classes (graph-canvas.js:240-538).
impact: When clone plus analysis takes longer than 2.5 s, or on any import in the hosted studio, users see diagrams of at most the first 30 files in tree order from a regex parser. These are presented as a verified SCPG of the whole repo. In that session the Rust engine's output is never shown, because customGraphIr pins the view (graph-canvas.js:100, 604-617).
recommendation: Make /api/analyze asynchronous (job id plus polling) or raise the timeout well above clone time. Label any fallback result as a partial in-browser sample, report the true parsed-file count, and remove the fabricated hash and verified fields.

SRV.note: Server side done: an async job mode ('async':true returns 202 and a poll URL at /api/jobs/<id>), the real scpg_hash in responses, and a session cookie. The studio's 2.5 s abort and its 'Verified' label live in web/ (handoff)
